verdicts.stale: a newer primary source says otherwise
verdicts.imprecise: right direction, wrong detail (overstated, wrong cohort, altered interval)
verdicts.wrong: the source does not say this or says the opposite; an identifier for another paper
verdicts.unsourced: no source on the record bears on the claim
verdicts.unreachable: the source could not be read; not counted as an error

claims.claim: Low-dose CT screening cuts mortality by 20-24%.
claims.note: NLST abstract: 'relative reduction in mortality from lung cancer ... of 20.0%'; NELSON abstract: 'cumulative rate ratio for death from lung cancer at 10 years was 0.76' among men (primary analysis), women 0.67 (0.38-1.14, not significant). The figures are lung cancer mortality, not mortality; the 24% is the male primary analysis.
claims.fixed: 'cuts mortality by 20-24%' -> 'cuts lung cancer mortality by 20-24% (20% in NLST; 24% in men in NELSON)' in lung-core.ts NSCLC_EXISTING and the identical cancers.ts nsclc summary

claims.claim: Non-small-cell disease is about 85 percent of lung cancer, so the world figures for the site are very close to the figures for this disease: 2,637,005 new lung cancers and 1,861,839 deaths a year, first in the world on both counts (GLOBOCAN 2024).
claims.note: Fact sheet header prints 'GLOBOCAN 2024'; Lung incidence rank 1, '2 637 005', mortality rank 1, '1 861 839'. Wikipedia NSCLC: 'Non-small-cell lung cancer accounts for about 85% of all lung cancers.'

claims.claim: GLOBOCAN does not split lung cancer by histology, so the split has to be read from registry series: of 1,572,045 lung cancers in men in 2022, 45.6 percent were adenocarcinoma, 29.4 percent squamous cell carcinoma and 6.5 percent large-cell carcinoma, and of 908,630 in women, 59.7, 17.1 and 6.5 percent, which is 81.5 percent of men's and 83.3 percent of women's lung cancers in the three non-small-cell types (Lancet Respiratory Medicine 2025).
claims.note: Lancet Respir Med 2025 abstract: '1 572 045 new cases ... among male individuals, of which 717 211 (45·6%) were adenocarcinoma, 461 171 (29·4%) were SCC ... 101 861 (6·5%) were large-cell'; women '908 630 ... (59·7%) ... (17·1%) ... (6·5%)'. Sums 81.5 and 83.3 are arithmetic from these. Dated 2022 (GLOBOCAN 2022 base).

claims.claim: In the UK the site total is around 50,200 cases and 32,800 deaths a year (Cancer Research UK); in the United States 229,410 cases and 124,990 deaths are projected for 2026, with a five-year relative survival of 29.5 percent for the site (SEER).
claims.note: CRUK: '50,218 new cases of lung cancer, 2019, 2021-2022, UK' and '32,800 deaths from lung cancer, 2022-2024, UK'. SEER: 'Estimated New Cases in 2026 229,410', 'Estimated Deaths in 2026 124,990', 5-year relative survival 29.5%.

claims.claim: In the United States lung cancer incidence is falling 1.9 percent a year and mortality 4.1 percent a year, the mortality falling faster than the incidence because more cancers are found early and because targeted drugs and immunotherapy work.
claims.note: SEER: 'age-adjusted rates for new lung and bronchus cancer cases have been falling on average 1.9% each year over 2014-2023. Age-adjusted death rates have been falling on average 4.1% each year over 2015-2024.' The causal explanation (earlier detection, drugs) is not stated by SEER; no figure attached to it.

claims.claim: In the UK incidence is down 11 percent since the early 1990s and mortality down 40 percent since the early 1970s, but the projection to 2038 to 2040 is for around 66,200 cases a year: rates fall while the population ages, so the count rises.
claims.note: CRUK incidence: 'decreased by around a tenth (11%) in the UK since the early 1990s'; '66,200 new cases each year by 2038-2040'. CRUK mortality: 'decreased by two-fifths (40%) in the UK since the early 1970s'.

claims.claim: In England 34 percent of staged cases in 2022 were stage I or II; in the United States 24 percent are localised at diagnosis, 21 percent regional and 51 percent already distant (Cancer Research UK;
claims.note: CRUK: 'In 2022, 34% (around 12,200) of lung cancer cases with a known stage were diagnosed at an early stage (I & II) in England.' SEER: 'Localized (24%)', 'Regional (21%)', 'Distant (51%)'.

claims.claim: Cancer Research UK attributes 72 percent of UK lung cancer cases to tobacco, 71 percent to active smoking and 1 percent to second-hand smoke, and about 86 percent of UK lung cancer deaths to smoking.
claims.note: CRUK risk: '72% of lung cancer cases in the UK are caused by smoking - 71% caused by active smoking, and 1% caused by environmental tobacco smoke' and 'An estimated 86% of lung cancer deaths in the UK are causes by tobacco smoking.'

claims.claim: Stopping works and works better the earlier it happens: of British men who smoke all their lives 15.9 percent die of lung cancer by age 75, against 9.9 percent of those who stop by 60, 6 percent by 50, 3 percent by 40 and 1.7 percent by 30; in women the figures are 9.5 percent for lifelong smokers, 5.3 percent for stopping by 60 and 2.2 percent by 50.
claims.note: CRUK risk: 'In men, 15.9% of those who smoke all their lives die from lung cancer by age 75, compared with 9.9% ... by age 60, 6% ... by age 50, 3% ... by age 40, and 1.7% ... by age 30. In women, 9.5% ... 5.3% ... by age 60, and 2.2% ... by age 50.'

claims.claim: Risk in people who stopped about 7 years ago is 43 percent lower than in current smokers, and 72 percent lower about 12 years after stopping.
claims.note: CRUK risk: 'quit around 7 years previously is 43% lower compared with current smokers' and 'quit around 12 years previously is 72% lower'.

claims.claim: Starting younger is worse: lung cancer death risk is 37 percent higher per five years younger at starting (Cancer Research UK, quoting the studies behind each figure).
claims.note: CRUK risk: 'Lung cancer death risk is 37% higher per five years younger at smoking initiation, a cohort study of women showed.' The page applied a women-only cohort figure to everyone.
claims.fixed: Now reads 'in a cohort study of women, lung cancer death risk was 37 percent higher per five years younger at starting'

claims.claim: Workplace exposures account for 13 percent of UK cases, and asbestos alone is linked to 6 to 8 percent of UK lung cancer deaths each year, with lung cancer mortality 77 percent higher in asbestos-exposed workers than in the general population.
claims.note: CRUK risk: '13% of lung cancer cases in the UK are caused by workplace exposures'; 'An estimated 6-8% of lung cancer deaths in the UK each year are linked to asbestos exposure'; 'Lung cancer mortality is 77% higher in asbestos-exposed workers, compared with the general population'.

claims.claim: Outdoor air pollution accounts for 8 percent of UK cases; adenocarcinoma risk is 40 percent higher per 10 micrograms per cubic metre of fine particulate matter, and overall lung cancer risk 9 percent higher, with no significant association for the coarser PM10 fraction.
claims.note: CRUK risk: '8% of lung cancer cases in the UK are caused by air pollution'; 'Lung adenocarcinoma risk is 40% higher per 10µg/m3 of PM2.5'; 'Lung cancer risk overall is associated only with PM2.5 (9% higher risk per 10µg/m3); the association with PM10 is not significant'. (CRUK also gives adenocarcinoma 29% per PM10; the page's 'no significant association' sits with overall risk.)

claims.claim: Ionising radiation accounts for 5 percent, of which indoor radon is the largest part: an estimated 9 percent of European lung cancer deaths are linked to indoor radon, and risk rises 16 percent per 100 becquerels per cubic metre of usual home radon.
claims.note: CRUK risk: '5% of lung cancer cases in the UK are caused by ionising radiation'; 'An estimated 9% of lung cancer deaths in Europe are linked to indoor radon exposure'; '16% higher per 100 becquerel/cubic metre'. 'Radon is the largest part' is not stated by CRUK but carries no figure.

claims.claim: Second-hand smoke accounts for 1 percent of all cases but an estimated 15 percent of cases in people who have never smoked, raising their risk by 31 percent.
claims.note: CRUK risk: '1% of lung cancer cases in the UK are caused by environmental tobacco smoke'; 'An estimated 15% of lung cancer cases in never-smokers in the UK are linked to ETS'; 'Lung cancer risk in people who have never smoked is 31% higher in those exposed'.

claims.claim: Family history matters independently of smoking: risk is 82 percent higher with an affected sibling and 25 to 37 percent higher with an affected parent.
claims.note: CRUK risk: 'Lung cancer risk is 82% higher in people whose sibling has/had lung cancer, and 25-37% higher in people whose parent has/had the disease ... The association is independent of smoking.'

claims.claim: Previous lung disease matters too, with risk 43 to 57 percent higher after pneumonia and 104 to 144 percent higher after emphysema.
claims.note: CRUK risk: 'Lung cancer risk is 43-57% higher in people with a history of pneumonia'; 'Lung cancer risk is 104-144% higher in people with a history of emphysema'.

claims.claim: The smaller occupational exposures each account for a fraction of a percent of British cases: silica 0.02 percent, diesel engine exhaust 0.02 percent, painting 0.01 percent, welding 0.001 percent (Cancer Research UK).
claims.note: CRUK risk: silica 'An estimated 0.02% of lung cancers in Britain', diesel engine exhaust '0.02%', painter '0.01%', welder '0.001%'.

claims.claim: Fifteen percent of lung cancers diagnosed in the UK arise in never-smokers, which would make it the 8th commonest cancer in the country if it were counted as a disease of its own (BJC Reports 2023); worldwide the figure is put at 15 to 25 percent depending on the region, and if counted separately it would be the 7th commonest cause of cancer death (OLIVE protocol, BMJ Open Respiratory Research 2026;
claims.note: BJC Reports 2023 abstract: 'LCINS accounts for 15% of lung cancers diagnosed in the UK, making it the 8th most common cancer.' OLIVE protocol: 'if considered separately, LCINS is the seventh most common cause of cancer-related death worldwide.' HSR 2026: '~15%-25% depending on the geographic region'.

claims.claim: The UK's largest prospective look at it, the Million Women Study, followed 634,039 never-smoking women for 14 years and found 1,469 lung cancers, 0.2 percent of the cohort; of 34 candidate risk factors only three reached significance, non-white ethnicity (relative risk 2.34), asthma requiring treatment (1.32) and height of 165 cm or more (1.16), and restricting the analysis to adenocarcinoma did not change the result.
claims.note: Pirie 2016 abstract: 'half (634,039) reported that they had never smoked ... during 14 (SD3) years of follow-up, 0.2% (1,469) ... 34 potential risk factors, of which 31 were nonsignificant ... non-white vs. white ethnicity (RR = 2.34 ...), asthma requiring treatment (RR = 1.32 ...) and taller stature (height >= 165 cm vs. <160 cm: RR = 1.16 ...). The findings were not materially affected by restricting the analyses to adenocarcinomas'.

claims.claim: In England in 2019 about 26 percent of lung cancers were diagnosed after an urgent suspected cancer referral and 33 percent after an emergency presentation (Cancer Research UK).
claims.note: CRUK: 'For lung cancer cases diagnosed in England in 2019, around 1 in 4 (26%) were diagnosed via an urgent suspected cancer (two week wait) referral and 1 in 3 (33%) via an emergency presentation.'

claims.claim: The National Lung Screening Trial gave 53,454 Americans aged 55 to 74 with 30 or more pack-years three annual low-dose CT scans or chest radiographs and cut lung cancer mortality by 20.0 percent (95 percent confidence interval 6.8 to 26.7) and all-cause mortality by 6.7 percent.
claims.note: NLST abstract: 53,454 enrolled, three annual screenings with low-dose CT or chest radiography, 'relative reduction in mortality from lung cancer ... of 20.0% (95% CI, 6.8 to 26.7)', all-cause 'by 6.7%'; full text: 'between 55 and 74 years ... at least 30 pack-years'.

claims.claim: NELSON gave 13,195 men and 2,594 women aged 50 to 74 volume CT at baseline and years 1, 3 and 5.5, and found a lung cancer death rate ratio of 0.76 (0.61 to 0.94) in men at ten years, with only 2.1 percent of participants referred for a suspicious nodule.
claims.note: NELSON abstract: 13,195 men and 2594 women aged 50-74, screening at T0, year 1, year 3, year 5.5; 'cumulative rate ratio for death from lung cancer at 10 years was 0.76 (95% CI, 0.61 to 0.94)' in men. On referral it says only 'The overall referral rate for suspicious nodules was 2.1%', without saying the denominator is participants; the page turned it into '2.1 percent of participants referred'.
claims.fixed: 'with only 2.1 percent of participants referred for a suspicious nodule' -> 'with an overall referral rate for suspicious nodules of 2.1 percent' (the abstract's wording)

claims.claim: The number needed to screen to prevent one lung cancer death is 323 over 6.5 years in the National Lung Screening Trial and 130 over ten years in NELSON.
claims.note: USPSTF evidence report (Jonas 2021) abstract: NLST 'number needed to screen [NNS] to prevent 1 lung cancer death, 323 over 6.5 years'; NELSON 'NNS ... of 130 over 10 years'.

claims.claim: The harms are real and are the reason screening is targeted rather than universal: 24.2 percent of low-dose CT screens in the National Lung Screening Trial were positive and 96.4 percent of those positives were false; false positives led to 17 invasive procedures per 1,000 people screened, with fewer than one major complication; incidental findings were reported in 4.4 to 40.7 percent of people screened; and estimates of overdiagnosis, the cancers found that would never have caused harm, ranged from 0 to 67 percent across studies (US Preventive Services Task Force evidence report, 2021).
claims.note: NLST abstract: 'rate of positive screening tests was 24.2% with low-dose CT', '96.4% of the positive screening results in the low-dose CT group ... were false positive'; Jonas 2021: 'false-positive results led to 17 invasive procedures ... and fewer than 1 person having a major complication', 'Overdiagnosis estimates varied greatly (0%-67%...)', 'Incidental findings ... (4.4%-40.7% of persons screened)'.

claims.claim: In the United States the Task Force recommends annual low-dose CT from 50 to 80 for people with a 20 pack-year history who smoke or stopped within the past 15 years (grade B, 2021), widened from the 55 to 80 and 30 pack-year criteria of 2013.
claims.note: USPSTF 2021 statement abstract: 'annual screening ... in adults aged 50 to 80 years who have a 20 pack-year smoking history and currently smoke or have quit within the past 15 years ... (B recommendation)', replacing 2013 'aged 55 to 80 years who have a 30 pack-year smoking history'.

claims.claim: The UK National Screening Committee recommended targeted screening in June 2022 for people aged 55 to 74 identified as being at high risk, with smoking cessation built into the service, and named England's Targeted Lung Health Check programme as the starting point.
claims.note: UK NSC page: 'Based on the last UK NSC review ... June 2022. ... Targeted screening for lung cancer is recommended for people aged 55 to 74 identified as being at high risk', 'with integrated smoking cessation service provision. The Targeted Lung Health Checks (TLHC) programme provides a feasible and effective starting point for implementation in England.'

claims.claim: The national programme was announced on 26 June 2023, costs £270 million a year at full size and is expected to deliver almost one million scans and find as many as 9,000 cancers a year.
claims.note: GOV.UK, 'Published: 26 June 2023': 'will cost £270 million annually once fully implemented - is expected to detect cancer in as many as 9,000 people, deliver almost one million scans'.

claims.claim: Eligibility is not age alone: a person's GP record identifies ever-smokers aged 55 to 74, and a risk model decides who is scanned, using PLCOm2012 or the Liverpool Lung Project version 2 in England, at a PLCOm2012 threshold of 1.51 percent risk over six years.
claims.note: GOV.UK: 'GP records for those aged 55 to 74 to identify current or former smokers ... risk of cancer assessed'; Cancer Epidemiol 2023 full text: 'NHS England protocol specified that individuals aged 55-74 years be referred for LDCT screening if their lung cancer risk exceeds 1.51 % by the PLCOm2012 model (six year risk) or 2.5 % by the Liverpool Lung Project version 2'.

claims.claim: The first phase invited about 900,000 people, made 375,000 risk assessments, carried out 200,000 scans and found more than 2,000 cancers, of which 76 percent were early stage against 29 percent outside the programme in 2019, and about 70 percent of the scanning was done in mobile units parked in places such as supermarket car parks, deliberately in more deprived areas where people are four times more likely to smoke.
claims.note: GOV.UK: 'almost 900,000 people were invited for checks, 375,000 risk assessments made and 200,000 scans ... More than 2,000 people were detected as having cancer, 76% at an earlier stage compared to 29% in 2019 outside of the programme', 'approximately 70% of the screening took place in mobile units ... supermarket car parks ... more deprived areas where people are 4 times more likely to smoke'.

claims.claim: By March 2025 the programme had invited over two million people and diagnosed 7,193 lung cancers, 63.1 percent at stage 1 and 12.6 percent at stage 2, and the early-stage share of all lung cancer in England rose over the five years, most in the most deprived regions.
claims.note: Nature Medicine 2026 abstract: 'invited over two million people, with 7,193 lung cancers diagnosed-63.1% at ... stage 1 and 12.6% stage 2-to March 2025. This has increased the early-stage proportion of lung cancer in England over 5 years, particularly in socioeconomically deprived regions.'

claims.claim: Enlarged nodes (10 mm or more in short axis on CT) or other lesions are biopsied in preference to the primary when the nodal stage decides treatment.
claims.note: NICE NG122 1.2.17: 'Biopsy any enlarged intrathoracic nodes (10 mm or larger maximum short axis on CT) or other lesions in preference to the primary lesion if determination of nodal stage affects treatment.'

claims.claim: Brain imaging is staged to the stage: none for clinical stage 1 without neurological symptoms, where the prevalence of brain metastases is about 4 percent; contrast-enhanced brain CT for clinical stage 2; contrast-enhanced brain MRI for stage 3.
claims.note: NG122 1.2.24-1.2.26 (no brain imaging stage 1 without symptoms, contrast CT stage 2, contrast MRI stage 3) and rationale: 'prevalence of detectable brain metastases is fairly low (around 4%)'.

claims.claim: One caution a reader should know: NG122's recommendations were written against the 7th edition of the American Joint Committee on Cancer staging system, which NICE says on the page, while staging in the clinic has moved two editions on.
claims.note: NG122: 'The guideline recommendations were developed using the 7th edition of the American Joint Committee on Cancer (AJCC) staging system.' Ninth edition effective 1 January 2025 (BJR 2025 abstract).

claims.claim: The International Association for the Study of Lung Cancer built a new database of 124,581 patients diagnosed between 2011 and 2019 and analysed 76,518 of them.
claims.note: Rami-Porta JTO 2024: '76,518 patients from a total of 124,581 registered patients were available for analyses'; M-descriptor paper: 'A database of 124,581 patients diagnosed between 2011 and 2019'.

claims.claim: The M descriptors changed at the far end, splitting M1c into M1c1, multiple metastases in one extrathoracic organ system, and M1c2, multiple metastases in several organ systems; both stay in stage group IVB.
claims.note: Rami-Porta JTO 2024: 'M1c1, multiple extrathoracic metastases in one organ system, and M1c2, multiple extrathoracic metastases in multiple organ systems ... M1c1 and M1c2 remain in stage group IVB.'

claims.claim: The stage groups moved to follow: T1N1 to IIA, T1N2a to IIB, T3N2a to IIIA, and T2aN2b and T2bN2b to IIIB.
claims.note: Rami-Porta JTO 2024: 'T1N1, T1N2a, and T3N2a subgroups are assigned to IIA, IIB, and IIIA ... T2aN2b and T2bN2b subgroups are assigned to IIIB.'

claims.claim: Because tobacco causes about 72 percent of UK cases, prevention is tobacco control and stopping smoking, and nothing else comes close.
claims.note: CRUK risk factors: '72% of lung cancer cases in the UK are caused by smoking'.

claims.claim: NICE NG209 covers the whole of it, from preventing uptake in people aged 24 and under to treating dependence in everyone aged 12 and over, and was last updated on 4 February 2025 to add recommendations on cytisinicline.
claims.note: NICE NG209: 'Last updated: 04 February 2025'; 'support to stop smoking for everyone aged 12 and over', 'young adults aged 24 and under from taking up smoking'; 'We reviewed the evidence for cytisinicline ... new and updated recommendations'.

claims.claim: About 85 percent of lung cancer, and lung cancer is first in the world for both new cases and deaths: 2,637,005 cases and 1,861,839 deaths a year (GLOBOCAN 2024).
claims.note: IARC fact sheet, edition printed 'GLOBOCAN 2024 - 08.07.2026': lung rank 1, '2 637 005' cases, rank 1, '1 861 839' deaths; labelled GLOBOCAN 2024 on the page. Wikipedia NSCLC: 'accounts for about 85% of all lung cancers'.

claims.claim: Around 50,200 UK lung cancers and 32,800 UK deaths a year (Cancer Research UK);
claims.note: CRUK lung statistics: '50,218 new cases of lung cancer, 2019, 2021-2022, UK', '32,800 deaths from lung cancer, 2022-2024, UK'.

claims.claim: 229,410 US cases and 124,990 deaths projected for 2026, with five-year relative survival of 29.5 percent for the site (SEER).
claims.note: SEER stat facts: "Estimated New Cases in 2026 229,410 ... Estimated Deaths in 2026 124,990 ... 5-Year Relative Survival 29.5% 2016-2022".

claims.claim: Of lung cancers in men worldwide 45.6 percent are adenocarcinoma, 29.4 percent squamous and 6.5 percent large-cell; in women 59.7, 17.1 and 6.5 percent (Lancet Respiratory Medicine 2025).
claims.note: Lancet Respir Med 2025 (Europe PMC abstract): "In 2022, we estimated ... 1 572 045 new cases ... among male individuals ... 717 211 (45.6%) adenocarcinoma, 461 171 (29.4%) SCC ... 101 861 (6.5%) large-cell"; women 59.7/17.1/6.5%. Figures match but are GLOBOCAN-2022-derived estimates presented undated in the present tense.
claims.fixed: Dated: "Of lung cancers in men worldwide in 2022, 45.6 percent were ..." and labelled "estimates from GLOBOCAN 2022".

claims.claim: In the United States 29.5 percent of people diagnosed with lung and bronchus cancer in 2016 to 2022 were alive five years later relative to people of the same age without the disease; by stage that is 65.5 percent for localised disease (24 percent of cases), 38.2 percent for regional (21 percent), 10.5 percent for distant (51 percent) and 17.5 percent for unstaged (4 percent) (SEER).
claims.note: SEER: "Localized ... 24% 65.5% Regional ... 21% 38.2% Distant ... 51% 10.5% Unknown Unstaged 4% 17.5%"; 29.5% for 2016-2022.

claims.claim: In the UK, 11.1 percent of people are predicted to survive ten years or more, up from 3.3 percent in the 1970s;
claims.note: CRUK: "around 1 in 10 (11.1%) people diagnosed with lung cancer survive their disease for ten years or more (2018)"; "In the 1970s, almost 5 in 100 (3.3%)".

claims.claim: 18.1 percent of people diagnosed in England survive five years, rising to 43.5 percent among those who have already survived one year.
claims.note: CRUK: "Almost 1 in 5 (18.1%) people diagnosed with lung cancer in England survive ... five years ... already survived for one year, more than 4 in 10 (43.5%)".

claims.claim: Survival is higher in women than men and falls steeply with age: 32.7 percent of women and 22.2 percent of men diagnosed at 15 to 44 survive ten years, against 9.2 percent of women and 5.2 percent of men diagnosed at 75 to 99.
claims.note: CRUK: "1 in 3 (32.7%) females and more than 1 in 5 (22.2%) males ... aged 15-44 survive ... ten years ... compared with around 1 in 10 (9.2%) females and 5 in 100 (5.2%) males diagnosed aged 75-99 (2018)".

claims.claim: It also tracks deprivation: 20.1 percent five-year survival in the most deprived group in England against 27.6 percent in the least (Cancer Research UK).
claims.note: CRUK: "1 in 5 (20.1%) ... most deprived group in England survive ... five years ... compared with more than 1 in 4 (27.6%) in the least deprived group (2018-2022)".

claims.claim: 5-year PFS 60% with lorlatinib in ALK+ disease.
claims.note: CROWN 5-year, JCO 2024 abstract: "5-year PFS was 60% (95% CI, 51 to 68) and 8%". The cancers.ts card has no link of its own; the CROWN trial record (NCT03052608) on the same page carries the trial.

claims.claim: Lorlatinib: 5-year PFS 60% in ALK-positive disease, the longest for any targeted therapy in metastatic solid tumours.
claims.note: CROWN 5-year, JCO 2024: 5-year PFS 60%; conclusion "the longest PFS ever reported with any single-agent molecular targeted treatment in advanced NSCLC and across all metastatic solid tumors" (post hoc, investigator-assessed).

claims.claim: Adjuvant osimertinib after surgery roughly halves the risk of dying from EGFR-mutant disease (ADAURA, OS HR 0.49); adjuvant alectinib cuts recurrence by 76% (ALINA).
claims.note: ADAURA OS, NEJM 2023: "overall hazard ratio for death, 0.49"; ALINA, NEJM 2024: "hazard ratio for disease recurrence or death, 0.24" (stage II-IIIA).

claims.claim: Amivantamab + lazertinib is the first regimen to beat osimertinib, with median OS more than 12 months longer (MARIPOSA).
claims.note: MARIPOSA final OS, NEJM 2025: "hazard ratio for death, 0.75 ... 3-year overall survival was 60% and 51%"; median OS was not reached with amivantamab-lazertinib vs 36.7 months with osimertinib, so "median OS more than 12 months longer" is a projection, not a measured difference.
claims.fixed: Now: "first regimen to beat osimertinib on overall survival (MARIPOSA, HR 0.75; 3-year survival 60% vs 51%; median not reached vs 36.7 months)".

claims.claim: First-in-class bispecific ivonescimab beat pembrolizumab on PFS and OS in China; the US decision (PDUFA 14 Nov 2026) hinges on HARMONi.
claims.note: Summit 8-K (29 Jan 2026): "The FDA provided a Prescription Drug User Fee Act goal action date of November 14, 2026" for the BLA in EGFR-mutant NSCLC post-TKI (HARMONi). Summit 8-K exhibit (2 Sep 2026): HARMONi-2 "ivonescimab monotherapy demonstrated a statistically significant improvement" in OS; PFS HR 0.51.

claims.claim: 5-year survival with pembrolizumab in PD-L1-high disease is 31.9% in the KEYNOTE-024 five-year analysis, against 16.3% with platinum chemotherapy in the same trial.
claims.note: KEYNOTE-024 5-year, JCO 2021: "5-year OS rate were 31.9% for the pembrolizumab group and 16.3% for the chemotherapy group".

claims.claim: Adenocarcinoma is oncogene-addicted: EGFR 12 to 47% by ancestry, KRAS 27 to 33%, ALK 3 to 6%, MET exon 14 skipping 2 to 4%, ERBB2 exon 20 insertion about 2%, ROS1 1 to 3%, RET 1 to 2%, BRAF V600E 1 to 2%, NTRK and NRG1 below 0.5%.
claims.note: Summary of the adenocarcinoma landscape rows (cBioPortal counts). Re-counted EGFR 143/302 (47.4%) luad_oncosg_2020 and 70/566 (12.4%) TCGA PanCan; KRAS 787/2,653 (29.7%) and 33/302 (10.9%); per-gene ranges match the rows (ALK 2.9-5.6, MET ex14 1.6-3.7, ERBB2 ex20 1.7-2.2, ROS1 1.7-2.7, RET 1.3-2.1, BRAF V600E 0.7-2.2, NTRK 0.2, NRG1 0.3).
claims.checkedSource: https://www.cbioportal.org/api (mutation and discrete CNA fetch, re-counted)

claims.claim: Squamous carcinoma is copy-number driven: TP53 83 to 94%, SOX2 amplified about 40%, PIK3CA amplified 38%, TP63 about 30%, CDKN2A deleted 26%, FGFR1 17 to 22%, NFE2L2 12 to 15%, with targetable kinase alterations at 1 to 3%.
claims.checkedSource: https://www.cbioportal.org/api (mutation and discrete CNA fetch, re-counted)

claims.claim: EGFR is mutated in 47.4% of East Asian lung adenocarcinomas and 12.4% of the resected, mostly-smoker TCGA series;
claims.note: cBioPortal re-count: EGFR mutated in 143 of 302 sequenced (47.4%) in luad_oncosg_2020 and 70 of 566 (12.4%) in luad_tcga_pan_can_atlas_2018.
claims.checkedSource: https://www.cbioportal.org/api (mutation and discrete CNA fetch, re-counted)

claims.claim: KRAS runs the other way, 29.7% against 10.9%;
claims.note: cBioPortal re-count: KRAS 787/2,653 (29.7%) luad_mskcc_2023_met_organotropism vs 33/302 (10.9%) luad_oncosg_2020.
claims.checkedSource: https://www.cbioportal.org/api (mutation and discrete CNA fetch, re-counted)

claims.claim: TP53 falls from 52 to 54% in smoker cohorts to 15.5% in never-smoker whole genomes.
claims.note: cBioPortal: TP53 36/232 (15.5%) in lung_nci_2022 (re-counted); 52.1-53.9% in TCGA PanCan/MSK cohorts per the landscape row.
claims.checkedSource: https://www.cbioportal.org/api (mutation and discrete CNA fetch, re-counted)

claims.claim: PD-L1 is the only measurement that changes first-line treatment, and it is not standardised: four scoring rules on five assays, with 22C3, 28-8 and SP263 agreeing on tumour cells, SP142 staining less and 73-10 more, and agreement between pathologists of 0.18 to 0.19 on immune cells against 0.86 to 0.93 on tumour cells.
claims.note: Blueprint phase 2, JTO 2018: "highly comparable staining by the 22C3, 28-8 and SP263 assays; less sensitivity with the SP142 assay; and higher sensitivity with the 73-10 assay"; "TC ... ICC = 0.86-0.93, poor reliability in IC ... ICC = 0.18-0.19".

claims.claim: It tracks benefit from single-agent checkpoint blockade within every PD-L1 stratum, but the best data-derived cut-off was more than 19 mutations per megabase rather than the licensed 10, and it predicted nothing for pembrolizumab with chemotherapy, the regimen most patients receive.
claims.note: Ricciuti, JAMA Oncol 2022: "low TMB (<=19.0 mutations per megabase) and high TMB (>19.0)", associated with better outcomes "in each PD-L1 tumor proportion score subgroup"; Garassino, JTO CRR 2023: "no association ... between continuous tTMB score and OS or PFS for pembrolizumab-combination".

claims.claim: Small-cell lung cancer has one genotype and four states: TP53 and RB1 are both inactivated in nearly every tumour, and the classification that matters is transcriptional, ASCL1-dominant 69%, NEUROD1-dominant 17%, POU2F3 7%, and an inflamed class that gains most from immunotherapy.
claims.note: Baine, JTO 2020: "69% of cases were ASCL1-dominant and 17% were NEUROD1-dominant. POU2F3 was expressed in 7%"; Gay 2021: SCLC-I "experiences the greatest benefit from the addition of immunotherapy".

claims.claim: Screening (age 50-80, ≥20 pack-years): Annual low-dose CT with Lung-RADS reporting;
claims.note: USPSTF 2021 (JAMA), a link on the low-dose-ct-screening record: "annual screening for lung cancer with LDCT in adults aged 50 to 80 years who have a 20 pack-year smoking history".

claims.claim: Stage III unresectable: Concurrent platinum chemoradiation → durvalumab 1 year (PACIFIC), or osimertinib until progression if EGFR-mutant (LAURA).
claims.note: PACIFIC, NEJM 2017: durvalumab "every 2 weeks for up to 12 months" after platinum chemoradiotherapy.

claims.claim: 5-year PFS 60%) or alectinib first line; on progression, neladalkib (under review) or lorlatinib if not used; local therapy for oligoprogression; chemotherapy.
claims.note: CROWN 5-year, JCO 2024: "5-year PFS was 60%".

claims.claim: Metastatic, MET exon 14 skipping: Capmatinib or tepotinib first line; telisotuzumab vedotin for c-Met-overexpressing EGFR-wild-type disease after chemotherapy (accelerated 2025).
claims.note: FDA: "On May 14, 2025, the Food and Drug Administration granted accelerated approval" to telisotuzumab vedotin-tllv (openFDA: ORIG 20250514, priority).

claims.claim: Metastatic, driver-negative, PD-L1 TPS ≥50%: Pembrolizumab (KEYNOTE-024) or cemiplimab monotherapy; add chemotherapy for high burden or rapid progression.
claims.note: KEYNOTE-024 enrolled "PD-L1 tumor proportion score of at least 50%" (JCO 2021 abstract).

claims.claim: Metastatic, driver-negative, PD-L1 TPS <50%: Pembrolizumab + platinum doublet (KEYNOTE-189 non-squamous;
claims.note: The <50% split is a pathway category (pembrolizumab monotherapy is the >=50% option); KEYNOTE-189 enrolled regardless of PD-L1, so pembrolizumab-chemotherapy for TPS <50% is consistent. No trial figure is misstated.

claims.claim: See a GP for a cough lasting more than 3 weeks; ask for an urgent appointment or call NHS 111 if you cough up blood; call 999 if you are struggling to breathe or have pain in the chest or upper back (NHS)
claims.note: NHS: "See a GP if: you've had a cough for longer than 3 weeks ... urgent GP appointment or get help from NHS 111 if: you've coughed up blood ... Call 999 ... struggling to breathe ... pain in your chest or upper back".

claims.claim: Image-guided biopsy for peripheral lesions when treatment can be planned from that alone; biopsy enlarged nodes (10 mm or more short axis on CT) in preference to the primary when the nodal stage matters (NICE NG122 1.2.16, 1.2.17)
claims.note: NG122 1.2.17: "Biopsy any enlarged intrathoracic nodes (10 mm or larger maximum short axis on CT) or other lesions in preference to the primary lesion if determination of nodal stage affects treatment".

claims.claim: Brain imaging by stage: none for clinical stage 1 without neurological symptoms (brain metastasis prevalence about 4 percent), contrast-enhanced CT for stage 2, contrast-enhanced MRI for stage 3 (NICE NG122 1.2.24 to 1.2.26)
claims.note: NG122 rationale: "clinical stage 1 ... no neurological symptoms, the prevalence of detectable brain metastases is fairly low (around 4%)"; 1.2.24-1.2.26 none / contrast CT / contrast MRI.

claims.claim: TNM 9th edition, in force since 1 January 2025 and built on 124,581 patients diagnosed 2011 to 2019 (British Journal of Radiology 2025;
claims.note: BJR 2025: "The ninth edition of the TNM classification, effective January 1, 2025"; IASLC (JTO 2024): "Data on 124,581 patients diagnosed with lung cancer from January 1, 2011 to December 31, 2019".

claims.claim: M1c1 and M1c2 both sit in stage IVB
claims.note: IASLC stage groups, JTO 2024: "M1c1 and M1c2 remain in stage group IVB".

claims.claim: Stage groups that moved in the ninth edition: T1N1 to IIA, T1N2a to IIB, T3N2a to IIIA, T2aN2b and T2bN2b to IIIB
claims.note: IASLC stage groups, JTO 2024: "T1N1, T1N2a, and T3N2a subgroups are assigned to IIA, IIB, and IIIA ... T2aN2b and T2bN2b subgroups are assigned to IIIB".

claims.claim: NICE NG122's recommendations were written against the 7th edition of the AJCC staging system, which the guideline states on the page; the clinic is two editions ahead of it
claims.note: NG122: "The guideline recommendations were developed using the 7th edition of the American Joint Committee on Cancer (AJCC) staging system".

claims.claim: In England 34 percent of staged lung cancers in 2022 were stage I or II; in the United States 24 percent are localised, 21 percent regional and 51 percent distant at diagnosis (Cancer Research UK;
claims.note: CRUK: "In 2022, 34% (around 12,200) of lung cancer cases with a known stage were diagnosed at an early stage (I & II) in England"; SEER 24/21/51%.

claims.claim: Screening uptake is under 20% in the US and lower elsewhere; never-smoker adenocarcinoma has no screening pathway.
claims.note: No source on the record bore on screening uptake (low-dose-ct-screening and nsclc links are trials/USPSTF). American Lung Association State of Lung Cancer: "Nationally, only 18.2% of those at high risk were screened" (2022 data). Figure is right; source added.
claims.fixed: Added ALA link to the nsclc record links (lung-core.ts) and the figure "18.2% of eligible people were screened in 2022, American Lung Association".

claims.claim: KRAS G12C inhibitors add only ~1-2 months of PFS over docetaxel; non-G12C KRAS (G12D, G12V) remains undrugged outside trials.
claims.note: CodeBreaK 200, Lancet 2023: median PFS 5.6 vs 4.5 months (1.1 months); KRYSTAL-12, Lancet 2024: 5.5 vs 3.8 months (1.7 months).

claims.claim: ADCs after TKI failure have not yet shown a survival benefit over platinum chemotherapy (HERTHENA-Lung02, TROPION-Lung01), and ILD limits combinations.
claims.note: No longer true: OptiTROP-Lung04 (NEJM 2026) found sacituzumab tirumotecan vs pemetrexed-platinum after EGFR-TKI "Overall survival was significantly longer ... (hazard ratio for death, 0.60 ...)". Also TROPION-Lung01 compared with docetaxel, not platinum chemotherapy.
claims.fixed: Rewritten: outside China no ADC survival benefit yet (HERTHENA-Lung02 vs platinum; TROPION-Lung01 vs docetaxel); OptiTROP-Lung04 (China) OS HR 0.60; OptiTROP link added to the nsclc record links.

claims.claim: Brain metastases occur in 30-50% of driver-positive patients;
claims.note: No source on the record states a brain-metastasis rate; the 30-50% found in the literature (e.g. CNS Oncol 2024, doi 10.1080/20450907.2024.2395804) is for NSCLC overall, not driver-positive patients.
claims.fixed: Figure removed: "Brain metastases are common in driver-positive disease;".

claims.claim: Fifty-one percent of American cases are already distant at diagnosis and survive 10.5 percent at five years, against 65.5 percent for the quarter found while the cancer is confined to the lung (SEER).
claims.note: SEER: distant 51% of cases, 10.5% five-year relative survival; localised (confined to primary site) 24%, 65.5%.

claims.claim: Fifteen percent of UK cases and 15 to 25 percent worldwide arise in people who never smoked, and every eligibility rule starts from a smoking history, so the fastest-growing part of the disease is the part no programme is looking for.
claims.note: BJC Reports 2023: "LCINS accounts for 15% of lung cancers diagnosed in the UK"; Health Sci Rep 2026 (on the record): "~15%-25% depending on the geographic region".

claims.claim: The largest UK prospective study found only three significant factors of 34 examined in 634,039 never-smoking women, and two of them, height and ethnicity, are not actionable (Million Women Study 2016).
claims.note: Million Women Study, IJC 2016: 634,039 never smokers; "34 potential risk factors, of which 31 were nonsignificant"; ethnicity, asthma, height.

claims.claim: The staging change of January 2025 breaks every survival series that spans it.
claims.note: BJR 2025: ninth edition "effective January 1, 2025".

claims.claim: N2a and N2b patients were one group until 2024, several stage groups moved, and a cohort staged either side of the line cannot be pooled without restaging.
claims.note: N2 split into N2a/N2b in the ninth edition effective 1 January 2025 (BJR 2025); stage groups moved (JTO 2024).

claims.claim: NG122 states that its recommendations were developed with the 7th edition of the AJCC system while the ninth edition of TNM has been in force since January 2025, and the thresholds in the guideline (for example which stage triggers brain imaging) were fixed against the older groupings.
claims.note: NG122 states 7th edition AJCC; ninth edition TNM effective 1 January 2025 (BJR 2025).

claims.claim: More than half of KRAS-mutant lung adenocarcinoma has no approved inhibitor: G12C is 41 to 51% of KRAS records, and G12V, G12D, G12A, G13X and Q61X together are the rest.
claims.note: cBioPortal re-count: G12C 344 of 797 KRAS records (43.2%) in luad_mskcc_2023_met_organotropism; the landscape row gives 40.7-50.9% across cohorts.
claims.checkedSource: https://www.cbioportal.org/api (mutation and discrete CNA fetch, re-counted)

claims.claim: A coding-exon panel returns wild-type for ALK, ROS1, RET, NTRK and NRG1 rearrangements and for MET exon 14 skipping, together about 8 to 10% of lung adenocarcinoma, and the patients most likely to be under-tested are never smokers, who are the likeliest to have one.
claims.note: Not stated by any source; summing the landscape rows gives ALK+ROS1+RET+NTRK+NRG1 fusions plus MET exon 14 at 11.3% (luad_mskcc_2023_met_organotropism), about 10.8% (lung_msk_2017) and 9.8% (nsclc_ctdx_msk_2022), so "8 to 10%" understates the cited cohorts.
claims.checkedSource: https://www.cbioportal.org/api (mutation and discrete CNA fetch, re-counted)
claims.fixed: Now "about 10 to 11% of lung adenocarcinoma in the large panel cohorts".

claims.claim: The transcriptional subtypes of small-cell lung cancer have no approved assay, no prospective trial, and a moving target: 37% of tumours express two of the four markers at once and platinum shifts tumours towards the inflamed state.
claims.note: Baine, JTO 2020: "37% ASCL1+/NEUROD1+"; Gay 2021: "Cisplatin treatment of SCLC-A patient-derived xenografts induces intratumoral shifts toward SCLC-I".

claims.claim: EGFR mutations were discovered in 2004 when three Boston groups worked out why a minority of lung cancers, mostly in never-smoking women and East Asian patients, melted away on gefitinib.
claims.note: Wikipedia (the record's cited source) cites the two 2004 Boston papers: Lynch et al. NEJM 2004 (Massachusetts General Hospital, Boston) and Paez et al. Science 2004 (Dana-Farber, Boston). The third 2004 paper usually grouped with them, Pao et al. PNAS 2004, came from Memorial Sloan-Kettering, New York. 'Three Boston groups' is wrong; 2004 is right.
claims.fixed: 'three Boston groups' changed to 'two Boston groups'

claims.claim: The IPASS trial (2009) then showed that in mutation carriers gefitinib beat chemotherapy and in non-carriers it was worse, which made EGFR testing mandatory before first-line treatment and established the model of a driver mutation matched to a pill.
claims.note: Neither the Wikipedia page nor NCCN cited on the record mentions IPASS, and IPASS is not linked from the record. The claim matches the paper (Mok, NEJM 2009): EGFR mutation-positive PFS HR 0.48 favouring gefitinib; mutation-negative subgroup favoured carboplatin-paclitaxel.
claims.fixed: Added IPASS NEJM 2009 link to the record's links; text unchanged

claims.claim: Osimertinib, designed against the T790M resistance mutation, beat gefitinib and erlotinib first line in FLAURA (2018): median progression-free survival 18.9 versus 10.2 months and overall survival 38.6 versus 31.8 months, with far less brain progression.
claims.note: FLAURA (trial linked on the record): 'median progression-free survival ... 18.9 months vs. 10.2 months; hazard ratio ... 0.46'; OS paper: 'median overall survival was 38.6 months ... and 31.8 months'.

claims.claim: Two trials then built on it: FLAURA2 (2023) added platinum-pemetrexed to osimertinib (progression-free survival 25.5 versus 16.7 months, hazard ratio 0.62, with the 2025 survival analysis also in favour), and MARIPOSA (2024) combined the EGFR-MET bispecific antibody amivantamab with lazertinib (23.7 versus 16.6 months, hazard ratio 0.70, and longer overall survival), at the cost of rash, nail changes and venous thrombosis.
claims.note: FLAURA2: CT.gov results PFS 25.5 vs 16.7 months; NEJM 2023 abstract HR 0.62; final OS NEJM (epub 2025) median OS 47.5 months, record result OS HR 0.77. MARIPOSA NEJM 2024: '23.7 vs. 16.6 months; hazard ratio ... 0.70'; OS NEJM 2025 HR 0.75.

claims.claim: For exon 20 insertions, PAPILLON (2023) showed amivantamab plus chemotherapy beat chemotherapy (11.4 versus 6.7 months, hazard ratio 0.40) and sunvozertinib was approved in 2025 after platinum chemotherapy.
claims.note: PAPILLON (NCT04538664, linked): 'median, 11.4 months and 6.7 months ... hazard ratio ... 0.40'. Sunvozertinib: US accelerated approval 2 July 2025 (FDA, via the drug's Wikipedia page).

claims.claim: In early disease ADAURA (2020) showed that three years of adjuvant osimertinib after resection cut recurrence by 83 percent in stage II to IIIA (hazard ratio 0.17) and improved five-year overall survival from 78 to 88 percent, and LAURA (2024) showed that osimertinib after chemoradiation for unresectable stage III disease extended progression-free survival from 5.6 to 39.1 months.
claims.note: ADAURA: DFS HR 0.17 is stage II-IIIA (correct as written). Five-year OS 88% vs 78% is the overall stage IB-IIIA population; in stage II-IIIA it was 85% vs 73% (NEJM 2023). The sentence put the IB-IIIA OS figures on the stage II-IIIA cohort. LAURA 39.1 vs 5.6 months correct.
claims.fixed: Added 'across stage IB to IIIA' to the OS figure; added ADAURA OS NEJM 2023 link to the record

claims.claim: About 15 percent of lung adenocarcinomas in Europe and North America and 40 to 50 percent in East Asia carry an activating EGFR mutation; it is the commonest driver in never-smokers and in women.
claims.note: No source on the record states regional EGFR prevalence. mutMapII (Midha 2015, 151 studies) gives EGFR mutation in NSCLC adenocarcinoma: Europe 15% (1527/10464), North America 22% (1638/7396), Asia-Pacific 47% (5958/12819). North America is 22%, not about 15%.
claims.fixed: Changed to 15 percent Europe, 22 percent North America, 47 percent Asia-Pacific; added mutMapII link

claims.claim: Exon 19 deletions and L858R make up about 85 percent of cases, exon 20 insertions about 10 percent.
claims.note: No source on the record. Arcila 2013 (1,500 adenocarcinomas): exon 20 insertions 'at least 9% of all EGFR-mutated cases, representing the third most common type of EGFR mutation after exon 19 deletions and L858R'; Riess 2018 (14,483 NSCLC): '12% (263 of 2251) of cases with EGFR mutations'. No primary source read states the 85 percent share for exon 19 deletions plus L858R.
claims.fixed: Removed the unsourced 85 percent; exon 20 insertions now '9 to 12 percent in two large series'; added both links

claims.claim: Surgery has cured lung cancer since Evarts Graham's pneumonectomy in 1933, and lobectomy with mediastinal node dissection became the standard after the 1995 Lung Cancer Study Group trial found more recurrences with lesser resections.
claims.note: The record's Wikipedia link is a redirect to Cardiothoracic surgery, whose lung section mentions neither Graham nor the LCSG trial. Primary sources: Graham and Singer, JAMA 28 Oct 1933 (Crossref 10.1001/jama.1933.02740430017005); LCSG, Ann Thorac Surg 1995: limited resection had 'an observed 75% increase in recurrence rates' and lobectomy 'must be considered the surgical procedure of choice'. Claim agrees.
claims.fixed: Added Graham 1933 and LCSG 1995 links to the record; text unchanged

claims.claim: Two trials in 2022 and 2023, JCOG0802 and CALGB 140503, showed that segmentectomy or wedge resection is as good as lobectomy for peripheral tumours of 2 cm or less, the tumours that screening finds, and most resections are now by video-assisted or robotic thoracoscopy.
claims.note: CALGB 140503 (linked trial; NEJM 2023): sublobar resection noninferior for T1aN0 tumours 2 cm or less. JCOG0802 (Lancet 2022): segmentectomy vs lobectomy, clinical stage IA, tumour 2 cm or less. Years and size match.

claims.claim: Adjuvant cisplatin doublet chemotherapy, established by the LACE meta-analysis in 2008, adds about 5 percent to five-year survival in stage II and III.
claims.note: No source on the record. LACE (JCO 2008): 'overall HR of death was 0.89 ... corresponding to a 5-year absolute benefit of 5.4%'; HR stage II 0.83, stage III 0.83, IB 0.93, IA 1.40. The 5.4 percent is all stages pooled, not stage II and III; the sentence put the overall figure on the stage II-III subgroup.
claims.fixed: Now 'about 5 percent to five-year survival overall, with the benefit seen in stage II and III'; added LACE link

claims.claim: ADAURA (2020) showed that three years of adjuvant osimertinib in EGFR-mutated stage IB to IIIA cut recurrence by 83 percent and improved five-year survival from 78 to 88 percent, and ALINA (2024) did the same for two years of alectinib in ALK-positive disease (hazard ratio 0.24).
claims.note: ADAURA NEJM 2020: stage II-IIIA DFS HR 0.17; overall stage IB-IIIA DFS HR 0.20. The sentence gave the stage II-IIIA 83 percent for the IB-IIIA population. Five-year OS 88 vs 78 percent is IB-IIIA (NEJM 2023), correct. ALINA HR 0.24 correct (stage II-IIIA and ITT both 0.24).
claims.fixed: Now 'cut the risk of recurrence or death by 80 percent (83 percent in stage II to IIIA)'; added ADAURA OS link

claims.claim: For the majority without a driver, IMpower010 (2021) showed adjuvant atezolizumab improved disease-free survival in PD-L1-positive stage II to IIIA (hazard ratio 0.66), CheckMate 816 (2022) showed that three cycles of nivolumab with chemotherapy before surgery raised pathological complete response from 2 to 24 percent and improved event-free and, later, overall survival, and the perioperative trials that give immunotherapy before and after surgery, KEYNOTE-671 (pembrolizumab, event-free survival hazard ratio 0.58, overall survival hazard ratio 0.72), AEGEAN (durvalumab, hazard ratio 0.68) and CheckMate 77T (nivolumab, hazard ratio 0.58), all followed, with approvals between 2022 and 2024.
claims.note: IMpower010 PD-L1>=1% stage II-IIIA DFS HR 0.66; CheckMate 816 pCR 24.0% vs 2.2%, OS later HR 0.72 (NEJM 2025); KEYNOTE-671 EFS HR 0.58 (NEJM 2023), OS HR 0.72 (Lancet 2024); AEGEAN EFS HR 0.68; CheckMate 77T EFS HR 0.58. Approvals March 2022 to October 2024.

claims.claim: About a quarter to a third of non-small-cell lung cancers are found while still resectable, a share rising with low-dose CT screening; five-year survival ranges from over 80 percent for screen-detected stage IA tumours to about 40 percent for stage IIIA.
claims.note: No source on the record bears on the resectable share or on stage survival. I-ELCAP (NEJM 2006): '412 (85%) had clinical stage I lung cancer, and the estimated 10-year survival rate was 88%'. No readable primary source was found for 'a quarter to a third' resectable or 'about 40 percent' at stage IIIA; the IASLC stage-group full texts refused a script.
claims.fixed: Removed the quarter-to-a-third and stage IIIA 40 percent figures; replaced the screen-detected figure with I-ELCAP's 85 percent stage I and 88 percent ten-year survival; added link

claims.claim: Perioperative chemoimmunotherapy (CheckMate 816, KEYNOTE-671, AEGEAN, CheckMate 77T) cuts recurrence by about 40 percent and improves survival in driver-negative disease.
claims.note: EFS HRs: CheckMate 816 0.63, KEYNOTE-671 0.58, AEGEAN 0.68, CheckMate 77T 0.58, so a 32 to 42 percent reduction ('about 40 percent'). OS gain shown in CheckMate 816 (HR 0.72) and KEYNOTE-671 (HR 0.72).

claims.claim: Targeted adjuvant therapy for EGFR (ADAURA) and ALK (ALINA) tumours with hazard ratios of 0.17 and 0.24 for recurrence.
claims.note: ADAURA HR 0.17 and ALINA HR 0.24 are both stage II-IIIA DFS (recurrence or death). ADAURA's overall IB-IIIA HR was 0.20. On a stage I-III page, the subgroup label was missing.
claims.fixed: Added 'or death in stage II to IIIA'

claims.claim: Stage IA, peripheral, 2 cm or less: Segmentectomy or lobectomy by video-assisted or robotic thoracoscopy with node dissection (CALGB 140503, JCOG0802); no systemic therapy; stereotactic radiotherapy if not fit for surgery.
claims.note: CALGB 140503 (in refs): T1aN0, 2 cm or less, sublobar noninferior to lobar; JCOG0802 same size limit.

claims.claim: Stage IB to IIIA without EGFR or ALK alteration: Neoadjuvant nivolumab plus platinum chemotherapy for three cycles (CheckMate 816) or perioperative pembrolizumab (KEYNOTE-671), durvalumab (AEGEAN) or nivolumab (CheckMate 77T) with chemotherapy before and immunotherapy for a year after surgery; or surgery first then adjuvant cisplatin doublet and atezolizumab or pembrolizumab if PD-L1-positive (IMpower010).
claims.note: CheckMate 816: three cycles of neoadjuvant nivolumab plus chemotherapy (correct). Adjuvant duration: KEYNOTE-671 'up to 13 cycles' every 3 weeks (about nine months); AEGEAN 12 cycles every 4 weeks; CheckMate 77T 'for 1 year'. 'For a year' overstated KEYNOTE-671.
claims.fixed: 'for a year' changed to 'for about nine months to a year'; adjuvant pembrolizumab no longer attributed to IMpower010 or limited to PD-L1-positive: now 'pembrolizumab at any PD-L1 level (KEYNOTE-091)', keynote-091 added to refs (PEARLS/KEYNOTE-091 Lancet Oncol 2022, doi 10.1016/s1470-2045(22)00518-6, enrolled 'of any histology or PD-L1 expression level')

claims.claim: Extensive-stage small-cell lung cancer has been treated with platinum plus etoposide since the 1980s, with response rates of 60 to 70 percent but relapse within months, and thirty years of trials of added drugs, maintenance and dose intensity failed.
claims.note: Wikipedia (cited) gives complete response 15 to 30 percent, not overall response; no other source on the record. NCI PDQ (updated 14 May 2025): current regimens 'yield overall response rates of 50% to 80% and complete response rates of 0% to 30% in patients with ED SCLC'. Etoposide-cisplatin first-line use dates from at least 1985 (Evans, JCO 1985).
claims.fixed: Response rates changed from 60-70 to 50-80 percent; added PDQ and Evans 1985 links

claims.claim: IMpower133 (2018) was the first success: adding atezolizumab to carboplatin-etoposide lengthened median overall survival from 10.3 to 12.3 months (hazard ratio 0.70), and CASPIAN (2019) did the same with durvalumab (13.0 versus 10.3 months, hazard ratio 0.73); both were approved in 2019 and 2020 and a long tail of about 15 percent of patients alive at three years appeared.
claims.note: IMpower133 NEJM 2018: OS 12.3 vs 10.3 months, HR 0.70. CASPIAN Lancet 2019: 13.0 vs 10.3, HR 0.73. FDA approvals 19 March 2019 (atezolizumab) and 27 March 2020 (durvalumab). Three-year OS: 16% with atezolizumab (IMbrella A, linked on the impower133 record) and 17.6% with durvalumab (CASPIAN 3-year), so 'about 15 percent' is a fair rounding.

claims.claim: Chinese trials followed with serplulimab (ASTRUM-005, 15.4 versus 10.9 months, hazard ratio 0.63), adebrelimab and benmelstobart.
claims.note: ASTRUM-005 JAMA 2022: median OS 15.4 vs 10.9 months, HR 0.63.

claims.claim: IMforte (2025) then showed that adding lurbinectedin to atezolizumab maintenance after induction extended survival from 10.6 to 13.2 months (hazard ratio 0.73), approved in October 2025.
claims.note: IMforte Lancet 2025: OS stratified HR 0.73; Roche release 3 October 2025: median OS '13.2 months versus 10.6 months' and FDA approval.

claims.claim: Second-line treatment was topotecan, with response rates around 20 percent, until lurbinectedin received accelerated approval in 2020 on a 35 percent response rate.
claims.note: Lurbinectedin: Trigo, Lancet Oncol 2020, overall response 35.2%; US approval June 2020 (Wikipedia, cited). Topotecan 'around 20 percent' has no source on the record; von Pawel JCO 1999 (pivotal topotecan vs CAV) gives 'Response rate was 26 of 107 patients (24.3%)'.
claims.fixed: Topotecan now 'a response rate of about 24 percent in its pivotal trial'; added von Pawel 1999 link

claims.claim: Tarlatamab, a bispecific T-cell engager that binds DLL3 on small-cell cells and CD3 on T cells, produced a 40 percent response rate in DeLLphi-301 (2023) with cytokine release syndrome in about half, mostly mild, and received accelerated approval in May 2024;
claims.note: DeLLphi-301 NEJM 2023: objective response 40% at 10 mg; CRS in 51%, 'most ... grade 1 or 2'. FDA accelerated approval 16 May 2024.

claims.claim: DeLLphi-304 (2025) then showed it lengthened median overall survival to 13.6 months against 8.3 months with chemotherapy (hazard ratio 0.60), the first randomised survival gain after relapse in this disease, and it is now the standard second-line treatment.
claims.note: DeLLphi-304 NEJM 2025: 'median, 13.6 months ... vs. 8.3 months ... hazard ratio for death, 0.60'.

claims.claim: Radiotherapy still has roles: prophylactic cranial irradiation improved survival when brain imaging was not routine (Slotman 2007) but not in the Japanese trial with MRI surveillance (Takahashi 2017), so MRI surveillance is increasingly preferred, and thoracic consolidation radiotherapy helps patients with residual chest disease.
claims.note: Slotman NEJM 2007: PCI improved 1-year survival 27.1% vs 13.3%, brain imaging only for symptoms. Takahashi Lancet Oncol 2017: MRI-screened, no OS benefit (HR 1.27). Years correct.

claims.claim: About 70 percent of small-cell lung cancers are extensive stage at diagnosis, spread beyond one side of the chest, most often to liver, bone, brain and adrenal glands; median survival was about 10 months with chemotherapy alone and is now 12 to 15 months with chemoimmunotherapy, with about one in eight patients alive at three years.
claims.note: No source on the record gives the extensive-stage share. NCI PDQ: 'approximately two-thirds of patients with SCLC have clinical evidence of metastases'. Medians: chemotherapy controls 10.3 months; chemo-immunotherapy 12.3, 13.0 and 15.4 months (IMpower133, CASPIAN, ASTRUM-005). Three-year survival 16% (IMpower133/IMbrella A) and 17.6% (CASPIAN), about one in six; 'one in eight' (12%) is the IMpower133 five-year figure.
claims.fixed: 'About 70 percent' changed to 'About two thirds'; 'one in eight' at three years changed to 'one in six'; PDQ link added

claims.claim: Chemoimmunotherapy first line (IMpower133, CASPIAN) with a tail of about 15 percent alive at three years.
claims.note: Three-year OS 16% (IMpower133/IMbrella A) and 17.6% (CASPIAN 3-year update); 'about 15 percent' is a fair rounding.

claims.claim: Tarlatamab second line: median survival 13.6 versus 8.3 months against chemotherapy in DeLLphi-304, the first randomised gain after relapse.
claims.note: DeLLphi-304: median OS 13.6 vs 8.3 months.

claims.claim: Surveillance is a real alternative rather than a lesser one: the Takahashi trial randomised patients with a negative baseline MRI and found median overall survival of 11.6 months with prophylactic irradiation against 13.7 months with MRI surveillance alone, so irradiating the brain before anything is seen there did not help.
claims.note: Takahashi (takahashi-pci in refs): 'median overall survival was 11.6 months ... in the prophylactic cranial irradiation group and 13.7 months ... in the observation group (hazard ratio 1.27 ...; p=0.094)'.

claims.claim: Thoracic consolidation: Consolidative thoracic radiotherapy (30 Gy in 10 fractions) for patients with residual chest disease after chemotherapy.
claims.note: The row's refs (imrt-igrt, hypofractionated-radiotherapy, consolidation-therapy) are technique records that do not bear on the dose. CREST (Lancet 2015): 'thoracic radiotherapy (30 Gy in ten fractions)'; NCI PDQ cites the same. The CREST trial record already exists in the corpus (crest-thoracic-rt).
claims.fixed: Added crest-thoracic-rt to the row's refs; text unchanged

claims.claim: First-line chemo-immunotherapy (IMpower133 2018, CASPIAN 2019, ASTRUM-005 2022) added two to five months of median survival and a small tail of long-term survivors.
claims.note: IMpower133 NEJM 2018: 'median overall survival was 12.3 months ... and 10.3 months'; CASPIAN Lancet 2019: '13.0 months ... versus 10.3 months'; ASTRUM-005 JAMA 2022: '15.4 months ... 10.9 months'. Gains 2.0, 2.7 and 4.5 months fit 'two to five months'.

claims.claim: Consolidation durvalumab after chemoradiotherapy for limited-stage disease (ADRIATIC, approved December 2024) was the first curative-intent advance in 30 years, lifting median survival to nearly five years.
claims.note: ADRIATIC NEJM 2024: 'median, 55.9 months ... vs. 33.4 months' (nearly five years); OncLive 4 Dec 2024 'FDA Approves Durvalumab for Limited-Stage Small Cell Lung Cancer', investigator: 'very little change in the treatment paradigm for the past 30 or so years'.

claims.claim: In relapsed disease, tarlatamab, the DLL3 T-cell engager, became the first drug to beat chemotherapy on overall survival (DeLLphi-304; full FDA approval November 2025), and lurbinectedin plus atezolizumab became the first approved first-line maintenance regimen (IMforte, October 2025).
claims.note: FDA notifications: 'On November 19, 2025, the Food and Drug Administration granted traditional approval to tarlatamab-dlle'; 'On October 2, 2025 ... approved lurbinectedin in combination with atezolizumab ... maintenance'. DeLLphi-304 NEJM 2025: OS 13.6 vs 8.3 months vs chemotherapy.

claims.claim: Small-cell lung cancer makes up about 15% of lung cancers, roughly 250,000 cases a year worldwide, almost entirely in current or former smokers.
claims.note: PDQ (record link): 'SCLC accounts for approximately 15% of bronchogenic carcinomas' supports 15%. No source on the record gives a worldwide case count; GLOBOCAN does not split lung cancer by histology, and 15% of GLOBOCAN 2022 lung cases would be about 370,000, not 250,000.
claims.fixed: Removed 'roughly 250,000 cases a year worldwide'; kept 'about 15%' (PDQ).

claims.claim: In ADRIATIC, median survival with durvalumab consolidation after chemoradiotherapy was 55.9 months against 33.4 with placebo; in extensive-stage disease first-line chemo-immunotherapy gives a median of about a year.
claims.note: ADRIATIC NEJM 2024: 55.9 vs 33.4 months. First-line chemo-immunotherapy medians 12.3 (IMpower133), 13.0 (CASPIAN), 15.4 (ASTRUM-005) months: 'about a year'.

claims.claim: Extensive-stage first line: chemo-immunotherapy, now with lurbinectedin-atezolizumab maintenance (IMforte, 2025).
claims.note: IMforte Lancet 2025 (OS HR 0.73); FDA approval 2 October 2025 for lurbinectedin plus atezolizumab maintenance.

claims.claim: Relapse: tarlatamab (DLL3×CD3) improved OS over chemotherapy (DeLLphi-304) and received full approval in November 2025.
claims.note: FDA: 'On November 19, 2025 ... granted traditional approval to tarlatamab-dlle'; DeLLphi-304: 'significantly longer overall survival than chemotherapy'.

claims.claim: Very limited stage (T1-2 N0, ~5%): Lobectomy with mediastinal node dissection or SBRT, followed by adjuvant platinum-etoposide;
claims.note: None of the referenced records (sbrt, platinum-etoposide, prophylactic-cranial-irradiation) nor the record's links give a share for very limited stage; PDQ says only 'the minority of LD patients with very limited disease'. T1-2 N0 matches NICE 1.9.1 'T1 to 2a, N0, M0' closely enough.
claims.fixed: Removed '~5%' from the row setting.

claims.claim: Limited stage: Concurrent cisplatin-etoposide with thoracic radiotherapy (45 Gy twice daily or 60-70 Gy once daily), then durvalumab consolidation up to 2 years (ADRIATIC);
claims.note: CONVERT Lancet Oncol 2017: '45 Gy radiotherapy in 30 twice-daily fractions ... or 66 Gy in 33 once-daily fractions' (66 within 60-70); ADRIATIC: durvalumab 'every 4 weeks for up to 24 months'. The NCCN 60-70 Gy range itself is behind a login.

claims.claim: Extensive stage, first line: Carboplatin-etoposide plus atezolizumab or durvalumab (4 cycles), then maintenance immunotherapy; lurbinectedin added to atezolizumab maintenance since 2025 (IMforte).
claims.note: IMpower133: carboplatin-etoposide with atezolizumab 'for four 21-day cycles'; CASPIAN 'up to four cycles' then maintenance durvalumab; IMforte lurbinectedin plus atezolizumab maintenance, FDA 2 Oct 2025.

claims.claim: Relapsed, platinum-sensitive (≥90 days): Tarlatamab (preferred, OS benefit); platinum-etoposide rechallenge; lurbinectedin; topotecan.
claims.note: PDQ (record link): 'Sensitive patients have a first-line response that lasted more than 90 days after treatment was completed.' DeLLphi-304: tarlatamab longer OS than chemotherapy.

claims.claim: Relapsed, platinum-resistant (<90 days): Tarlatamab; lurbinectedin; topotecan; clinical trials (I-DXd, RYZ101, DLL3 bispecifics).
claims.note: PDQ: sensitive defined as response lasting more than 90 days; resistant otherwise. Threshold matches.

claims.claim: It says (1.8.1) to arrange for people with small-cell lung cancer to have an assessment by a thoracic oncologist within 1 week of deciding to recommend treatment, which is a far shorter interval than anything in the non-small-cell pathway, and (1.10.2) to start radiotherapy during the first or second cycle of chemotherapy for limited-stage disease rather than after the chemotherapy is finished.
claims.note: NG122 1.8.1: 'assessment by a thoracic oncologist within 1 week of deciding to recommend treatment'; 1.10.2: 'Start the radiotherapy during the first or second cycle of chemotherapy.'

claims.claim: Limited stage: 4 to 6 cycles of cisplatin-based combination chemotherapy, with carboplatin substituted where kidney function, performance status or other illnesses make that safer (1.10.1); twice-daily radiotherapy given with the chemotherapy for people with a performance status of 0 or 1 whose disease fits in a radical radiotherapy volume, or once daily if they decline or cannot manage twice (1.10.2 and 1.10.3); sequential radiotherapy for people who are not well enough for concurrent treatment but respond to chemotherapy (1.10.4); preventive radiotherapy to the brain at 25 Gy in 10 fractions for performance status 0 to 2 where the disease has not progressed (1.10.5); and durvalumab afterwards where the disease has not progressed after chemoradiotherapy (1.10.6).
claims.note: NG122 1.10.1 '4 to 6 cycles of cisplatin-based combination chemotherapy. Consider substituting carboplatin...'; 1.10.2-1.10.3 twice-daily for WHO PS 0 or 1, once daily if declined; 1.10.4 sequential; 1.10.5 'prophylactic cranial irradiation at a dose of 25 Gy in 10 fractions ... WHO performance status of 0 to 2'; 1.10.6 durvalumab.

claims.claim: Extensive stage: platinum-based combination chemotherapy if you are fit enough, to a maximum of 6 cycles depending on response and toxicity (1.11.1 and 1.11.2), with durvalumab or atezolizumab added (1.11.3), and thoracic radiotherapy with preventive brain radiotherapy considered for people who responded (1.11.4 and 1.11.5).
claims.note: NG122 1.11.1 platinum-based combination if fit enough; 1.11.2 'up to a maximum of 6 cycles ... depending on response and toxicity'; 1.11.3 durvalumab (TA1041) and atezolizumab (TA638); 1.11.4 thoracic radiotherapy with PCI; 1.11.5 PCI.

claims.claim: At relapse it says to offer assessment by a thoracic oncologist (1.12.1), to tell people whose disease did not respond to first-line treatment that there is very limited evidence that second-line chemotherapy will benefit them (1.12.2), to offer an anthracycline-containing or a further platinum-based regimen to a maximum of 6 cycles where chemotherapy is suitable (1.12.3), and to offer radiotherapy for palliation of local symptoms (1.12.5).
claims.note: NG122 1.12.1, 1.12.2 'very limited evidence that second-line chemotherapy will be of benefit', 1.12.3 'anthracycline-containing regimen or further treatment with a platinum-based regimen to a maximum of 6 cycles', 1.12.5 palliative radiotherapy: all as stated.

claims.claim: For 16 years after pemetrexed-cisplatin (2004) nothing improved survival except, modestly, adding bevacizumab (MAPS, 2016).
claims.note: Drugs@FDA NDA021462 (Alimta) original approval 2004-02-04; MAPS Lancet 2016: OS 18.8 vs 16.1 months, HR 0.77; PDQ lists CheckMate 743 nivolumab-ipilimumab as next OS gain (2020), 16 years after 2004.

claims.claim: Radical surgery, long assumed beneficial, was shown by MARS 2 (2024) to shorten survival and worsen quality of life, and is now largely confined to trials.
claims.note: MARS 2 Lancet Respir Med 2024: median survival 19.3 vs 24.8 months with surgery vs chemotherapy alone; full text: 'Differences in patient-reported quality of life favoured the chemotherapy alone group.'

claims.claim: What comes next is biology-led: PRMT5 and MAT2A inhibitors for the ~40-50% of tumours with MTAP deletion, mesothelin-directed CAR-T delivered into the pleural space, ADCs and T-cell engagers against mesothelin, and better use of histology and BAP1/CDKN2A status to choose therapy.
claims.note: Neither record link (PDQ mesothelioma, NICE NG12) nor the MTAP/biomarker records give a share of tumours with MTAP deletion; PDQ does not mention MTAP.
claims.fixed: Removed '~40-50% of' (now 'for tumours with MTAP deletion').

claims.claim: Mesothelioma causes about 30,000 cases a year worldwide, ~3,000 in the US, almost all from asbestos exposure 20-50 years earlier, so incidence is still rising in Asia and parts of Europe.
claims.note: GLOBOCAN 2022 (repo public/globocan/countries.json, code 18): World 30,633 cases, USA 3,114, presented undated as 'a year'. Current GCO fact sheet is GLOBOCAN 2024: 27,350. PDQ: 'A history of asbestos exposure is reported in about 70% to 80% of mesothelioma cases', so 'almost all' overstated; no record source gives the 20-50-year latency.
claims.fixed: Dated to GLOBOCAN 2022 (about 30,600 worldwide, about 3,100 US); 'almost all' changed to 'most' (PDQ 70-80%); '20-50 years' changed to 'decades' (unsourced figure).

claims.claim: Immunotherapy has produced the first tail of long-term survivors: in CheckMate 743 five-year survival was 14% against 6% with chemotherapy.
claims.note: CheckMate 743 five-year JCO 2026: '5-year OS rates, 14% v 6%; hazard ratio [HR], 0.74'.

claims.claim: Median survival across series is 12-18 months, which means half of the people in those series lived longer.
claims.note: PDQ: median survival 'reported as 16 months for patients with malignant pleural disease'; first-line trial arms in PDQ 12.1 (historical control), 14.1, 18.1 months; MAPS 16.1 and 18.8. 12-18 months fits.

claims.claim: Five-year survival with nivolumab-ipilimumab 14% vs 6% with chemotherapy: a small but real tail of long-term survivors.
claims.note: CheckMate 743 five-year JCO 2026: '5-year OS rates, 14% v 6%'.

claims.claim: The World Health Organization's Classification of Thoracic Tumours, fifth edition (2021), names the tumour types: adenocarcinoma and its patterns, squamous cell carcinoma, large cell carcinoma, the sarcomatoid carcinomas, adenosquamous carcinoma, the salivary-gland-type tumours, and a separate chapter of neuroendocrine neoplasms holding typical carcinoid, atypical carcinoid, large cell neuroendocrine carcinoma and small cell carcinoma.
claims.note: Nicholson JTO 2022 abstract: "The 2021 WHO Classification of Thoracic Tumours was published earlier this year"; fifth edition, neuroendocrine chapter.

claims.claim: The IARC fact sheet, served with the GLOBOCAN 2024 estimates, counts 2,637,005 new cases a year (age-standardised rate 23.9 per 100,000) and 1,861,839 deaths (16.3 per 100,000).
claims.note: Fact sheet headed "GLOBOCAN 2024": Lung rank 1, 2 637 005 cases ASR 23.9; 1 861 839 deaths ASR 16.3. Page names the 2024 estimates.

claims.claim: Asia carries 1,730,334 of the cases (65.6 percent) and 1,196,664 of the deaths (64.3 percent);
claims.note: Fact sheet continent table: Asia 1 730 334 (65.6%), deaths 1 196 664 (64.3%).

claims.claim: Europe 478,683 and 369,740 (18.2 and 19.9 percent);
Northern America 258,423 and 151,406 (9.8 and 8.1 percent);
claims.note: Northern America 258 423 (9.8%), deaths 151 406 (8.1%).

claims.claim: Latin America and the Caribbean 103,726 and 89,548;
claims.note: Latin America and the Caribbean 103 726 and 89 548.

claims.claim: Africa 47,006 and 41,045;
claims.note: Africa 47 006 and 41 045.

claims.claim: Oceania 18,833 and 13,436.
claims.note: Oceania 18 833 and 13 436.

claims.claim: The highest national rate in men is Hungary at 61.8 per 100,000, and in women Hungary and Denmark at 36.0.
claims.note: Page 2 bar charts (positions read with pdftotext -bbox): males "Hungary (61.8)"; females "Denmark (36.0)". "Hungary (36.0)" sits in the both-sexes chart under Mortality, i.e. Hungary's death rate, not a female incidence rate.
claims.fixed: Women: "Hungary and Denmark at 36.0" -> "Denmark at 36.0".

claims.claim: Five-year prevalence is lower relative to yearly incidence than for most cancers, because survival after a lung cancer diagnosis is shorter: 2,345,582 of the world's prevalent cases are in Asia (65.7 percent).
claims.note: Prevalence table: Asia 2 345 582 (65.7%).

claims.claim: Using the GLOBOCAN 2022 base with the recorded incidence of Cancer Incidence in Five Continents volume XII, of 1,572,045 lung cancers in men worldwide 717,211 (45.6 percent) were adenocarcinoma, 461,171 (29.4 percent) squamous cell carcinoma, 180,063 (11.5 percent) small-cell carcinoma and 101,861 (6.5 percent) large-cell carcinoma; of 908,630 in women, 541,971 (59.7 percent) were adenocarcinoma, 155,598 (17.1 percent) squamous, 87,902 (9.7 percent) small-cell and 59,271 (6.5 percent) large-cell (Lancet Respiratory Medicine 2025).

Adenocarcinoma is now the commonest type in both sexes everywhere the data allow the question to be asked, and the highest adenocarcinoma rates are in east Asia (27.12 per 100,000 men, 19.04 per 100,000 women).
claims.note: Rates correct ("east Asia for adenocarcinoma (27.12 ... ) ... (19.04 ...)"), but the abstract supports adenocarcinoma as commonest worldwide only; "everywhere the data allow the question to be asked" is not stated (east Europe has the highest SCC rate in men).
claims.fixed: "everywhere the data allow the question to be asked" -> "worldwide".

claims.claim: The same study attributed 114,486 male and 80,378 female adenocarcinomas in 2022 to ambient particulate matter pollution.
claims.note: Abstract: "114 486 adenocarcinoma cases among male individuals and 80 378 ... among female individuals were attributable to ambient PM pollution worldwide in 2022".

claims.claim: Lung cancer is the 3rd commonest cancer in the UK, with around 50,200 new cases a year, nearly 140 a day, 11 percent of all new cancer cases: about 25,500 in males and 24,700 in females (Cancer Research UK, 2019 and 2021 to 2022).
claims.note: CRUK incidence: "3rd most common cancer in the UK with around 50,200 new cases every year; that's nearly 140 every day (2019, 2021-2022)"; "11% of all new cancer cases ... around 24,700 ... females and around 25,500 ... males".

claims.claim: It is the commonest cause of cancer death, with around 32,800 deaths a year, 90 a day (2022 to 2024).
claims.note: CRUK mortality: "around 32,800 deaths every year; that's 90 every day (2022-2024)".

claims.claim: Almost half of new cases (46 percent) are in people aged 75 and over, and rates are highest at 80 to 84.
claims.note: CRUK incidence: "almost half (46%) ... aged 75 and over"; "highest in people aged 80 to 84".

claims.claim: Incidence has fallen about 11 percent since the early 1990s and 5 percent in the last decade; mortality has fallen 40 percent since the early 1970s and 22 percent in the last decade.
claims.note: CRUK: incidence "decreased by around a tenth (11%) ... since the early 1990s ... a twentieth (5%) in the last decade"; mortality "two-fifths (40%) ... since the early 1970s ... more than a fifth (22%) in the last decade".

claims.claim: The lifetime risk of a diagnosis is nearly 1 in 13 for females and 1 in 14 for males born in 1961 (both about 7 percent).
claims.note: CRUK risk factors: "nearly 1 in 13 (7%) for females, and 1 in 14 (7%) for males born in 1961".

claims.claim: The SEER programme projects 229,410 new cases (10.8 percent of all cancers) and 124,990 deaths (20.0 percent of all cancer deaths) for 2026, which makes lung and bronchus cancer the 3rd commonest cancer diagnosed and by a wide margin the commonest cause of cancer death.
claims.note: SEER: "Estimated New Cases in 2026 229,410; 10.8%; Estimated Deaths 124,990; 20.0%"; rank 3 of new cases; "first leading cause of cancer death".

claims.claim: The rate of new cases is 47.2 per 100,000 a year (2019 to 2023) and the death rate 30.2 (2020 to 2024); both are falling, incidence by 1.9 percent a year over 2014 to 2023 and mortality by 4.1 percent a year over 2015 to 2024, the fastest fall of any common cancer.
claims.note: Figures match SEER ("47.2 ... 2019-2023"; "30.2 ... 2020-2024"; "falling on average 1.9% each year over 2014-2023 ... 4.1% each year over 2015-2024") but SEER does not say it is "the fastest fall of any common cancer".
claims.fixed: Removed "the fastest fall of any common cancer".

claims.claim: The median age at diagnosis is 71 and at death 73; about 5.2 percent of Americans will be diagnosed in their lifetime;
claims.note: SEER: median age at diagnosis 71, at death 73; "Approximately 5.2 percent ... lifetime".

claims.claim: 661,853 people were living with the disease in 2023.
claims.note: SEER: "In 2023, there were an estimated 661,853 people living with lung and bronchus cancer".

claims.claim: Rates differ by group: 63.7 per 100,000 in non-Hispanic Black men and 57.0 in non-Hispanic White men against 29.8 in Hispanic men;
claims.note: SEER new-case rates, males: NH Black 63.7, NH White 57.0, Hispanic 29.8.

claims.claim: 50.9 in non-Hispanic White women and 48.6 in non-Hispanic American Indian and Alaska Native women against 23.2 in Hispanic women.
claims.note: SEER females: NH White 50.9, NH AIAN 48.6, Hispanic 23.2.

claims.claim: The National Lung Screening Trial randomised 53,454 Americans aged 55 to 74 with at least 30 pack-years to three annual low-dose CT scans or chest radiographs and found 20.0 percent fewer lung cancer deaths (95 percent confidence interval 6.8 to 26.7) and 6.7 percent fewer deaths from any cause.
claims.note: NLST abstract: 53,454; "relative reduction ... 20.0% (95% CI, 6.8 to 26.7)"; all-cause "6.7%"; full text: "between 55 and 74 years ... at least 30 pack-years".

claims.claim: NELSON randomised 13,195 men and 2,594 women aged 50 to 74 in the Netherlands and Belgium to volume CT at baseline and years 1, 3 and 5.5 or to nothing, and found a death rate ratio of 0.76 (0.61 to 0.94) in men at ten years and 0.67 (0.38 to 1.14) in women.
claims.note: NELSON abstract: "13,195 men ... and 2594 women between the ages of 50 and 74 ... T0, year 1, year 3, and year 5.5 or no screening"; RR 0.76 (0.61-0.94) men, 0.67 (0.38-1.14) women at 10 years.

claims.claim: The UK National Screening Committee recommended targeted screening at 55 to 74 for people at high risk in June 2022;
claims.note: UK NSC page: "last UK NSC review ... June 2022"; "Targeted screening ... recommended for people aged 55 to 74 identified as being at high risk".

claims.claim: England's Targeted Lung Health Check programme, running since 2019, became the national Lung Cancer Screening Programme and by March 2025 had invited over two million people and diagnosed 7,193 lung cancers, 63.1 percent at stage 1 and 12.6 percent at stage 2, with full coverage expected in 2030.
claims.note: Nature Medicine 2026 abstract: launched 2019, now national programme, "full coverage expected by 2030", "invited over two million people, with 7,193 lung cancers diagnosed-63.1% at ... stage 1 and 12.6% stage 2-to March 2025".

claims.claim: Every type is staged by the same system, the ninth edition of the TNM classification, in force since 1 January 2025; every type is investigated down the same pathway of chest X-ray, contrast-enhanced CT, PET-CT and needle sampling of mediastinal nodes through the airway wall; and every type is caused overwhelmingly by the same exposure, so the same prevention works on all of them.
claims.note: BJR 2025 abstract: "The ninth edition of the TNM classification, effective January 1, 2025".

claims.claim: The commonest cancer in the world and the commonest cause of cancer death, the only cancer that tops both lists: 2,637,005 new cases and 1,861,839 deaths a year (GLOBOCAN 2024), with 65.6 percent of cases in Asia.
claims.note: GLOBOCAN 2024 fact sheet: lung rank 1 for cases and deaths, 2 637 005 and 1 861 839, Asia 65.6%; labelled GLOBOCAN 2024.

claims.claim: Around 50,200 UK cases and 32,800 UK deaths a year, the 3rd commonest cancer and the commonest cause of cancer death (Cancer Research UK);
