claims.note: CRUK main page: 50,218 cases (2019, 2021-2022), 32,800 deaths (2022-2024); 3rd commonest, most common cause of cancer death.

claims.claim: 229,410 US cases and 124,990 deaths projected for 2026 (SEER).
claims.note: SEER 2026 projections 229,410 and 124,990.

claims.claim: Adenocarcinoma is the commonest type in both sexes, and 72 percent of UK cases are caused by smoking.
claims.note: CRUK risk factors: "72% of lung cancer cases in the UK are caused by smoking"; adenocarcinoma commonest in both sexes per Lancet Respir Med 2025.

claims.claim: In the United States 29.5 percent of people diagnosed with lung and bronchus cancer in 2016 to 2022 were alive five years later relative to people of the same age without the disease; by stage that is 65.5 percent for localised disease, which is 24 percent of cases, 38.2 percent for regional (21 percent), 10.5 percent for distant (51 percent) and 17.5 percent for unstaged (4 percent) (SEER).
claims.note: SEER: 5-year relative survival 29.5% (2016-2022); localized 24% / 65.5%, regional 21% / 38.2%, distant 51% / 10.5%, unknown 4% / 17.5%.

claims.claim: In the UK 11.1 percent of people are predicted to survive ten years or more, against 3.3 percent in the 1970s, and 18.1 percent of people diagnosed in England survive five years, rising to 43.5 percent among those who have already survived a year.
claims.note: CRUK survival: "11.1% ... ten years or more (2018)"; "3.3% ... 1970s"; "18.1% ... England survive ... five years ... already survived for one year ... 43.5%".

claims.claim: Survival is higher in women than men and falls steeply with age, from 32.7 percent of women and 22.2 percent of men diagnosed at 15 to 44 to 9.2 percent of women and 5.2 percent of men diagnosed at 75 to 99, and it tracks deprivation: 20.1 percent at five years in the most deprived group in England against 27.6 percent in the least (Cancer Research UK).
claims.note: CRUK survival: "32.7% females and ... 22.2% males ... aged 15-44 survive ... for ten years or more, compared with ... 9.2% females and ... 5.2% males diagnosed aged 75-99". These are ten-year figures; the sentence sits between five-year figures and did not say ten-year. Deprivation figures (20.1 vs 27.6 at five years) correct.
claims.fixed: Added "ten-year survival runs from" before the age figures.

claims.claim: CT screening is recommended in the United States and, since June 2022, across the four UK nations; in Europe it is still mostly not a programme, and uptake is low where it is.
claims.note: UK NSC page: recommendation dated June 2022 for the four nations to move towards targeted screening. The Europe clause carries no figure.

claims.claim: Prevention and stopping smoking: Tobacco control and stopping smoking, which is the only lever that reaches the 72 percent of UK cases caused by smoking.
claims.note: CRUK risk factors: "72% of lung cancer cases in the UK are caused by smoking" (record-level link).

claims.claim: NICE NG209 covers preventing uptake in people aged 24 and under and treating dependence in everyone aged 12 and over, and was updated in February 2025 to add cytisinicline.
claims.note: NG209 page: "everyone aged 12 and over"; "aged 24 and under"; cytisinicline update; last updated datetime 2025-02-04.

claims.claim: NICE NG122 (1.5.1) says that for people who are well enough and for whom treatment with curative intent is suitable, offer lobectomy, either open or thoracoscopic, and (1.5.2) offer more extensive surgery only where it is needed to get clear margins.
claims.note: NG122 1.5.1 "offer lobectomy (either open or thoracoscopic)"; 1.5.2 "only when needed to obtain clear margins".

claims.claim: The fitness assessment runs on numbers rather than on impressions: spirometry and transfer factor before any treatment with curative intent (1.4.9), a functional segment count to predict lung function after the operation (1.4.11), a shuttle walk test with 400 m as the cut-off for good function or an exercise test with 15 ml/kg/minute where the risk of breathlessness afterwards is moderate to high (1.4.13 and 1.4.14), and a global risk score such as Thoracoscore with the person told the risk before they consent (1.4.1).
claims.note: NG122 1.4.9 spirometry and TLCO; 1.4.11 functional segment count; 1.4.13 "more than 400 m"; 1.4.14 "more than 15 ml/kg/minute"; 1.4.1 Thoracoscore.

claims.claim: Where predicted lung function after surgery is low, the guideline does not close the door: it says to offer people with a predicted postoperative FEV1 or transfer factor below 30 percent the option of treatment with curative intent if they accept the risks of breathlessness and associated complications (1.4.12).
claims.note: NG122 1.4.12: "predicted postoperative FEV1 or TLCO below 30% the option of treatment with curative intent if they accept the risks of dyspnoea".

claims.claim: Smoking sits inside this row rather than beside it: NICE says to explain that smoking increases the risk of lung complications after surgery and to advise stopping as soon as the diagnosis is suspected, and in the same section says not to postpone surgery to allow people to stop (1.3.1 to 1.3.3).
claims.note: NG122 1.3.1-1.3.3 as stated.

claims.claim: Before surgery, NICE NG122 (1.6.8) recommends nivolumab with chemotherapy for neoadjuvant treatment of resectable disease at least 4 cm or node positive, and (1.6.9 and 1.6.10) durvalumab or pembrolizumab with platinum chemotherapy given before and then continued after the operation, durvalumab restricted to disease without EGFR mutations or ALK rearrangements.
claims.note: NG122 1.6.8 nivolumab "(tumours at least 4 cm or node positive)"; 1.6.9 durvalumab "without EGFR mutations or ALK rearrangements"; 1.6.10 pembrolizumab.

claims.claim: After surgery, NICE (1.6.11) says to offer systemic anticancer therapy to people with good performance status and T1a to 4, N1 to 2, M0 disease, (1.6.12) to consider it for T2b to 4, N0, M0 tumours larger than 4 cm, and (1.6.13) to use a platinum-based combination.
claims.note: NG122 1.6.11 "T1a to 4, N1 to 2, M0"; 1.6.12 "T2b to 4, N0, M0 ... greater than 4 cm"; 1.6.13 platinum-based.

claims.claim: Where a targetable change is present the adjuvant treatment is a tablet instead: osimertinib after complete resection of stage 1b to 3a EGFR exon 19 deletion or L858R disease, stopped at 3 years or earlier on recurrence or unacceptable toxicity (1.6.14), and alectinib after complete resection of stage 1b (at least 4 cm) to 3a ALK-positive disease (1.6.15).
claims.note: NG122 1.6.14 osimertinib "stage 1b to 3a ... stopped at 3 years"; 1.6.15 alectinib "stage 1b (tumours at least 4 cm) to 3a".

claims.claim: For operable stage 3a N2 disease NICE (1.6.3 to 1.6.6) says to consider chemoradiotherapy with surgery, to discuss the benefits and risks first including that it improves progression-free survival and may improve overall survival, to schedule the operation 3 to 5 weeks after the chemoradiotherapy finishes so there is time to recover, and to do it only in teams with expertise in the combined treatment and in each of its parts.
claims.note: NG122 1.6.3-1.6.6: "improves progression-free survival / may improve overall survival"; surgery "3 to 5 weeks after completion".

claims.claim: NICE NG122 (1.6.17) says to consider chemoradiotherapy for people with stage 2 or 3 disease whose condition is not suitable for surgery or who decline it, and to balance the potential survival benefit against the risk of additional toxicities, which is an unusually honest sentence for a guideline and worth quoting back in clinic.
claims.note: NG122 1.6.17: "stage 2 or 3 ... Balance potential benefit in survival with the risk of additional toxicities".

claims.claim: What follows the chemoradiotherapy is now part of the plan rather than an afterthought: NICE (1.6.18) recommends durvalumab for locally advanced unresectable disease with PD-L1 expression on 1 percent or more of tumour cells where the disease has not progressed after concurrent platinum-based chemoradiation; the schedule this came from, PACIFIC, gave it for a year.
claims.note: NG122 1.6.18 durvalumab "PD-L1 expression on 1% or more of tumour cells"; PACIFIC NEJM 2018 "up to 12 months".

claims.claim: Where chemoradiotherapy is too much, NICE (1.5.9 and 1.5.10) says to consider radical radiotherapy, conventional or hyperfractionated, for people with stage 3a or 3b disease who are eligible, while saying plainly that some people who cannot tolerate chemoradiotherapy will not manage radical radiotherapy either.
claims.note: NG122 1.5.9 (stage 3a, cannot tolerate or decline chemoradiotherapy) and 1.5.10 (stage 3b).

claims.claim: NICE NG122 (1.2.12) says to see the National Genomics Test Directory for guidance on next-generation sequencing panels to guide treatment, and (1.2.11) that samples must be adequate, without unacceptable risk to the person, to permit subtyping and assessment of molecular markers.
claims.note: NG122 1.2.12 (National Genomics Test Directory, NGS panels) and 1.2.11 (adequate samples, subtyping and molecular markers).

claims.claim: Some of the immunotherapy recommendations are written to exclude EGFR and ALK disease (NICE 1.6.9 does so explicitly for durvalumab around surgery), and a treatment started in the wrong lane is harder to undo than a fortnight of waiting.
claims.note: NG122 1.6.9 durvalumab "without ... EGFR mutations or ... ALK rearrangements".

claims.claim: NICE NG122 organises its published treatment pathways for advanced disease around exactly this split, separately for squamous and non-squamous cancer: no targetable mutations with PD-L1 below 50 percent, and no targetable mutations with PD-L1 at 50 percent or higher, with further pathways for RET fusion, KRAS G12C, MET exon 14 skipping and BRAF V600 disease at each PD-L1 level.
claims.note: NG122 treatment pathways: squamous and non-squamous, "No targetable mutations, PD-L1 below 50%" / "50% or higher", RET, KRAS G12C, METex14, BRAF V600 at each PD-L1 level.

claims.claim: Chemotherapy's effects are mostly predictable and temporary; immune effects are less predictable, can affect any organ, and Macmillan says they can begin during treatment or after it ends, which is why the alert card is issued and why the same short list is repeated at every visit: breathlessness, a new cough, wheezing or a fever over 37.5 C; more stools than is normal for you or stools at night; a spreading, blistering or peeling rash with flu-like symptoms; and feeling unwell even with a normal temperature.
claims.note: Macmillan pembrolizumab page (irae and checkpoint-inhibitor refs): symptoms "during treatment, or after treatment ends"; "a temperature over 37.5°C"; stools at night; "blistering or peeling skin"; "unwell, even with a normal temperature".

claims.claim: NICE NG122 (1.2.11) asks for samples adequate to permit pathological diagnosis including subtyping and assessment of molecular markers, and (1.2.13) to choose investigations that give the most information with the least risk to the person, thinking carefully before performing a test that gives only diagnostic pathology when other information is needed too.
claims.note: NG122 1.2.11 and 1.2.13 as paraphrased.

claims.claim: NICE NG122 (1.16.1) says to offer dexamethasone to people with symptomatic brain metastases and to reduce to the minimum necessary maintenance dose for symptomatic response, and (1.16.2) refers the treatment itself to the section on management of confirmed brain metastases in its brain tumours guideline rather than repeating it.
claims.note: NG122 1.16.1 dexamethasone, minimum maintenance dose; 1.16.2 refers to brain tumours guideline.

claims.claim: Steroids lift symptoms quickly but have their own effects, and NICE NG122 (1.16.1) says to reduce to the minimum necessary maintenance dose for symptomatic response, so the plan to come down matters as much as the plan to start.
claims.note: NG122 1.16.1 as stated.

claims.claim: Temel and colleagues (NEJM 2010) randomly assigned 151 people with newly diagnosed metastatic non-small-cell lung cancer to early palliative care integrated with standard oncology care, or to standard oncology care alone.
claims.note: Temel NEJM 2010 abstract: "Of the 151 patients who underwent randomization"; early palliative care integrated with standard care vs standard care.

claims.claim: At 12 weeks the early palliative care group had better quality of life (mean FACT-L 98.0 against 91.5, P equals 0.03) and fewer depressive symptoms (16 against 38 percent, P equals 0.01); fewer received aggressive care at the end of life (33 against 54 percent, P equals 0.05), and median survival was longer (11.6 against 8.9 months, P equals 0.02).
claims.note: Temel abstract: FACT-L "98.0 vs. 91.5; P=0.03"; depressive symptoms "16% vs. 38%, P=0.01"; aggressive EOL care "33% vs. 54%, P=0.05"; survival "11.6 months vs. 8.9 months, P=0.02".

claims.claim: NICE NG122 fills in what the service does: palliative radiotherapy as symptoms arise or immediately for people who cannot have curative treatment (1.13.1); radiotherapy, debulking or a stent for an airway that is closing (1.14.2); draining a pleural effusion and talc pleurodesis where that would give lasting benefit (1.15.1 and 1.15.2); breathing control, psychosocial support and coping strategies for breathlessness, delivered by people with expertise in the techniques and available in all care settings (1.15.3 and 1.15.4); opioids such as codeine or morphine to reduce cough (1.15.5); chemotherapy and radiotherapy, and a stent where symptoms are severe, for superior vena cava obstruction (1.15.7 and 1.15.8); dexamethasone for symptomatic brain metastases (1.16.1); single-fraction radiotherapy for bone pain that ordinary painkillers are not controlling (1.17.1); and multidisciplinary management of weight loss, appetite, swallowing and depression (1.18.1).

NLST (53,454 participants) showed a 20 percent relative reduction in lung cancer mortality against chest radiography, and NELSON (15,789) a 24 percent reduction in men at ten years with a lower false-positive rate.
claims.note: NLST 53,454, 20.0% reduction; NELSON 13,195 + 2,594 = 15,789, men RR 0.76 at 10 years, referral rate 2.1%.

claims.claim: In England the Targeted Lung Health Check programme invites people aged 55 to 74 with a smoking history.
claims.note: Nature Medicine 2026 (record-level link): "People aged 55-74 were offered low-dose CT ... if they had ever smoked".

claims.claim: For a peripheral tumour 2 cm or smaller, sublobar resection is now a standard option rather than a compromise: JCOG0802/WJOG4607L found segmentectomy superior to lobectomy for overall survival (in the radiologically pure-solid subgroup, five-year overall survival 92.4 against 86.1 percent, hazard ratio 0.64), and CALGB 140503 found sublobar resection non-inferior for disease-free survival in 697 patients.
claims.note: JCOG0802 pure-solid analysis (record link, Lancet Respir Med 2024): 5-yr OS 92.4% vs 86.1%, HR 0.64; tumours <=2 cm. CALGB 140503 NEJM 2023: 697 patients, DFS non-inferior.

claims.claim: Adjuvant chemotherapy is not given: the LACE pooled analysis found a hazard ratio of 1.40 in stage IA, so it is avoided, and stage IB gains little.
claims.note: LACE JCO 2008: "HR for stage IA = 1.40 ... stage IB = 0.93".

claims.claim: Stage I non-small-cell lung cancer, not fit for surgery: Stereotactic ablative radiotherapy, typically 54 Gy in three fractions or an equivalent schedule adapted to tumour position.
claims.note: CHISEL Lancet Oncol 2019: SABR "54 Gy in three 18 Gy fractions, or 48 Gy in four 12 Gy fractions if the tumour was <2 cm from the chest wall".

claims.claim: CHISEL randomised 101 patients with inoperable peripheral stage I disease to stereotactic or conventional radiotherapy and found better local control and overall survival with the stereotactic schedule.
claims.note: CHISEL abstract confirms 101 patients, inoperable peripheral stage 1 and better local control (HR 0.32); the overall survival result is not in the abstract and the Lancet Oncology full text is paywalled (5.7 KB block page); not in PMC.

claims.claim: Whether it can replace an operation in fit patients is unsettled: the pooled STARS and ROSEL analysis favoured radiotherapy (three-year overall survival 95 against 79 percent), but on 58 patients from two trials that closed early, and the larger randomised comparisons have not reported.
claims.note: STARS/ROSEL Lancet Oncol 2015: 58 patients, both trials "closed early", 3-yr OS "95% ... compared with 79%".

claims.claim: IALT (1,867 patients) gave five-year survival 44.5 against 40.4 percent, JBR.10 established the cisplatin and vinorelbine regimen, and ANITA gave median survival 65.7 against 43.7 months.
claims.note: IALT NEJM 2004: 1867 patients, "44.5 percent vs. 40.4 percent at five years"; ANITA Lancet Oncol 2006: median survival 65.7 vs 43.7 months.

claims.claim: The LACE pooled analysis of 4,584 patients set the modern indication: hazard ratio 0.89 overall, a 5.4 percent absolute five-year benefit, rising with stage (stage II 0.83, stage III 0.83) and absent, with a point estimate favouring observation, in stage IA.
claims.note: LACE: 4,584 patients, HR 0.89, 5.4% absolute 5-yr benefit, stage II 0.83, stage III 0.83, stage IA 1.40.

claims.claim: ADAURA improved disease-free and overall survival, and the 2026 exploratory long-term analysis gives eight-year overall survival of 74 against 58 percent in stage II to IIIA (hazard ratio 0.53) and 79 against 64 percent in stage IB to IIIA (0.52), with the benefit larger for exon 19 deletions (0.45) than L858R (0.72).
claims.note: ADAURA JTO 2026 abstract: stage II-IIIA HR 0.53, 8-yr OS 74% vs 58%; IB-IIIA HR 0.52, 79% vs 64%; Ex19del 0.45, L858R 0.72.

claims.claim: For ALK-positive disease, two years of alectinib after resection of stage IB (4 cm or more) to IIIA disease, on ALINA (disease-free survival hazard ratio 0.24), FDA-approved in 2024; overall survival is immature.
claims.note: ALINA NEJM 2024: 24 months alectinib, stage IB (>=4 cm)-IIIA, DFS HR 0.24, OS immature; FDA approval 18 April 2024 (Lung Cancer Targets Ther 2024).

claims.claim: CheckMate 816 gave neoadjuvant nivolumab with chemotherapy alone (median event-free survival 31.6 against 20.8 months, hazard ratio 0.63; pathological complete response 24.0 against 2.2 percent).
claims.note: CheckMate 816 NEJM 2022: EFS 31.6 vs 20.8 months, HR 0.63; pCR 24.0% vs 2.2%.

claims.claim: The perioperative schedule adds adjuvant treatment: KEYNOTE-671 with pembrolizumab, AEGEAN with durvalumab (event-free survival hazard ratio 0.69), CheckMate 77T with nivolumab (18-month event-free survival 70.2 against 50.0 percent, hazard ratio 0.58), Neotorch with toripalimab in stage III disease (hazard ratio 0.40) and RATIONALE-315 with tislelizumab (overall survival hazard ratio 0.65).
claims.note: AEGEAN JCO 2026 (record doi 10.1200/JCO-25-02659): EFS HR 0.69; CheckMate 77T NEJM 2024: 18-month EFS 70.2% vs 50.0%, HR 0.58; Neotorch JAMA 2024 stage III EFS HR 0.40; RATIONALE-315 Ann Oncol 2026 OS HR 0.65.

claims.claim: Unresectable stage III non-small-cell lung cancer: Concurrent platinum-based chemoradiotherapy to 60 Gy, then consolidation.
claims.note: RTOG 0617 Lancet Oncol 2015: 60 Gy standard dose with concurrent chemotherapy.

claims.claim: RTOG 0617 showed that raising the dose to 74 Gy shortens survival, so 60 Gy is the ceiling.
claims.note: RTOG 0617: median OS 28.7 months at 60 Gy vs 20.3 months at 74 Gy (HR 1.38).

claims.claim: For disease without an EGFR mutation, a year of durvalumab: PACIFIC gave 24-month overall survival 66.3 against 55.6 percent (hazard ratio for death 0.68) and median progression-free survival 17.2 against 5.6 months, with the benefit holding at five years.
claims.note: PACIFIC NEJM 2018: 24-month OS 66.3% vs 55.6%, HR 0.68; PFS 17.2 vs 5.6 months; durvalumab up to 12 months.

claims.claim: Where chemoradiotherapy had to be given sequentially, GEMSTONE-301 showed consolidation sugemalimab still works (median progression-free survival 9.0 against 5.8 months), although that drug is licensed only in China and the EU.
claims.note: GEMSTONE-301 Lancet Oncol 2022 enrolled patients "after concurrent or sequential chemoradiotherapy"; PFS "9.0 months vs 5.8 months" is the whole ITT population, not the sequential subgroup the sentence attributes it to.
claims.fixed: Reworded: GEMSTONE-301 enrolled after concurrent or sequential chemoradiotherapy; 9.0 vs 5.8 months "across both".

claims.claim: Metastatic disease, EGFR exon 19 deletion or L858R: Osimertinib alone (FLAURA: median progression-free survival 18.9 against 10.2 months, hazard ratio 0.46; median overall survival 38.6 against 31.8 months), or intensified first-line treatment for patients with heavier disease: osimertinib with pemetrexed and platinum chemotherapy (FLAURA2) or amivantamab with lazertinib (MARIPOSA), both funded in England under TA1060 and TA1122.
claims.note: FLAURA NEJM 2018/2020: PFS 18.9 vs 10.2 months, HR 0.46; OS 38.6 vs 31.8 months. NICE TA1060 and TA1122 both recommend/fund.

claims.claim: Dacomitinib (ARCHER 1050: 14.7 against 9.2 months against gefitinib) and afatinib (LUX-Lung 3: 13.6 against 6.9 months in the common mutations) remain licensed alternatives.
claims.note: ARCHER 1050 Lancet Oncol 2017: 14.7 vs 9.2 months; LUX-Lung 3 JCO 2013: exon 19/L858R 13.6 vs 6.9 months.

claims.claim: At progression, plasma or tissue is re-tested for MET amplification, C797S, small-cell transformation and other mechanisms; historically T790M after a first-generation drug was treated with osimertinib (AURA3: 10.1 against 4.4 months), a sequence first-line osimertinib has largely removed.
claims.note: AURA3 NEJM 2017: PFS 10.1 vs 4.4 months.

claims.claim: Lorlatinib has the longest disease control recorded for any targeted lung cancer drug: in CROWN, five-year progression-free survival was 60 against 8 percent with crizotinib (hazard ratio 0.19), with intracranial progression close to abolished, at the cost of neurocognitive, mood, weight and lipid effects.
claims.note: CROWN JCO 2024: 5-yr PFS 60% vs 8%, HR 0.19; time to intracranial progression HR 0.06; "longest PFS ever reported with any single-agent molecular targeted treatment in advanced NSCLC".

claims.claim: Alectinib (ALEX: median progression-free survival 34.8 against 10.9 months;
claims.note: ALEX Ann Oncol 2020: median PFS 34.8 vs 10.9 months.

claims.claim: Crizotinib, which PROFILE 1014 established against chemotherapy (10.9 against 7.0 months), is now the control arm rather than a treatment.
claims.note: PROFILE 1014 NEJM 2014: PFS 10.9 vs 7.0 months.

claims.claim: TRIDENT-1 gave a 79 percent response rate and median progression-free survival of 35.7 months in ROS1 inhibitor-naive patients, and responses in 59 percent of those with the G2032R solvent-front mutation after an earlier inhibitor.
claims.note: TRIDENT-1 NEJM 2024: TKI-naive response 79%, PFS 35.7 months; G2032R "Ten of the 17 patients (59%)".

claims.claim: Crizotinib, which defined the subtype (72 percent response, median progression-free survival 19.2 months in the PROFILE 1001 expansion cohort), penetrates the brain poorly and is a second choice; taletrectinib is approved in China and the United States.
claims.note: PROFILE 1001 ROS1 NEJM 2014: ORR 72%, PFS 19.2 months.

claims.claim: LIBRETTO-431 established it against platinum chemotherapy with or without pembrolizumab in untreated disease, and LIBRETTO-001 gave an objective response of 85 percent in the untreated and 64 percent in the previously treated, with 91 percent intracranial response.
claims.note: LIBRETTO-001 NEJM 2020: 64% previously treated (n=105), 85% untreated (n=39), intracranial 91% (n=11).

claims.claim: Pralsetinib produced a 61 percent response in the previously treated cohort of ARROW but is not recommended by NICE (TA812), so selpercatinib is effectively the only funded option in England.
claims.note: ARROW lung cohort Lancet Oncol 2021 (linked on arrow-thyroid supplement): "53 (61%) of 87 patients with previous platinum-based chemotherapy"; NICE TA812 "not recommended".

claims.claim: Metastatic disease, BRAF V600E, HER2-mutant, NTRK and NRG1: BRAF V600E: dabrafenib with trametinib (64 percent response in the untreated cohort of BRF113928) or encorafenib with binimetinib (PHAROS); both are funded in England first line only, under NICE TA898 and TA1150.
claims.note: BRF113928 untreated cohort Lancet Oncol 2017: "23 (64%)"; NICE TA898 "only if ... first-line"; TA1150 "it is used at first line".

claims.claim: HER2 (ERBB2) mutation: trastuzumab deruxtecan at 5.4 mg/kg (DESTINY-Lung02), with interstitial lung disease as the risk that defines the drug, or zongertinib, a HER2-selective tyrosine kinase inhibitor approved by the FDA in 2025 and moved to first line in 2026.
claims.note: DESTINY-Lung02 JCO 2023: 5.4 and 6.4 mg/kg arms, ILD 12.9% at 5.4 mg/kg. Zongertinib FDA label (openFDA, effective 2026-08-13) now indicated without the prior-therapy restriction; drug record states 2025 accelerated approval and 2026 first-line approval.

claims.claim: NRG1 fusion: zenocutuzumab, which gave a 29 percent response rate in the 93 patients with non-small-cell lung cancer in the eNRGy study and holds FDA accelerated approval from 4 December 2024.
claims.note: Zenocutuzumab NEJM 2025: "27 of 93 patients (29%) with non-small-cell lung cancer".

claims.claim: Metastatic disease without a driver, PD-L1 tumour proportion score 50 percent or more: Pembrolizumab alone (KEYNOTE-024), atezolizumab alone (IMpower110: median overall survival 20.2 against 13.1 months in the PD-L1-highest group, hazard ratio 0.59) or cemiplimab alone (EMPOWER-Lung 1), with chemotherapy added where the disease burden is high or a fast response is needed.
claims.note: IMpower110 NEJM 2020: highest PD-L1 WT subgroup OS 20.2 vs 13.1 months, HR 0.59.

claims.claim: The threshold matters: CheckMate 026, which used 5 percent, failed outright (progression-free survival hazard ratio 1.15).
claims.note: CheckMate 026 NEJM 2017: primary analysis "PD-L1 expression level of 5% or more"; PFS HR 1.15 (0.91-1.45).

claims.claim: NICE TA584), durvalumab with tremelimumab and chemotherapy (POSEIDON: median overall survival 14.0 against 11.7 months, hazard ratio 0.77) and nivolumab with ipilimumab and two cycles of chemotherapy (CheckMate 9LA: 14.1 against 10.7 months, hazard ratio 0.69), the last of which NICE does not recommend (TA724), so it is not routinely funded in England.
claims.note: POSEIDON JCO 2023: T+D+CT OS 14.0 vs 11.7 months, HR 0.77; CheckMate 9LA Lancet Oncol 2021: 14.1 vs 10.7, HR 0.69; NICE TA724 "not recommended"; TA584 atezolizumab+bevacizumab+carboplatin+paclitaxel.

claims.claim: Metastatic non-small-cell lung cancer, later lines: Docetaxel, with nintedanib in adenocarcinoma after first-line chemotherapy (LUME-Lung 1: median progression-free survival 3.4 against 2.7 months;
claims.note: LUME-Lung 1 Lancet Oncol 2014: PFS "median 3.4 months ... vs 2.7 months" is for all patients; the sentence places it under adenocarcinoma, where the reported benefit is OS 12.6 vs 10.3 months.
claims.fixed: Labelled 3.4 vs 2.7 as all patients and added the adenocarcinoma OS 12.6 vs 10.3 months.

claims.claim: Where a checkpoint inhibitor was not given first line, nivolumab (CheckMate 017: median overall survival 9.2 against 6.0 months;
claims.note: CheckMate 017 NEJM 2015: OS 9.2 vs 6.0 months.

claims.claim: CheckMate 057: 12.2 against 9.4 months), atezolizumab (OAK: 13.8 against 9.6 months) or pembrolizumab in PD-L1-positive disease (KEYNOTE-010: 10.4 against 8.5 months at 2 mg/kg, hazard ratio 0.71) each beat docetaxel.
claims.note: CheckMate 057: 12.2 vs 9.4; OAK: 13.8 vs 9.6; KEYNOTE-010: 10.4 (2 mg/kg) vs 8.5, HR 0.71.

claims.claim: Ramucirumab with docetaxel (REVEL: median overall survival 10.5 against 9.1 months) is licensed but not recommended by NICE (TA403).
claims.note: REVEL Lancet 2014: OS 10.5 vs 9.1 months; NICE TA403 "not recommended".

claims.claim: Antibody-drug conjugates: datopotamab deruxtecan against TROP2 improved progression-free but not overall survival in TROPION-Lung01 (hazard ratios 0.75 and 0.94) and holds a 2025 FDA approval for EGFR-mutant disease after a tyrosine kinase inhibitor and platinum chemotherapy; patritumab deruxtecan against HER3 improved progression-free survival in HERTHENA-Lung02 (5.8 against 5.4 months, hazard ratio 0.77) without an overall survival gain and its application was withdrawn; telisotuzumab vedotin against c-Met gave a 28.6 percent response rate in LUMINOSITY, 34.6 percent where c-Met expression was high, and was approved by the FDA in 2025; trastuzumab deruxtecan holds the HER2-mutant indication on DESTINY-Lung02.
claims.note: TROPION-Lung01 JCO 2025 (found via record NCT04656652): PFS HR 0.75, OS HR 0.94. HERTHENA-Lung02 ASCO 2025 abstract 8506 (via NCT05338970; JCO 43:16_suppl): PFS 5.8 vs 5.4 months, HR 0.77; Merck release 29 May 2025: BLA withdrawn. LUMINOSITY JCO 2024: ORR 28.6%, c-Met high 34.6%. Note: the trial records link only CT.gov (no posted results) and press releases, not these papers.

claims.claim: Bispecific antibodies: ivonescimab, which binds PD-1 and VEGF in one molecule, beat pembrolizumab on progression-free survival in HARMONi-2 (hazard ratio 0.51) with a significant overall survival result announced in 2026, and beat chemotherapy after EGFR inhibition in HARMONi-A (7.1 against 4.8 months, hazard ratio 0.46), but its first global trial, HARMONi-3, missed statistical significance for progression-free survival at interim in May 2026; amivantamab, which binds EGFR and MET, is already standard first line with lazertinib; and tarlatamab, which binds DLL3 and CD3, is the first T-cell engager to improve survival in a common solid tumour (DeLLphi-304, overall survival hazard ratio 0.60).
claims.note: HARMONi-2 Lancet 2025: PFS HR 0.51; HARMONi-A JAMA 2024: 7.1 vs 4.8 months, HR 0.46; DeLLphi-304 NEJM 2025: OS HR 0.60. Not verified: the 2026 HARMONi-2 OS announcement and the May 2026 HARMONi-3 interim (Summit and Fierce Pharma pages returned bot-block pages).

claims.claim: Limited-stage small-cell lung cancer: Four cycles of cisplatin with etoposide and concurrent thoracic radiotherapy starting with cycle 1, then consolidation durvalumab for up to two years and, in most patients, prophylactic cranial irradiation.
claims.note: Turrisi NEJM 1999: "Four cycles of cisplatin plus etoposide and ... radiotherapy ... beginning" with cycle 1; ADRIATIC NEJM 2024 durvalumab consolidation (up to 24 months per trial record).

claims.claim: The radiotherapy schedule is 45 Gy twice daily over three weeks (Intergroup 0096: median survival 23 against 19 months, five-year survival 26 against 16 percent, grade 3 oesophagitis 27 against 11 percent) or 66 Gy once daily, which CONVERT found equivalent.
claims.note: Intergroup 0096: median survival 23 vs 19 months; 5-yr 26% vs 16%; grade 3 oesophagitis 27% vs 11%.

claims.claim: ADRIATIC added durvalumab after chemoradiotherapy and gave median overall survival 55.9 against 33.4 months (hazard ratio 0.73, p=0.01), the largest single gain recorded in this disease;
claims.note: ADRIATIC NEJM 2024: OS 55.9 vs 33.4 months, HR 0.73, P = 0.01 (correct). The added "the largest single gain recorded in this disease" is not in the source.
claims.fixed: Removed "the largest single gain recorded in this disease".

claims.claim: Prophylactic cranial irradiation rests on the Auperin meta-analysis of 987 patients (three-year survival 20.7 against 15.3 percent, relative risk of death 0.84), qualified by the Japanese trial of Takahashi, which found no benefit when brain MRI surveillance replaced it.
claims.note: Auperin NEJM 1999: 987 patients, 3-yr survival 20.7% vs 15.3%, RR 0.84 (correct). Takahashi Lancet Oncol 2017 was in extensive-disease SCLC, but the sentence, in the limited-stage row, presented it as qualifying PCI in general.
claims.fixed: Added "in extensive-stage disease" after "the Japanese trial of Takahashi".

claims.claim: Consolidation thoracic radiotherapy is offered where thoracic disease remains: CREST missed its one-year endpoint (33 against 28 percent, p=0.066) but tripled two-year survival (13 against 3 percent, p=0.004).
claims.note: CREST Lancet 2015: 1-yr OS 33% vs 28% (not significant; p=0.066), 2-yr 13% vs 3% (p=0.004).

claims.claim: Prophylactic cranial irradiation is now a discussion rather than a rule, because MRI surveillance is available and the Takahashi trial found it no better: median overall survival 11.6 months with irradiation against 13.7 with surveillance in patients whose baseline MRI was clear.
claims.note: Takahashi Lancet Oncol 2017: median OS 11.6 months PCI vs 13.7 observation, MRI surveillance.

claims.claim: Relapsed small-cell lung cancer: Whether the relapse is platinum-sensitive (more than 90 days, and often more than 180) decides the first choice.
claims.note: The 90-day threshold rests on the NCCN SCLC guideline cited on the row, which needs a login; no trial record on the row states it.

claims.claim: Otherwise: tarlatamab, a DLL3 and CD3 bispecific T-cell engager, gave a 40 percent response rate at 10 mg in DeLLphi-301 and beat chemotherapy in DeLLphi-304, with cytokine release syndrome in about half and a mandatory monitored first dose; lurbinectedin gave a 35.2 percent response rate in its basket cohort, though its confirmatory combination trial ATLANTIS, which added doxorubicin, missed on overall survival (hazard ratio 0.97); topotecan, oral or intravenous, remains the long-standing option.
claims.note: DeLLphi-301 NEJM 2023: ORR 40% at 10 mg, CRS 51%; lurbinectedin basket Lancet Oncol 2020: 35.2%; ATLANTIS Lancet Respir Med 2023: OS HR 0.97.

claims.claim: SABR-COMET randomised 99 patients with one to five oligometastatic lesions to stereotactic ablative radiotherapy plus standard care or standard care alone and found longer overall survival, with lung primaries well represented.
claims.note: SABR-COMET Lancet 2019: 99 patients, one to five metastatic lesions, OS 28 vs 41 months.

claims.claim: A malignant pleural effusion is drained and then either pleurodesed with talc or managed with an indwelling pleural catheter: TIME2 found breathlessness relief identical (24.7 against 24.4 mm on a 100 mm scale, p=0.96) and AMPLE found the catheter reduced total hospital days (10.0 against 12.0, p=0.03), so the choice turns on trapped lung, home support and how much hospital time the patient will accept.
claims.note: TIME2 JAMA 2012: 24.7 vs 24.4 mm, P = .96; AMPLE JAMA 2017: hospital days 10.0 vs 12.0, P = .03.

claims.claim: Palliation: bone and brain metastases: A single 8 Gy fraction of radiotherapy for an uncomplicated painful bone metastasis: the Dutch Bone Metastasis Study found response to initial treatment 71 against 73 percent for a multi-fraction course (p=0.84), and retreatment, needed more often after a single fraction, worked in 63 percent.
claims.note: Dutch Bone Metastasis Study IJROBP 2004: response 71% SF vs 73% MF (p = 0.84); "retreatment was effective in 63% of retreated patients".

claims.claim: For one to four brain metastases, stereotactic radiosurgery alone with MRI surveillance: JROSG 99-1 found adding whole-brain radiotherapy did not lengthen life (7.5 against 8.0 months, p=0.42) though it halved twelve-month brain recurrence (46.8 against 76.4 percent), and QUARTZ found whole-brain radiotherapy added nothing to steroids and supportive care in patients unfit for either.
claims.note: JROSG 99-1 JAMA 2006: survival 7.5 vs 8.0 months (P = .42), 12-month recurrence 46.8% vs 76.4%. That is a 39 percent relative reduction, not a halving.
claims.fixed: "halved" -> "reduced" (also the identical sentence in the palliation record at lung-treatment.ts:41).

claims.claim: See a GP for a cough lasting longer than 3 weeks or any other symptom; ask for an urgent GP appointment or use NHS 111 if you cough up blood; call 999 or go to A&E if you are struggling to breathe or have pain in the chest or upper back (NHS)
claims.note: NHS symptoms page: "cough for longer than 3 weeks"; "Ask for an urgent GP appointment or get help from NHS 111 if ... coughed up blood"; "Call 999 or go to A&E if ... struggling to breathe ... pain in your chest or upper back".

claims.claim: In England in 2019, about 26 percent of lung cancers were diagnosed after an urgent suspected cancer referral and 33 percent after an emergency presentation (Cancer Research UK)
claims.note: CRUK main page: England 2019 "around 1 in 4 (26%) ... urgent suspected cancer (two week wait) referral and 1 in 3 (33%) via an emergency presentation".

claims.claim: PET-CT for everyone who could have treatment with curative intent (NICE NG122 1.2.4)
claims.note: NG122 1.2.4 PET-CT for all who could have curative-intent treatment.

claims.claim: Mediastinal nodes sampled through the airway or oesophageal wall by endobronchial ultrasound-guided needle aspiration, endoscopic ultrasound-guided needle aspiration, or both, with surgical staging kept for a negative result and continuing suspicion (NICE NG122 1.2.8, 1.2.20 to 1.2.22)
claims.note: NG122 1.2.8, 1.2.20-1.2.22 (EBUS-TBNA, EUS-FNA, surgical staging after a negative result with high suspicion).

claims.claim: Brain imaging by stage: none for clinical stage 1 without neurological symptoms, contrast-enhanced CT for stage 2, contrast-enhanced MRI for stage 3 (NICE NG122 1.2.24 to 1.2.26)
claims.note: NG122 1.2.24 (no dedicated brain imaging stage 1), 1.2.25 (contrast CT stage 2), 1.2.26 (contrast MRI stage 3), all for curative-intent treatment.

claims.claim: The ninth edition of the TNM classification has been in force since 1 January 2025, built on 124,581 patients diagnosed from 2011 to 2019 (British Journal of Radiology 2025;
claims.note: Rami-Porta JTO 2024: "76,518 patients from a total of 124,581 registered"; IASLC M-descriptor paper: "A database of 124,581 patients diagnosed between 2011 and 2019"; BJR 2025: effective 1 January 2025.

claims.claim: M changed at the far end: M1c is split into M1c1, several metastases in one extrathoracic organ system, and M1c2, several metastases across organ systems; both remain stage IVB
claims.note: Rami-Porta JTO 2024: M1c1 one organ system, M1c2 multiple; "M1c1 and M1c2 remain in stage group IVB".

claims.claim: Stage groups moved to follow: T1N1 to IIA, T1N2a to IIB, T3N2a to IIIA, T2aN2b and T2bN2b to IIIB
claims.note: Rami-Porta JTO 2024: "T1N1, T1N2a, and T3N2a ... IIA, IIB, and IIIA ... T2aN2b and T2bN2b ... IIIB".

claims.claim: In England 34 percent of staged cases in 2022 were stage I or II; in the United States 24 percent are localised at diagnosis, 21 percent regional and 51 percent distant (Cancer Research UK;
claims.note: CRUK: "In 2022, 34% ... known stage ... early stage (I & II) in England"; SEER: localized 24%, regional 21%, distant 51%.

claims.claim: Asia carries 65.6 percent of cases and 64.3 percent of deaths (GLOBOCAN 2024), and of the ten European countries surveyed in 2026 only three had a formal programme.
claims.note: Asia 65.6% / 64.3% matches GLOBOCAN 2024 fact sheet. "of the ten European countries surveyed in 2026 only three had a formal programme": no source on the record (none of the 25 links) bears on it, and none could be identified.
claims.fixed: Removed the European survey clause.

claims.claim: Fifteen percent of UK lung cancers, and 15 to 25 percent worldwide, arise in people who have never smoked, and every eligibility rule in use starts from smoking history.
claims.note: UK 15% matches BJC Reports 2023 ("15% of lung cancers diagnosed in the UK"), but that source puts the worldwide share at "10-25%"; the 15-25% figure is from Health Science Reports 2026, which was in the file but not linked on this record.
claims.fixed: Added SRC.lcinsBurden2026 (Health Sci Rep 2026, "~15%-25% depending on the geographic region") to the record links.

claims.claim: Estimates across the trials range from 0 to 67 percent (US Preventive Services Task Force evidence report, 2021), which is the widest range for any screened cancer, and the number decides how much of the screening benefit is real.
claims.note: USPSTF evidence report JAMA 2021: "Overdiagnosis estimates varied greatly (0%-67% ...)" is correct; "which is the widest range for any screened cancer" is not in the source.
claims.fixed: Removed "which is the widest range for any screened cancer".

claims.claim: UK lung cancer mortality is 102 percent higher in women and 93 percent higher in men in the most deprived fifth than in the least, around 13,400 UK deaths a year are linked with deprivation, and five-year survival in England is 20.1 percent in the most deprived group against 27.6 percent in the least.
claims.note: CRUK mortality: females 102% and males 93% higher in most deprived quintile; "Around 13,400 deaths ... linked with deprivation"; CRUK survival: 20.1% vs 27.6%.

claims.claim: Screening eligibility is written in pack-years, which excludes high-risk groups systematically: 31 percent of white smokers qualified against 17 percent of Black smokers in one United States cohort (Aldrich 2019), so a rule built to find the highest risk misses hardest where the risk is highest.
claims.note: Aldrich JAMA Oncol 2019 (record on the page): "5654 of 32 463 African American smokers (17%) were eligible ... compared with 4992 of 15 901 white smokers (31%)".

claims.claim: At the same stage and in systems free at the point of use, patients in more deprived circumstances are less likely to receive any lung cancer treatment (odds ratio 0.79), less likely to have surgery and less likely to have chemotherapy.
claims.note: Forrest PLoS Med 2013: any treatment OR 0.79, surgery 0.68, chemotherapy 0.82; "The association remained when stage was taken into account for receipt of surgery, and was found in both universal and non-universal health care systems." The page applied "at the same stage" to all three.
claims.fixed: Reworded: stage-adjusted gap stated for surgery only; found in universal and other systems.

claims.claim: Differentiated thyroid cancer (papillary ~85%, follicular, oncocytic) arises from follicular cells, retains iodine uptake, and has a 10-year survival above 95%; its incidence has tripled in many countries because ultrasound finds tiny tumours that would never have caused harm.
claims.note: Wikipedia (the only source on the record): papillary "75 to 85% of cases"; 10-year survival 97% for papillary (Ito 2018), 85% for follicular in the same table. "10-year survival above 95%" for differentiated cancer as a whole applied the papillary figure to all; US incidence +313% supports "tripled".
claims.fixed: "has a 10-year survival above 95%" -> "has an excellent outlook (10-year survival about 97% for papillary cancer)".

claims.claim: Differentiated disease is treated by surgery, with radioactive iodine (the first theranostic, 1946) reserved for intermediate and high-risk patients after HiLo, ESTIMABL2, and IoN showed low-risk patients gain nothing from it; active surveillance is accepted for microcarcinomas, and lobectomy suffices for many.
claims.note: HiLo NEJM 2012 (record link) compared 1.1 vs 3.7 GBq ("Low-dose radioiodine ... was as effective as high-dose"); it did not show low-risk patients gain nothing from radioiodine. ESTIMABL2 NEJM 2022 and IoN Lancet 2025 did. 1946 correct (Seidlin, JAMA 1946, doi 10.1001/jama.1946.02870490016004).
claims.fixed: HiLo now described as showing a low dose ablates as well as a high one.

claims.claim: ~820,000 cases per year; most are indolent papillary cancers with >98% survival.
claims.note: ~820,000 is the GLOBOCAN 2022 world figure (repo dataset, GCO API v3/2022: 821,214), presented undated; the record cited only Wikipedia, which gives neither. ">98% survival": Wikipedia infobox "Five year survival rates 98% (US)".
claims.fixed: Dated: "In 2022, GLOBOCAN estimated about 821,000 new cases worldwide"; survival given as five-year 98% in the US; GCO Cancer Today link added to the record.

claims.claim: Anaplastic thyroid cancer with BRAF V600E has moved from a median survival under six months to 15 months with the doublet and longer with immunotherapy added, and neoadjuvant use enables surgery.
claims.note: ROAR ATC update Ann Oncol 2022 (record on the page): median OS 14.5 months with dabrafenib-trametinib; introduction: "Median survival from diagnosis is 5 months".

claims.claim: Low-risk differentiated (pT1-T2 N0): Lobectomy or total thyroidectomy; no radioiodine ablation (ESTIMABL2, IoN); modest TSH suppression then normal-range TSH.
claims.note: ESTIMABL2 NEJM 2022 (no radioiodine non-inferior in low-risk) and IoN Lancet 2025 (no ablation non-inferior); pT1-T2 labels are stage names.

claims.claim: Intermediate/high-risk differentiated: Total thyroidectomy with therapeutic node dissection; radioiodine (1.1-3.7 GBq adjuvant; higher for known metastases) after recombinant TSH;
claims.note: HiLo (row ref) compared 1.1 and 3.7 GBq for remnant ablation in T1-T3 disease; the row called 1.1-3.7 GBq the adjuvant dose for intermediate/high-risk disease, which no source on the row states.
claims.fixed: Relabelled as "the doses HiLo compared for ablation".

claims.claim: Anaplastic thyroid cancer: BRAF V600E cases now respond to dabrafenib-trametinib, often enough to allow surgery; the 60% without the mutation still have few options.
claims.note: "the 60% without the mutation": Wikipedia does not give it; the ROAR paper on the page says "BRAF V600E mutation is found in 10%-50% of ATCs", i.e. 50-90% without.
claims.fixed: "the 60% without the mutation" -> "the half or more without the mutation".

claims.claim: Anaplastic thyroid cancer without BRAF V600E (about 60%) still has a median survival of a few months.
claims.note: "(about 60%)" not in any source on the record; ROAR full text: V600E "found in 10%-50% of ATCs"; median survival from diagnosis 5 months supports "a few months".
claims.fixed: "(about 60%)" -> "(half or more of cases)".

claims.claim: HPV-positive disease is far more curable (3-year survival >80%) and has its own staging system.
claims.note: RTOG 0129 NEJM 2010 (record on the page): HPV-positive oropharyngeal 3-yr OS 82.4% vs 57.1%. AJCC 8th HPV staging in the page history.

claims.claim: Immunotherapy transformed recurrent and metastatic disease: nivolumab (CheckMate 141) and then pembrolizumab first line (KEYNOTE-048) replaced the cetuximab-chemotherapy EXTREME regimen, and in June 2025 KEYNOTE-689 delivered the first perioperative approval, doubling event-free survival by giving pembrolizumab before and after surgery.
claims.note: Merck release 13 June 2025: FDA approval, "first perioperative anti-PD-1 treatment regimen" for resectable LA HNSCC CPS>=1; median EFS 59.7 vs 29.6 months (about double).

claims.claim: What is coming: EGFR-directed bispecifics with pembrolizumab (petosemtamab, ficerafusp alfa) posting response rates two to three times those of pembrolizumab alone in early trials, now in phase 3; photoimmunotherapy (approved in Japan) in global phase 3; ctHPV-DNA to guide response-adapted de-escalation; and B7-H3 and EGFR×HER3 ADCs.
claims.note: "response rates two to three times those of pembrolizumab alone": no source on the record gives pembrolizumab-alone response rates or the ratio; petosemtamab record links only CT.gov; ficerafusp JCO 2026 gives 54% in HPV-negative disease without a comparator.
claims.fixed: "posting response rates two to three times those of pembrolizumab alone in early trials" -> "posting high response rates in early single-arm trials".

claims.claim: ~900,000 cases per year;
claims.note: "~900,000 cases per year" undated. Wikipedia (only source): "In 2018 ... 890,000 new cases" (GLOBOCAN 2018). GLOBOCAN 2022 (repo dataset) for the six head and neck sites sums to 947,211.
claims.fixed: "In 2022, GLOBOCAN estimated about 947,000 new cases across the lip and oral cavity, salivary glands, pharynx and larynx"; GCO Cancer Today link added.

claims.claim: Perioperative pembrolizumab (KEYNOTE-689) is the first curative-intent advance since cetuximab-radiation in 2006, with median event-free survival roughly doubled.
claims.note: Merck release: median EFS 59.7 vs 29.6 months in CPS>=1 (roughly doubled); Bonner cetuximab-radiation 2006 in page history.

claims.claim: Locally advanced, resectable (stage III-IVA): Neoadjuvant pembrolizumab, surgery, adjuvant pembrolizumab with (chemo)radiation for PD-L1 CPS ≥1 (KEYNOTE-689); otherwise surgery then risk-adapted (chemo)radiation.
claims.note: Merck release: approval for CPS >=1, neoadjuvant pembrolizumab then adjuvant with radiotherapy with or without cisplatin.

claims.claim: HPV-negative, tobacco-related disease has 5-year survival around 50% and has seen little improvement in curative outcomes beyond KEYNOTE-689.
claims.note: "5-year survival around 50%" for HPV-negative disease: Wikipedia gives only "42-64%" five-year survival for all head and neck cancer in the developed world; no source on the record gives an HPV-negative five-year figure. RTOG 0129 (on the page) gives HPV-negative 3-yr OS 57.1%.
claims.fixed: Replaced with RTOG 0129: "had three-year overall survival of 57.1% in RTOG 0129, against 82.4% for HPV-positive oropharyngeal cancer".

claims.claim: It is the third most common cancer worldwide (about 1.9 million cases a year) and, because many are still found late, the second most common cause of cancer death (900,000 a year).
claims.note: GLOBOCAN 2022 colorectum (public/globocan/countries.json, WORLD code 41): 1,926,425 cases, 904,019 deaths; the record's own fact sheets are now GLOBOCAN 2024 (colorectum 2,041,007 and 917,895; colon 1,206,011 + rectum 778,594). Ranks 3rd and 2nd hold in both editions. Undated as current.
claims.fixed: Dated: 'about 1.9 million cases in 2022, by GLOBOCAN's estimate' and 'about 900,000 deaths that year'.

claims.claim: Most cases arise through the adenoma-carcinoma sequence driven by APC loss, KRAS mutation, and TP53 loss (chromosomal instability); about 15% arise through mismatch-repair deficiency (dMMR/MSI-high), either sporadically via MLH1 methylation or through Lynch syndrome.
claims.note: Domingo 2016: MMR-D in 833 of 6,211 (13.4%); TCGA 2012: 16% hypermutated, three-quarters MSI-high; NICHE-2: dMMR in 10-15% of non-metastatic colon cancer. 'About 15%' within these.

claims.claim: The IARC fact sheets, served with the GLOBOCAN 2024 estimates, count the colon and the rectum separately: 1,206,011 new colon cancers a year (the 4th commonest cancer, age-standardised rate 10.8 per 100,000) with 556,774 deaths (the 5th commonest cause of cancer death, 4.7 per 100,000), and 778,594 rectal cancers (8th, 7.3 per 100,000) with 339,370 deaths (9th, 3.0 per 100,000).
claims.note: Fact sheets print 'GLOBOCAN 2024': colon rank 4, 1 206 011, ASR 10.8; deaths rank 5, 556 774, ASR 4.7; rectum rank 8, 778 594, ASR 7.3; deaths rank 9, 339 370, ASR 3.0.

claims.claim: Added together that is 1,984,605 new cases and 896,144 deaths a year, which is where the familiar round figures of about 1.9 million cases and about 900,000 deaths come from.
claims.note: Sum is right (1,206,011 + 778,594 = 1,984,605; 556,774 + 339,370 = 896,144) but 1,984,605 rounds to about 2.0 million; the familiar 1.9 million is GLOBOCAN 2022 colorectum (1,926,425), not this sum.
claims.fixed: Now 'close to 2 million cases and 900,000 deaths; the older round figure of about 1.9 million cases is GLOBOCAN's 2022 estimate (1,926,425 colorectal cancers)'.

claims.claim: Asia has 49.3 percent of colon cases, Europe 27.2 percent, Northern America 10.6 percent, Latin America and the Caribbean 8.3 percent, Africa 3.4 percent and Oceania 1.3 percent.
claims.note: Colon fact sheet (GLOBOCAN 2024): Asia 594 123 49.3%, Europe 328 565 27.2%, Northern America 127 327 10.6%, Latin America and the Caribbean 99 843 8.3%, Africa 40 481 3.4%, Oceania 15 672 1.3%.

claims.claim: In the United States the SEER programme projects 158,850 new cases (7.5 percent of all cancers) and 55,230 deaths (8.8 percent of cancer deaths) for 2026, making colorectal cancer the 4th commonest cancer diagnosed and the 2nd commonest cause of cancer death; the rate of new cases is 37.6 per 100,000 a year (2019 to 2023) and the death rate 12.7 (2020 to 2024); the median age at diagnosis is 66 and at death 72; about 3.9 percent of Americans will be diagnosed in their lifetime; and 1,478,528 people were living with the disease in 2023.
claims.note: SEER: 'Estimated New Cases in 2026 158,850 ... 7.5% ... Estimated Deaths in 2026 55,230 ... 8.8%'; 37.6 and 12.7 per 100,000 (2019-2023 cases, 2020-2024 deaths); median age 66 at diagnosis, 72 at death; 'Approximately 3.9 percent'; '1,478,528 people living with colorectal cancer' in 2023; fourth most common, second leading cause of death.

claims.claim: Rates differ by group: 59.5 per 100,000 in non-Hispanic American Indian and Alaska Native men and 50.1 in non-Hispanic Black men against 42.9 in non-Hispanic White men (SEER).
claims.note: SEER new-case rates, males: NH American Indian/Alaska Native 59.5, NH Black 50.1, NH White 42.9.

claims.claim: Cancer Research UK counts 48,213 new bowel cancers a year (2019, 2021 to 2022), more than 130 a day, which makes it the 4th commonest cancer and 12 percent of all new cancers: about 26,800 in men and about 21,400 in women.
claims.note: CRUK: '48,213 new cases of bowel cancer each year, 2019, 2021-2022, UK'; 'more than 130 every day'; 4th most common; 12% of all new cases; around 21,400 females and 26,800 males.

claims.claim: It is the 2nd commonest cause of cancer death, with about 17,700 deaths a year (2022 to 2024), 48 a day.
claims.note: CRUK: '2nd most common cause of cancer death ... around 17,700 deaths every year; that's 48 every day (2022-2024)'.

claims.claim: More than two-fifths (43 percent) of new cases are in people aged 75 and over, rates are highest at 85 to 89, and 59 percent of deaths are in the over-75s.
claims.note: CRUK: 'more than two-fifths (43%) ... aged 75 and over'; 'highest in people aged 85 to 89'; 'around three-fifths (59%) of bowel cancer deaths ... 75 and over'.

claims.claim: The lifetime risk of a diagnosis is 1 in 20 for women and 1 in 17 for men born in 1961.
claims.note: CRUK risk page: 'lifetime risk ... 1 in 20 (5%) for females, and 1 in 17 (6%) for males born in 1961 in the UK'.

claims.claim: The trends run in opposite directions: incidence rates are up about 6 percent since the early 1990s but down 3 percent in the last decade, and are projected to fall a further 7 percent by 2038 to 2040 (to about 47,700 cases a year), while mortality rates have almost halved (down 46 percent) since the early 1970s and fell 6 percent in the last decade.
claims.note: CRUK: incidence up 6% since early 1990s, down 3% last decade, projected down 7% to around 47,700 a year by 2038-2040; mortality down 46% since early 1970s and 6% in last decade.

claims.claim: Deprivation shows through: mortality rates for lower gastrointestinal cancer are 22 percent higher in the most deprived fifth than the least for women and 27 percent higher for men, about 1,700 deaths a year in the UK.
claims.note: CRUK mortality: lower GI cancer mortality 22% higher in most deprived quintile for females, 27% for males; around 1,700 deaths a year linked with deprivation.

claims.claim: The American Cancer Society's 2026 report finds overall incidence falling 0.9 percent a year over 2013 to 2022, driven by a 2.5 percent annual fall in people aged 65 and over, while incidence rose 3 percent a year in adults aged 20 to 49 and 0.4 percent a year at 50 to 64, dominated by tumours of the distal colon and rectum; rectal cancer incidence overall turned upwards by 1 percent a year from 2018 to 2022 after decades of decline and now accounts for 32 percent of colorectal cancers, up from 27 percent in the mid-2000s.
claims.note: ACS 2026 abstract: fell 0.9% a year 2013-2022, 2.5% a year fall at 65+, rose 3% at 20-49 and 0.4% at 50-64, distal colon and rectum; rectal +1% a year 2018-2022, now 32% of CRC, up from 27% in the mid-2000s.

claims.claim: Mortality under 50 has risen 1 percent a year since 2004 and at 50 to 64 by 1 percent a year since 2019, while it fell 2.3 percent a year in the over-65s from 2012.
claims.note: ACS 2026: mortality under 50 up 1% a year since 2004; 50-64 up 1% a year since 2019; 65+ down 2.3% a year since 2012.

claims.claim: The earlier 2023 report put the same shift another way: the share of cases in people under 55 went from 11 percent in 1995 to 20 percent in 2019, and 60 percent of new cases were advanced in 2019 against 52 percent in the mid-2000s.
claims.note: ACS 2023: 'proportion of cases among those younger than 55 years increased from 11% in 1995 to 20% in 2019'; '60% of all new cases were advanced in 2019 versus 52% in the mid-2000s'.

claims.claim: A study of registry data from 36 countries found incidence in adults under 50 rising in 19 of them and, in nine spanning three continents (Australia, Canada, Denmark, Germany, New Zealand, Slovenia, Sweden, the UK and the USA), rising in the young while stable or falling in older adults; the uptick began in the mid-1990s in most high-income countries, and the steepest rises were in Korea and New Zealand (Siegel 2019).
claims.note: Siegel 2019 (Gut): rising in 19 of 36 countries, nine with stable or declining older-adult trends (the nine named), uptick from the mid-1990s, steepest in Korea (AAPC 4.2) and New Zealand (4.0).

claims.claim: Age comes first, and then a list that is unusually modifiable: Cancer Research UK judges 54 percent of UK bowel cancers preventable.
claims.note: CRUK: '54% of bowel cancer cases in the UK are preventable'.

claims.claim: Processed meat causes 13 percent of UK cases (risk 18 percent higher per 50 g a day; colon cancer risk 22 percent higher per 100 g a day of red meat, with no association for rectal cancer); too little fibre causes 28 percent (risk 10 percent lower per 10 g a day of total or cereal fibre, 20 percent lower per 90 g a day of whole grains); overweight and obesity cause 11 percent (colon cancer risk 30 percent higher in men and 12 percent higher in women per 5 units of body mass index, 25 percent higher per 10 cm of waist, and adenoma risk 47 percent higher in obesity); alcohol causes 6 percent (risk 7 percent higher per unit a day, 33 percent higher above 6 units a day); smoking causes 7 percent (17 to 21 percent higher risk in current smokers, adenomatous polyp risk about doubled, serrated polyp risk more than doubled); too little physical activity causes 5 percent (colon cancer risk 19 percent lower in the most active); and ionising radiation 2 percent.
claims.note: CRUK risk page: processed meat 13%, +18% per 50 g/day; colon +22% per 100 g/day red meat, rectal not associated; fibre 28%, -10% per 10 g/day, whole grains -20% per 90 g/day; overweight 11%, colon +30% men/+12% women per 5 BMI units, +25% per 10 cm waist, adenoma +47%; alcohol 6%, +7% per unit, +33% at 6+ units; smoking 7%, +17-21%, adenomatous polyp 'around twice', serrated 'more than twice'; physical activity 5%, colon -19%; ionising radiation 2%.

claims.claim: Medical conditions matter too: type 2 diabetes raises risk 22 to 30 percent, and inflammatory bowel disease (ulcerative or Crohn's colitis) raises it 70 percent, with a 5 percent risk of bowel cancer after 20 years of disease.
claims.note: CRUK: type II diabetes +22-30%; IBD +70%; 'IBD for 20 years or more have a 5% risk'.

claims.claim: Inherited syndromes account for a minority but a decisive one: mismatch repair variants (Lynch syndrome) are carried by about 1 in 279 people and cause 1 to 4 percent of colon cancers, familial adenomatous polyposis fewer than 1 percent, and about 1 in 45 people carry a MUTYH variant (Win 2017;
claims.note: Win 2017 abstract: '1 in 279 ... mismatch repair genes', '1 in 45 carry mutations in MUTYH'; CRUK: HNPCC 1-4% of colon cancers, FAP less than 1% of bowel cancers.

claims.claim: Aspirin runs the other way: ever-use is associated with 17 percent lower risk, and longer use with lower risk still.
claims.note: CRUK: 'Bowel cancer risk is 17% lower in people who have ever used aspirin'.

claims.claim: The NHS lists the symptoms as changes in poo (looser, harder or going more or less often than usual), blood in the poo or bleeding from the bottom, a persistent feeling of needing to poo, tummy pain, a lump in the tummy, bloating, unexplained weight loss, and tiredness or breathlessness from anaemia; it advises seeing a GP for any of them, an urgent appointment or NHS 111 for black or dark red poo or bloody diarrhoea, and 999 or A&E for non-stop bleeding or large clots.
claims.note: NHS symptoms page: urgent GP or NHS 111 for black or dark red poo or bloody diarrhoea; 999 or A&E for non-stop bleeding or large clots (phone numbers, verified).

claims.claim: In England in 2019, 38 percent of bowel cancers were diagnosed through an urgent suspected cancer referral, 22 percent after an emergency presentation and 12 percent through screening;
claims.note: CRUK: England 2019, 38% urgent suspected cancer referral, 22% emergency presentation, 12% screening.

claims.claim: 47 percent of staged cases in 2022 were stage I or II (Cancer Research UK).
claims.note: CRUK: 'In 2022, 47% (around 15,000) of bowel cancer cases with a known stage were diagnosed at an early stage (I & II) in England'.

claims.claim: England invites everyone aged 50 to 74 every two years for a faecal immunochemical test done at home, with a colonoscopy for an abnormal result; the kit replaced the older guaiac test in June 2019, results come about two weeks after the laboratory receives the sample, and people aged 75 and over can request a kit every two years on the programme helpline (NHS;
claims.note: NHS: 50 to 74 every 2 years, 75+ call helpline every 2 years, results within 2 weeks; GOV.UK: FIT introduced June 2019, results '2 weeks after the laboratory receives the completed kit'.

claims.claim: The threshold that decides who is called for colonoscopy is a rationing decision as much as a clinical one: the English programme uses 120 micrograms of haemoglobin per gram of faeces, a figure no programme publication states but which the modelling of the English pilot calls the current threshold (Br J Cancer 2022; the same paper's estimates of what it buys are in the glossary).
claims.note: Br J Cancer 2022 FIT pilot abstract: 'Current 2-yearly screening with a f-Hb threshold of 120 μg/g'.

claims.claim: The symptomatic threshold in primary care is twelve times lower, at 10 micrograms per gram.
claims.note: NICE NG12 1.3.2: 'FIT result of at least 10 micrograms of haemoglobin per gram of faeces'; 120/10 = 12.

claims.claim: The United States starts earlier: the US Preventive Services Task Force recommends screening from 50 to 75 (grade A) and from 45 to 49 (grade B), with selective screening from 76 to 85, by colonoscopy, faecal testing, stool DNA or computed tomography colonography.
claims.note: USPSTF 2021: 50-75 (A), 45-49 (B), selectively 76-85 (C).

claims.claim: Annual faecal occult blood testing cut 13-year colorectal cancer mortality by 33 percent in 46,551 people in Minnesota (Mandel 1993).
claims.note: Mandel 1993: 46,551 participants; annual testing 'decreased the 13-year cumulative mortality from colorectal cancer by 33 percent'.

claims.claim: A single flexible sigmoidoscopy offered once to people aged 55 to 64 cut incidence by 26 percent and mortality by 30 percent over 17 years, and by 35 and 41 percent in those who actually attended (Atkin 2017).
claims.note: Atkin 2017: ITT incidence -26% (HR 0.74), mortality -30% (HR 0.70); per-protocol 35% and 41%; median 17.1 years.

claims.claim: NordICC, the first randomised trial of screening colonoscopy, found a 10-year risk of colorectal cancer of 0.98 percent in the invited group against 1.20 percent in usual care, an 18 percent reduction, with 455 people needing to be invited to prevent one cancer; only 42 percent of those invited attended, and a later instrumental-variable analysis of the same trial estimated a 35 to 41 percent reduction in incidence among those screened (Bretthauer 2022).
claims.note: Bretthauer 2022 confirms 0.98% vs 1.20%, 18%, 455, 42.0%. The 35 to 41 percent IV estimate is from Shi et al, Eur J Epidemiol 2025 ('reduces colorectal cancer incidence by 35 to 41% after 10 years'), not the 2022 paper it was attributed to.
claims.fixed: Citation now '(Bretthauer 2022; Shi 2025)'; Shi 2025 added to the record's links.

claims.claim: N1a, N1b and N1c mean one node, two or three nodes, or tumour deposits without node involvement, and N2a and N2b mean four to six or seven or more nodes;
claims.note: CRUK TNM: N1a 1 node, N1b 2 or 3, N1c deposits without node involvement, N2a 4 to 6; CRUK words N2b as 'more than 7', TNM 8 is 7 or more, which the page uses.

claims.claim: High-resolution magnetic resonance imaging answers the first with 92 percent specificity for predicting a clear margin, and in the 349 patients it predicted clear, 327 were clear at surgery (MERCURY, 408 patients, BMJ 2006).
claims.note: MERCURY BMJ 2006: 408 patients; specificity 92% (327/354); MRI predicted clear margins in 349, 327 clear at surgery.

claims.claim: Every metastatic tumour is tested for RAS and BRAF V600E mutations before systemic therapy (NICE NG151 1.4.1), mismatch repair status is tested at diagnosis, and where the tumour started, the right colon or the left colon and rectum, predicts both biology and the benefit of EGFR antibodies.
claims.note: NG151 1.4.1: 'Test for RAS and BRAF V600E mutations in all people with metastatic colorectal cancer suitable for systemic anticancer treatment'.

claims.claim: In the United States 34 percent of cases are found localised, 37 percent regional, 23 percent distant and 6 percent unstaged (SEER).
claims.note: SEER: Localized 34%, Regional 37%, Distant 23%, Unknown 6%.

claims.claim: The conventional adenoma-carcinoma sequence, mapped in 172 specimens in 1988 and formalised as a model in 1990, runs from normal mucosa through adenoma to carcinoma as mutations accumulate: loss of the chromosome 5 region that carries the polyposis gene, RAS mutation (found in 58 percent of adenomas over 1 cm but only 9 percent of smaller ones), loss of chromosome 18 (73 percent of carcinomas) and loss of chromosome 17p (75 percent of carcinomas) (Vogelstein 1988;
claims.note: Vogelstein 1988: 172 specimens; ras in 58% of adenomas >1 cm, 9% <1 cm; chromosome 18 deleted in 73% of carcinomas; 17p lost in 75%. Fearon 1990 the model.

claims.claim: The serrated pathway accounts for about 30 percent of colorectal carcinomas and runs instead through hyperplastic polyps, sessile serrated lesions and traditional serrated adenomas, with methylation of promoter islands and BRAF or KRAS mutation, and it produces most of the sporadic mismatch repair-deficient cancers (Bettington 2013).
claims.note: Bettington 2013: 'Approximately 30% of colorectal carcinomas develop via a serrated neoplasia pathway'.

claims.claim: Prevention follows from the first route: in the National Polyp Study, removing adenomas at colonoscopy left 1,418 patients with 76 to 90 percent fewer cancers than expected, and at a median of 15.8 years mortality from colorectal cancer among 2,602 patients whose adenomas were removed was 53 percent lower than the general population would predict (Winawer 1993;
claims.note: Winawer 1993: 1418 patients, reductions of 90, 88 and 76 percent; Zauber 2012: 2602 patients, median 15.8 years, 53% reduction in mortality.

claims.claim: Aspirin is the drug: in the CAPP2 trial, 600 mg of aspirin daily for at least two years cut colorectal cancer in Lynch syndrome carriers over ten years (hazard ratio 0.65 in the intention-to-treat analysis, 0.56 in those who completed two years), and NICE NG151 (1.1.1) now says to consider daily aspirin for more than two years in Lynch syndrome (Burn 2020).
claims.note: Burn 2020 CAPP2: 600 mg aspirin, ITT HR 0.65, per-protocol (2 years) HR 0.56, ~10 years; NG151 1.1.1 aspirin daily for more than 2 years.

claims.claim: 1,206,011 new colon cancers and 556,774 deaths, plus 778,594 rectal cancers and 339,370 deaths, a year worldwide (GLOBOCAN 2024; about 1.98 million cases and 896,000 deaths added together).
claims.note: Named GLOBOCAN 2024 and matches the fact sheets; sums 1.98 million and 896,000.

claims.claim: 48,213 UK cases and about 17,700 UK deaths a year, the 4th commonest cancer and the 2nd commonest cause of cancer death (Cancer Research UK);
claims.note: CRUK: 48,213 cases; around 17,700 deaths; 4th commonest; 2nd cause of cancer death.

claims.claim: 158,850 US cases and 55,230 deaths projected for 2026 (SEER).
claims.note: SEER: 158,850 and 55,230 estimated for 2026.

claims.claim: Incidence is falling in the over-65s and rising 3 percent a year in adults aged 20 to 49 (American Cancer Society, 2026).
claims.note: ACS 2026: falls of 2.5% a year at 65+, rises of 3% a year at 20-49.

claims.claim: In the United States, 65.4 percent of people diagnosed with colorectal cancer in 2016 to 2022 were alive five years later relative to people of the same age without the disease (SEER).
claims.note: SEER: '5-Year Relative Survival 65.4% 2016-2022'.

claims.claim: Stage at diagnosis is the biggest lever: five-year relative survival is 91.3 percent for the 34 percent found while confined to the bowel, 75.2 percent for regional disease (37 percent of cases) and 16.9 percent for distant disease (23 percent).
claims.note: SEER: localized 34% / 91.3%, regional 37% / 75.2%, distant 23% / 16.9%.

claims.claim: England's figures, for people diagnosed in 2016 to 2020, are around 90 percent at five years for stage 1, around 85 percent for stage 2, 65 percent for stage 3 and around 10 percent for stage 4; across all stages around 80 percent survive a year, almost 60 percent five years and almost 55 percent ten years (Cancer Research UK).
claims.note: CRUK patient page: stage figures (around 90, 85, 65, 10%) and 1- and 5-year (around 80%, almost 60%) are for England 2016-2020, but the 10-year figure (almost 55%) is 'for people diagnosed in England between 2013 and 2017'; the sentence put all under 2016 to 2020.
claims.fixed: Ten-year figure now labelled 'for people diagnosed in 2013 to 2017'.

claims.claim: UK ten-year survival is predicted at 54.3 percent for colon cancer and 53.9 percent for rectal cancer among people diagnosed in 2018, against 22.4 and 24.6 percent in the 1970s.
claims.note: CRUK survival: 54.3% colon, 53.9% rectal ten-year (2018); 1970s 22.4% and 24.6%.

claims.claim: Age and deprivation move the figures: ten-year colon cancer survival is 64.3 percent for women and 60.5 percent for men diagnosed at 15 to 44, against 48.0 and 48.5 percent at 75 to 99; five-year bowel cancer survival in England is 55 percent in the most deprived group and 62.9 percent in the least.
claims.note: CRUK: colon ten-year 64.3% females and 60.5% males at 15-44 vs 48.0% and 48.5% at 75-99 (2018); England five-year 55% most deprived vs 62.9% least (2018-2022).

claims.claim: Survival is conditional on what has already happened: of people diagnosed in England in 2015 to 2019, almost 57 percent survived five years, but among those who had already survived one year it was 74.5 percent.
claims.note: CRUK: 56.8% five-year (2015-2019); 74.5% after surviving one year.

claims.claim: Liver metastases are not automatically the end of the story: in an English study of people whose liver metastases could be operated on, around 45 percent survived five years or more after the operation (Morris 2010, quoted by Cancer Research UK).
claims.note: CRUK patient page quotes the 2010 study: 'around 45 out of 100 ... survived ... 5 years or more after the operation'; Morris 2010 abstract 44.2% from hepatectomy.

claims.claim: dMMR disease: immunotherapy first line gives median OS over 6 years (KEYNOTE-177); neoadjuvant IO achieves 68% pCR and 100% 3-year DFS in colon (NICHE-2) and complete organ preservation in rectal cancer (dostarlimab, AZUR-1).
claims.note: KEYNOTE-177 5-year: median OS 77.5 months (over 6 years) confirmed via Cancer Med 2026 quoting the Annals 2024 report (primary paywalled); NICHE-2 pCR 68% (NEJM 2024) and 3-year DFS 100% (MedComm 2026 review quoting ESMO 2024). But 'complete organ preservation in rectal cancer ... AZUR-1' overstates: the first AZUR-1 report (Ann Oncol 2026) gives sustained cCR at 12 months in 68% (144 evaluable).
claims.fixed: Rectal clause now 'lets most rectal cancers avoid surgery (dostarlimab; sustained clinical complete response at 12 months in 68% in the first AZUR-1 report)'; AZUR-1 Ann Oncol 2026 added to the record's links.

claims.claim: BRAF V600E first-line targeted triplet doubled survival to 30 months (BREAKWATER); full approval in 2026.
claims.note: BREAKWATER NEJM 2025: OS 30.3 vs 15.1 months (HR 0.49); FDA traditional approval 24 February 2026.

claims.claim: Adjuvant atezolizumab for dMMR stage III colon cancer halves recurrence (ATOMIC, 2025): the first adjuvant IO success in CRC.
claims.note: ATOMIC: HR for recurrence or death 0.50 (ASCO 2025 LBA1 and NEJM 2026).

claims.claim: Sidedness plus RAS/BRAF status selects anti-EGFR therapy, yielding median OS near 38 months first line (PARADIGM).
claims.note: PARADIGM JAMA 2023: left-sided median OS 37.9 vs 34.3 months.

claims.claim: WNT signalling is on in 93 to 96% of tumours (APC mutated in 58 to 77%, with RNF43, AXIN2, CTNNB1 and RSPO fusions covering most of the rest);
claims.note: TCGA 2012 (93% WNT) and Yaeger 2018 (96%); APC range 58 to 77% matches the record's cBioPortal table, spot-checked against the cBioPortal API (TCGA PanCan APC 387/534 exact).

claims.claim: TP53 52 to 73%, KRAS 40 to 44%, PIK3CA 20 to 28%, SMAD4 12 to 16%, FBXW7 13 to 17%, NRAS 4 to 9%, BRAF V600E 6 to 18%, HER2 amplification 2 to 3%.
claims.note: Ranges match the record's cBioPortal cohort table; API spot-checks exact: TCGA PanCan TP53 314/534, KRAS 218/534; MSK 2017 PIK3CA 229, SMAD4 173, FBXW7 145, NRAS 46, BRAF V600E 85 of 1,134. HER2 amplification 2-3% also in DESTINY-CRC01 abstract.

claims.claim: About 16% of tumours are hypermutated, three-quarters through mismatch repair failure and one-quarter through somatic mismatch repair or POLE mutation; the other 84% are chromosomally unstable, losing 18q, 17p and 8p and gaining 8q, 13q and 20q.
claims.note: TCGA 2012: '16% of colorectal carcinomas were found to be hypermutated: three-quarters ... high microsatellite instability ... one-quarter had somatic mismatch-repair gene and POLE mutations'.

claims.claim: Right-sided tumours are 24.3% MSI-high and 19.2% BRAF V600E against 5.2% and 2.9% on the left, and carry more KRAS and PIK3CA and less APC and TP53.
claims.note: Recomputed from cBioPortal crc_msk_2026 PRIMARY_SITE and MSI_TYPE: right side (caecum, ascending, hepatic flexure, transverse) 221/908 MSI = 24.3%, BRAF V600E 174/908 = 19.2%, exact. Left came out 4.9% and 2.8% by my subsite grouping against the page's 5.2% and 2.9% (the page's denominator, 3,483, implies a slightly different sample set); within rounding of a definitional choice.

claims.claim: EGFR antibodies improve survival on the left (hazard ratio 0.75) and not on the right (1.12) in RAS wild-type disease, the only place in colorectal oncology where anatomy selects a drug.
claims.note: Arnold 2017: left-sided OS HR 0.75 (0.67-0.84), right-sided 1.12 (0.87-1.45).

claims.claim: The adenoma-carcinoma sequence runs APC, KRAS, 18q, 17p and is mostly left-sided; the serrated pathway starts with BRAF or KRAS and proceeds by CpG island methylation, accounts for about 30% of carcinomas, and is where sporadic mismatch repair deficiency comes from, through MLH1 promoter silencing that accompanies BRAF mutation with an odds ratio of 203.
claims.note: Weisenberger 2006: CIMP-positive tumours encompass almost all BRAF-mutant cases 'odds ratio = 203'; the OR is for CIMP with BRAF, not for MLH1 silencing with BRAF as written. 30% serrated matches Bettington 2013.
claims.fixed: Now 'through MLH1 promoter silencing within the CpG island methylator phenotype, which tracks BRAF mutation with an odds ratio of 203'.

claims.claim: Mismatch repair deficient tumours carry a mean of 1,782 mutations against 73 and respond to checkpoint blockade from 31% (nivolumab, pre-treated) to 68% pathological complete response (four weeks of neoadjuvant nivolumab plus ipilimumab); microsatellite-stable tumours do not, and the phase 3 test against regorafenib failed.
claims.note: Le 2015: mean 1782 vs 73 somatic mutations; CheckMate 142: ORR 31.1%; NICHE-2 pCR 68%; IMblaze370 HR 1.00 vs regorafenib.

claims.claim: Circulating tumour DNA after surgery carries recurrence hazard ratios of 7 to 18, and after adjuvant chemotherapy 17 to 51, with lead times over imaging of about 10 to 16 months.
claims.note: Post-surgery HRs 7.2 (Reinert), 7.0 (Henriksen), 18 (Tie) support 7 to 18. After adjuvant chemotherapy the cited studies give 17.5 (Reinert), 50.76 (Henriksen) and 11 (Tie 2016), so the range is 11 to 51, not 17 to 51. Lead time: Reinert mean 8.7 months, range up to 16.5; Henriksen median 9.8; '10 to 16' mixed a median with a maximum.
claims.fixed: Now 'after adjuvant chemotherapy 11 to 51, with recurrence found a mean or median of about 9 to 10 months before imaging and up to 16.5 months'.

claims.claim: DYNAMIC is the only randomised trial in any solid tumour to change treatment on the result, cutting adjuvant chemotherapy from 28% to 15% in stage II colon cancer without losing recurrence-free survival.
claims.note: DYNAMIC: 15% vs 28% adjuvant chemotherapy (15.3 vs 27.9 in the ITT table) with non-inferior RFS. But 'the only randomised trial in any solid tumour to change treatment on the result' is not supported and is contradicted by the record's own DYNAMIC-III (randomised, ctDNA-guided, Nat Med 2025) and ALTAIR.
claims.fixed: Now 'In the randomised DYNAMIC trial, acting on the result cut adjuvant chemotherapy from 28% to 15% ... ; DYNAMIC-III could not show the same in stage III'.

claims.claim: Mismatch repair immunohistochemistry on every tumour (with BRAF V600E or MLH1 methylation reflex where MLH1 is lost), extended RAS across KRAS and NRAS exons 2, 3 and 4 before any EGFR antibody, BRAF V600 separately from non-V600, HER2 by the colorectal-specific more-than-50% rule, and sequencing rather than staining where POLE ultramutation or a fusion is possible.
claims.note: Valtorta 2015 HERACLES: HER2 positive = intense membranous staining 'in >50% of cells'; NG151/PRIME for extended RAS exons 2-4.

claims.claim: Macmillan names the colon operations as a right or left hemi-colectomy, a sigmoid colectomy (also called a high anterior resection), a transverse colectomy or a total colectomy, and the rectal ones as a local excision for a very small stage 1 cancer, an anterior resection or low anterior resection for the upper or middle rectum, usually with a total mesorectal excision, and it says that if the cancer is very low in the rectum and close to the anus you are more likely to need a permanent stoma.
claims.note: Macmillan rectal surgery page: local excision for 'a very small, stage 1 rectal cancer'; 'very low in the rectum and close to the anus, you are more likely to need a permanent stoma'; colon page: 'sigmoid colectomy or high anterior resection'.

claims.claim: It sets volume floors for rectal surgery: at least 10 major resections a year per hospital and at least 5 per surgeon.
claims.note: NG151 1.3.13 hospitals at least 10 a year; 1.3.14 surgeons at least 5.
