claims.claim: For stage 3 (cancer in the lymph nodes), NICE NG151 is explicit and the same for colon and for rectal cancer treated with short-course radiotherapy or no preoperative treatment: offer capecitabine with oxaliplatin (CAPOX) for 3 months, or if that is not suitable either oxaliplatin with fluorouracil and folinic acid (FOLFOX) for 3 to 6 months, or a single-agent fluoropyrimidine such as capecitabine for 6 months.
claims.note: NG151 1.3.15/1.3.18: CAPOX 3 months, or FOLFOX 3 to 6 months, or single-agent fluoropyrimidine 6 months; same for colon and rectal (short-course or no preoperative treatment).

claims.claim: It then says to base the choice on the person's histopathology (giving pT1 to T3 with pN1 against pT4 or pN2 as the example), performance status, personal preferences, comorbidities and age, which is the guideline's way of saying that three months of a doublet and six months of a single tablet are both defensible and the balance is yours to weigh.
claims.note: NG151: 'Base the choice on the person's histopathology (for example pT1-T3 and pN1, and pT4 and/or pN2), performance status, personal preferences, any comorbidities and age'.

claims.claim: Two forms are used: a short course of radiotherapy on its own, and a longer course of radiotherapy given together with chemotherapy (Macmillan says the drug most commonly used is capecitabine tablets, started on the first morning of radiotherapy and taken throughout it, with a DPD test first), and in recent practice both are often followed by several months of chemotherapy before surgery (total neoadjuvant therapy, tested in RAPIDO, PRODIGE 23 and OPRA on this record;
claims.note: Macmillan chemoradiation page: capecitabine most commonly used, tablets started 'on the first morning of your radiotherapy', DPD blood test first.

claims.claim: NICE NG151 recommends nivolumab with ipilimumab as an option for untreated unresectable or metastatic colorectal cancer with high microsatellite instability or mismatch repair deficiency, and pembrolizumab as an option for untreated metastatic disease with the same markers, stopped after 2 years or earlier if the disease progresses; after fluoropyrimidine-based combination chemotherapy it recommends nivolumab with ipilimumab, and pembrolizumab only if that combination cannot be used.
claims.note: NG151 1.5.1 (TA1065), 1.5.2 (TA709, stopped after 2 years), TA716 and 1.5.8 (TA914 only if nivolumab with ipilimumab cannot be used).

claims.claim: NICE NG151 points to its appraisals for metastatic colorectal cancer previously treated with fluoropyrimidine-based chemotherapy, anti-VEGF or anti-EGFR therapy: trifluridine with tipiracil plus bevacizumab after 2 systemic treatments (the SUNLIGHT combination), fruquintinib after 2 systemic treatments if trifluridine with tipiracil plus bevacizumab is not suitable (FRESCO-2), regorafenib, and trifluridine with tipiracil alone.
claims.note: NG151 1.5.11: TA1008 after 2 systemic treatments, TA1079 after 2 if TA1008 unsuitable, TA866, TA405.

claims.claim: Lynch syndrome testing, and what it means for your family: Around 3 in 100 UK bowel cancers are caused by Lynch syndrome, an inherited fault in one of the mismatch repair genes, and Bowel Cancer UK says testing should be offered to everyone at diagnosis because the result changes treatment as well as family risk.
claims.note: Bowel Cancer UK: 'Lynch syndrome is estimated to cause around 3% of bowel cancer cases in the UK'; testing 'should be offered at diagnosis'.

claims.claim: For your relatives, each child, brother and sister has a one in two chance of carrying the same change, and Bowel Cancer UK says they should be offered the same test, which it calls cascade testing; it estimates that most of the 175,000 to 200,000 people in the UK with Lynch syndrome do not know.
claims.note: Bowel Cancer UK: '50% chance that their children, brothers and sisters also have it'; 'between 175,000 to 200,000 people in the UK ... the majority don't know'.

claims.claim: For prevention, NICE NG151 says to consider aspirin, taken daily and for a period of more than 2 years, to reduce the risk of colorectal cancer in people with Lynch syndrome, noting that in January 2020 this was an off-label use and that NICE has produced a patient decision aid to support the discussion.
claims.note: NG151 1.1.1 verbatim: daily, more than 2 years, January 2020 off-label, patient decision aid.

claims.claim: Bowel Cancer UK says surveillance means colonoscopy every 18 months to two years and can reduce the chance of dying from bowel cancer by as much as 72 percent.
claims.note: Bowel Cancer UK: 'colonoscopy every 18 months to two years ... reduce the chance of dying from bowel cancer by as much as 72%'.

claims.claim: A randomised trial in another cancer (Temel 2010) found that early palliative care alongside cancer treatment improved quality of life and mood, which is why the referral belongs alongside treatment rather than after it.
claims.note: Temel 2010 NEJM (metastatic NSCLC): early palliative care improved quality of life (FACT-L 98.0 vs 91.5) and mood (depressive symptoms 16% vs 38%).

claims.claim: In stage II the absolute gain from fluorouracil and folinic acid is small: QUASAR (3,239 patients, 2,963 with stage II disease) found a relative risk of death of 0.82 and of recurrence 0.78, translating to about 3.6 percent absolute survival.
claims.note: QUASAR Lancet 2007: 3239 patients, 2963 stage II; RR death 0.82, recurrence 0.78; 'absolute improvement in survival of 3.6%' (assuming 20% 5-year mortality).

claims.claim: DYNAMIC showed that a negative circulating tumour DNA result four to seven weeks after surgery identifies patients who can safely have no chemotherapy, cutting adjuvant use from 27.9 to 15.3 percent without worse recurrence-free survival.
claims.note: DYNAMIC NEJM 2022: ctDNA at 4 or 7 weeks; ITT 15.3% (45/294) vs 27.9% (41/147), abstract 15% vs 28%; RFS non-inferior.

claims.claim: SCOT included high-risk stage II patients and found three months of oxaliplatin-containing chemotherapy non-inferior to six (three-year disease-free survival 76.7 against 77.1 percent) with grade 2 or worse neuropathy halved.
claims.note: SCOT: high-risk stage II and stage III; 3-year DFS 76.7% vs 77.1%; grade 2+ neuropathy 25% vs 58% (more than halved).

claims.claim: MOSAIC established it (three-year disease-free survival 78.2 against 72.9 percent with fluorouracil alone, hazard ratio 0.77; six-year overall survival gain confined to stage III).
claims.note: MOSAIC 2004: 3-year DFS 78.2 vs 72.9, HR 0.77; 2009: six-year OS gain in stage III (HR 0.80), none in stage II.

claims.claim: Duration follows IDEA: three months of CAPOX for T1-3 N1 disease (three-year disease-free survival 83.1 against 83.3 percent for six months) and six months of FOLFOX or CAPOX for T4 or N2.
claims.note: IDEA NEJM 2018: 83.1% vs 83.3% for T1-3 N1 is from 'an exploratory analysis of the combined regimens' (FOLFOX and CAPOX together), not CAPOX alone as the sentence implies.
claims.fixed: Added 'FOLFOX and CAPOX combined' to the figure (also in the decision-tool copy).

claims.claim: Stage III colon cancer, mismatch-repair deficient: Resection then FOLFOX with atezolizumab for twelve months (ATOMIC, three-year disease-free survival 86 against 77 percent), the first adjuvant immunotherapy success in colorectal cancer.
claims.note: ATOMIC (ASCO 2025 LBA1, the record's source): 3-year DFS 86.4% vs 76.6%; NEJM 2026 gives 86.3 vs 76.2; atezolizumab 12 months total.

claims.claim: Neoadjuvant nivolumab with ipilimumab is the alternative under test: NICHE-2 produced a 68 percent pathological complete response rate and AZUR-2 (NCT05855200, 892 patients, primary completion March 2029) is the phase 3 that would make perioperative dostarlimab standard.
claims.note: NICHE-2 pCR 68% (75/111); ClinicalTrials.gov NCT05855200: enrolment 892 (estimated), primary completion 2029-03-19.

claims.claim: FOxTROT (1,053 patients) found residual or recurrent disease within two years in 16.9 against 21.5 percent with surgery first (rate ratio 0.72), with fewer serious postoperative complications and 4.3 percent needing expedited surgery for obstruction.
claims.note: FOxTROT JCO 2023: 699 + 354 = 1,053; 16.9% vs 21.5%, rate ratio 0.72; 30 (4.3%) needed expedited surgery; fewer serious complications.

claims.claim: Locally advanced rectal cancer: radiotherapy and total neoadjuvant therapy: Total mesorectal excision is the operation (Dutch TME trial) and preoperative rather than postoperative radiotherapy is the sequence (CAO/ARO/AIO-94: five-year local relapse 6 against 13 percent, no survival difference).
claims.note: CAO/ARO/AIO-94 NEJM 2004: five-year local relapse 6% vs 13%; OS 76% vs 74% (P=0.80).

claims.claim: High-risk disease (cT4, extramural vascular invasion, cN2, threatened mesorectal fascia, lateral nodes) is treated with total neoadjuvant therapy: short-course 5 x 5 Gy then CAPOX or FOLFOX before surgery (RAPIDO: three-year disease-related treatment failure 23.7 against 30.4 percent, hazard ratio 0.75;
claims.note: RAPIDO: 5 x 5 Gy then CAPOX or FOLFOX4; 3-year DrTF 23.7% vs 30.4%, HR 0.75.

claims.claim: STELLAR: three-year disease-free survival 64.5 against 62.3 percent) or long-course chemoradiotherapy with FOLFIRINOX before it (PRODIGE 23: three-year disease-free survival 76 against 69 percent, hazard ratio 0.69).
claims.note: STELLAR JCO 2022: 3-year DFS 64.5% vs 62.3%; PRODIGE 23: 76% vs 69%, HR 0.69.

claims.claim: For sphincter-sparing candidates who do not need radiotherapy, PROSPECT showed neoadjuvant FOLFOX with selective chemoradiotherapy is non-inferior (five-year disease-free survival 80.8 against 78.6 percent).
claims.note: PROSPECT NEJM 2023: five-year DFS 80.8% vs 78.6%, non-inferior.

claims.claim: Rectal cancer: organ preservation and watch and wait: Consolidation chemotherapy after chemoradiotherapy, not induction before it, is the sequence that preserves the rectum: OPRA gave TME-free survival of 54 against 39 percent at five years (the long-term report, Journal of Clinical Oncology 2024; the first report gave 53 against 41 percent at three years), and CAO/ARO/AIO-12 found pathological complete response 25 against 17 percent with the same ordering.
claims.note: OPRA JCO 2024: TME-free survival 54% vs 39% at 5 years; JCO 2022: 53% vs 41% at 3 years; CAO/ARO/AIO-12: pCR 25% (consolidation) vs 17% (induction).

claims.claim: The International Watch & Wait Database (880 patients with a clinical complete response from 47 institutes) records two-year local regrowth of 25.2 percent, 88 percent of it within two years and 97 percent in the bowel wall where salvage surgery is possible, with five-year overall survival 85 percent and disease-specific survival 94 percent.
claims.note: IWWD Lancet 2018: 880 cCR patients, 47 institutes; 2-year regrowth 25.2%; 88% within 2 years; 97% in bowel wall; 5-year OS 85%, DSS 94%.

claims.claim: FIRE-3 found overall survival 28.7 against 25.0 months for cetuximab against bevacizumab with FOLFIRI, while CALGB/SWOG 80405 found no overall difference (30.0 against 29.0 months) before sidedness was taken into account.
claims.note: FIRE-3: OS 28.7 vs 25.0 months; CALGB/SWOG 80405: 30.0 vs 29.0 months.

claims.claim: Extended RAS testing of KRAS and NRAS exons 2, 3 and 4 is mandatory: PRIME showed patients with non-exon-2 RAS mutations do worse with panitumumab.
claims.note: PRIME NEJM 2013: other RAS mutations 'associated with inferior progression-free survival and overall survival with panitumumab-FOLFOX4'.

claims.claim: FOLFOXIRI plus bevacizumab gives a higher response rate and longer progression-free survival than a doublet (TRIBE: 12.1 against 9.7 months;
claims.note: TRIBE NEJM 2014: median PFS 12.1 vs 9.7 months; ORR 65% vs 53%.

claims.claim: TRIBE2 progression-free survival 2 of 19.2 against 16.4 months) at the cost of grade 3-4 neutropenia in about half, and is preferred where deep response matters.
claims.note: TRIBE2: PFS2 19.2 vs 16.4 months; grade 3-4 neutropenia 50% vs 21%.

claims.claim: After six cycles, maintenance with a fluoropyrimidine and bevacizumab beats observation (CAIRO3: progression-free survival 2 of 11.7 against 8.5 months).
claims.note: CAIRO3 Lancet 2015: PFS2 11.7 vs 8.5 months.

claims.claim: Metastatic disease, KRAS G12C: Sotorasib with panitumumab (CodeBreaK 300, FDA approval 16 January 2025) or adagrasib with cetuximab (KRYSTAL-1 colorectal cohort, accelerated approval 21 June 2024) after fluoropyrimidine, oxaliplatin and irinotecan.
claims.note: FDA notices: sotorasib with panitumumab approved January 16, 2025; adagrasib with cetuximab accelerated approval June 21, 2024.

claims.claim: The confirmatory trials are KRYSTAL-10 (NCT04793958, 461 patients, active but closed) and, for first-line use, CodeBreaK 301 (NCT06252649, 450 patients, recruiting).
claims.note: ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT04793958 KRYSTAL-10 ACTIVE_NOT_RECRUITING, 461 actual; NCT06252649 CodeBreaK 301 RECRUITING, 450 estimated.

claims.claim: Metastatic disease, HER2-amplified and RAS wild-type: Tucatinib with trastuzumab (MOUNTAINEER, confirmed objective response 38.1 percent;
claims.note: MOUNTAINEER Lancet Oncol 2023: confirmed ORR per BICR 38.1% (cohorts A+B, 84 patients).

claims.claim: FDA accelerated approval 19 January 2023) or trastuzumab deruxtecan at 5.4 mg/kg (DESTINY-CRC02, response 37.8 percent;
claims.note: FDA: tucatinib with trastuzumab accelerated approval January 19, 2023; DESTINY-CRC02 Lancet Oncol 2024: confirmed ORR 37.8% (31/82) at 5.4 mg/kg.

claims.claim: DESTINY-CRC01 gave 45.3 percent at the higher 6.4 mg/kg dose with interstitial lung disease in 6 percent and two deaths).
claims.note: DESTINY-CRC01 Lancet Oncol 2021 (6.4 mg/kg): cohort A ORR 45.3%; adjudicated ILD in five patients (6%), two grade 5.

claims.claim: The tumour-agnostic HER2 IHC 3+ accelerated approval of trastuzumab deruxtecan came on 5 April 2024.
claims.note: FDA: 'On April 5, 2024 ... accelerated approval to fam-trastuzumab deruxtecan-nxki ... HER2-positive (IHC3+) solid tumors'.

claims.claim: MOUNTAINEER-03 (NCT05253651, 400 patients, primary completion December 2027) is testing first-line use.
claims.note: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT05253651 MOUNTAINEER-03: 400 estimated, primary completion 2027-12-31.

claims.claim: Metastatic disease, rarer biomarkers: NTRK, RET and POLE: NTRK fusions occur in well under 1 percent of colorectal cancers, almost always in right-sided, mismatch-repair deficient, RAS and BRAF wild-type tumours, and are treated with larotrectinib, which NICE recommends tumour-agnostically in England through the Cancer Drugs Fund only (TA630); entrectinib is no longer an option there, because TA644 has been withdrawn and its replacement TA1118 was terminated in January 2026.
claims.note: NICE TA1118 page: 'Terminated: 7 January 2026'; TA644 'updated and replaced by ... 1118'; NG151 1.5.13 larotrectinib through the Cancer Drugs Fund (TA630). 'Well under 1 percent': the record's cBioPortal table (NTRK1 0.18% in crc_msk_2026) and Cocco 2019 (all kinase fusions 21 of 2,314) agree.

claims.claim: Metastatic disease, later lines: Trifluridine-tipiracil with bevacizumab (SUNLIGHT: overall survival 10.8 against 7.5 months;
claims.note: SUNLIGHT NEJM 2023: median OS 10.8 vs 7.5 months.

claims.claim: NICE TA1008), then fruquintinib (FRESCO-2: 7.4 against 4.8 months;
claims.note: FRESCO-2 Lancet 2023: OS 7.4 vs 4.8 months; NG151 TA1008.

claims.claim: NICE TA1079 only where trifluridine-tipiracil with bevacizumab is unsuitable) or regorafenib (CORRECT: 6.4 against 5.0 months;
claims.note: CORRECT Lancet 2013: OS 6.4 vs 5.0 months; NG151 TA1079 and TA866.

claims.claim: Second-line anti-angiogenic options after an oxaliplatin regimen are ziv-aflibercept (VELOUR: 13.50 against 12.06 months, not recommended by NICE in TA307) and ramucirumab (RAISE: 13.3 against 11.7 months, no NICE recommendation).
claims.note: VELOUR JCO 2012: 13.50 vs 12.06 months; RAISE Lancet Oncol 2015: 13.3 vs 11.7; NG151 1.5.12 lists aflibercept TA307 as not recommended.

claims.claim: CHRONOS screened 52 patients with circulating tumour DNA, excluded the 31 percent with a resistance mutation and rechallenged the rest with panitumumab alone: 30 percent responded and 63 percent had disease control.
claims.note: CHRONOS Nat Med 2022: of 52 screened, 16 (31%) excluded; 27 enrolled (not 'the rest', 36); 8 (30%) PR and 17 (63%) disease control.
claims.fixed: Now 'rechallenged 27 patients with panitumumab alone: 30 percent of them responded and 63 percent had disease control'.

claims.claim: CAVE rechallenged with cetuximab and avelumab and found median overall survival 17.3 months where baseline plasma RAS and BRAF were wild-type against 10.4 months where they were mutated (hazard ratio 0.49).
claims.note: CAVE JAMA Oncol 2021: mOS 17.3 vs 10.4 months, HR 0.49.

claims.claim: IMblaze370 confirmed that adding a MEK inhibitor does not change this (overall survival 8.87 against 8.51 months with regorafenib, hazard ratio 1.00).
claims.note: IMblaze370: OS 8.87 vs 8.51 months, HR 1.00.

claims.claim: The most promising current approach is Fc-enhanced CTLA-4 blockade: botensilimab with balstilimab gave an objective response rate of 17 percent (17 of 101 response-evaluable patients among 148 treated) with disease control in 61 percent and median progression-free survival 3.5 months in the phase 1 (Bullock, Nature Medicine 2024), and 21 percent with median overall survival 21.2 months in the 123 patients of the later cohort selected for the absence of liver metastases (Clinical Cancer Research 2026).
claims.note: Bullock Nat Med 2024: 148 treated, 101 evaluable, ORR 17% (17/101), DCR 61%, median PFS 3.5 months; Clin Cancer Res 2026: 123 patients without liver metastases, ORR 21%, median OS 21.2 months.

claims.claim: Liver-limited and oligometastatic disease: Resection with curative intent where all disease can be removed with an adequate remnant; perioperative FOLFOX is the reference, although EORTC 40983 found the progression-free survival gain did not become a survival gain at 8.5 years (61.3 against 54.3 months, hazard ratio 0.88).
claims.note: EORTC 40983 Lancet Oncol 2013: median follow-up 8.5 years; median OS 61.3 vs 54.3 months, HR 0.88 (p=0.34).

claims.claim: Thermal ablation is the only local treatment with randomised survival evidence: CLOCC gave eight-year overall survival of 35.9 against 8.9 percent when radiofrequency ablation was added to systemic treatment.
claims.note: CLOCC JNCI 2017: eight-year OS 35.9% vs 8.9%.

claims.claim: Cetuximab must not be added around liver resection: New EPOC found median overall survival 55.4 against 81.0 months with it.
claims.note: New EPOC Lancet Oncol 2020: median OS 81.0 (chemotherapy alone) vs 55.4 months (with cetuximab).

claims.claim: Peritoneal metastases: Complete cytoreductive surgery in selected patients with a Peritoneal Cancer Index of 25 or less gives a median overall survival above three years, but adding heated intraperitoneal oxaliplatin does not: PRODIGE 7 found 41.7 against 41.2 months with more late grade 3 or worse complications.
claims.note: PRODIGE 7 Lancet Oncol 2021: PCI 25 or less; median OS 41.7 vs 41.2 months; grade 3+ events at 60 days 26% vs 15%.

claims.claim: Circulating tumour DNA after surgery: A tumour-informed assay four to seven weeks after resection is the strongest single predictor of recurrence: GALAXY within CIRCULATE-Japan and DYNAMIC-III both show a large separation (DYNAMIC-III three-year recurrence-free survival 87 percent if negative against 49 percent if positive).
claims.note: DYNAMIC-III Nat Med 2025: 3-year RFS 87% (ctDNA negative) vs 49% (positive).

claims.claim: De-escalation on a negative result is proven only in stage II (DYNAMIC, adjuvant chemotherapy use 15.3 against 27.9 percent with equal recurrence-free survival); in stage III, DYNAMIC-III could not show non-inferiority.
claims.note: DYNAMIC 15.3% vs 27.9% (ITT); DYNAMIC-III de-escalation 'not meeting the non-inferiority margin'.

claims.claim: Escalation on a positive result has failed twice: ALTAIR missed its disease-free survival endpoint (9.30 against 5.55 months, hazard ratio 0.79, p=0.107) and DYNAMIC-III's escalation arm gave no benefit.
claims.note: ALTAIR Nat Med 2026: DFS 9.30 vs 5.55 months, HR 0.79, P = 0.107; DYNAMIC-III escalation 2-year RFS 51% vs 61%.

claims.claim: The failed and stopped programmes: Adjuvant cetuximab (N0147, PETACC-8) gave no benefit and more toxicity; cetuximab around liver resection shortened life (New EPOC, 55.4 against 81.0 months).
claims.note: New EPOC 55.4 vs 81.0 months.

claims.claim: Oxaliplatin HIPEC failed three times (PRODIGE 7, COLOPEC, PROPHYLOCHIP).
claims.note: Three negative trials: PRODIGE 7 (no OS gain), COLOPEC (no gain in peritoneal metastasis-free survival), PROPHYLOCHIP (no DFS gain).

claims.claim: Checkpoint inhibition with a MEK inhibitor failed in microsatellite-stable disease (IMblaze370, hazard ratio 1.00 against regorafenib).
claims.note: IMblaze370 HR 1.00 vs regorafenib.

claims.claim: In access, NICE did not recommend ziv-aflibercept (TA307) despite a positive phase 3 trial.
claims.note: NG151 1.5.12: aflibercept (TA307, 2014) not recommended; VELOUR positive (HR 0.817).

claims.claim: UK access to treatments (NICE, September 2026): Funded in England: cetuximab and panitumumab first line in RAS wild-type disease (TA439); pembrolizumab first line for MSI-high or dMMR disease (TA709) and after chemotherapy where nivolumab with ipilimumab is unsuitable (TA914); nivolumab with ipilimumab first line (TA1065) and after previous treatment (TA716); encorafenib with cetuximab after previous treatment in BRAF V600E disease (TA668); trifluridine-tipiracil (TA405) and with bevacizumab after two lines (TA1008); regorafenib (TA866); fruquintinib at third line or later where trifluridine-tipiracil with bevacizumab is unsuitable (TA1079); bevacizumab with fluoropyrimidine chemotherapy first and second line where targeted treatment or immunotherapy is unsuitable (TA1136); larotrectinib for NTRK fusions, through the Cancer Drugs Fund rather than routine commissioning (TA630).
claims.note: NG151 recommendations list each TA as stated: TA439, TA709, TA914, TA1065, TA716, TA668, TA405, TA1008, TA866, TA1079, TA1136 (1.5.5 first line, 1.5.10 second line), TA630 through the Cancer Drugs Fund.

claims.claim: In CReST, stenting as a bridge to elective surgery relieved obstruction in 82.4 percent and cut stoma formation from 67.9 to 47.5 percent in patients treated with curative intent, with no difference in 30-day mortality, hospital stay, 3-year recurrence or survival.
claims.note: CReST BJS 2022: relief of obstruction 82.4%; stoma 47.5% vs 67.9% in curative intent; no difference in 30-day mortality, stay, 3-year recurrence or mortality.

claims.claim: Diet, weight, alcohol, smoking and physical activity account for the 54 percent of UK cases Cancer Research UK judges preventable.
claims.note: CRUK: 54% preventable.

claims.claim: Referral when symptoms suggest bowel cancer: Offer a quantitative faecal immunochemical test to the symptom groups NICE lists and refer on the suspected cancer pathway at 10 micrograms of haemoglobin per gram of faeces or above; refer a rectal mass without testing first; safety net people who do not return a sample or test below the threshold, and do not let a low result delay referral where clinical concern is strong.
claims.note: NG12 1.3.1-1.3.5: FIT, refer at 10 µg/g or above, safety netting, rectal mass referral.

claims.claim: See a GP for any of these; ask for an urgent GP appointment or use NHS 111 for black or dark red poo or bloody diarrhoea; call 999 or go to A&E for non-stop bleeding from the bottom or large blood clots (NHS)
claims.note: NHS symptoms page as quoted (111, 999 are phone numbers).

claims.claim: In England in 2019, 38 percent of bowel cancers came through an urgent suspected cancer referral, 22 percent after an emergency presentation and 12 percent through screening (Cancer Research UK)
claims.note: CRUK: 38%, 22%, 12% in England 2019.

claims.claim: Staging: computed tomography of the chest, abdomen and pelvis for everyone, plus high-resolution magnetic resonance imaging of the pelvis for every rectal cancer to read the circumferential resection margin and extramural venous invasion (MERCURY 2006)
claims.note: MERCURY BMJ 2006 is the cited source and year; MRI for CRM prediction.

claims.claim: NG151 1.6.1 puts it in follow-up, alongside computed tomography of the chest, abdomen and pelvis for the first three years
claims.note: NG151 1.6.1: follow-up 'for the first 3 years' with CEA and CT chest, abdomen and pelvis.

claims.claim: In the United States 34 percent of cases are localised at diagnosis, 37 percent regional, 23 percent distant and 6 percent unstaged (SEER); in England 47 percent of staged cases in 2022 were stage I or II (Cancer Research UK)
claims.note: SEER 34/37/23/6%; CRUK 47% of staged cases stage I or II in England 2022.

claims.claim: Outcomes differ sharply by race, income and geography, and the gap survives adjustment for stage: five-year bowel cancer survival in England is 55 percent in the most deprived group against 62.9 percent in the least (Cancer Research UK), and emergency presentation, which carries the worst outlook, is concentrated in the same places.
claims.note: CRUK: 55% most deprived vs 62.9% least deprived, England 2018-2022.

claims.claim: Microsatellite-stable disease, 95% of metastatic colorectal cancer, has no working immunotherapy: the phase 3 test of atezolizumab with or without a MEK inhibitor matched regorafenib, and the best signal so far, botensilimab plus balstilimab, comes from single-arm cohorts (17% of 101 response-evaluable patients in the phase 1, Bullock 2024;
claims.note: MSI-H 4-7% of metastatic CRC (ESMO Gastrointest Oncol 2026 review) so about 95% MSS; IMblaze370 matched regorafenib; Bullock 2024 ORR 17% of 101.

claims.claim: 21% of 123 patients selected for the absence of liver metastases in the 2026 report).
claims.note: Clin Cancer Res 2026: 123 patients without active liver metastases, ORR 21%.

claims.claim: KRAS G12D, the commonest colorectal KRAS allele at about 29% of KRAS mutations, and G13D at about 18%, have no approved inhibitor; the only targeted allele, G12C, is about 3% of cases and needs an EGFR antibody alongside it.
claims.note: Record's cBioPortal table: G12D 908/3,169 = 28.7% (crc_msk_2026), G13D 18.0%, G12C 6.9% of KRAS records x ~43% KRAS = about 3% of cases; table spot-checks against the API matched exactly.

claims.claim: POLE-ultramutated tumours, 1% of cases and the most mutated in the disease, are invisible to the mismatch repair immunohistochemistry and MSI tests that every patient gets, so they are found only where sequencing is done.
claims.note: Domingo 2016: pathogenic somatic POLE mutations in 66 (1.0%) of 6,517.

claims.claim: Screening delivers the effect of its uptake, not of its test: 40.4 percent of the Nottingham screening group never returned a kit, and endoscopy capacity and the endoscopist's adenoma detection rate then decide what a positive test is worth.
claims.note: Hardcastle 1996: '30,415 (40.4%) did not complete any test'.

claims.claim: Incidence in adults under 50 is rising by 1.6 to 7.9 percent a year across Europe and the United States, the stage shift screening bought is reversing (60 percent of United States cases advanced in 2019 against 52 percent in the mid-2000s), and the only mechanistic lead is a bacterial toxin signature enriched 3.3-fold in cancers diagnosed before 40.
claims.note: 1.6 to 7.9 percent a year are European figures only (Vuik 2019, Gut: 20 European countries, 7.9% at 20-29, 4.9% at 30-39, 1.6% at 40-49); the US figure is 3% a year at 20-49 (ACS 2026). 60 vs 52 advanced is ACS 2023, correct; colibactin signature 3.3 times more common before 40 than over 70 (Diaz-Gay, Nature 2025), correct.
claims.fixed: Now 'rising by 1.6 to 7.9 percent a year across Europe, depending on age, and by 3 percent a year at 20 to 49 in the United States'.

claims.claim: Circulating tumour DNA identifies who will relapse but has still not been shown to tell anyone what to do about it outside stage II colon cancer: DYNAMIC-III could not prove de-escalation non-inferior in stage III, its escalation arm gave no benefit, and ALTAIR's post-adjuvant trifluridine/tipiracil missed its endpoint while causing grade 3 or higher haematological toxicity in 73 percent.
claims.note: ALTAIR: grade 3 or higher haematologic adverse events 73.0% vs 3.3%; DYNAMIC-III non-inferiority not met; escalation no benefit.

claims.claim: Why adding cetuximab around resection of colorectal liver metastases shortened median survival from 81.0 to 55.4 months in New EPOC has never been explained, and until it is, the safety of any targeted drug in a curative pathway rests on assumption rather than mechanism.
claims.note: New EPOC median OS 81.0 vs 55.4 months.

claims.claim: The HER2 and KRAS G12C combinations approved in the United States on response rate alone have no confirmatory phase 3 result yet (MOUNTAINEER-03 completes December 2027, KRYSTAL-10 is closed but unreported, CodeBreaK 301 completes September 2028) and none is funded in England, so a patient's access to a biomarker-matched treatment now depends more on country than on biology.
claims.note: ClinicalTrials.gov: MOUNTAINEER-03 primary completion 2027-12-31 but study completion 2030-07-03; CodeBreaK 301 primary completion 2028-09-25, study completion 2032-04-25. 'Completes' gave the primary-completion dates as completion.
claims.fixed: Now 'reaches primary completion in December 2027 ... CodeBreaK 301 reaches it in September 2028'.

claims.claim: NordICC found only 42 percent of invited people attended, and the English programme's own standards set an acceptable uptake of 62 percent at ages 60 to 74 with no level yet agreed for the newly invited 50 to 59 group.
claims.note: NordICC 42.0% attended; BCSP standards: uptake acceptable (60-74) 62.0%, '(50-59): to be set'.

claims.claim: They cause about 30 percent of colorectal cancers, bleed rarely so faecal tests find few of them, and are flat and pale enough to be missed at colonoscopy; interval cancers concentrate here.
claims.note: Bettington 2013: approximately 30% via the serrated pathway.

claims.claim: Two identically designed adjuvant trials in 855 colon and 796 rectal cancer patients showed that adding folinic acid to fluorouracil improved seven-year overall survival in colon but not rectal cancer, with different patterns of recurrence (Clinical Colorectal Cancer 2013).
claims.note: Clin Colorectal Cancer 2013: colon n=855, rectal n=796; folinic acid improved 7-year OS in colon (66.8% vs 54.1%) but not rectal; different recurrence patterns.

claims.claim: Within the colon, right-sided (proximal) tumours are more often mismatch-repair deficient, BRAF-mutant, mucinous and worse-prognosis in the metastatic setting, and left-sided tumours respond better to EGFR antibodies; a pooled analysis of 2,879 metastatic patients found no outcome difference between left-sided colon and rectal primaries (European Journal of Cancer 2018).
claims.note: ARCAD Eur J Cancer 2018: 2,879 patients; left-sided colon vs rectal OS HR 0.99, PFS HR 0.92, no difference.

claims.claim: GLOBOCAN counts colon and rectum together (1,926,425 new colorectal cancers in 2022); most colorectal cancers arise in the colon.
claims.note: 1,926,425 is GLOBOCAN 2022 colorectum (site dataset, WORLD code 41) and is dated, so the number is right. But 'GLOBOCAN counts colon and rectum together' is wrong in substance: GLOBOCAN publishes colon (C18) and rectum separately as well as the colorectum total (the fact sheets 8-colon and 9-rectum), and the summary's 'no separate GLOBOCAN figure' contradicted the colorectal page.
claims.fixed: Now 'GLOBOCAN reports the colon and the rectum separately as well as together (1,926,425 new colorectal cancers in 2022)'; summary line changed to 'the colorectal page gives GLOBOCAN's separate colon figures'.

claims.claim: In the Munich registry, 34 percent of ordinary adenocarcinomas were in the proximal colon (J Cancer Res Clin Oncol 2016).
claims.note: Munich registry, J Cancer Res Clin Oncol 2016: 'AC were less frequently localized in the proximal colon (34 %)'.

claims.claim: Total mesorectal excision, described by Heald in 1982, cut local recurrence from a quarter of patients to well under a tenth, and the German CAO/ARO/AIO-94 trial (2004) moved chemoradiation to before surgery, halving local recurrence again.
claims.note: Heald 1982 (BJS) reports only that 50 curative operations had no pelvic or staple-line recurrence at two years; 'from a quarter of patients to well under a tenth' is not in it, and the rectal record linked only Wikipedia and NCCN. CAO/ARO/AIO-94 halving (13% to 6%) is correct (Sauer 2004, a key paper).
claims.fixed: Now 'described by Heald in 1982 (none of his first 50 curative operations had a pelvic or staple-line recurrence at two years), made local recurrence far rarer'; Heald 1982 added to the record's links.

claims.claim: For locally advanced disease the sequence has been rebuilt as total neoadjuvant therapy: RAPIDO (2020) gave one week of radiotherapy then all the chemotherapy before surgery and cut distant failure and doubled complete responses;
claims.note: RAPIDO: pCR 28.4% vs 14.3%; 3-year distant metastases 20.0% vs 26.8% (Clin Transl Radiat Oncol 2026 review quoting Bahadoer 2021; abstract confirms design).

claims.claim: PRODIGE 23 (2021) gave induction mFOLFIRINOX before chemoradiation and improved disease-free and, later, overall survival.
claims.note: PRODIGE 23: DFS HR 0.69; update at 82 months: significant OS benefit (RMST +4.3 months).

claims.claim: OPRA (2022) showed that with chemoradiation followed by consolidation chemotherapy about half of patients could avoid surgery through watch and wait without losing disease control, building on the Habr-Gama series from Sao Paulo.
claims.note: OPRA JCO 2022: 'Organ preservation is achievable in half of the patients'; DFS 76% both arms.

claims.claim: PROSPECT (2023) then showed that intermediate-risk tumours suitable for sphincter-sparing surgery can be treated with FOLFOX alone, with radiotherapy reserved for the 9 percent who do not respond.
claims.note: PROSPECT: 53 (9.1%) of the FOLFOX group received preoperative chemoradiotherapy, given if the tumour shrank by less than 20% OR FOLFOX was stopped for side effects; 'the 9 percent who do not respond' mislabels the group.
claims.fixed: Now 'with chemoradiation before surgery needed by only 9 percent, those whose tumour shrank too little or who had to stop FOLFOX'.

claims.claim: The 5 to 10 percent of rectal cancers that are mismatch-repair deficient respond so completely to PD-1 blockade that surgery and radiotherapy can be omitted: in the Memorial Sloan Kettering study every patient treated with six months of dostarlimab had a clinical complete response (NEJM 2022, expanded 2025), and AZUR-1 is the registration study.
claims.note: Cercek NEJM 2022: 'All 12 patients (100%) had a clinical complete response'; NEJM 2025: 'all 49 patients who completed treatment had a clinical complete response'. Cercek 2022 full text: 'Approximately 5 to 10% of rectal adenocarcinomas are mismatch-repair deficient'.

claims.claim: About a third of colorectal cancers start in the rectum, the last 15 cm of the bowel; because the rectum sits in the narrow pelvis next to the bladder, sexual organs and sphincter, local recurrence, stomas and function matter more than for colon cancer.
claims.note: Rectal record linked only Wikipedia and NCCN; neither page read states 'a third' or '15 cm'. ACS 2026 full text: rectal cancer 'accounted for one in three (32%) CRCs' in the US in 2022. '15 cm' found in no linked source.
claims.fixed: Now 'About a third of colorectal cancers start in the rectum, the last part of the large bowel (32 percent in the United States in 2022, American Cancer Society)'; '15 cm' removed; ACS 2026 added to the record's links.

claims.claim: Intermediate risk, sphincter-sparing surgery planned: Six cycles of FOLFOX with chemoradiation only if the tumour shrinks by less than 20 percent (PROSPECT), then total mesorectal excision.
claims.note: PROSPECT: chemoradiation 'only if the primary tumor decreased in size by <20%'.

claims.claim: In metastatic disease KEYNOTE-177 (2020) showed that pembrolizumab alone doubled progression-free survival against chemotherapy (16.5 versus 8.2 months), with 54.8 percent of patients alive at five years and a median survival of 77.5 months;
claims.note: KEYNOTE-177 NEJM 2020: PFS 16.5 vs 8.2 months; 5-year OS 54.8%, median OS 77.5 months (Annals 2024, read as quoted in Cancer Med 2026, PMC13079066).

claims.claim: CheckMate 8HW (2024) showed that nivolumab plus ipilimumab cut progression by 79 percent against chemotherapy (median progression-free survival 54.1 versus 5.9 months) and beat nivolumab alone, and the combination was approved first line in April 2025.
claims.note: CheckMate 8HW: PFS HR 0.21 vs chemotherapy (79% reduction); median PFS 5.9 months with chemotherapy (ESMO GO 2026 review) and 54.1 months with nivolumab plus ipilimumab (Signal Transduct Target Ther 2025 table); Lancet 2025 beat nivolumab alone (HR 0.62); FDA approval April 8, 2025.

claims.claim: In localised disease four weeks of neoadjuvant nivolumab and ipilimumab produced pathological complete response in 68 percent of colon cancers in NICHE-2 with no recurrence at three years; the ATOMIC phase 3 trial (2025) showed that adding atezolizumab to adjuvant FOLFOX improves disease-free survival in stage III disease; and in rectal cancer six months of dostarlimab produced a clinical complete response in every patient treated, allowing surgery and radiotherapy to be omitted.
claims.note: NICHE-2 pCR 68%, 3-year DFS 100%; ATOMIC 2025 DFS gain; Cercek 2022/2025 every patient completing six months had cCR.

claims.claim: About 15 percent of localised and 5 percent of metastatic colorectal cancers have lost DNA mismatch repair, most often through methylation of the MLH1 gene in right-sided tumours of older women and, in about a fifth, through inherited Lynch syndrome.
claims.note: dMMR in 10-15% of non-metastatic colon cancer (NICHE-2 abstract) and 4-7% of metastatic CRC (ESMO GO 2026); Lynch about 3% of UK bowel cancers (Bowel Cancer UK), about a fifth of 15%.

claims.claim: Lynch syndrome carriers: Colonoscopy every one to two years from age 25 (earlier for MLH1 and MSH2), daily aspirin (CAPP2), cascade germline testing of relatives, hysterectomy and oophorectomy after childbearing for women.
claims.note: NCCN (cited) is not script-readable; the BSG/ACPGBI/UKCGG 2020 guideline (independent primary source) says 'colonoscopy from age 25 years for MLH1 and MSH2 mutation carriers and 35 years for MSH6 and PMS2', 2-yearly. The page had it inverted: MLH1/MSH2 are the earliest starters at 25, not 'earlier' than 25.
claims.fixed: Now 'Colonoscopy every one to two years, from age 25 for MLH1 and MSH2 carriers and from 35 for MSH6 and PMS2 carriers in the UK guideline'; BSG 2020 added to the record's links.

claims.claim: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma is defined by late presentation, a near-universal KRAS mutation (G12D about 40%, G12V about 32%, G12R about 16%, G12C 1 to 2%;
claims.note: No link on the record gave KRAS allele shares. cBioPortal pdac_msk_2024 (read via the cBioPortal API, 2,207 KRAS mutations in 2,188 of 2,336 samples): G12D 889 (40.3%), G12V 709 (32.1%), G12R 354 (16.0%), G12C 28 (1.3%), so the figures hold.
claims.fixed: Added cBioPortal pdac_msk_2024 and Singhi 2019 as links on the record; figures unchanged

claims.claim: 6 to 12% KRAS-wild-type with actionable fusions in NRG1, NTRK, ALK, or BRAF), a desmoplastic stroma that occupies most of the tumour, and an immunologically cold microenvironment.
claims.note: No record link stated the wild-type share. Singhi 2019 abstract: "We found KRAS mutations in 88% of samples" (12% wild-type); cBioPortal pdac_msk_2024: 2,188 of 2,336 samples KRAS-mutant (6.3% wild-type). 6 to 12% holds.
claims.fixed: Added Singhi 2019 and cBioPortal pdac_msk_2024 as links on the record

claims.claim: Surgery is the only cure and only ~20% of patients present resectable; five-year survival remains ~13% overall but exceeds 40% for resected patients who complete adjuvant mFOLFIRINOX.
claims.note: SEER: 5-year relative survival 13.7% (page said ~13%). PRODIGE 24 five-year (Conroy, JAMA Oncol 2022): "5-year overall survival was 43.2% vs 31.4%" in all randomised patients, not only those who completed treatment. "~20% present resectable" has no source on the record (SEER gives 15% localised, a different measure).
claims.fixed: "only ~20% ... resectable" to "only a minority ... resectable"; "~13%" to "~14%"; "resected patients who complete adjuvant mFOLFIRINOX" to "fit resected patients given adjuvant mFOLFIRINOX (43.2% in PRODIGE 24)"; JAMA Oncol 2022 added to links

claims.claim: For thirty years the story was chemotherapy: gemcitabine (1997), FOLFIRINOX (2011), gemcitabine/nab-paclitaxel (2013), adjuvant mFOLFIRINOX (PRODIGE 24, 2018), NALIRIFOX (2024), with olaparib maintenance for germline BRCA carriers (POLO, 2019) and zenocutuzumab for NRG1 fusions (2024) as the only biomarker-directed drugs.
claims.note: Years match the cited trials: Burris 1997 (gemcitabine), Conroy NEJM 2011 (FOLFIRINOX), Von Hoff NEJM 2013 (MPACT), Conroy NEJM 2018 (PRODIGE 24), Golan NEJM 2019 (POLO); NALIRIFOX FDA 2024 and zenocutuzumab FDA 4 Dec 2024 (checked in the treatment rows).

claims.claim: Daraxonrasib, a pan-RAS(ON) inhibitor, nearly doubled overall survival in previously treated metastatic disease in RASolute 302 (13.2 vs 6.7 months, HR 0.40), presented in the ASCO 2026 plenary with simultaneous NEJM publication, and the FDA approved it on 26 August 2026 for metastatic disease after at least one systemic therapy or when multi-agent chemotherapy is unsuitable; no European or UK decision had been made by 24 September 2026.
claims.note: FDA notice: "On August 26, 2026, the Food and Drug Administration approved daraxonrasib ... for adults with metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma who have received at least one prior systemic therapy or who are not candidates for multiagent systemic therapy"; "median OS was 13.2 months ... and 6.7 months ... (Hazard ratio 0.40".

claims.claim: The IARC pancreas fact sheet, served with the GLOBOCAN 2024 estimates, counts 531,318 new pancreatic cancers a year (the 11th commonest cancer, age-standardised rate 4.7 per 100,000) and 490,786 deaths (the 6th commonest cause of cancer death, 4.2 per 100,000).
claims.note: The served fact sheet is headed "GLOBOCAN 2024": Pancreas incidence rank 11, 531 318 cases, ASR 4.7; mortality rank 6, 490 786 deaths, ASR 4.2. The page names the 2024 estimates.

claims.claim: Asia has 45.9 percent of cases, Europe 27.7 percent, Northern America 13.6 percent, Latin America and the Caribbean 7.8 percent, Africa 3.9 percent and Oceania 1.1 percent, and the highest rates are in Western Europe and Northern America, the lowest in South Central Asia.
claims.note: GLOBOCAN 2024 fact sheet, incidence by region: Asia 45.9%, Europe 27.7%, Northern America 13.6%, Latin America and the Caribbean 7.8%, Africa 3.9%, Oceania 1.1%; Western Europe and Northern America top, South Central Asia bottom of the ASR ranking.

claims.claim: Countries with very high human development had the highest incidence and mortality (age-standardised rates 7.7 and 4.9 in 2018), incidence rose in 14 of 48 countries with registry data for men and 17 for women over the decade to 2017, and higher national rates travel with smoking, alcohol, inactivity, obesity, hypertension and high cholesterol (Huang 2021).
claims.note: Huang 2021 abstract: "very high (ASRs, 7.7 and 4.9) ... in 2018"; increases "From 2008 to 2017, 2007 to 2016, or 2003 to 2012, depending on the availability of the data ... in 14 ... and 17 ... countries". The trend windows end between 2012 and 2017, not uniformly "the decade to 2017".
claims.fixed: "over the decade to 2017" to "over the latest decade of data (ending between 2012 and 2017)"

claims.claim: In the United States the SEER programme projects 67,530 new cases (3.2 percent of cancers) and 52,740 deaths (8.4 percent of cancer deaths) for 2026; the rate of new cases is 13.9 per 100,000 a year (2019 to 2023) and the death rate 11.3 (2020 to 2024); it is the third leading cause of cancer death;
claims.note: SEER: "Estimated New Cases in 2026 67,530 ... 3.2% ... Estimated Deaths in 2026 52,740 ... 8.4%"; "13.9 per 100,000 ... 11.3 ... based on 2019–2023 cases and 2020–2024 deaths"; "third leading cause of cancer death".

claims.claim: 113,931 people were living with it in 2023.
claims.note: SEER: "In 2023, there were an estimated 113,931 people living with pancreatic cancer in the United States."

claims.claim: Applying current rates to population growth, pancreatic cancer is projected to become the second leading cause of cancer death in the United States by 2040 (46,000 deaths, behind lung cancer's 63,000), overtaking colorectal cancer (Rahib 2021; the 2014 Rahib projection is in the key papers).
claims.note: Rahib 2021 abstract: "Lung cancer (63 000 deaths) ... with pancreatic cancer (46 000 deaths) ... surpassing colorectal cancer (34 000 deaths) to become the second".

claims.claim: Pancreatic cancer is the 10th commonest cancer with 11,479 new cases a year (2019 and 2021 to 2022), 31 a day and 3 percent of all cancers, about 5,600 in females and 5,800 in males; almost half (48 percent) are diagnosed at 75 or over and rates are highest at 90 and over.
claims.note: CRUK incidence: "10th most common cancer in the UK with around 11,500 new cases every year; that's 31 every day (2019, 2021-2022)"; "3% of all new cancer cases ... around 5,600 ... females and around 5,800 ... males"; "almost half (48%) ... aged 75 and over"; "highest in people aged 90+"; main page "11,479 new cases".

claims.claim: Incidence rates have risen by about a fifth (21 percent) since the early 1990s and by 7 percent in the last decade, and are projected to rise a further 4 percent by 2038 to 2040 with the count reaching about 16,000 a year; rates are lower in the Asian and mixed ethnic groups and higher in the Black ethnic group than in the White group in England (2013 to 2017).
claims.note: CRUK incidence: "increased by around a fifth (21%) ... since the early 1990s ... (7%) in the last decade"; "projected to increase by 4% ... around 16,000 new cases each year by 2038-2040"; ethnicity statement (2013-2017) matches.

claims.claim: It is the 5th commonest cause of cancer death with about 10,200 deaths a year (2022 to 2024), 28 a day, more than half (54 percent) at 75 or over; mortality rates have stayed flat since the early 1970s, and although rates are projected to fall 4 percent, deaths are projected to reach about 12,600 a year by 2038 to 2040 as the population ages.
claims.note: CRUK mortality: "fifth most common cause of cancer death ... around 10,200 deaths every year; that's 28 every day (2022-2024)"; "more than half (54%) ... aged 75 and over"; "stable ... since the early 1970s"; "projected to decrease by 4% ... around 12,600 deaths each year by 2038-2040".

claims.claim: Mortality is 20 percent higher for men and 25 percent higher for women in the most deprived areas of England than the least deprived (2007 to 2011).
claims.note: CRUK mortality: "England-wide data for 2007-2011 show European age-standardised mortality rates are 20% higher for males living in the most deprived areas ... and 25% higher for females."

claims.claim: The lifetime risk of a diagnosis is 1 in 59 for females and 1 in 55 for males born in 1961.
claims.note: CRUK risk page: "lifetime risk ... is 1 in 59 (2%) for females, and 1 in 55 (2%) for males born in 1961 in the UK".

claims.claim: Cancer Research UK's summary page says 37 percent of cases are preventable and its risk page 31 percent; both figures are recorded here.
claims.note: CRUK summary page: "37% of pancreatic cancer cases are preventable"; risk page: "31% of pancreatic cancer cases in the UK are preventable".

claims.claim: In England in 2022, 26 percent of cases with a known stage (around 1,600) were stage I or II;
claims.note: CRUK summary: "In 2022, 26% (around 1,600) of pancreatic cancer cases with a known stage were diagnosed at an early stage (I & II) in England."

claims.claim: Northern Ireland reports 30 percent, Scotland 19 percent (2023) and Wales 19 percent.
claims.note: CRUK summary: Northern Ireland "On average, 30% ... per year between 2015 and 2019"; Scotland "In 2023, 19%"; Wales "On average, 19% ... between 2017 and 2019". Figures match (NI and Wales periods not stated on the page).

claims.claim: Age is the main risk factor: the US median age at diagnosis is 71, 32.7 percent of cases are diagnosed at 65 to 74 and only 3 percent under 45 (SEER 21, 2019 to 2023); the US rate is slightly higher in men (15.7 against 12.4 per 100,000) and highest in non-Hispanic Black men and women (18.0 and 15.4) against 16.3 and 12.3 in non-Hispanic White, 13.6 and 12.1 in Hispanic and 11.5 and 9.8 in Asian and Pacific Islander people.
claims.note: SEER: median age at diagnosis 71; 65–74 32.7%; under 45 0.2+0.8+2.0 = 3.0%; males 15.7, females 12.4; NH Black 18.0/15.4, NH White 16.3/12.3, Hispanic 13.6/12.1, NH Asian/Pacific Islander 11.5/9.8 (SEER 21 2019–2023).

claims.claim: Smoking: current smokers have 2.2 times the risk of never smokers, former smokers 1.2 times, rising to 3.4 times at 35 or more cigarettes a day, and the risk returns to that of never smokers about 20 years after quitting (Bosetti 2012, 6,507 cases in the PanC4 consortium);
claims.note: Bosetti 2012 abstract: "6507 pancreatic cases"; "OR was 1.2 ... for former smokers and 2.2 ... for current"; "OR=3.4 for ≥35 cigarettes per day"; "reaches the level of never smokers ∼20 years after quitting".

claims.claim: 22 percent of UK cases are caused by smoking (Cancer Research UK).
claims.note: CRUK risk page: "22% of pancreatic cancer cases in the UK are caused by smoking."

claims.claim: Body size: obesity (body mass index 30 or more) carries 1.47 times the risk of a normal weight, being overweight in early adulthood and obese later 1.54 times, and a high waist-to-hip ratio 1.35 times, in 846,340 people across 14 cohorts (Genkinger 2011);
claims.note: Genkinger 2011 abstract: 14 cohorts, 846,340 individuals; obese "47% higher" (reference BMI 21-22.9); overweight early and obese at baseline "54% higher"; WHR "MVRR = 1.35".

claims.claim: Cancer Research UK puts 12 percent of UK cases down to overweight and obesity, with a 10 percent rise in risk per 5 units of body mass index.
claims.note: CRUK risk page: "12% of pancreatic cancer cases in the UK are caused by overweight and obesity"; "10% higher per 5-unit body mass index (BMI) increase".

claims.claim: Diabetes: type 2 diabetes carries about 1.8 to 1.9 times the risk (odds ratio 1.82 in 36 studies, Huxley 2005; relative risk 1.94 in 35 cohorts, Ben 2011), and the association is strongest when the diabetes is recent, which is where cause and consequence blur: 47 percent of 512 newly diagnosed patients had diabetes against 7 percent of controls, much of it new-onset and resolving after resection, so the tumour itself is diabetogenic (Pannala 2008).
claims.note: Huxley 2005: "17 case-control and 19 cohort" studies, "summary odds ratio was 1.82"; Ben 2011: "thirty-five cohort studies ... RRs=1.94"; Pannala 2008: 512 cases, "DM was more prevalent (47% vs 7%", often new-onset, "resolves following cancer resection".

claims.claim: Chronic pancreatitis: about 16 times the risk within two years of the pancreatitis diagnosis, falling to about 8 times at five years and 3.5 times at nine years or more, part of the early excess being cancers first misread as pancreatitis (Kirkegard 2017); hereditary pancreatitis with a PRSS1 mutation raises risk more than 50-fold (Cancer Research UK).
claims.note: Kirkegard 2017: "16.16 ... within 2 years", "5 years (EE: 7.90)", "minimum of 9 years (EE: 3.53)" (correct). CRUK risk page: "increased more than 50-fold in people with hereditary pancreatitis"; it does not name PRSS1.
claims.fixed: "hereditary pancreatitis with a PRSS1 mutation" to "hereditary pancreatitis", as CRUK states it

claims.claim: Alcohol at 3 or more units a day raises risk by 15 to 19 percent; gallstones by 25 percent, mostly soon after diagnosis; metabolic syndrome by 58 percent in women; red meat by 21 percent in men (Cancer Research UK risk page).
claims.note: CRUK risk page: "15-19% higher in people who consume 24g or more (3+ units) of alcohol per day"; gallstones "25% higher ... may only be increased shortly after gallstones diagnosis"; metabolic syndrome "58% higher in women"; red meat "21% higher in men".

claims.claim: 531,318 new cases and 490,786 deaths a year worldwide (GLOBOCAN 2024;
claims.note: GLOBOCAN 2024 fact sheet: 531 318 cases (rank 11), 490 786 deaths (rank 6); the sentence names GLOBOCAN 2024.

claims.claim: 11,479 UK cases and about 10,200 UK deaths a year (Cancer Research UK);
67,530 US cases and 52,740 deaths projected for 2026 (SEER).
claims.note: SEER: 67,530 estimated new cases and 52,740 deaths in 2026.

claims.claim: Incidence is rising (21 percent in the UK since the early 1990s) and 45 percent of English cases arrive as emergencies.
claims.note: CRUK incidence: "increased by around a fifth (21%) ... since the early 1990s"; CRUK summary: England 2019 "almost 1 in 2 (45%) via an emergency presentation".

claims.claim: In the United States, 13.7 percent of people diagnosed with pancreatic cancer in 2016 to 2022 were alive five years later relative to people of the same age without the disease (SEER).
claims.note: SEER: "5-Year Relative Survival 13.7% ... Based on data from SEER 21 (Excluding IL) 2016–2022".

claims.claim: Stage at diagnosis is the biggest lever: five-year relative survival is 43.6 percent for the 15 percent found while confined to the pancreas, 17.0 percent for regional disease (28 percent of cases) and 3.4 percent for distant disease (51 percent).
claims.note: SEER stage table: localized 15% / 43.6%, regional 28% / 17.0%, distant 51% / 3.4%.

claims.claim: In the UK, 4.3 percent of people diagnosed in 2018 are predicted to survive ten years or more, against 2.4 percent in the 1970s; ten-year survival is 29.3 percent for women and 17.6 percent for men diagnosed at 15 to 44 but under 2 percent at 75 to 99; five-year survival is 7.6 percent in the most deprived fifth of England and 10.3 percent in the least deprived (2018 to 2022);
claims.note: CRUK survival: "(2.4%) ... in the 1970s ... by 2018 ... (4.3%)"; "(29.3%) females and ... (17.6%) males ... aged 15-44 ... (1.8%) females and ... (1.7%) males diagnosed aged 75-99"; "(7.6%) ... most deprived ... (10.3%) in the least deprived (2018-2022)".

claims.claim: By stage in England, Wales and Northern Ireland (ICBP SURVMARK-2, diagnoses 2012 to 2014): localised disease, almost 55 percent alive at one year and more than 25 percent at three; regional, around 50 and 15 percent; distant, around 10 and 1 percent (Cancer Research UK patient page).
claims.note: CRUK patient survival page (ICBP SURVMARK-2, 2012-2014, England, Wales, NI): localised "almost 55%" 1 year, "more than 25%" 3 years; regional "around 50%" and "around 15%"; distant "around 10%" and "1%".

claims.claim: Screen-detected cancers in high-risk surveillance behave differently: 73.3 percent five-year survival and a median of 9.8 years in the CAPS cohorts (Dbouk 2022).
claims.note: Dbouk 2022: "Five-year survival to date of the patients with a screen-detected PDAC is 73.3%, and median overall survival is 9.8 years".

claims.claim: These figures describe people diagnosed before the RAS inhibitors reported in 2026 and do not reflect them; the resected patients who complete adjuvant chemotherapy in the treatment rows do far better than the averages.
claims.note: The only date is the 2026 RAS inhibitor reports (RASolute 302, FDA notice 26 August 2026); SEER and CRUK survival periods (2016-2022, 2018) predate them.

claims.claim: A first-degree relative with pancreatic cancer raises risk by 62 to 76 percent (Cancer Research UK); in the Johns Hopkins registry, members of familial kindreds (at least one pair of affected first-degree relatives) had 9.0 times the expected incidence, rising to 6.4 times with two and 32 times with three affected first-degree relatives, while spouses and unrelated relatives had no excess (Klein 2004).
claims.note: CRUK risk page: "62-76% higher in people with a first-degree relative". Klein 2004 abstract: FPC kindred members 9.0; "elevated in individuals with three (32.0 ...), two (6.4 ...), or one (4.6 ...) first-degree relative(s)"; spouses no excess. "rising to 6.4 times with two" misread the series as rising from 9.0.
claims.fixed: "9.0 times the expected incidence, rising to 6.4 times with two and 32 times with three" to "9.0 times the expected incidence (4.6 times with one, 6.4 times with two and 32 times with three ...)"

claims.claim: Germline testing of 3,030 unselected patients found a pathogenic variant in one of six genes in 5.5 percent (7.9 percent with a family history of pancreatic cancer, 5.2 percent without): ATM 2.3 percent of cases (odds ratio 5.71), BRCA2 1.9 percent (6.20), BRCA1 0.6 percent (2.58), CDKN2A 0.3 percent (12.33), TP53 0.2 percent (6.70) and MLH1 0.13 percent (6.66) (Hu 2018);
claims.note: Hu 2018 abstract: 3030 patients; CDKN2A 0.3% OR 12.33; TP53 0.2% 6.70; MLH1 0.13% 6.66; BRCA2 1.9% 6.20; ATM 2.3% 5.71; BRCA1 0.6% 2.58; "5.5% of all ... 7.9% ... with a family history ... 5.2% ... without".

claims.claim: 3.9 percent of 854 apparently sporadic resected cancers carried a deleterious germline mutation, and only 3 of those 33 patients had reported a family history (Shindo 2017), which is why guidelines now offer germline testing to every patient.
claims.note: Shindo 2017: "Thirty-three (3.9% ...) of 854 patients ... had a deleterious germline mutation"; "Only three of these 33 patients had reported a family history of pancreatic cancer".

claims.claim: Syndromes: Peutz-Jeghers more than 100 times the risk, familial atypical multiple mole melanoma (CDKN2A) 13 to 38 times, Lynch syndrome up to about 9 times, BRCA2 3.5 times and BRCA1 up to 2.3 times (Cancer Research UK).
claims.note: CRUK risk page: "Peutz-Jeghers syndrome - more than 100 times higher risk; FAMMM - 13-38 times; Lynch - up to around 9 times; BRCA2 - 3.5 times; BRCA1 - up to 2.3 times".

claims.claim: Pancreatic cysts: intraductal papillary mucinous and mucinous cystic neoplasms are precursors, and cysts of 2 mm or more were found on MRCP in 49.1 percent of 1,077 adults in a German population study, though only about 6 percent of cysts were over 1 cm and no cancer arose in five years of follow-up (Kromrey 2018); the cyst pages of this record carry the surveillance rules.
claims.note: Kromrey 2018: 1077 participants, cysts ≥2 mm on MRCP, "weighted prevalence of 49.1%"; "no pancreatic cancer was observed ... during a 5-year follow-up"; "Only about 6% of cysts ... of more than 1 cm".

claims.claim: The pancreas sits deep behind the stomach and the early tumour is silent; roughly 75 percent of cancers start in the head (Cancer Research UK types page), where they block the bile duct and cause painless jaundice, dark urine, pale stools and itching, while body and tail tumours present later with pain in the upper abdomen or back that is worse after eating or lying down and eased by leaning forward, weight loss, loss of appetite, fatty stools (steatorrhoea), nausea, indigestion, new diabetes, fever and blood clots (Cancer Research UK symptoms page;
claims.note: CRUK types page: "Roughly 75 out of 100 pancreatic cancers (roughly 75%) start in the head of the pancreas."

claims.claim: In the SYMPTOM pancreatic study of 391 people referred with suspected pancreatic cancer, 119 (30 percent) had it and 34 percent of those were already metastatic; no first symptom separated cancer from no cancer, but jaundice as a later symptom did (49 percent against 12 percent), and the authors asked clinicians to stay alert to evolving gut and systemic symptoms, particularly in people with diabetes or mental health conditions (Walter 2016).
claims.note: Walter 2016: "391 participants ... 119 (30%) ... diagnosed with pancreatic cancer (41 [34%] had metastatic disease)"; "no initial symptoms were reported more frequently"; "jaundice (51 [49%] of 105 ... vs 25 [12%] of 211"; vigilance "particularly in those with diabetes or mental health comorbidities".

claims.claim: NICE NG12 (1.2.4) sends anyone aged 40 or over with jaundice on the suspected cancer pathway and (1.2.5) asks for an urgent direct-access CT, or ultrasound if CT is unavailable, for anyone 60 or over with weight loss and any of diarrhoea, back pain, abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, constipation or new-onset diabetes; the NHS page asks for an urgent GP appointment or NHS 111 for yellowing of the eyes or skin, vomiting for more than two days or diarrhoea for more than seven.
claims.note: NG12: "1.2.4 Refer people using a suspected cancer pathway referral ... aged 40 and over and have jaundice"; "1.2.5 Consider an urgent, direct access CT scan ... aged 60 and over with weight loss and any of ...". The page said NG12 "asks for" the CT, a stronger word than "Consider". NHS: urgent help if eyes or skin turn yellow, "sick for more than 2 days", "diarrhoea for more than 7 days" (correct).
claims.fixed: "(1.2.5) asks for an urgent direct-access CT" to "(1.2.5) asks clinicians to consider an urgent direct-access CT"

claims.claim: Even so, in England in 2019 only 22 percent of cases were diagnosed through an urgent suspected cancer referral and 45 percent through an emergency presentation (Cancer Research UK), the route that carries substantially lower one-year survival across cancers (Elliss-Brookes 2012); a 2026 US Veterans Affairs measure found 60.9 percent of 4,415 patients presenting as emergencies, with 1.38 times the odds of advanced stage and 1.64 times the mortality, and missed diagnostic opportunities in nearly one in five (Br J Cancer 2026).
claims.note: CRUK summary: England 2019 "more than 1 in 5 (22%) ... urgent suspected cancer ... almost 1 in 2 (45%) via an emergency presentation". Khalaf, Br J Cancer 2026: "Among 4415 ... 60.9% were identified as EPs"; "adjusted OR 1.38"; "adjusted HR 1.64"; "Nearly one in five EP cases had missed opportunities".

claims.claim: In the United States 51 percent of cases are distant at diagnosis, 28 percent regional and 15 percent localised (SEER).
claims.note: SEER stage table: distant 51%, regional 28%, localized 15%.

claims.claim: Weight loss is part of the presentation, not only a complication: 85 percent of patients meet the definition of cancer cachexia (Hendifar 2019) and 40.5 percent of 227 patients scheduled for surgery were already cachectic, which halved their chance of a resection (48.9 against 77.8 percent) because metastases were found more often (Bachmann 2008).
claims.note: Hendifar 2019: "85% of pancreatic cancer patients meet the classic definition of cancer cachexia" (correct). Bachmann 2008: 227 patients, "In 40.5% ... cachexia was already present", "resection rate ... reduced (77.8% vs. 48.9%)". 48.9 against 77.8 is a reduction by about a third, not a halving.
claims.fixed: "which halved their chance of a resection" to "which lowered their chance of a resection"

claims.claim: NICE NG85 (1.1) sets the UK sequence: for obstructive jaundice with suspected pancreatic cancer, a pancreatic protocol CT before the bile duct is drained (1.1.1); if the diagnosis is still unclear, FDG PET-CT and or endoscopic ultrasound with EUS-guided tissue sampling (1.1.2), and a biliary brushing for cytology if ERCP is used to relieve the obstruction without a tissue diagnosis (1.1.3); for pancreatic abnormalities without jaundice, the same CT then PET-CT or EUS (1.1.4 to 1.1.6); for cysts, CT or MRI with MRCP, the other test if more is needed, EUS with fine-needle aspiration and CEA on the fluid when malignancy is in question (1.1.7 to 1.1.13).
claims.note: NG85 1.1.1 to 1.1.13 read in raw text: protocol CT before draining the bile duct (1.1.1); FDG-PET/CT and/or EUS with tissue sampling (1.1.2); biliary brushing if ERCP without tissue diagnosis (1.1.3); no-jaundice sequence 1.1.4 to 1.1.6; cysts CT or MRI/MRCP, the other test, EUS, FNA with CEA (1.1.7 to 1.1.13).

claims.claim: CA 19-9 has a sensitivity of 79 to 81 percent and specificity of 82 to 90 percent in symptomatic patients but a positive predictive value of 0.5 to 0.9 percent as a screening test, is falsely negative in the 5 to 10 percent of people who are Lewis antigen-negative, and levels above 100 U/mL suggest unresectable or metastatic disease (Ballehaninna 2012); in 1,482 Chinese patients 8.4 percent were Lewis-negative and, contrary to the textbook, 27.4 percent of them still had a raised CA 19-9, while Lewis-negative status itself predicted shorter survival (hazard ratio 1.30, Luo 2018).
claims.note: Ballehaninna 2012: "sensitivity and specificity of 79-81% and 82-90%"; "low positive predictive value (0.5-0.9%)"; "Lewis negative phenotype (5-10%)"; "A CA 19-9 serum level of 100 U/mL suggest unresectablity or metastatic disease". Luo 2018: 1482 patients, "8.4% ... Lewis (-)", "elevated (>37 U/mL) in 27.4%", "HR, 1.30".

claims.claim: Stage 1 is T1 or T2 without nodes (1A and 1B by size), stage 2 is T3 without nodes (2A) or T1 to T3 with one to three nodes (2B), stage 3 is four or more nodes or a T4 tumour, and stage 4 is any metastasis (Cancer Research UK stages page).
claims.note: CRUK stage pages: stage 1A T1 N0 M0, 1B T2 N0 M0; stage 3 "4 or more nearby lymph nodes" (T1-3 N2) or T4 any N; stage 4 any T any N M1; TNM page N1 "1 to 3 nearby lymph nodes". Stage 2A/2B grouping follows the same TNM page.

claims.claim: The 8th edition's size-based T and count-based N categories were validated in 2,318 margin-negative resections from three US centres (Allen 2017) and in 8,960 SEER resections, where they discriminated survival about as well as the 7th edition (c-index 0.60 against 0.59) while stratifying resected patients more finely by nodal burden (Kamarajah 2017).
claims.note: Allen 2017: "Two thousand three hundred eighteen patients" (MSK, MGH, JHH, R0 resections). Kamarajah 2017: 8960 SEER resections, "c-index for the AJCC 8th ... [0.60 ...] was comparable with ... 7th (0.59)", "finer stratification ... according to extent of nodal involvement".

claims.claim: The second system is resectability, which is what decides treatment: the NCCN classes of resectable, borderline resectable and locally advanced (unresectable) are defined by the tumour's contact with the superior mesenteric artery, coeliac axis and common hepatic artery (arterial contact of less than 180 degrees without stenosis is borderline; more, or encasement, is locally advanced) and with the superior mesenteric and portal veins (contact with narrowing or occlusion that can be reconstructed is borderline; unreconstructable occlusion is locally advanced), and the 2017 international consensus added a biological dimension (suspected but unproven metastases or nodes on PET-CT or biopsy, or a CA 19-9 above 500 U/mL) and a conditional one (performance status 2 or worse) (Isaji 2018;
claims.note: Isaji 2018: anatomic contact with SMA/coeliac "of less than 180° without showing stenosis"; biological "suspicious for (but unproven) distant metastases or regional lymph nodes metastases diagnosed by biopsy or PET-CT ... CA 19-9 level more than 500 units/ml"; conditional "ECOG performance status of 2 or more".

claims.claim: Staging tests in the UK are a pancreatic protocol CT of chest, abdomen and pelvis for every new diagnosis (NG85 1.3.1), FDG PET-CT for everyone with localised disease on CT who will have treatment (1.3.2), and, when the decision still turns on it, MRI for suspected liver metastases, EUS for tumour and node staging, or laparoscopy with laparoscopic ultrasound for small-volume peritoneal or liver disease before an attempted resection (1.3.3).
claims.note: NG85 1.3.1 protocol CT of chest, abdomen and pelvis; 1.3.2 FDG-PET/CT for localised disease on CT who will have treatment; 1.3.3 MRI for liver metastases, EUS for tumour and node staging, laparoscopy with laparoscopic ultrasound.

claims.claim: About 80 percent of pancreatic cancers are ductal adenocarcinomas (Cancer Research UK types page), the entity this record describes: gland-forming tumours in a dense desmoplastic stroma, with the KRAS, CDKN2A, TP53 and SMAD4 alterations set out in the biomarkers list.
claims.note: CRUK types page: "Around 80 out of 100 pancreatic cancers (around 80%) are ductal adenocarcinomas."

claims.claim: The 2019 WHO classification of digestive tumours (5th edition, Nagtegaal 2020) lists its variants, each with a page linked from this record: adenosquamous carcinoma, colloid (mucinous non-cystic) carcinoma, undifferentiated carcinoma with or without osteoclast-like giant cells, and the carcinomas arising in intraductal papillary mucinous and mucinous cystic neoplasms; acinar cell carcinoma, solid pseudopapillary neoplasm and pancreatoblastoma are separate non-ductal tumours, and the neuroendocrine tumours of the islets are a different disease with their own record.
claims.note: Nagtegaal, Histopathology 2020 is the summary of the 2019 WHO Classification of Tumours of the Digestive System (5th edition); the only figures are the edition and year.

claims.claim: Precursors: pancreatic intraepithelial neoplasia (PanIN), the microscopic duct lesion named and graded in 2001 (Hruban 2001) and reduced to two tiers, low grade and high grade, by the 2015 Baltimore consensus, which also set 0.5 to 1 cm as the boundary between a large PanIN and a small (incipient) IPMN (Basturk 2015); high-grade PanIN was present in 4 percent of 173 autopsy pancreata without cancer, always multifocal and more often in the body and tail, in people with diabetes and in the old (Matsuda 2017).
claims.note: Hruban 2001 PanIN nomenclature (Am J Surg Pathol 2001). Basturk 2015: "a 2-tiered system (low vs. high grade)"; "Intraductal lesions 0.5 to 1 cm can be either large PanINs or small IPMNs". Matsuda 2017: 173 autopsy cases, "PanIN-3 was found in 4%", "always multifocal", "more frequently in the pancreatic body and tail", "diabetes mellitus and/or older age".

claims.claim: Margins are reported by the 1 mm rule: the Royal College of Pathologists calls tumour within 1 mm of a margin R1, a definition that, applied with inked margins and axial slicing, raised the reported R1 rate to 76 to 85 percent of head resections (Verbeke 2006;
claims.note: Verbeke 2006: R1 = tumour within 1 mm; standardised protocol R1 "for pancreatic (22 of 26 85 per cent)". Esposito 2008: "The R1 rate for resections carried out with the standardized protocol was 76%". Campbell 2009: 128 of 163 (79%) R1. The 76 to 85 percent range holds.

claims.claim: Campbell 2009), and in the ESPAC-3 trial 43.9 percent of 1,151 patients were R1, with direct margin involvement carrying the worst survival and more local recurrence (Ghaneh 2019).
claims.note: Ghaneh 2019 (ESPAC-3): "There were 1151 patients, of whom 505 (43.9%) had an R1 resection"; "R1-direct resections were associated with significantly reduced overall and recurrence-free survival"; "increased risk for local recurrence".

claims.claim: There is no population screening: the UK National Screening Committee does not recommend it and Cancer Research UK explains why (the cancer is relatively uncommon, so many people would have unnecessary tests, and the benefits do not outweigh the costs), and the US Preventive Services Task Force reaffirmed a grade D recommendation against screening asymptomatic adults in 2019 (Owens 2019).
claims.note: Owens 2019 (USPSTF reaffirmation, JAMA 2019): "The USPSTF recommends against screening for pancreatic cancer in asymptomatic adults. (D recommendation)."

claims.claim: NICE NG85 offers it (1.1.15) to people with hereditary pancreatitis and a PRSS1 mutation, to carriers of BRCA1, BRCA2, PALB2 or CDKN2A with one or more first-degree relatives with pancreatic cancer, and to Peutz-Jeghers syndrome, and asks clinicians to consider it (1.1.16) for two or more first-degree relatives across two generations and for Lynch syndrome with an affected first-degree relative, by MRI with MRCP or EUS (1.1.17), or by pancreatic protocol CT in hereditary pancreatitis where EUS is not used (1.1.18, 1.1.19).
claims.note: NG85 1.1.15 offer surveillance: hereditary pancreatitis and PRSS1; BRCA1, BRCA2, PALB2 or CDKN2A with 1 or more first-degree relatives; Peutz-Jeghers. 1.1.16 consider: 2 or more first-degree relatives across 2 or more generations; Lynch with any first-degree relative. 1.1.17 MRI/MRCP or EUS; 1.1.18 protocol CT in hereditary pancreatitis; 1.1.19 no EUS in hereditary pancreatitis.

claims.claim: The International CAPS consortium (2020) sets the goal as high-grade dysplasia and T1N0M0 cancer, starts familial surveillance at 50 or 55 or ten years before the youngest affected relative, uses EUS and MRI/MRCP yearly, and added ATM carriers with one affected relative (Goggins 2020).
claims.note: Goggins 2020: goals "high-grade dysplastic precursor lesions and T1N0M0 pancreatic cancer"; start "no earlier than age 50 or 10 years earlier than the youngest relative ... split on whether to start at age 50 or 55"; ATM carriers with one affected first-degree relative eligible; EUS and MRI/MRCP; annual surveillance.

claims.claim: The programmes: in CAPS, 7 percent of 354 high-risk people progressed over 16 years, 1.6 percent a year, and 93 percent had worrisome features first (Canto 2018); in CAPS5, 1,461 people were enrolled, 7 of 9 cancers found under surveillance were stage I (77.8 percent), and across CAPS1 to 5 (1,731 people) 57.9 percent of the 19 surveillance-detected cancers were stage I against 85.7 percent stage IV for the seven found outside surveillance, with five-year survival of 73.3 percent and a median of 9.8 years for screen-detected disease (Dbouk 2022); in the Netherlands the cumulative incidence was 9.3 percent in mutation carriers and 0 percent in mutation-negative familial kindreds over an average of 63 months, with EUS outperforming MRI and four of ten cancers presenting between visits (Overbeek 2022); in 347 CDKN2A carriers 8.9 percent developed cancer (20.7 percent by age 70), 83.3 percent resectable at imaging and 33.3 percent stage I, with five-year survival of 32.4 percent (Klatte 2022).
claims.note: Canto 2018: 354 individuals, "24 of 354 patients (7%) ... over a 16-year period; ... 1.6%/year, and 93% had detectable lesions with worrisome features". Dbouk 2022: 1,461 in CAPS5, 7 of 9 (77.8%) stage I; CAPS1-5 1,731, 19 within surveillance 57.9% stage I, 6 of 7 (85.7%) outside stage IV, 73.3% five-year, 9.8 years. Overbeek 2022: 9.3% carriers, 0% FPC, 63 months, four interval cancers of ten, EUS outperformed MRI. Klatte 2022: 347 carriers, 31 (8.9%), 20.7% by 70, 83.3% resectable, 33.3% stage I, 32.4% five-year.

claims.claim: EUROPAC, the European Registry of Hereditary Pancreatitis and Familial Pancreatic Cancer based in Liverpool, screened 321 people from 258 kindreds and found one cancer, two low-grade neuroendocrine tumours and 41 cystic lesions, the branch-duct IPMNs being unrelated to inherited risk (Sheel 2019).
claims.note: Sheel 2019: "321 individuals from 258 kindreds ... One PDAC, two low-grade neuroendocrine tumours and 41 cystic lesions"; "The risk of finding BD-IPMN was independent of genetic predisposition".

claims.claim: PRECEDE (Pancreatic Cancer Early Detection consortium) published its recommendations for an organised approach in 2021 (Gonda 2021) and its 20,000-person registry study has a trial record on this site.
claims.note: Gonda 2021 (Gastroenterology) is the PRECEDE recommendations paper. ClinicalTrials.gov API for NCT04970056 (the precede trial record): enrollment 20000, type ESTIMATED, recruiting; the registry size is a target.

claims.claim: New-onset diabetes after 50 is the other route: about 1 percent are diagnosed with pancreatic cancer within three years (Chari 2005), the ENDPAC score (weight change, glucose change, age) picks out a group with 3.6 percent prevalence (Sharma 2018), and in over a fifth of cancers the diabetes began while the cancer was still asymptomatic, a median of 6.5 months before diagnosis (Aggarwal 2012); the glossary term and the ideas linked from this record carry the detail.
claims.note: Chari 2005: "Approximately 1% of diabetes subjects aged > or =50 years will be diagnosed with pancreatic cancer within 3 years". Sharma 2018: weight change, glucose change, age; "prevalence of PC in patients with a score of at least 3 (3.6%)". Aggarwal 2012: "In over a fifth of PaC, the onset of DM occurs when the cancer is asymptomatic"; "median duration of DM prior to PaC diagnosis was 6.5".

claims.claim: RASolute 302 (2026): first targeted therapy to nearly double survival in pancreatic cancer; daraxonrasib approved by the FDA on 26 August 2026 for previously treated metastatic disease.
claims.note: FDA notice: approval on August 26, 2026 for metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma after at least one prior systemic therapy; RASolute 302 overall population median OS 13.2 against 6.7 months, HR 0.40 ("nearly double" holds).

claims.claim: G12D-selective zoldonrasib combinations with 50% response rates in previously treated disease.
claims.note: OncLive report of ESMO GI 2026 (linked from the zoldonrasib record in this record's pipeline): second-line zoldonrasib plus daraxonrasib (n = 30) "the ORR was 50%"; third line and beyond "47% ORR". The card has no link of its own.

claims.claim: Adjuvant mFOLFIRINOX gives median OS beyond 4 years in resected fit patients.
claims.note: PRODIGE 24: median OS 54.4 months (NEJM 2018) and 53.5 months at five years (Conroy, JAMA Oncol 2022), both beyond 4 years.

claims.claim: High-risk surveillance shifts ~3 in 4 detected cancers to stage I in carriers.
claims.note: Dbouk 2022 (CAPS5): 1,461 high-risk individuals, of whom 48.5% carried a pathogenic variant; "seven (77.8%) had a stage I PDAC"; across CAPS1-5, 57.9% of 19 surveillance-detected cancers stage I. The ~3 in 4 figure is the 9-case CAPS5 series of all high-risk people, not carriers.
claims.fixed: "shifts ~3 in 4 detected cancers to stage I in carriers" to "found 7 of 9 cancers at stage I in the CAPS5 cohort (57.9% across all CAPS studies)"

claims.claim: Personalised mRNA vaccine responders remain recurrence-free for years (autogene cevumeran phase 1).
claims.note: Sethna, Nature 2025: at 3.2-year median follow-up responders (n = 8) had RFS "median not reached" against 13.4 months, but "Two responders recurred". "Remain recurrence-free for years" overstated it for all responders.
claims.fixed: Reworded to "mostly remain recurrence-free at a median 3.2 years of follow-up (autogene cevumeran phase 1; 2 of 8 responders recurred)"

claims.claim: KRAS mutation in 88 to 94% (G12D about 40%, G12V about 32%, G12R about 16%, Q61 about 7%, G12C 1 to 2%), TP53 66 to 76%, CDKN2A loss 37 to 48%, SMAD4 loss 17 to 33%; the 6 to 12% of KRAS wild-type tumours carry the fusions and alternative drivers instead, and 4 to 10% of patients carry a germline susceptibility variant.
