claims.note: EORTC 22961: 5-year mortality 19.0% vs 15.2%, HR 1.42 (correct). RTOG 92-02 (Horwitz 2008): LTAD 'superior to STAD for all end points except survival' (OS 51.6% v 53.9%, P=.36); Gleason 8-10 OS 45.1% v 31.9%. Page said 'on every endpoint'. DART: high-dose RT, long ADT better (correct).
claims.fixed: 'on every endpoint' -> 'on every endpoint except overall survival'.

claims.claim: A low-dose-rate brachytherapy boost doubles freedom from biochemical failure at 9 years (83 against 62 percent, ASCENDE-RT) without a survival difference.
claims.note: ASCENDE-RT: 9-year b-PFS 83% LDR boost vs 62% DE-EBRT; 'twice as likely to be free of biochemical failure'; 'no significant overall survival difference'.

claims.claim: Adding abiraterone for two years improved 6-year metastasis-free survival from 69 to 82 percent in the STAMPEDE non-metastatic comparison; adding docetaxel improved 4-year overall survival from 89 to 93 percent in RTOG 0521.
claims.note: STAMPEDE M0 meta-analysis (Attard 2022): 6-year MFS 82% vs 69%. RTOG 0521: 4-year OS 89% vs 93%.

claims.claim: RADICALS-RT (1,396 men), RAVES (333) and GETUG-AFU 17 (424) all found the same, and the prospectively planned ARTISTIC meta-analysis of all 2,153 gave an event-free survival hazard ratio of 0.95 (95 percent confidence interval 0.75 to 1.21), a 1 percentage point difference at 5 years.
claims.note: RADICALS-RT 1396 randomised; RAVES 333; GETUG-AFU 17 424; ARTISTIC: 2153 patients, 'HR 0.95, 95% CI 0.75-1.21 ... only a 1 percentage point ... change in 5-year event-free survival'.

claims.claim: The gain is in what is avoided: only 33 percent of the RADICALS-RT observation group needed radiotherapy within 8 years, and adjuvant treatment caused more incontinence at 1 year and more grade 3 to 4 urethral stricture (6 against 4 percent).
claims.note: RADICALS-RT: '228 (33%) of 699 in the salvage radiotherapy group reported radiotherapy within 8 years'; incontinence worse at 1 year; 'Grade 3-4 urethral stricture within 2 years ... 6% ... versus 4%'.

claims.claim: GETUG-AFU 17 measured the same harm larger: late grade 2 or worse genitourinary toxicity 27 against 7 percent and erectile dysfunction 28 against 8 percent.
claims.note: GETUG-AFU 17: late GU grade 2+ 27% vs 7%; late ED grade 2+ 28% vs 8%.

claims.claim: When salvage radiotherapy is given, add androgen deprivation: GETUG-AFU 16 raised 120-month progression-free survival from 49 to 64 percent with 6 months of goserelin, SPPORT raised 5-year freedom from progression from 70.9 to 81.3 percent by adding short-term androgen deprivation and to 87.4 percent by adding pelvic nodal radiotherapy as well, and RADICALS-HD found 24 months better than 6 (10-year metastasis-free survival 78.1 against 71.9 percent) at the cost of more grade 3 toxicity (19 against 14 percent).
claims.note: GETUG-AFU 16: 120-month PFS 64% vs 49% with goserelin. SPPORT: 5-year FFP 70.9%, 81.3%, 87.4%. RADICALS-HD: 10-year MFS 78.1% vs 71.9%; grade 3+ toxicity 19% vs 14%.

claims.claim: Docetaxel: CHAARTED found median overall survival 57.6 against 44.0 months (hazard ratio 0.61) with the benefit concentrated in high-volume disease, and the STAMPEDE docetaxel comparison agreed;
claims.note: CHAARTED: median OS 57.6 vs 44.0 months, HR 0.61.

claims.claim: GETUG-AFU 15, with 385 men, was the underpowered exception.
claims.note: GETUG-AFU 15: 192 + 193 = 385 randomised; OS HR 1.01.

claims.claim: Androgen receptor pathway inhibitors: abiraterone in LATITUDE and STAMPEDE (hazard ratio for death 0.63 in STAMPEDE's 1,917 men), apalutamide in TITAN (24-month overall survival 82.4 against 73.5 percent, hazard ratio 0.67), enzalutamide in ARCHES and ENZAMET, darolutamide in ARANOTE.
claims.note: STAMPEDE abiraterone (James 2017): 1917 patients, HR for death 0.63 (whole trial, which included 48% non-metastatic men; metastatic HR 0.61). TITAN: 24-month OS 82.4% vs 73.5%, HR 0.67.

claims.claim: Castration itself can be delivered orally with relugolix (NICE TA995) or, in trials, by transdermal oestradiol patches, which give fewer hot flushes (35 against 86 percent) and better bone density with no excess cardiovascular events.
claims.note: PATCH (Lancet 2021): hot flushes 86% LHRHa vs 35% tE2; no difference in time to first cardiovascular event. Clin Oncol 2024: lumbar spine BMD -3.0% LHRHa vs +7.9% tE2.

claims.claim: Continuous, not intermittent: SWOG 9346 could not exclude a 20 percent higher risk of death with treatment breaks.
claims.note: SWOG 9346: 'we cannot rule out a 20% greater risk of death with intermittent therapy'.

claims.claim: Hormone-relapsed non-metastatic prostate cancer with a fast-rising PSA: Apalutamide or darolutamide added to continuing androgen deprivation, for men whose PSA doubling time is 10 months or less.
claims.note: SPARTAN eligibility: 'a prostate-specific antigen doubling time of 10 months or less'.

claims.claim: SPARTAN (1,207 men) found median metastasis-free survival 40.5 against 16.2 months with apalutamide (hazard ratio 0.28), and PROSPER and ARAMIS found the same size of effect with enzalutamide and darolutamide.
claims.note: SPARTAN: 1207 men, MFS 40.5 vs 16.2 months, HR 0.28 (correct). PROSPER HR 0.29 but ARAMIS HR 0.41 (MFS 40.4 vs 18.4), so 'the same size of effect' overstated ARAMIS.
claims.fixed: 'found the same size of effect' -> 'PROSPER (hazard ratio 0.29) and ARAMIS (0.41) found similar benefits'.

claims.claim: The cost is measurable: in SPARTAN, rash 23.8 against 5.5 percent, hypothyroidism 8.1 against 2.0 percent and fracture 11.7 against 6.5 percent.
claims.note: SPARTAN: 'rash (23.8% vs. 5.5%), hypothyroidism (8.1% vs. 2.0%), and fracture (11.7% vs. 6.5%)'.

claims.claim: COU-AA-301, AFFIRM after docetaxel); docetaxel with prednisone (TAX 327, median survival 18.9 against 16.5 months against mitoxantrone, with pain relief in 35 against 22 percent); cabazitaxel after docetaxel (TROPIC, 15.1 against 12.7 months;
claims.note: TAX 327: median survival 18.9 (3-weekly docetaxel) vs 16.5 months; pain reduction 35% vs 22%. TROPIC: 15.1 vs 12.7 months.

claims.claim: PROSELICA showed 20 mg/m2 is non-inferior to 25 with grade 3 or 4 events in 39.7 against 54.5 percent;
claims.note: PROSELICA: non-inferiority met; grade 3 or 4 TEAEs 39.7% (C20) vs 54.5% (C25).

claims.claim: FIRSTANA was negative, finding neither cabazitaxel dose superior to docetaxel first line at 24.5, 25.2 and 24.3 months, which is why cabazitaxel is given after docetaxel rather than instead of it); olaparib for BRCA-mutated disease after a newer hormonal treatment (NICE TA887;
claims.note: FIRSTANA: median OS 24.5 (C20), 25.2 (C25), 24.3 months (D75); no superiority.

claims.claim: TRITON3 shows the effect is BRCA-dependent and absent in ATM-altered disease); lutetium-177 PSMA radioligand therapy (VISION, TheraP, PSMAfore, but NICE TA930 does not recommend it in England); radium-223 for symptomatic bone-predominant disease without visceral metastases (ALSYMPCA, NICE TA412, only after or instead of docetaxel), now with an overall survival benefit in combination with enzalutamide when bone-protecting agents are given (PEACE-3, 38.2 against 32.6 months).
claims.note: TRITON3: BRCA subgroup HR 0.50; exploratory ATM subgroup rPFS HR 0.95 (0.59-1.52). PEACE-3 final OS: 38.2 vs 32.6 months, HR 0.76; BPA co-administration required.

claims.claim: The one hard sequencing rule comes from CARD: after rapid failure of one androgen receptor pathway inhibitor, cabazitaxel beats switching to the other (imaging-based progression-free survival 8.0 against 3.7 months, overall survival 13.6 against 11.0 months).
claims.note: CARD: median imaging-based PFS 8.0 vs 3.7 months; median OS 13.6 vs 11.0 months.

claims.claim: Combinations and strategies that were tested and abandoned: Checkpoint inhibitors in unselected men do not work: IMbassador250, KEYNOTE-641, KEYNOTE-921, KEYNOTE-991 and CA184-043 between them randomised more than 5,000 men and none improved survival.
claims.note: Randomised: IMbassador250 759, KEYNOTE-921 1030, KEYNOTE-641 1244, KEYNOTE-991 1251, CA184-043 799 = 5083; none met an OS endpoint.

claims.claim: Anti-angiogenic drugs do not work: CALGB 90401 with bevacizumab and COMET-1 with cabozantinib both improved progression endpoints and neither improved survival, and bevacizumab quadrupled treatment-related deaths (4.0 against 1.2 percent).
claims.note: CALGB 90401: PFS improved, OS not; 'treatment-related deaths (4.0% v 1.2%)', a 3.3-fold rise, not quadrupled. COMET-1: rPFS improved, OS not.
claims.fixed: 'quadrupled' -> 'more than tripled'.

claims.claim: Radium-223 must not be combined with abiraterone without bone protection: ERA 223 found fractures in 29 against 11 percent and no benefit.
claims.note: ERA 223: 'Fractures (any grade) occurred in 112 (29%) ... radium-223 ... and 45 (11%) ... placebo'; SSE-free survival HR 1.122, no benefit.

claims.claim: Two drugs improved radiographic progression-free survival substantially and did nothing for survival, orteronel in ELM-PC 4 and tasquinimod in 10TASQ10, which is why an imaging endpoint alone is not accepted here.
claims.note: ELM-PC 4: rPFS 13.8 vs 8.7 months (HR 0.71), OS HR 0.92 p=0.31. 10TASQ10: rPFS HR 0.64, OS HR 1.10.

claims.claim: Prostate cancer is the most common cancer in men in most high-income countries and a spectrum: most PSA-detected disease is indolent and safely watched (ProtecT: ~3% prostate-cancer mortality at 15 years whatever the strategy), while de novo metastatic disease, treated with hormonal doublets and triplets and since 2026 with radioligand therapy added, has a median overall survival of about five years in the trial populations behind those regimens, which means half of those men lived longer; it is the second most common cause of cancer death in men.
claims.note: ProtecT ~3% PCSM at 15 years correct (Hamdy 2023: 3.1/2.2/2.9%). Median OS about five years broadly supported (ARASENS: 62.7% alive at 4 years on darolutamide triplet). But 'it is the second most common cause of cancer death in men' was stated without geography: CRUK: 'Prostate cancer is the 2nd most common cause of cancer death in males the UK'; the cited Wikipedia line rests on outdated 1.2 million/350,000 figures, and worldwide (GLOBOCAN) prostate ranks lower for deaths.
claims.fixed: Scoped the death ranking to the UK: 'in the UK it is the second most common cause of cancer death in men'.

claims.claim: Digital-pathology AI (ArteraAI Prostate, 2025) and gene-expression classifiers (Decipher) refine who needs treatment and who benefits from adding hormone therapy.
claims.note: openFDA device record: 'ArteraAI Prostate DEN240068 decision_date 2025-07-31 DENG' (De Novo granted 2025). Artera site: 'The US FDA has granted De Novo marketing authorization for ArteraAI Prostate'.

claims.claim: Treatment is built on androgen deprivation, the first targeted cancer therapy (Huggins, 1941).
claims.note: Huggins and Hodges, Cancer Research 1941 (record paper-huggins-hodges-castration-serum-phosphatases-prostate-1941; Europe PMC indexes no abstract, only the 1972 reprint). Year matches the record's journal year.

claims.claim: Metastatic hormone-sensitive disease is treated with doublets (ADT + abiraterone, enzalutamide, apalutamide or darolutamide) or triplets adding docetaxel (ARASENS, PEACE-1), and since 31 July 2026 with 177Lu-PSMA-617 added to ADT + ARPI (PSMAddition, rPFS HR 0.72).
claims.note: FDA: 'On July 31, 2026, the Food and Drug Administration approved lutetium Lu 177 vipivotide tetraxetan ... in combination with androgen receptor pathway inhibitor (ARPI) therapy'; 'hazard ratio 0.72 [95% CI: 0.58, 0.90]'.

claims.claim: PTEN-deficient disease gained capivasertib + abiraterone in 2026.
claims.note: TRUQAP label (DailyMed, revised 06/2026): 'Indications and Usage (1.2) 06/2026'; 'in combination with abiraterone and prednisone ... prostate cancer that is PTEN-deficient'.

claims.claim: Competing 177Lu-PSMA-I&T products (SPLASH, ECLIPSE) have improved progression but not yet survival; alpha-emitting 225Ac-PSMA agents are in phase 3 (AlphaBreak, AcTION) and produce responses after lutetium failure.
claims.note: ClinicalTrials.gov: AlphaBreak NCT06402331 'phases: PHASE2' (the corpus record itself says phase 2); AcTION NCT04597411 'PHASE1'. Novartis' 225Ac-PSMA-617 randomised trial is PSMAcTION NCT06780670, PHASE2/PHASE3. Neither named trial is phase 3.
claims.fixed: 'in phase 3 (AlphaBreak, AcTION)' -> 'in phase 2 (AlphaBreak) and phase 2/3 (PSMAcTION) trials after phase 1 work (AcTION)'.

claims.claim: ~1.5 million new cases per year worldwide; lifetime risk ~1 in 8 men in high-income countries; median age at diagnosis 67; most PSA-detected disease is indolent and safely watched. ~400,000 deaths per year worldwide, mostly from disease that was already metastatic at diagnosis.
claims.note: GLOBOCAN 2022 (repo copy of GCO 2022, WORLD): prostate 1,467,854 cases, 397,430 deaths, presented undated as 'per year'. SEER: 'Approximately 13.2 percent of men' (US) and 'Median Age At Diagnosis 68' (page said 67); CRUK: lifetime risk 17% UK, so '~1 in 8 in high-income countries' over-generalised. 'mostly from disease that was already metastatic at diagnosis' is stated by no source on the record.
claims.fixed: Dated both GLOBOCAN figures to 2022; lifetime risk given as about 13 percent (1 in 8) in the US and 17 percent in the UK; median age corrected to 68 (US); unsourced 'mostly metastatic at diagnosis' clause removed.

claims.claim: Triplet therapy (ADT + ARPI + docetaxel) for high-volume de novo disease, with OS HR ~0.7 (ARASENS, PEACE-1).
claims.note: ARASENS OS HR 0.68; PEACE-1 docetaxel population OS HR 0.75 (overall 0.82): '~0.7' fair.

claims.claim: Genotype-directed doublets: PARP inhibitor + ARPI for HRR-mutant (OS benefit in TALAPRO-2) and capivasertib + abiraterone for PTEN-deficient disease (2026).
claims.note: Capivasertib + abiraterone PTEN-deficient indication added to the TRUQAP label 06/2026.

claims.claim: The androgen receptor is reactivated by five different routes and most men with castration-resistant disease have more than one: amplification of the gene in about half of castration-resistant cohorts against 1% of untreated primaries, amplification of an enhancer 624 kb upstream in 81% of deeply sequenced metastases, ligand-binding-domain mutation in 13.7 to 18.0%, the AR-V7 splice variant, and raised receptor expression with no genomic change at all.
claims.note: Quigley 2018: 'amplification of an intergenic enhancer region 624 kb upstream of the androgen receptor (AR) in 81% of patients'. cBioPortal API re-run: AR amplification prad_su2c_2019 217/444 = 48.9%, prad_tcga_pan_can_atlas_2018 5/489 = 1.0%.

claims.claim: TP53 runs from 3.4% in localised whole genomes to 41% at rapid autopsy, AR amplification from 1.0% to 57%, PTEN deletion from 12% to 41%.
claims.note: cBioPortal API re-run: TP53 mutation prad_cpcg_2017 16/477 = 3.4%, prad_mich (rapid autopsy) 25/61 = 41.0%; AR amplification TCGA 1.0%, prad_fhcrc 85/149 = 57.0%; PTEN deep deletion prad_mskcc_2017 12.3% / prad_p1000 12.2%, prad_mich 41.0%.

claims.claim: DNA repair is the one axis that changes both treatment and a family's future: inherited mutations in 11.8% of 692 men with metastatic disease, led by BRCA2 at 5.3%, with no difference by family history or age, which is why germline testing is offered to everyone with metastatic disease.
claims.note: Pritchard 2016: 'identified in 82 men (11.8%) ... BRCA2 (37 men [5.3%])'; 'Mutation frequencies did not differ according to whether a family history ... or according to age at diagnosis'.

claims.claim: The four PARP inhibitor routes ask for four different gene lists, from BRCA2 alone to a 14-gene panel, and the response evidence does not spread evenly across them: in PROfound, confirmed response was 56% with BRCA2, 10% with ATM and 6% with CDK12.
claims.note: Lynparza label table 27: single mutation BRCA2 43, 24 (56); ATM 30, 3 (10); CDK12 34, 2 (6). Label gene list for mCRPC monotherapy has 14 genes.

claims.claim: Mismatch repair deficiency is present in 3.1% of prostate cancers and is the only setting in this disease where checkpoint blockade gives durable responses; one carrier in five also has Lynch syndrome, and in prostate the gene is usually broken by a complex MSH2 or MSH6 rearrangement rather than by MLH1 methylation.
claims.note: Abida 2019: '32 (3.1%) had MSI-H/dMMR'; 'Seven of the 32 ... (21.9%) had a pathogenic germline mutation in a Lynch syndrome-associated gene'. Pritchard 2014: 'frequently complex MSH2 or MSH6 structural rearrangements rather than MLH1 epigenetic silencing'.

claims.claim: PSMA PET replaced CT and bone scan on accuracy, 92% against 65% in a randomised comparison, and it is the entry ticket for radioligand therapy, but about three men in ten screened for that treatment are ineligible because parts of their tumour no longer express the target.
claims.note: proPSMA: '92% [88-95] vs 65% [60-69]' correct. 'About three men in ten screened for that treatment are ineligible' generalises TheraP (291 screened, 200 eligible on PSMA plus FDG criteria = 31% ineligible); VISION's PSMA-only screen excluded 12.6%.
claims.fixed: Attributed to TheraP: 'in the TheraP trial about three men in ten screened were ineligible on PSMA and FDG PET criteria'.

claims.claim: Plasma works better here than in most cancers because the metastases are in bone: tumour DNA is detectable in 94% of men with advanced disease, BRCA concordance with tissue is 93%, and plasma sees the polyclonal androgen receptor and reversion events one biopsy cannot.
claims.note: Tukachinsky 2021: '3,129 patients (94%) had detectable ctDNA'; '72 of 837 ... BRCA1/2 mutations detected in tissue, 67 (93%) of which were also identified using ctDNA'.

claims.claim: Screening: Shared-decision PSA testing from 50 (45 if Black or family history/BRCA), risk-adapted intervals;
claims.note: No ref on the row (psa, mp-mri, precision-mri, germline-testing, erspc, plco-prostate) states starting ages. EAU guideline (read): 'early testing with PSA can be recommended starting at the age of 50 ... family history ... African descent ... 45 years ... BRCA2 mutations ... 40 years'. Page put BRCA at 45.
claims.fixed: Ages corrected to the EAU guideline (50; 45 for African descent or family history; 40 for BRCA2 carriers) and the EAU chapter added as the row's guideline link.

claims.claim: The decision is shared because the two large trials disagreed: ERSPC found fewer prostate cancer deaths with screening, while the prostate component of PLCO found a rate ratio of 1.13 (0.75 to 1.70), not significant, in a trial where PSA testing in the control group rose from 40 to 52 percent and so compared screening with screening.
claims.note: PLCO 2009: 'rate ratio, 1.13; 95% CI, 0.75 to 1.70'; 'Rates of screening in the control group increased from 40% in the first year to 52% in the sixth year for PSA'. ERSPC: rate ratio 0.80.

claims.claim: Screening trade-off: PSA reduces mortality by ~20% but overdiagnoses;
claims.note: ERSPC 2009: 'PSA-based screening reduced the rate of death from prostate cancer by 20% but was associated with a high risk of overdiagnosis' (ERSPC record is cited on the same page's screening row).

claims.claim: Neuroendocrine / lineage-plastic transformation in 10.5 to 17% of late mCRPC (Kench 2022;
claims.note: Kench 2022 (PMC9542779): 'Treatment-related neuroendocrine prostatic carcinoma is found in 10.5%-17% of patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer after treatment with androgen receptor signalling inhibitors'.

claims.claim: 17% of metastatic biopsies in Aggarwal) has no targeted therapy;
claims.note: Aggarwal 2018 (record paper-aggarwal-t-sccpc-jco-2018, DOI 10.1200/JCO.2017.77.6880): 'The overall incidence of t-SCNC detection was 17%'.

claims.claim: Radioligand sequencing and resistance: about a tenth of men screen out for PSMA-negative disease on VISION's single-tracer criteria and 31% on TheraP's PSMA plus FDG criteria, heterogeneity, and no proven therapy after 177Lu failure outside trials;
claims.note: VISION full text: 'The eligibility criteria for PSMA imaging were not met in 126 patients (12.6%...)' of 1003 scanned: one in eight, not 'about a tenth'. TheraP: 291 screened, 200 eligible (31% out) correct.
claims.fixed: 'about a tenth' -> 'about one man in eight (12.6 percent of those scanned)'; same correction made in the record's subtypes line.

claims.claim: Equity: Black men have ~70% higher incidence and double the mortality yet are under-enrolled in trials; earlier, risk-adapted screening is the lever.
claims.note: SEER Stat Facts: incidence non-Hispanic Black 200.1 vs non-Hispanic White 122.2 per 100,000 (64% higher, not ~70%); death rate 36.2 vs 18.1 (double, correct). The page did not say this was US data.
claims.fixed: '~70% higher incidence' -> 'in the United States ... about 64% higher incidence and double the mortality (SEER)'.

claims.claim: Overdiagnosis is real, unavoidable with the current test, and unquantified to within a factor of thirty: estimates across epidemiological, clinical and autopsy studies range from 1.7 to 67 percent, modelling puts it at 23 to 42 percent of screen-detected cancers in United States calibration and 66 percent in the Rotterdam one, and autopsy studies find prostate cancer in 18.5 to 38.5 percent of men who died of something else.
claims.note: Loeb 2014: 'estimates ranging widely from 1.7% to 67%'; 'Autopsy studies have reported PCa in 18.5-38.5%'. Draisma 2009: 'overdiagnosis ranged from 23% to 42%'; Rotterdam MISCAN 66%.

claims.claim: Overtreatment is the harm that overdiagnosis causes, and it is measured in the men who bear it: about 1 in 5 who have radical prostatectomy develop long-term urinary incontinence and 2 in 3 long-term erectile dysfunction, against about 1.3 prostate cancer deaths and about 3 metastatic cases prevented per 1,000 men screened over roughly 13 years.
claims.note: USPSTF 2018: 'approximately 1.3 deaths from prostate cancer over approximately 13 years per 1000 men screened'; 'approximately 3 cases of metastatic prostate cancer'; 'About 1 in 5 ... long-term urinary incontinence, and 2 in 3 ... long-term erectile dysfunction'.

claims.claim: TRANSFORMER measured a difference of 8.6 months in progression-free survival through crossover between two sequences of the same two treatments, which is larger than the gain most of the individual drugs were licensed on.
claims.note: TRANSFORMER: 'The PFS2 for BAT->enzalutamide was 28.2 versus 19.6 months' (8.6-month difference).

claims.claim: The homologous recombination repair gene list is used as one biomarker and is not one: BRCA2 loss predicted response to olaparib in every case in TOPARP-A, ATM alteration gave a hazard ratio of 0.95 in TRITON3, and CDK12-altered tumours, 6 percent of the disease, are infrequently high for genome-wide loss of heterozygosity and are not homologous recombination deficient in the sense PARP inhibitors need.
claims.note: TOPARP-A: response in 'all 7 patients with BRCA2 loss'. TRITON3 ATM subgroup HR 0.95. Chung 2019: 'CDK12 (6%)'; 'CDK12-altered tumors were infrequently gLOH high'.

claims.claim: In a minority of men, treatment turns prostate cancer into a different disease: combined TP53 and RB1 loss allows a switch to an androgen receptor-independent, often neuroendocrine phenotype, found in 17 percent of metastatic biopsies in one prospective cohort, for which there is no approved treatment and no prospective surveillance strategy.
claims.note: Aggarwal 2018 prospective cohort of 202 men: 'overall incidence of t-SCNC detection was 17%'.

claims.claim: Checkpoint immunotherapy does not work here and nobody can say which few patients it does work in: objective response rates of 5 percent in PD-L1-positive and 3 percent in PD-L1-negative disease, a median tumour mutational burden of 2.6 mutations per megabase, and mismatch repair deficiency in 4 percent of tumours, with durable responses in a subgroup that cannot be identified in advance.
claims.note: KEYNOTE-199: ORR 5% cohort 1 (PD-L1 positive), 3% cohort 2 (PD-L1 negative). Chung 2019: 'Median TMB was low (2.6 mutations/Mb)'; 'mismatch repair (4%) GAs'.

claims.claim: Magnetic resonance imaging is reported as a patient-level test and used as a lesion-level map: sensitivity is 93 percent for whether a man has clinically significant cancer and 65 percent for whether a given significant lesion is seen, with at least one significant focus missed in 34 percent of men and 45 percent of those with multifocal disease, and no service publishes its own per-lesion figure.
claims.note: PROMIS: MP-MRI sensitivity 93% for clinically significant cancer. Johnson 2019: '65% of clinically significant lesions'; 'missed at least one clinically significant focus in 34% of patients overall, and in 45% of men with multifocal lesions'.

claims.claim: The TMPRSS2-ERG fusion defines roughly half of all prostate cancers, has been known since 2005, and has produced no treatment; the same is true of the seven-subtype TCGA taxonomy, which leaves a quarter of primary tumours unclassified.
claims.note: TCGA 2015: '74% of these tumors fell into one of seven subtypes' (a quarter unclassified); Tomlins 2005 for the fusion; ERG fusion 45.6% of 333 TCGA primaries (roughly half).

claims.claim: Across 142 men in the non-BRCA, non-ATM PROfound cohort, 89 had CDK12 and the remaining eleven genes supplied between one and twelve men each, with no responses; talazoparib's list names a mismatch repair gene, MLH1, and its own label states that no approved test for it exists.
claims.note: Lynparza label table 25: cohort B N=142, CDK12 89; other genes CHEK2 12, PPP2R2A 10, RAD51B 5, RAD54L 5, PALB2 4, BRIP1 3, CHEK1 2, BARD1 1, RAD51D 1, and 'No patients were enrolled who had mutations in ... FANCL and RAD51C' (so 9 of 11, not all 11, supplied 1-12 men); no responses in rarer genes (table 27). Current TALZENNA label (revised 10/2026) selects patients 'as detected by an FDA-authorized test' and no longer states that no approved test exists.
claims.fixed: Gene count corrected (nine of the remaining eleven genes supplied 1-12 men, two none); removed the outdated label statement about no approved test. Same outdated statement removed from the record's science note 4 of 7, whose 'eleven rarer genes, one or two men each' was corrected to 'rarer genes, one to six men each'.

claims.claim: The commonest genomic alteration in the disease, the TMPRSS2-ERG fusion, has no treatment and no prognostic value, and the drivers that might be treatable follow a long tail: 97 significantly mutated genes, 70 of them new, most below 3% prevalence.
claims.note: Armenia 2018: 'We identify a total of 97 SMGs, including 70 not previously implicated'; 'many genes mutated in less than 3% of cases'. Pettersson 2012: TMPRSS2:ERG 'does not strongly predict recurrence or mortality'.

claims.claim: AR-V7 is the closest this disease has to a test that chooses between two treatment classes and it is in no label, needs intact circulating tumour cells, and the two available assays disagree on 18% of samples.
claims.note: PROPHECY: 'The observed percentage agreement between the two AR-V7 assays was 82%' (18% disagreement).

claims.claim: In the one large Chinese cohort the founder event that defines almost half of Western tumours is uncommon, and in a 2,069-man single-centre series tumours from Black men carried more 8q gain, an adverse feature, with community-level income associated with that gain after adjusting for race and ancestry.
claims.note: Ren 2018 (65 Chinese tumours): 'low rate of TMPRSS2-ERG fusion'. Stopsack 2022: 'tumors from Black men had more aneuploidy, particularly chromosome arm 8q gains, an adverse prognostic factor'; 'Community-level average income was associated with chr8q gains after adjusting for race and ancestry'.

claims.claim: The state in which nearly all prostate cancer deaths occur, about 400,000 a year worldwide; median survival from first treatment is now around three years, longer for men who have not had an androgen receptor inhibitor.
claims.note: 'About 400,000 a year' is GLOBOCAN 2022 (397,430 prostate deaths) presented undated. 'Median survival from first treatment is now around three years' is stated by none of the record's sources (the Wikipedia CRPC link redirects to the prostate cancer article, which gives no mCRPC median; NCCN not script-readable; COU-AA-302 and PREVAIL abstracts give no such median).
claims.fixed: Dated the deaths figure to GLOBOCAN 2022; removed the unsourced median-survival clause.

claims.claim: Three quarters are clear-cell tumours defined by loss of the VHL gene, which leaves the oxygen-sensing HIF-2α switch permanently on and makes the tumour intensely vascular and immune-infiltrated.
claims.note: Neither cited source states the clear-cell share: the NCI PDQ (health professional) gives '85% of renal cell cancers are adenocarcinomas' and says 'most clear cell renal cell carcinomas carried a variant' (VHL); the Annals of Oncology link resolves (Crossref) to the CheckMate 214 8-year paper. NCI genetics PDQ also silent.
claims.fixed: 'Three quarters are clear-cell tumours' -> 'Most are clear-cell tumours'.

claims.claim: That biology explains the whole modern treatment story: anti-VEGF pills (2005-2012), immunotherapy (2015 onward), their combination (2018 onward), and the first HIF-2α inhibitor, belzutifan (2021).
claims.note: Years match FDA approvals: sorafenib 2005, axitinib 2012 (corpus drug records); belzutifan WELIREG label 'Initial U.S. Approval: 2021'. PDQ lists the anti-VEGF agents, nivolumab and belzutifan.

claims.claim: For metastatic disease, four immunotherapy-based first-line regimens have survival benefit: nivolumab-ipilimumab (CheckMate 214, durable remissions in a fifth of intermediate/poor-risk patients, still visible at eight years) and three IO-TKI doublets (pembrolizumab-axitinib, nivolumab-cabozantinib, lenvatinib-pembrolizumab).
claims.note: CheckMate 214 at 8 years (Tannir 2024, the cited Annals link): 'PFS probabilities at 90 months were 22.8% versus 10.8% (ITT), 25.4% versus 8.5% (I/P)'; complete response 11.8% in I/P. 'Durable remissions in a fifth of intermediate/poor-risk patients' conflated progression-free status with remission and used the ITT fraction for the I/P group.
claims.fixed: -> 'with about a quarter of intermediate/poor-risk patients still free of progression at 90 months'.

claims.claim: After surgery, adjuvant pembrolizumab (KEYNOTE-564) was the first adjuvant immunotherapy in any solid tumour to improve overall survival, and in 2026 belzutifan plus pembrolizumab (LITESPARK-022) became the first adjuvant combination, though three other adjuvant immunotherapy trials were negative.
claims.note: KEYNOTE-564 OS (Choueiri NEJM 2024): 'A significant improvement in overall survival ... hazard ratio for death, 0.62'. WELIREG label: adjuvant ccRCC with pembrolizumab, Indications 1.2 09/2026. PDQ cites negative IMmotion010 and CheckMate 914; the trial record names PROSPER as the third.

claims.claim: Renal cell carcinoma causes about 430,000 cases a year worldwide, with incidence rising as imaging finds more small tumours, many of which need no treatment; ~20-30% are metastatic at diagnosis, and immunotherapy doublets now give durable remissions in about a fifth of those patients. ~180,000 deaths a year; registry five-year survival for metastatic disease is ~15% overall, higher with modern IO regimens.
claims.note: GLOBOCAN 2022 (kidney, C64): 434,840 cases, 155,953 deaths. Page: '~180,000 deaths' (wrong), '430,000 cases a year' undated and labelled RCC. SEER (record prognosis source): distant 15% of cases, 5-year relative survival 20.3%; page said '~20-30% metastatic at diagnosis' and '~15%' survival, neither in any cited source. 'Durable remissions in about a fifth' is PFS at 90 months (22.8%) in CheckMate 214.
claims.fixed: Rewritten with GLOBOCAN 2022 dated figures (about 435,000 cases, 156,000 deaths, all kidney cancers), SEER 15% metastatic at diagnosis and 20.3% five-year relative survival for distant disease, and CheckMate 214 progression-free fraction; dropped unsourced 'higher with modern IO regimens'.

claims.claim: Four immunotherapy-based first-line regimens with survival benefit; durable remissions off treatment in ~20% with nivolumab-ipilimumab at 8 years.
claims.note: CheckMate 214 8-year: PFS 22.8% at 90 months (ITT); nothing in the source supports 'off treatment' or 'remission' for that fraction (CR 12.0%).
claims.fixed: -> 'about a fifth of patients (22.8%) still free of progression at 90 months with nivolumab-ipilimumab'.

claims.claim: Adjuvant pembrolizumab improves overall survival (KEYNOTE-564); pembrolizumab + belzutifan approved as adjuvant combination (2026).
claims.note: KEYNOTE-564 OS HR 0.62; WELIREG adjuvant combination indication added 2026.

claims.claim: High-risk after nephrectomy (clear-cell): Adjuvant pembrolizumab for 1 year (KEYNOTE-564, OS benefit); pembrolizumab + belzutifan approved 2026 (LITESPARK-022); sunitinib adjuvant rarely used.
claims.note: KEYNOTE-564: pembrolizumab 'for up to 17 cycles (approximately 1 year)', OS benefit; WELIREG label adjuvant combination with pembrolizumab (2026).

claims.claim: No predictive biomarker to choose between IO-IO and IO-TKI, or to identify the 20% who achieve durable remission.
claims.note: 'The 20% who achieve durable remission' rests on CheckMate 214's 22.8% progression-free at 90 months (ITT), not remission.
claims.fixed: -> 'the roughly one in five who are still free of progression at 90 months on nivolumab-ipilimumab'.

claims.claim: Muscle-invasive disease (25%) has required radical cystectomy with neoadjuvant cisplatin since the 2000s, and metastatic disease relied on platinum chemotherapy for four decades.
claims.note: NCI PDQ bladder: 'Approximately 70% to 80% of patients with newly diagnosed bladder cancer present with superficial bladder tumors (i.e., stage Ta, Tis, or T1)', leaving about a quarter muscle-invasive. Decades of platinum-based chemotherapy and neoadjuvant cisplatin are described in the same PDQ.

claims.claim: In metastatic disease, enfortumab vedotin plus pembrolizumab nearly doubled survival over chemotherapy (EV-302, 2023).
claims.note: EV-302 (Powles NEJM 2024; presented 2023): 'overall survival (median, 31.5 months vs. 16.1 months; hazard ratio for death, 0.47)'.

claims.claim: The same pair then moved around surgery: EV-303 in cisplatin-ineligible patients (EFS HR 0.40, approved November 2025) and EV-304 in cisplatin-eligible patients (positive December 2025), after NIAGARA had already established perioperative durvalumab (approved March 2025).
claims.note: EV-303: 'estimated EFS was 74.7% ... compared with 39.4% ... (HR, 0.40; 95% CI, 0.28 to 0.57)' (Urology Times on the NEJM paper); CancerNetwork 'November 21, 2025 FDA OKs Pembrolizumab/Enfortumab Vedotin in Muscle Invasive Bladder Cancer'; OncLive 'December 17, 2025 ... Meets EFS, OS, pCR End Points in Cisplatin-Eligible MIBC'; Urology Times 'March 28, 2025' durvalumab approval.

claims.claim: About 600,000 cases a year worldwide and the fourth most common cancer in men in the US.
claims.note: GLOBOCAN 2022 bladder (C67), WORLD: 614,298 cases, presented undated as 'a year'. NCI PDQ: 'It is the fourth most common cancer in men' (US) correct.
claims.fixed: Dated: 'In 2022, GLOBOCAN estimated about 614,000 new bladder cancers worldwide'.

claims.claim: Three quarters are non-muscle-invasive and managed for years with bladder-sparing treatment, which is why it has the highest lifetime treatment cost per patient of any cancer; ~220,000 deaths a year.
claims.note: Three quarters non-muscle-invasive matches PDQ's 70-80%. '~220,000 deaths a year' is GLOBOCAN 2022 (220,596) undated. The 'highest lifetime treatment cost per patient of any cancer' superlative carries no figure and no source on the record bears on it (left as is, flagged).
claims.fixed: Dated: 'GLOBOCAN estimated ~220,000 deaths in 2022'.

claims.claim: Perioperative durvalumab (NIAGARA) and adjuvant nivolumab (CheckMate 274) with overall survival benefit.
claims.note: NIAGARA: OS HR 0.75 (0.59-0.93), P=0.01 (correct). CheckMate 274: the record's OS source (NEJMoa2034442) is the 2021 DFS paper; the 5-year report (Urology Times, ESMO 2025) gives 'median overall survival is longer with nivolumab vs placebo on interim analysis ... 75 months ... 50.1 months ... hazard ratio of 0.83' with no significance stated. 'Overall survival benefit' overstated it.
claims.fixed: CheckMate 274 restated as 'longer median overall survival at an interim analysis (75 against 50.1 months)'.

claims.claim: NMIBC: Non-muscle-invasive: transurethral resection (TURBT) then intravesical BCG; novel intravesical agents for BCG-unresponsive disease; durvalumab + BCG for high-risk disease (2026).
claims.note: FDA: 'On May 28, 2026, the Food and Drug Administration approved durvalumab ... in combination with Bacillus Calmette-Guerin (BCG) ... BCG-naive, high-risk non-muscle invasive bladder cancer'.

claims.claim: CT urography; urine cytology; surveillance cystoscopy every 3-12 months by risk.
claims.note: Row refs (cystoscopy-turbt with a Wikipedia link; ct) state no interval. EAU NMIBC guideline table 8.2: low risk cystoscopy at 3 and 12 months then annually; intermediate at 3 months then every 6 months for 2 years; high risk every 3 months. The 3-12 month range is right.
claims.fixed: Added ref bcg-and-intravesical-therapy, whose record links the EAU NMIBC guideline that states the schedule; text unchanged.

claims.claim: Low / intermediate-risk NMIBC: TURBT with single immediate intravesical chemotherapy instillation; intermediate risk adds 1 year of intravesical chemotherapy (gemcitabine/mitomycin) or BCG.
claims.note: EAU NMIBC: 'administer a single immediate instillation of chemotherapy within 24 hours after TURBT'; 'Repeat chemotherapy instillations up to one year ... improve RFS in intermediate-risk patients'; 'one year of maintenance appears to be sufficient in intermediate-risk patients' (BCG). EAU is linked from the row's bcg-and-intravesical-therapy ref.

claims.claim: High-risk NMIBC, BCG-naive: TURBT then BCG induction and 1-3 years maintenance; durvalumab + BCG approved May 2026 (POTOMAC); radical cystectomy for very high-risk (T1 + CIS, variant histology).
claims.note: EAU: 'Three-year maintenance is more effective than one year ... in patients with high-risk tumours' (1-3 years). FDA: durvalumab + BCG approved May 28, 2026 (POTOMAC).

claims.claim: BCG-unresponsive NMIBC (CIS ± papillary): Radical cystectomy remains the oncologic gold standard; bladder-sparing options: TAR-200 (Inlexzo, 2025), N-803 + BCG (Anktiva, 2024), nadofaragene firadenovec (2022), pembrolizumab (2020); cretostimogene in registration.
claims.note: DailyMed labels: INLEXZO 'Initial U.S. Approval: 2025'; ANKTIVA 'Initial U.S. Approval: 2024'; ADSTILADRIN 'Initial U.S. Approval: 2022'. Pembrolizumab BCG-unresponsive indication (KEYNOTE-057) is in the Keytruda label; the 2020 year was not printed there and was not separately confirmed.

claims.claim: Muscle-invasive, cisplatin-eligible: Perioperative EV + pembrolizumab (EV-304, positive 2025; filing) or neoadjuvant durvalumab + gemcitabine-cisplatin with adjuvant durvalumab (NIAGARA, approved 2025), then radical cystectomy with lymph node dissection; trimodality bladder preservation (TURBT + chemoradiation) for selected patients.
claims.note: EV-304 topline positive December 17, 2025 (OncLive); NEJM 2026 paper confirms EFS HR 0.53 and OS HR 0.65. NIAGARA approval March 28, 2025.

claims.claim: After cystectomy (no perioperative IO): Adjuvant nivolumab for high-risk pathology (CheckMate 274); or ctDNA-guided adjuvant atezolizumab (IMvigor011, approved 2026).
claims.note: TECENTRIQ label: 'Muscle Invasive Bladder Cancer (MIBC) as adjuvant treatment of adult patients with MIBC after cystectomy who have circulating tumor DNA molecular residual disease'; Recent Major Changes 'Indications and Usage (1.6) 05/2026'.

claims.claim: Peripheral neuropathy and skin toxicity of enfortumab vedotin limit duration; safer Nectin-4 conjugates stalled in 2026.
claims.note: Only one safer Nectin-4 conjugate is documented as stalled: ApexOnco 17 March 2026, 'Bicycle Therapeutics ... zelenectide pevedotin ... the company has deprioritis[ed]' (the zelenectide record's source). 'Conjugates stalled' generalised from one programme.
claims.fixed: -> 'the leading safer Nectin-4 conjugate, zelenectide pevedotin, was deprioritised by its developer in March 2026'.

claims.claim: TNBC is defined by what it lacks: ER <1%, PR <1%, HER2 0-1+ (or 2+/ISH-negative).
claims.note: Allison 2020: "A sample is considered ER negative if < 1% ... immunoreactive"; Wolff 2018 HER2 IHC 0/1+ or 2+ ISH-negative is negative.

claims.claim: It is biologically heterogeneous (basal-like 1 and 2, mesenchymal, luminal androgen receptor, immunomodulatory subtypes), nearly always TP53-mutant, frequently HRD-positive (11 to 17% germline BRCA1/2 by cohort), and has the highest TROP2 expression and the most immune infiltration of any breast subtype.
claims.note: Couch 2015 "11.2% had mutations in the BRCA1 (8.5%) and BRCA2 (2.7%)"; Sharma 2014 15.4%; Hahnen 2017 "50 of the 291 patients (17.2%)" (molecular table on the record).

claims.claim: KEYNOTE-522 (2020-21) made pembrolizumab plus carboplatin-containing chemotherapy before surgery, continued after, the standard for stage II-III disease, with a 4.9-point overall survival gain at five years (86.6% against 81.7%).
claims.note: Schmid NEJM 2024: "overall survival at 60 months was 86.6% ... as compared with 81.7%".

claims.claim: In metastatic disease, pembrolizumab-chemotherapy (CPS ≥10) was joined by the TROP2 ADCs: sacituzumab govitecan (ASCENT, second line 2020; first-line ASCENT-03/04 2026) and datopotamab deruxtecan (TROPION-Breast02, first-line PD-1-ineligible, 2026, with an overall survival benefit), while T-DXd covers the roughly one third of TNBC that is HER2-low (24 to 37% by cohort).
claims.note: HER2-low 36.6% of TNBC (Schettini 2021), 34.0% (395/1162, Denkert 2021), 24.0% (Boissiere-Michot 2026); Trodelvy label revised 06/2026 with ASCENT-03/04, Datroway label 05/2026 with TROPION-Breast02 OS 23.7 vs 18.7.

claims.claim: What remains unsolved: residual disease after KEYNOTE-522 (RCB II-III) still carries ~40-50% relapse risk;
claims.note: No source on the record gives a 40-50% relapse risk after KEYNOTE-522; Symmans 2017 (on the record): 10-year RFS "86%, 81%, 55%, and 23% for triple receptor-negative", i.e. about 45% (RCB-II) and 77% (RCB-III) relapsed, without immunotherapy.
claims.fixed: tnbc-core.ts EXISTING_SUMMARY: replaced "~40-50% relapse risk" with "a high relapse risk (before immunotherapy, ten-year relapse-free survival was 55% for RCB-II and 23% for RCB-III, Symmans 2017)"

claims.claim: The IARC breast fact sheet, served today with the GLOBOCAN 2024 estimates, gives 2,434,087 new breast cancers a year (the second commonest cancer, age-standardised rate 47.8 per 100,000) and 693,660 deaths (fourth, 12.9 per 100,000), with 45.1 percent of cases in Asia, 22.3 percent in Europe, 13.2 percent in Northern America, 9.3 percent in Africa and 9.0 percent in Latin America and the Caribbean.
claims.note: Fact sheet printed "GLOBOCAN 2024": incidence rank 2, 2 434 087, ASR 47.8; mortality rank 4, 693 660, 12.9; Asia 45.1%, Europe 22.3%, Northern America 13.2%, Africa 9.3%, LAC 9.0%. Page names GLOBOCAN 2024 explicitly.

claims.claim: The triple-negative share in registries with receptor data runs from 8.4 percent of 1,151,724 US cases in 2010 to 2014 (Scott 2019) through 10.8 percent of US cases with a known subtype in SEER 21, 2019 to 2023 (the SEER subtype fact sheet), 12.2 percent of cases with known status in 2010 (Howlader 2014) and 12 percent in 2012 to 2016 (Howard and Olopade 2021), to around 15 percent on the Cancer Research UK patient page and 17 percent of 15,204 women treated at NCCN centres in 2000 to 2006 (Lin 2012).
claims.note: Scott 2019 8.4% of 1,151,724; Howlader 2014 12.2%; Howard 2021 12%; CRUK "around 15%"; Lin 2012 17% of 15,204 all correct. But SEER: "HR-/HER2- 10.7778%" of ALL cases with "Unknown 5.53%" in the denominator, so 10.8% is not "of cases with a known subtype" (that would be about 11.4%).
claims.fixed: tnbc-core.ts: "10.8 percent of US cases with a known subtype" -> "10.8 percent of all US cases, including those of unknown subtype"

claims.claim: Applied to 2.4 million, a share of 10 to 15 percent would be about 240,000 to 370,000 people a year; that is arithmetic on the figures above, not a published count.
claims.note: Arithmetic on GLOBOCAN 2024 2,434,087: 10% = 243k, 15% = 365k; labelled as arithmetic, not a published count.

claims.claim: In the United States the age-adjusted rate of hormone receptor-negative, HER2-negative breast cancer is 14.3 per 100,000 women a year against 132.5 for all breast cancer (SEER 21, 2019 to 2023), and 321,910 new female breast cancers of all subtypes are projected for 2026.
claims.note: SEER: "HR-/HER2- 14.3 ... Total 132.5"; "In 2026, it is estimated that there will be 321,910 new cases of female breast cancer".

claims.claim: Women under 40 had 1.53 times the odds of the triple-negative phenotype in the California registry (Bauer 2007) and 1.95 times the odds relative to women aged 50 to 64 in US Cancer Statistics (Scott 2019);
claims.note: Bauer 2007: "under age 40 (odds ratio [OR], 1.53)"; Scott 2019: "Women aged <40 years had the highest odds ... compared with women aged 50 to 64 years (OR, 1.95)".

claims.claim: Howlader found triple-negative patients 10 to 30 percent less likely to be diagnosed at older ages and 6.4 to 20 times more likely to present with high-grade disease;
claims.note: Howlader 2014: "10% to 30% less likely to be diagnosed at older ages ... 6.4-fold to 20.0-fold more likely to present with high-grade disease".

claims.claim: Cancer Research UK says the type develops more often in women under 40.
claims.note: CRUK TNBC page: "Triple negative breast cancer develops more often in women under 40 years."

claims.claim: Ethnicity: in SEER 21 (2019 to 2023) the rate of hormone receptor-negative, HER2-negative disease is 25.7 per 100,000 in non-Hispanic Black women against 13.0 in non-Hispanic White, 12.5 in Hispanic, 11.4 in American Indian and Alaska Native and 10.5 in Asian and Pacific Islander women, roughly a two-fold difference; non-Hispanic Black women had 2.27 times the odds of a triple-negative diagnosis in 2010 to 2014 (Scott 2019); the basal-like subtype was found in 39 percent of premenopausal African American women against 16 percent of non-African American women in the Carolina Breast Cancer Study (Carey 2006); and in 507 women in Nigeria and Senegal, triple-negative disease (basal-like 27 percent plus unclassified 28 percent) predominated, with a mean age of 44.8 (Huo 2009).
claims.note: SEER rates NH Black 25.7, NH White 13.0, Hispanic 12.5, AI/AN 11.4, API 10.5; Scott OR 2.27; Carey "39% ... non-African American women (16%)"; Huo "507 patients", "basal-like (27%) and unclassified subtype (28%)", mean age 44.8.

claims.claim: In the UK, the POSH cohort of women diagnosed at 40 or under found triple-negative tumours in 26.1 percent of Black against 18.6 percent of White patients (Copson 2014), and an analysis of 116,500 women in England (2013 to 2018) found greater adjusted odds of ER-negative, high-grade and high-stage tumours in ethnic minority women, most marked in Black African and Black Caribbean women (Gathani 2021).
claims.note: Copson 2014: "ER/PR/HER2-negative tumours were significantly more frequent in Blacks (26.1%) than Whites (18.6%"; Gathani 2021 title "over 116,500 women in England", 2013-2018, less favourable characteristics greater in Black groups.

claims.claim: Even after adjustment for stage, treatment delay and socioeconomic factors, African American women with triple-negative disease remain nearly twice as likely to die of it (Howard and Olopade 2021).
claims.note: Howard and Olopade 2021: "Even controlling for treatment delays, stage, and socioeconomic factors, African Americans with triple-negative breast cancer remain nearly twice as likely to die".

claims.claim: Inherited risk: 57.1 percent of breast cancers in BRCA1 carriers were triple-negative against 23.3 percent in BRCA2 carriers and 13.8 percent in non-carriers (Atchley 2008); in 6,893 carriers the triple-negative share fell with age at diagnosis in BRCA1 and rose in BRCA2 carriers, and medullary tumours were BRCA1-related (Mavaddat 2012).
claims.note: Atchley 2008: 57.1% / 23.3% / 13.8%; Mavaddat 2012: 4,325 BRCA1 + 2,568 BRCA2 carriers (6,893), TN proportion decreased with age in BRCA1 and increased in BRCA2, medullary tumours BRCA1-related.

claims.claim: Looked at from the other side, 14.6 percent of 1,824 triple-negative patients unselected for family history carried a deleterious mutation in one of 17 genes, 8.5 percent BRCA1, 2.7 percent BRCA2 and 1.2 percent PALB2 (Couch 2015); a prospective US registry found 15.4 percent with BRCA1 or BRCA2 mutations, 27.6 percent among those diagnosed at 50 or under, 11.4 percent at 51 to 60 and 4.9 percent at 61 or over (Sharma 2014); and 12 percent of 2,733 UK women with breast cancer at 40 or under carried a BRCA mutation (Copson 2018).
Cancer Research UK puts the lifetime breast cancer risk of a BRCA1 or BRCA2 carrier at 45 to 65 percent by age 70, with about 1 in 450 women carrying a mutation;
claims.note: CRUK risk factors: "a 45-65% chance of developing breast cancer by age 70" and "around 1 in 450 women carrying a mutation".

claims.claim: PALB2 carries a relative risk of 7.18 and a 53 percent risk to age 80 (Yang 2020).
claims.note: Yang 2020: "RR, 7.18" and "risks to age 80 years were 53%".

claims.claim: Breast cancer is the commonest cancer, with 59,413 new cases a year (2019 and 2021 to 2022), about 59,000 in females and 420 in males, 15 percent of all cancers; a quarter are diagnosed at 75 or over; incidence rates have risen 20 percent since the early 1990s and are projected to fall 1 percent by 2038 to 2040 while the count rises to about 70,300 a year; incidence rates are lower in the Asian and Black ethnic groups than the White group in England (2013 to 2017), which sits beside the higher triple-negative share in Black women noted above.
claims.note: CRUK statistics hub: "59,413 new cases of breast cancer each year, 2019, 2021-2022, UK"; incidence page: 59,000 females, 420 males, 15%, a quarter aged 75+, up 20% since early 1990s, projected -1% to 2038-2040 with ~70,300 cases, lower rates in Asian and Black groups (2013-2017).

claims.claim: There are about 11,200 deaths a year (2022 to 2024), the fourth commonest cause of cancer death and the second in women; mortality rates have fallen 46 percent since the early 1970s.
claims.note: CRUK mortality: "4th most common cause of cancer death ... around 11,200 deaths every year (2022-2024)", 2nd in females, "decreased by almost half (46%) ... since the early 1970s".

claims.claim: In England in 2022, 85 percent of cases with a known stage were stage I or II; in 2019, 53 percent were diagnosed through an urgent suspected cancer referral, 32 percent through screening and 4 percent after an emergency presentation.
claims.note: CRUK hub: "In 2022, 85% ... known stage ... early stage (I & II) in England"; 2019: 53% urgent referral, 4% emergency, 32% screening.

claims.claim: About 23 percent of UK breast cancers are judged preventable, 8 percent attributed to alcohol and 1 percent to ionising radiation.
claims.note: CRUK: "23% of breast cancer cases are preventable"; "8% ... caused by alcohol"; "1% ... caused by ionising radiation".

claims.claim: Cancer Research UK does not publish a separate UK incidence count for triple-negative disease; the around 15 percent share on its patient page, and the 20 percent share in the young-onset POSH cohort (558 of 2,733), are the UK figures found for this record.
claims.note: CRUK TN page "Around 15 out of 100 (around 15%)"; POSH 558 TNBC of 2,733 = 20.4%.

claims.claim: Reproduction runs the other way from hormone receptor-positive disease: in 23,353 cases and 71,072 controls pooled across 31 studies, parous women had a lower risk of every luminal and HER2-enriched-like subtype but a higher risk of triple-negative disease immediately after a birth (odds ratio 3.12 for multiparous women right after their last birth), attenuating over decades (Jung 2022); in African American women parity raised triple-negative risk (odds ratio 1.37) while breastfeeding lowered ER-negative risk (0.81), and ER-negative risk rose with each birth in women who had not breastfed (1.68 for four or more births) (Palmer 2014).
claims.note: Jung 2022: "up to 23 353 cases and 71 072 controls pooled from 31", "OR = 3.12" multiparous right after last birth; Palmer 2014: TN OR 1.37, lactation ER- OR 0.81, OR 1.68 for 4+ births without breastfeeding.

claims.claim: Obesity: triple-negative cases were more often obese than hormone receptor-positive cases (odds ratio 1.20 case-case, 1.24 case-control), a signal confined to premenopausal women (1.43) in an 11-study meta-analysis (Pierobon 2013), and 1.89 in an Atlanta case series (Trivers 2009);
claims.note: Pierobon 2013: "Eleven original articles", OR 1.20 case-case, 1.24 case-control, premenopausal 1.43; Trivers 2009 Atlanta OR 1.89.

claims.claim: Cancer Research UK notes the postmenopausal body-mass effect is largely limited to ER- and PR-positive tumours (adult weight gain raised ER- and PR-negative risk by 34 percent against 133 percent for positive tumours).
claims.note: CRUK risk page: "risk increase is larger for ER- and PR- positive tumours (133% increase) than ER- and PR-negative tumours (34% increase)".

claims.claim: What is shared with all breast cancer: alcohol (8 percent of UK cases), ionising radiation (1 percent) and breast density (3 to 5 times the risk in the most dense breasts).
claims.note: CRUK: 8% alcohol, 1% ionising radiation, "up to 3-5 times higher in women with the most dense breasts".

claims.claim: Triple-negative tumours are less often found by a screening mammogram (29 percent against 48 percent of hormone receptor-positive, HER2-negative tumours in NCCN centres) and present with a higher tumour category but are less likely to involve the lymph nodes (Lin 2012); they are over-represented among interval cancers, which appear between screens and carry worse prognostic features than screen-detected cancers (Houssami 2017); and they are more often high grade (Howlader 2014).
claims.note: Lin 2012: "less likely to present on the basis of an abnormal screening mammogram (29% vs 48%)", higher tumour classification, less lymph node involvement; Houssami 2017 full text: interval cancers more often triple-negative, worse prognostic features.

claims.claim: Relapse is early: in 1,601 Toronto patients the triple-negative group had 2.6 times the hazard of distant recurrence and 3.2 times the hazard of death within five years but not afterwards, with the risk of distant recurrence peaking at about three years and falling rapidly (Dent 2007); recurrence and death rates were higher only in the first three years in the MD Anderson neoadjuvant series, which also found more visceral and fewer bone relapses (Liedtke 2008); and in 116 patients with metastatic disease treated in 2000 to 2006, 46 percent developed brain metastases before death and median survival from the metastatic diagnosis was 13.3 months (Lin 2008), a figure that the later trials in the treatment rows have moved.
claims.note: Dent 2007: 1,601 patients, HR 2.6 distant recurrence, 3.2 death "within 5 years of diagnosis but not thereafter", "peaked at approximately 3 years"; Liedtke: higher rates only in first 3 years, more visceral, fewer bone; Lin 2008: 116 patients 2000-2006, 13.3 months, 46% CNS before death.

claims.claim: Triple-negative is then a laboratory definition: ER negative when fewer than 1 percent of tumour nuclei stain, PR likewise, with 1 to 10 percent reported as a new ER Low Positive category on which endocrine benefit is uncertain (ASCO/CAP 2020, Allison);
claims.note: Allison 2020: ER negative "< 1%"; "1% to 10% ... new reporting category, ER Low Positive"; limited data on endocrine benefit.

claims.claim: The 2023 ASCO-CAP update kept those categories but added a reporting comment because the difference between HER2 0 and 1+ now decides eligibility for trastuzumab deruxtecan (Wolff 2023).
claims.note: Wolff 2023: affirms 2018 recommendations and "offers a new HER2 testing reporting comment to highlight the current relevance of IHC 0 versus 1+".

claims.claim: Where the receptors are low rather than absent the behaviour is the same: ER 1 to 10 percent tumours matched ER-negative tumours for germline BRCA prevalence, response and survival in a US registry (Yoder 2022) and in an Italian series (Dieci 2021), and Sweden treats ER 1 to 9 percent HER2-negative tumours as triple-negative, with 9.9 percent of 5,655 such cancers in 2008 to 2020 falling in that band (Acs 2024).
claims.note: Yoder 2022: BRCA prevalence and survival not different between TNBC and low-ER; Dieci 2021: ER 1-9% similar iRFS, OS and pCR; Acs 2024: "Of the 5655 tumors ... 9.9% were ER-low", Sweden 2008-2020.

claims.claim: NG101 (1.3.6) adds one test that applies to this subtype alone: offer germline BRCA1 and BRCA2 testing to women under 50 with triple-negative breast cancer, including those with no family history.
claims.note: NG101 1.3.6: "Offer genetic testing for BRCA1 and BRCA2 mutations to women under 50 years with triple-negative breast cancer, including those with no family history".

claims.claim: Most triple-negative cancers are invasive carcinomas of no special type (the term the 2019 WHO classification, 5th edition, uses for what was called ductal carcinoma) of grade 3, with a high proliferation index: the Swedish cohort's median Ki-67 was 63 percent in ER-zero and 60 percent in ER-low tumours, and 80.8 percent of ER-zero tumours were grade III (Acs 2024).
claims.note: Acs 2024: "median Ki67 of 60% (63% in ER-zero tumors)", "grade III in 69.4% (80.8% in ER-zero tumors)".

claims.claim: By gene expression, 78.6 percent of triple-negative tumours are basal-like and 21.4 percent belong to other intrinsic subtypes, while 31.5 percent of basal-like tumours are not triple-negative (Prat 2013); basal-like tumours share many molecular features with high-grade serous ovarian cancer, and TP53 is the mutation that recurs across them (TCGA 2012).
claims.note: Prat 2013: "412 TN and 473 BL tumors, 21.4% and 31.5% were identified as non-BL and non-TN" (78.6% basal-like).

claims.claim: Within the triple-negative group, Lehmann's 2011 analysis of 587 cases found six expression subtypes (basal-like 1 and 2, immunomodulatory, mesenchymal, mesenchymal stem-like and luminal androgen receptor), refined in 2016 to four tumour-intrinsic subtypes once the immunomodulatory and stem-like signals were traced to infiltrating lymphocytes and stroma;
claims.note: Lehmann 2011: "587 TNBC cases ... identified 6 TNBC subtypes"; Lehmann 2016 refined to four after IM and MSL traced to lymphocytes and stroma.

claims.claim: The WHO classification also names special histological types that are usually triple-negative: metaplastic carcinoma (70.3 percent triple-negative in 2,451 US cases, Ong 2018), carcinoma with medullary pattern (no longer a separate type in the 5th edition, Thomas 2023;
claims.note: Ong 2018 says "2451 MBC ... 70.3% of MBC ... were triple negative" but Ong 2018 was not a link on the tnbc record (only on the subtype page). Thomas 2023 (on record) has no figure here.
claims.fixed: tnbc-core.ts: added SRC.ong2018 and SRC.cserni2020 to the tnbc record links (figure unchanged, verified)

claims.claim: Cserni 2020), adenoid cystic carcinoma (95 percent localised at diagnosis, 15-year relative survival 91.4 percent, Ghabach 2010), apocrine carcinoma (ER and PR negative, androgen receptor positive, Vranic 2013) and secretory carcinoma (ETV6-NTRK3 fusion in 92 percent, Tognon 2002).
claims.note: Ghabach 2010: "Ninety-five percent of cases presented with locali[zed]" and 15-year relative survival 91.4%; Tognon 2002: ETV6-NTRK3 "in 12 (92%) of 13"; Vranic 2013: ER/PR negative, AR positive. None was linked on the tnbc record.
claims.fixed: tnbc-core.ts: added SRC.ghabach2010, SRC.vranic2013, SRC.tognon2002 to the tnbc record links (figures unchanged, verified)

claims.claim: Rare subtypes together are 5 to 10 percent of triple-negative cancers (Thomas 2023), and the European Working Group for Breast Screening Pathology concludes that patients with the indolent pure forms (classical adenoid cystic, low-grade adenosquamous, fibromatosis-like metaplastic, secretory, acinic cell, tall cell with reversed polarity) are unlikely to benefit from chemotherapy (Cserni 2021).
claims.note: Thomas 2023: "comprising 5-10% of all TNBCs"; Cserni 2021: indolent pure subtypes listed "are unlikely to benefit from systemic chemotherapy".

claims.claim: Nodes are staged clinically (cN) before any treatment and pathologically (pN) from the sentinel node or clearance: pN1 one to three axillary nodes (pN1mi micrometastases 0.2 to 2 mm), pN2 four to nine, pN3 ten or more or infraclavicular, or axillary plus internal mammary, or supraclavicular nodes.
claims.note: CRUK TNM: pN1 1 to 3 nodes, micrometastases "larger than 0.2 mm but are less than 2 mm", pN2a 4 to 9, pN3a 10 or more.

claims.claim: 3C is any N3; stage 4 is any M1.
claims.note: CRUK number stages: "Stage 3C is the same as: Any T N3 M0"; stage 4 "Any T Any N M1".

claims.claim: The American Joint Committee on Cancer's 8th edition kept this anatomic stage but added a prognostic stage that folds grade, ER, PR and HER2 status (and, for some hormone receptor-positive tumours, a low Oncotype DX score) into the stage group (Giuliano 2017); in a 3,327-patient MD Anderson cohort the prognostic stage moved 29.5 percent of patients up and 28.1 percent down, and predicted disease-specific survival better than the anatomic stage (C index 0.84 against 0.74), with the same result in 54,727 Californian patients (Weiss 2018).
claims.note: Weiss 2018: 3327 patients, upstaged 29.5%, downstaged 28.1%, C index 0.8357 vs 0.737; "54 727 patients" in the California Cancer Registry, prognostic stage performed better.

claims.claim: The NHS Breast Screening Programme invites everyone registered as female from age 50 (first invitation between 50 and 53) every three years until their 71st birthday, and women 71 or over can ask for screening (NHS).
claims.note: NHS: "offered to women aged 50 up to your 71st birthday", first invitation "between the ages of 50 and 53", "every 3 years", 71+ can self-refer every 3 years.

claims.claim: NICE CG164 sets the UK rules: GPs refer to a specialist breast or genetics clinic on defined family patterns, and clinicians should seek genetics advice for families containing triple-negative breast cancer under 40, Jewish ancestry, sarcoma under 45 or glioma; genetic testing is offered when the combined BRCA1 and BRCA2 carrier probability is 10 percent or more (calculated with CanRisk, formerly BOADICEA, or the Manchester score); known BRCA1 or BRCA2 carriers are offered annual MRI from 30 to 49 and annual mammography from 40 to 69, TP53 carriers MRI from 20, and MRI is not offered to carriers aged 50 to 69 unless the breasts are dense.
claims.note: CG164 1.4.5 "triple negative breast cancer under the age of 40 years ... Jewish ancestry ... sarcoma ... younger than age 45 years ... glioma"; 1.5.13 carrier probability "10% or more"; CanRisk (BOADICEA) or Manchester; 1.6.7 MRI 30-49 BRCA, 20-49 TP53; 1.6.3 mammography 40-69; 1.6.14 no MRI 50+ without TP53 unless dense.

claims.claim: In the UK MARIBS study of 649 women at high familial risk, MRI sensitivity was 77 percent against 40 percent for mammography, 92 against 23 percent in BRCA1 carriers (Leach 2005).
claims.note: Leach 2005: 649 women, "CE MRI (77% ...) than for mammography (40%", BRCA1 "92%vs 23%".

claims.note: Rebbeck 2004: "two (1.9%) of 105 ... 184 (48.7%) of 378 ... mean follow-up of 6.4 years", "approximately 90%".

claims.claim: Rebbeck 2004) and pooled relative risk 0.114 in a 15-study meta-analysis, with contralateral mastectomy 0.072 and salpingo-oophorectomy 0.552 for breast cancer overall (Li 2016), though a prospective study of 3,722 carriers found oophorectomy did not lower breast cancer risk in BRCA1 carriers (hazard ratio 0.96) (Kotsopoulos 2017).
claims.note: Li 2016: 15 studies, BPM RR 0.114, PBSO RR 0.552, CPM 0.072; Kotsopoulos 2017: n = 3722, BRCA1 HR 0.96.

claims.claim: Chemoprevention has a gap that matters for this subtype: NICE offers tamoxifen (premenopausal) or anastrozole (postmenopausal) for five years to women at high risk, and considers them at moderate risk, but tamoxifen had no effect on invasive ER-negative breast cancer in IBIS-I (hazard ratio 1.05 over 16 years;
claims.note: CG164 1.7.21/1.7.22 tamoxifen or anastrozole "for 5 years"; Cuzick 2015 "median follow up of 16.0 years", ER-negative "HR 1.05".

claims.claim: Cuzick 2015) or NSABP P-1 (Fisher 1998), and anastrozole's 49 percent reduction in IBIS-II was in ER-positive disease (Cuzick 2020);
claims.note: Cuzick 2020: "a 49% reduction in breast cancer" is all breast cancer; "Invasive oestrogen receptor-positive breast cancer was reduced by 54%"; full text: "small, non-significant reduction ... oestrogen receptor-negative breast cancer (0.77, 0.41-1.44)". Fisher 1998 correct ("no difference in ... estrogen receptor-negative tumors").
claims.fixed: tnbc-core.ts: "anastrozole's 49 percent reduction in IBIS-II was in ER-positive disease" -> "came from ER-positive disease (54 percent fewer invasive ER-positive cancers, no significant effect on ER-negative cancer; Cuzick 2020)"

claims.claim: One observational signal runs the other way: tamoxifen after a first breast cancer was associated with a lower contralateral breast cancer risk in BRCA1 (hazard ratio 0.38) and BRCA2 (0.33) carriers regardless of the first tumour's ER status (Phillips 2013).
claims.note: Phillips 2013: "adjusted HR estimates were 0.38 ... and 0.33 ... for BRCA1 and BRCA2"; "HRs did not differ by estrogen receptor status of the first BC".

claims.claim: About 10 to 15 percent of breast cancers: 10.8 percent of US cases with a known subtype (SEER 21, 2019 to 2023) and around 15 percent on Cancer Research UK's patient page, against 2.43 million breast cancers a year worldwide (GLOBOCAN 2024).
claims.note: SEER: HR-/HER2- 10.78% is a share of all cases including 5.53% unknown, not "of cases with a known subtype"; CRUK "around 15%" and GLOBOCAN 2024 2,434,087 correct.

claims.claim: Diagnosed younger, about twice as often in Black women (25.7 against 13.0 per 100,000 in the United States) and in most breast cancers arising in BRCA1 carriers.
claims.note: SEER: NH Black 25.7, NH White 13.0; Atchley 57.1% of BRCA1 cancers triple-negative.

claims.claim: United States (SEER 21, excluding Illinois, people diagnosed 2016 to 2022): five-year relative survival for hormone receptor-negative, HER2-negative breast cancer is 78.7 percent, against 95.8 percent for hormone receptor-positive, HER2-negative disease and 91.9 percent for all breast cancer; by stage it is 92.8 percent for localised, 68.3 percent for regional and 14.9 percent for distant disease (the same fact sheet).
claims.note: SEER: 5-year relative survival HR-/HER2- 78.7%, HR+/HER2- 95.8%, total 91.9%; HR-/HER2- 92.8% / 68.3% / 14.9% localised/regional/distant; "SEER 21 (Excluding IL) 2016-2022".

claims.claim: Four-year breast cancer-specific survival was 77.0 percent for the triple-negative subtype in SEER cases diagnosed 2010 to 2013 (Howlader 2018), and in the California registry (1999 to 2003) non-Hispanic Black women with late-stage triple-negative disease had a five-year relative survival of 14 percent, the lowest of any group (Bauer 2007).
claims.note: Howlader 2018: 2010-2013, "worst survival for triple-negative subtype (77.0%)" at 4 years; Bauer 2007: late-stage NH Black TN "5-year relative survival of only 14%".

claims.claim: For all breast cancer in England (women diagnosed 2018 to 2022) five-year net survival is almost 100 percent at stage 1, 90 percent at stage 2, around 75 percent at stage 3 and more than 30 percent at stage 4 (Cancer Research UK, from NHS England), and 76.6 percent of UK women survive ten years or more (2018).
claims.note: CRUK survival page (diagnosed 2018-2022): stage 1 almost 100%, stage 2 90%, stage 3 around 75%, stage 4 more than 30%; CRUK hub "76.6% females survive breast cancer for 10 or more years, 2018".

claims.claim: Subtype-specific UK figures come from cohorts: in the POSH study of women diagnosed at 40 or under (2000 to 2008), ten-year overall survival among 558 triple-negative patients was 72 percent in BRCA carriers and 69 percent in non-carriers (Copson 2018), and in a Manchester single-centre series of women aged 40 or under (2010 to 2015) five-year survival was 70.8 percent for triple-negative against 86.3 percent for ER-positive, HER2-negative tumours (Monaghan 2024).
claims.note: Copson 2018: "Of 558 patients with triple-negative breast cancer ... 10 years (72% ... vs 69%"; Monaghan 2024: women 40 and under 2010-2015, TN 70.8%, ER+/HER2- 86.3%.

claims.claim: What moves the figures: stage at diagnosis above all; response to chemotherapy given before surgery, with ten-year relapse-free survival of 86 percent after a pathological complete response, 81 percent for residual cancer burden class I, 55 percent for class II and 23 percent for class III (Symmans 2017); and the newer regimens, with five-year overall survival of 86.6 percent for stage II and III disease treated with pembrolizumab and chemotherapy against 81.7 percent with chemotherapy alone in KEYNOTE-522 (Schmid 2024).
claims.note: Symmans 2017: TN 10-year RFS "86%, 81%, 55%, and 23%"; Schmid 2024 86.6% vs 81.7% at 60 months.

claims.claim: Relapse risk is concentrated in the first three to five years and is low thereafter (Dent 2007).
claims.note: Dent 2007: increased risk "within 5 years of diagnosis but not thereafter", peak at about 3 years.

claims.claim: Curative-intent: chemo-immunotherapy (KEYNOTE-522) cures more patients than ever; pCR ~65%.
claims.note: KEYNOTE-522 NEJM 2020: pCR "64.8%" with pembrolizumab-chemotherapy.

claims.claim: Metastatic: ADCs first line (sacituzumab, Dato-DXd), ADC + IO for PD-L1+ disease; median OS in first-line trials now approaches two years, roughly double the 2015 figure.
claims.note: "approaches two years" supported (KEYNOTE-355 CPS>=10 median OS 23.0 months, record link), but no source on the record gives a "2015 figure" to double; nearest is Lin 2008 median 13.3 months (2000-2006).
claims.fixed: cancers.ts stateOfArt: "roughly double the 2015 figure" -> "(23.0 months with pembrolizumab and chemotherapy at CPS 10 or more in KEYNOTE-355), against 13.3 months in a 2000 to 2006 series"

claims.claim: TP53 mutation in about 80% (79 to 90% by cohort), PIK3CA 10 to 18%, PTEN loss 12 to 35%, RB1 loss 15 to 20%, MYC amplification 18 to 35%, EGFR amplification 3 to 6%, NOTCH activation 5 to 9%, PI3K-AKT pathway alteration 20 to 27%; germline BRCA1 7 to 11%, BRCA2 3 to 4%, PALB2 1 to 2%, and homologous recombination deficiency in 59 to 71% (mostly BRCA1 promoter methylation and sporadic scars rather than germline mutation).
claims.note: Molecular table on the record: TP53 79.3-90.3% by cohort and 80% TCGA basal; PIK3CA 10.7-17.7%; MYC 17.6-35.0%; HRD 58.6% (Staaf) and 70.5% (Loibl: "136 (70.5%) of 193"); BRCA1 8.5/11.1%, BRCA2 2.7/4.3%, PALB2 1.2%.

claims.claim: TMB 10 or more in 4 to 5% of early and 18% of pretreated metastatic disease;
claims.note: cBioPortal TCGA 5/123 (4.1%) and Barroso-Sousa 2020 "Hypermutated tumors ... (5%)"; Barroso-Sousa CCR 2020 "High TMB (18%)" of 62 metastatic TNBC.

claims.claim: MSI-high 0 to 2%.
claims.note: Kurata 2020 "2 (0.9%) MSI-H" of 228; Ren 2021 none of 195 by PCR; Staaf ~1.7%.

claims.claim: Lehmann's TNBCtype-4: BL1 35% (TP53 92%, unstable, platinum-sensitive, pCR 41%), BL2 22% (growth-factor signalling, pCR 18%), mesenchymal 25% (EMT, immune-cold, PRC2-silenced MHC-I, lung-tropic) and LAR 16% (AR-driven, PIK3CA 55%, AKT1 13%, bone-tropic, pCR 29%, worst prognosis, modest AR-antagonist benefit); the immunomodulatory signal (21 to 25%) is the lymphocyte infiltrate and carries the best prognosis.
claims.note: Lehmann 2016 full text: "TNBCtype-4 resulted in a distribution of 35% BL1, 22% BL2, 25% M, 16% LAR"; pCR 41/18/29%; original call "21% IM"; Bareche 2018: BL1 TP53 92%, LAR PIK3CA 55%, AKT1 13%, LAR worse (HR 1.47), IM better (HR 0.68), IM 25%.

claims.claim: Burstein's BLIS and BLIA split basal-like disease by immune state; the FUSCC scheme repeats the four-way logic in 465 Chinese patients.
claims.note: Jiang 2019 (FUSCC): 465 Chinese TNBCs classified into four transcriptome subtypes (record summary of the paper).

claims.claim: By PAM50, 76% of TNBC is basal-like and 15% HER2-enriched.
claims.note: Bareche 2018 full text: "basal-like (76%), followed by HER2-enriched (15%)".

claims.claim: SP142 IC 1% or more (IMpassion130): 41 to 51%.
claims.note: Rugo 2021: SP142 IC>=1% "46.4%"; Sigurjonsdottir 2023 SP142 50.9%; IMpassion130 PD-L1-positive subgroup about 41% (Schmid 2018).

claims.claim: 22C3 CPS 10 or more (KEYNOTE-355, ASCENT-04): 27 to 38%.
claims.note: Sigurjonsdottir 2023 "22C3 CPS >= 10 ... 27.2%"; Keytruda label: KEYNOTE-355 "38% had tumor PD-L1 expression CPS >=10".

claims.claim: Stromal TILs average 23%, are 60% or more in about 30%, and predict chemotherapy response and survival with or without chemotherapy; spatial immune classes (immunoreactive, immune-cold B7-H4-high, stroma-restricted) refine the score.
