claims.note: NG101 1.3.6: women under 50 with triple-negative breast cancer, including no family history.

claims.claim: CG164's 10 percent carrier-probability rule for everyone else.
claims.note: CG164 1.5.13: combined BRCA1 and BRCA2 carrier probability "10% or more".

claims.claim: Surveillance and risk reduction for BRCA carriers (before any cancer): Annual MRI from 30 to 49 and annual mammography from 40 to 69 for known BRCA1 or BRCA2 carriers (MRI sensitivity 77 percent against 40 percent for mammography in MARIBS); bilateral risk-reducing mastectomy for a small proportion of women from high-risk families after genetic counselling, cutting breast cancer risk by about 90 percent; tamoxifen or anastrozole are offered to women at high risk in general but did not reduce ER-negative breast cancer in the prevention trials.
claims.note: CG164 MRI 30-49 and mammography 40-69 for BRCA carriers; MARIBS 77% vs 40%; PROSE "approximately 90%"; IBIS-I and P-1 no effect on ER-negative.

claims.claim: Chemotherapy before or after surgery: For most triple-negative cancers larger than 2 cm or with involved nodes, chemotherapy comes first (neoadjuvant): it can shrink the cancer so that breast-conserving surgery replaces a mastectomy, and the pathology report at surgery then shows how well it worked, which guides the treatment given afterwards.
claims.note: KEYNOTE-522 eligibility T1c N1-2 or T2-4 N0-2 (Pusztai 2024 abstract "stage T1c/N1-2 or T2-4/N0-2"), i.e. over 2 cm or node-positive.

claims.claim: NICE NG101 (2025) says where neoadjuvant chemotherapy is indicated for triple-negative disease, offer a regimen containing a platinum, a taxane and an anthracycline, and discuss the trade-off: 85 rather than 81 out of 100 alive at 3 years with a platinum, against more neutropenic sepsis, low blood counts and anaemia.
claims.note: NG101 1.8.1 [2025]: platinum, taxane and anthracycline; table 3: "81 out of 100 survived ... 85 out of 100 survived" with minimum 3-year follow-up.

claims.claim: No PD-L1 test is needed at this stage: the trial's gain in complete responses (64.8% against 51.2%) and in survival (86.6% against 81.7% alive at 5 years) was seen whatever the PD-L1 result.
claims.note: KEYNOTE-522: pCR 64.8% vs 51.2% (NEJM 2020); 60-month OS 86.6% vs 81.7% (NEJM 2024); benefit regardless of PD-L1 (ASCO 2026 final analysis report).

claims.claim: Residual disease is graded by residual cancer burden (RCB I to III); in triple-negative disease 10-year relapse-free survival fell from 86% after a complete response to 81%, 55% and 23% across the classes (Symmans 2017).
claims.note: Symmans 2017: TN 10-year RFS 86%, 81%, 55%, 23%.

claims.claim: For residual disease with a germline BRCA1 or BRCA2 variant, NICE TA886 recommends a year of olaparib (OlympiA: 4-year invasive disease-free survival 82.7% against 75.4%, with a survival gain).
claims.note: OlympiA OS analysis (Ann Oncol 2022, linked from the olympia record): "Four-year IDFS ... 82.7% versus 75.4%", OS HR 0.68 significant; NICE TA886.

claims.claim: Without a BRCA variant, six to eight cycles of capecitabine is the usual offer (CREATE-X: 5-year survival 78.8% against 70.3% in triple-negative disease; hand-foot syndrome in 73%).
claims.note: CREATE-X: TN "overall survival rate was 78.8% versus 70.3%"; "hand-foot syndrome ... occurred in 73.4%".

claims.claim: Two attempts to do better than capecitabine failed: ECOG-ACRIN EA1131 closed for futility, with platinum neither superior nor non-inferior to capecitabine in basal-like residual disease, and BRE12-158 found genomically directed therapy no better than the physician's choice (two-year disease-free survival 56.6 against 62.4 percent), though its post-surgical circulating tumour DNA did predict outcome.
claims.note: BRE12-158 JCO 2022: "2-year DFS ... 56.6% ... for arm A versus 62.4% ... for arm B".

claims.claim: The armpit is staged with a sentinel node biopsy (1 to 3 nodes); removing all the nodes raises the risk of lymphoedema and is reserved for involved nodes that need clearing.
claims.note: Macmillan lymph node page (record link): "surgeons remove the smallest number of lymph nodes possible (usually 1 to 3)".

claims.claim: NICE NG101 (2023): offer 26 Gy in 5 fractions over 1 week when the lymph nodes are not being treated (FAST-Forward: non-inferior to 40 Gy in 15 at 5 years), consider 40 Gy in 15 fractions over 3 weeks after implant reconstruction or where 3 weeks suits better, and offer 40 Gy in 15 fractions whenever regional nodes are irradiated (START-B).
claims.note: NG101 1.13.13 "Offer 26 Gy in 5 fractions over 1 week ... without regional lymph node irradiation" [2023]; 40 Gy in 15 considered/offered; FAST-Forward 5-year non-inferiority.

claims.claim: Options: embryo or egg freezing (about 2 to 3 weeks of ovarian stimulation, with random-start protocols to avoid delay), ovarian tissue freezing at a growing number of UK centres, and contraception during treatment because chemotherapy can damage eggs.
claims.note: CRUK fertility page (linked from fertility-preservation): egg collection "takes about 2 to 3 weeks".

claims.claim: Genetic testing and what a BRCA result means for your family: NICE NG101 says offer BRCA1 and BRCA2 testing to women under 50 with triple-negative breast cancer even with no family history;
claims.note: NG101 1.3.6: under 50 with triple-negative breast cancer including no family history.

claims.claim: Breast Cancer Now says anyone diagnosed under 60 should be offered a referral to discuss testing, and the NHS test directory criteria that NICE points to for PARP inhibitor eligibility (R444.1) may make people over 60 eligible too.
claims.note: Breast Cancer Now (record link): offered testing if "diagnosed with triple negative breast cancer before the age of 60".

claims.claim: Testing is free on the NHS when a hospital specialist refers you, results take about 1 to 3 months, and a genetic counsellor helps with what the result means.
claims.note: Breast Cancer Now: "Your results will usually be available within 1 to 3 months".

claims.claim: A pathogenic variant: opens olaparib after chemotherapy for residual disease (NICE TA886) and a PARP inhibitor in metastatic disease; raises the question of risk-reducing surgery to the other breast and the ovaries, managed by a multidisciplinary team with counselling first (NICE CG164); and means each child has a 1 in 2 chance of carrying it, so relatives can be offered predictive testing.
claims.note: Macmillan BRCA page (record link): "a 1 in 2 (50%) chance of passing the variant to each of their children".

claims.claim: First treatment for metastatic disease: the tests that decide: Three results decide the first treatment for cancer that has spread, so ask that all three are back before the choice is made, ideally on a fresh biopsy because receptors can change: PD-L1 combined positive score (CPS 10 or more opens pembrolizumab with chemotherapy, NICE TA801, or with sacituzumab govitecan), germline BRCA status (a PARP inhibitor, olaparib or talazoparib), and HER2 score (1+ or 2+ without amplification, HER2-low, opens trastuzumab deruxtecan after chemotherapy).
claims.note: KEYNOTE-355 CPS>=10 population and TA801; HER2-low IHC 1+ or 2+ non-amplified (DESTINY-Breast04).

claims.claim: Trastuzumab deruxtecan: interstitial lung disease in about 15% (2.2% fatal in the pooled analysis), mostly in the first year, so any new cough, breathlessness or fever is reported immediately; also sickness and low counts.

claims.claim: Brain metastases: radiosurgery, whole-brain radiotherapy, surgery and drugs: Triple-negative breast cancer spreads to the brain more often than other breast subtypes: about 29% of people with metastatic disease in a 433-patient series (25% within two years), and 46% before death in an older 116-patient series.

claims.note: Brown JAMA 2016: cognitive deterioration at 3 months "40/63 patients [63.5%]" vs "44/48 patients [91.7%]"; OS HR 1.02, no difference.

claims.claim: Choice of neoadjuvant backbone: the platinum debate: Carboplatin raises pathological complete response in every trial (GeparSixto 53.2 versus 36.9 percent, BrighTNess 58 versus 31, CALGB 40603) and improved disease-free survival in GeparSixto (hazard ratio 0.56) and event-free survival in BrighTNess (0.57) but not long-term outcomes in CALGB 40603 (not powered); it is part of the KEYNOTE-522 regimen and is standard in the UK.

claims.note: Couch 2015: "11.2% had mutations in the BRCA1 ... and BRCA2" genes.

claims.claim: Licensed in the US (2022) and EU (2023) for HER2-low regardless of hormone receptor status; not recommended by NICE (TA992, 29 July 2024; rapid review in development), so not commissioned in England.
claims.note: NICE TA992 page now reads "This guidance has been updated and replaced by NICE technology appraisal guidance 1197"; TA1197 (Published 07 October 2026) 1.1: "Trastuzumab deruxtecan can be used ... as an option to treat HER2-low metastatic or unresectable breast cancer ... after chemotherapy in the metastatic setting, or recurrence ... within 6 months", funded via the Cancer Drugs Fund until routine commissioning.
claims.fixed: tnbc-treatment.ts HER2-low row: replaced "not recommended by NICE (TA992 ...), so not commissioned in England" with TA1197 (7 October 2026) recommendation; guideline version and url now TA1197 (SRC.nice1197 added); the matching open problem on the tnbc record updated

claims.claim: Less often found by screening: 29 percent of triple-negative cancers against 48 percent of hormone receptor-positive, HER2-negative cancers presented through an abnormal screening mammogram in US cancer centres (Lin 2012)
claims.note: Lin 2012: "29% vs 48%" abnormal screening mammogram presentation.

claims.claim: Referral rules: an unexplained breast lump at 30 or over, or nipple discharge, retraction or other change in one nipple at 50 or over, goes on the suspected cancer pathway; skin changes or an unexplained axillary lump at 30 or over should prompt the same consideration (NICE NG12 1.4)
claims.note: NG12 1.4.1: 30 and over with unexplained breast lump, or 50 and over with discharge, retraction or other changes in one nipple; 1.4.2 consider for skin changes, or 30 and over with unexplained axillary lump.

claims.claim: Triple-negative means ER under 1 percent, PR under 1 percent (1 to 10 percent is ER Low Positive and behaves the same way) and HER2 0, 1+ or 2+ without gene amplification (ASCO/CAP 2020 and 2018)
claims.note: Allison 2020 ER <1% negative, 1-10% ER Low Positive; Wolff 2018 HER2 0, 1+, 2+ non-amplified negative.

claims.claim: HER2 0 versus 1+ is reported with a comment because the HER2-low category qualifies for trastuzumab deruxtecan later (ASCO-CAP 2023)
claims.note: Wolff 2023 reporting comment for IHC 0 versus 1+.

claims.claim: Germline BRCA1 and BRCA2 testing is offered to women under 50 with triple-negative disease even without a family history (NICE NG101 1.3.6); the familial cancer guideline adds a 10 percent carrier-probability rule for everyone else (CG164)
claims.note: NG101 1.3.6 under 50; CG164 10% carrier probability.

claims.claim: Nodes: cN before treatment, pN after surgery; pN1 one to three axillary nodes, pN2 four to nine, pN3 ten or more or infraclavicular, supraclavicular or axillary plus internal mammary nodes (Cancer Research UK)
claims.note: CRUK TNM page: pN1 1 to 3, pN2 4 to 9, pN3 10 or more, infraclavicular, supraclavicular or internal mammary combinations.

claims.claim: Stage 1 is T1 N0 (1B with micrometastases); stage 2 is T2 N0, T0 to T2 N1 or T3 N0; stage 3 is N2, T3 N1, T4 or N3; stage 4 is any spread beyond the regional nodes (Cancer Research UK)
claims.note: CRUK number stages: 1A T1 N0; 2A T0-T1 N1 or T2 N0; 2B T2 N1 or T3 N0; 3A N2 or T3 N1; 3B T4; 3C any N3; 4 M1.

claims.claim: Brain metastases (up to 30-45% of metastatic TNBC) remain undertreated;
claims.note: Lin 2008 (record link): 46% developed CNS metastases before death; 433-patient series 29% (linked from the palliation term); "up to 30-45%" spans these.

claims.claim: No UK registry publishes triple-negative incidence or survival as a subtype; the UK share rests on Cancer Research UK's around 15 percent and on cohorts such as POSH, while SEER publishes rates by receptor status every year.
claims.note: CRUK TN page "around 15%"; CRUK publishes no TN subtype incidence; SEER publishes rates by HR/HER2 subtype.

claims.claim: ER 1 to 10 percent tumours behave like triple-negative disease yet are excluded from most triple-negative trials, so the evidence for immunotherapy and ADCs in that band is thin (Yoder 2022;
claims.note: Allison 2020 ER 1-10% Low Positive; Yoder 2022 and Acs 2024 show TNBC-like behaviour.

claims.claim: PD-L1 assays disagree on about a quarter of tumours (SP142 46 percent positive, 22C3 73 percent, concordance 69 percent in IMpassion130;
claims.note: Rugo 2021: SP142 46.4%, 22C3 IC 73.1%, "concordance between SP142 and SP263 and 22C3 was 69.2% and 68.7%" — so the assays disagreed on about 31%, a third, not "about a quarter".
claims.fixed: tnbc-evidence.ts open problem: "disagree on about a quarter of tumours" -> "about a third"

claims.claim: 27 percent CPS 10 or more against 51 percent SP142-positive in the Swedish early cohort); only 22C3 combined positive score of 10 has an approved drug attached, laboratories are not harmonised, and no assay predicts benefit from the first-line antibody-drug conjugate plus pembrolizumab combinations.
claims.note: Sigurjonsdottir 2023: SP142 IC>=1% 50.9%, 22C3 CPS>=10 27.2%.

claims.claim: The disparity is measured in the United States and was measured once in the UK (POSH, women under 41, recruited to 2008);
claims.note: POSH: women aged 40 or under, recruited 24 January 2000 to 24 January 2008 (Copson 2018).

claims.claim: AKT inhibition failed twice in biomarker-selected metastatic disease (IPATunity130, CAPItello-290) despite positive phase 2 trials, so PIK3CA, AKT1 and PTEN alterations, present in a fifth to a quarter of tumours, are not actionable in triple-negative breast cancer today;
claims.note: Molecular table: PI3K-AKT pathway alteration 20% (PAKT, 28/140) to 26.7% (MSK) — "a fifth to a quarter".

claims.claim: Because there is no receptor to block, chemotherapy has carried the curative burden, and it is given before surgery whenever the tumour is over 2 cm or the nodes are involved, both to shrink it and because the response at surgery, measured as pathological complete response or residual cancer burden, is the strongest predictor of relapse.
claims.note: KEYNOTE-522 eligibility (T1c N1-2 or T2-4 N0-2, i.e. over 2 cm or node-positive) confirmed in Pusztai 2024; Symmans/Cortazar on pCR and RCB.

claims.claim: Platinum added to a taxane and anthracycline raised complete response rates in GeparSixto, CALGB 40603 and BrighTNess, and tumours under 1 cm without node involvement often need no chemotherapy at all, with high tumour-infiltrating lymphocytes marking a group whose outcome is excellent regardless.
claims.note: GeparSixto, CALGB 40603 and BrighTNess pCR gains are correct (read), but the "under 1 cm without node involvement often need no chemotherapy" threshold has no source on the tnbc-early record (four NEJM trial papers); NCCN/ESMO guidelines not readable by script.
claims.fixed: breast-subtypes.ts tnbc-early summary: "tumours under 1 cm without node involvement" -> "the smallest tumours without node involvement"

claims.claim: It randomised 1,174 patients with stage II or III disease to pembrolizumab or placebo with carboplatin and paclitaxel then an anthracycline and cyclophosphamide before surgery, followed by pembrolizumab or placebo for nine cycles after.
claims.note: KEYNOTE-522: "1174 patients", stage II or III, paclitaxel and carboplatin then AC/EC, adjuvant pembrolizumab or placebo "for up to nine cycles".

claims.claim: Pathological complete response rose from 51.2 to 64.8 percent, event-free survival improved (hazard ratio 0.63) and, unusually for a neoadjuvant trial, overall survival did too, with the seven-year update showing 85.1 against 77.2 percent alive; the FDA approved the regimen in July 2021 and it is given whatever the PD-L1 score.
claims.note: pCR 51.2 to 64.8 and EFS HR 0.63 are in KEYNOTE-522 NEJM 2020 (on record). The seven-year 85.1 vs 77.2 and the July 2021 FDA approval were not in any record source; read in raw text: OncLive ASCO 2026 report "The 7-year overall survival (OS) rates ... were 85.1% ... and 77.2%"; ASCO Post "On July 26, the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved pembrolizumab ... for high-risk, early-stage triple-negative breast cancer".
claims.fixed: breast-subtypes.ts tnbc-early: added links to the OncLive ASCO 2026 KEYNOTE-522 final-analysis report and the ASCO Post report of the 26 July 2021 FDA approval (figures unchanged, verified)

claims.claim: IMpassion031 showed atezolizumab raises complete response in the same setting (58 against 41 percent) but never became a standard.
claims.note: IMpassion031 not linked on tnbc-early. Lancet 2020 (read): pCR "95 (58% ...)" vs "69 (41% ...)".
claims.fixed: breast-subtypes.ts tnbc-early: added the IMpassion031 Lancet 2020 link (figures unchanged)

claims.claim: Women with residual disease and a germline BRCA mutation take olaparib for a year: OlympiA randomised 1,836 such patients with HER2-negative disease, about four in five triple-negative, and improved invasive disease-free survival (hazard ratio 0.58) and overall survival (hazard ratio 0.72).
claims.note: OlympiA NEJM 2021 (the record link): 1836 patients, IDFS HR 0.58, OS HR 0.68 (not significant at that interim); OS analysis Ann Oncol 2022: "hazard ratio 0.68"; Lynparza label 82% TNBC. No source on the record gives OS HR 0.72.
claims.fixed: breast-subtypes.ts tnbc-early: "overall survival (hazard ratio 0.72)" -> "at the 3.5-year analysis, overall survival (hazard ratio 0.68)"; added OlympiA Ann Oncol 2022 OS link

claims.claim: Others are offered six to eight cycles of capecitabine on the strength of CREATE-X, a Japanese trial of 910 women with residual HER2-negative disease in which five-year disease-free survival rose from 67.6 to 74.1 percent with the largest survival gain in the triple-negative group.
claims.note: CREATE-X: "910 patients", DFS "74.1% vs. 67.6%", TN OS 78.8 vs 70.3 (HR 0.52) against all-patient OS HR 0.59.

claims.claim: Most of the roughly 200,000 triple-negative breast cancers diagnosed each year are found before they have spread; relapses cluster in the first three years, so what happens around surgery decides most outcomes.
claims.note: "roughly 200,000 triple-negative breast cancers ... each year" has no source on the tnbc-early record and is below the 243,000-365,000 that 10-15% of GLOBOCAN 2024 2.43 million gives. "first three years" from Dent 2007 ("peaked at approximately 3 years").
claims.fixed: breast-subtypes.ts tnbc-early burden: removed "the roughly 200,000"; added the Dent 2007 link for the three-year relapse peak

claims.claim: Stage I, tumours 2 cm or less without node involvement: Surgery with sentinel node biopsy and radiotherapy; chemotherapy for tumours over 1 cm, often omitted below that, with tumour-infiltrating lymphocytes guiding de-escalation trials.
claims.note: The "over 1 cm" chemotherapy threshold has no source on the tnbc-early record (no links reach it; NCCN not readable).
claims.fixed: breast-subtypes.ts tnbc-early stage I row: "chemotherapy for tumours over 1 cm, often omitted below that" -> "chemotherapy for most, often omitted for the smallest tumours"

claims.claim: At relapse the tumour is retested, because receptors can change, and three results steer treatment: PD-L1 by combined positive score (10 or more in roughly four in ten patients), germline BRCA status and the HER2 immunohistochemistry score that identifies HER2-low disease.
claims.note: Keytruda label: KEYNOTE-355 "38% had tumor PD-L1 expression CPS >=10" (roughly four in ten).

claims.claim: IMpassion130 showed atezolizumab with nab-paclitaxel delays progression in PD-L1-positive disease and won an accelerated approval that was withdrawn in 2021 when IMpassion131 with paclitaxel failed.
claims.note: No IMpassion130/131 or withdrawal source on the tnbc-metastatic record. Roche 27 August 2021 (read): "decision to voluntarily withdraw the US accelerated approval for Tecentriq ... in combination with ... nab-paclitaxel", after IMpassion131 did not meet its primary endpoint.
claims.fixed: breast-subtypes.ts tnbc-metastatic: added the Roche 27 August 2021 release link (text unchanged)

claims.claim: KEYNOTE-355 (847 patients) showed pembrolizumab with chemotherapy extends survival in tumours with a combined positive score of 10 or more (hazard ratio 0.73) and became the first-line standard for that group.
claims.note: KEYNOTE-355 NEJM 2022: "A total of 847 patients", CPS-10 OS HR 0.73.

claims.claim: The TROP2 antibody-drug conjugates then moved into the first line: ASCENT-04 showed sacituzumab govitecan with pembrolizumab beats chemotherapy with pembrolizumab in PD-L1-positive disease, ASCENT-03 showed sacituzumab govitecan beats chemotherapy in PD-L1-negative disease, and TROPION-Breast02 (644 patients) showed datopotamab deruxtecan extends overall survival from 18.7 to 23.7 months in patients who cannot have immunotherapy, the first first-line antibody-drug conjugate to do so; all three were approved in 2026.
claims.note: TROPION-Breast02 and the 2026 approvals were not sourced on the tnbc-metastatic record. Ann Oncol 2026 (read): "644 patients", OS "23.7 months ... and 18.7 months"; Trodelvy label 06/2026 with ASCENT-03/04 and Datroway label 05/2026 with TROPION-Breast02.
claims.fixed: breast-subtypes.ts tnbc-metastatic: added TROPION-Breast02 (Ann Oncol 2026) and the Trodelvy and Datroway DailyMed label links (figures unchanged, verified)

claims.claim: ASCENT (529 patients with at least two prior lines) showed sacituzumab govitecan nearly doubles survival against chemotherapy (12.1 against 6.7 months, hazard ratio 0.48), the first antibody-drug conjugate approval in triple-negative disease in 2020.
claims.note: Bardia NEJM 2021: 12.1 vs 6.7 months, HR 0.48 are for the "468 patients without brain metastases"; Trodelvy label, all 529 randomised: "Median OS ... 11.8 ... 6.9", HR 0.51. The page attached the subgroup figures to all 529.
claims.fixed: breast-subtypes.ts tnbc-metastatic: now "(12.1 against 6.7 months, hazard ratio 0.48, in the 468 without brain metastases; 11.8 against 6.9 months, hazard ratio 0.51, in all 529)"

claims.claim: For germline BRCA carriers OlympiAD (302 patients) and EMBRACA (431) showed olaparib and talazoparib extend progression-free survival over chemotherapy (7.0 against 4.2 months, hazard ratio 0.58;
claims.note: OlympiAD 302, 7.0 vs 4.2, HR 0.58 correct (record link). EMBRACA (431) not linked on the record; NEJM 2018 (read): "431 patients".
claims.fixed: breast-subtypes.ts tnbc-metastatic: added the EMBRACA NEJM 2018 link (figures unchanged)

claims.claim: 8.6 against 5.6 months, hazard ratio 0.54) without a significant survival gain.
claims.note: EMBRACA NEJM 2018 (read, now linked): "8.6 months vs. 5.6 months; hazard ratio ... 0.54"; final OS HR 0.848 not significant.
claims.fixed: breast-subtypes.ts tnbc-metastatic: added the EMBRACA NEJM 2018 link (figures unchanged)

claims.claim: Worldwide there are 2,434,087 new breast cancers and 693,660 deaths a year, second for cases among all cancers and fourth for deaths (GLOBOCAN 2024).
claims.note: Fact sheet headed "GLOBOCAN 2024": Breast incidence rank 2, cases 2 434 087; mortality rank 4, deaths 693 660. Page names GLOBOCAN 2024.

claims.claim: In the UK there are 59,413 new cases a year, about 59,000 in females and 420 in males, 15 percent of all cancers, and 11,200 deaths a year (Cancer Research UK).
claims.note: CRUK: "59,413 new cases of breast cancer each year, 2019, 2021-2022, UK"; "15% of all new cancer cases ... around 59,000 new cases in females and around 420 new cases in males"; "11,200 deaths from breast cancer, 2022-2024, UK".

claims.claim: In England in 2022, 85 percent of cases with a known stage were stage I or II.
claims.note: CRUK: "In 2022, 85% (around 35,000) of breast cancer cases with a known stage were diagnosed at an early stage (I & II) in England."

claims.claim: By receptor subtype, in American women diagnosed between 2016 and 2022, five-year relative survival was 95.8 percent for hormone receptor-positive HER2-negative disease, 92.2 percent for hormone receptor-positive HER2-positive, 87.0 percent for hormone receptor-negative HER2-positive and 78.7 percent for triple-negative disease, against 91.9 percent for all breast cancer (SEER 21).
claims.note: SEER 21 (excluding IL) 2016-2022 five-year relative survival: HR+/HER2- 95.8%, HR+/HER2+ 92.2%, HR-/HER2+ 87.0%, HR-/HER2- 78.7%, total 91.9%.

claims.claim: By stage the same source gives, for hormone receptor-positive HER2-negative disease, 100.0 percent localised, 91.1 percent regional and 38.1 percent distant; for triple-negative disease 92.8, 68.3 and 14.9 percent.
claims.note: SEER stage table: HR+/HER2- 100.0% localised, 91.1% regional, 38.1% distant; HR-/HER2- 92.8%, 68.3%, 14.9%.

claims.claim: In the UK, 76.6 percent of women survive breast cancer for ten years or more (2018 prediction, Cancer Research UK), and mortality rates have fallen 46 percent since the early 1970s.
claims.note: CRUK: "76.6% females survive breast cancer for 10 or more years, 2018, UK"; mortality page: "decreased by almost half (46%) in the UK since the early 1970s".

claims.claim: Survival is not evenly distributed: five-year survival in England is 82.6 percent in the most deprived group against 89.6 percent in the least (2018 to 2022).
claims.note: CRUK survival: "(82.6%) women diagnosed with breast cancer in the most deprived group in England survive ... five years or more, compared with 9 in 10 (89.6%) in the least deprived group (2018-2022)".

claims.claim: The single largest lever on all of these numbers is the stage at which the cancer is found, which is why 85 percent of English cases being diagnosed at stage I or II matters more than any of the treatment comparisons on the pages below.
claims.note: CRUK: 85% of English cases with a known stage diagnosed at stage I or II in 2022.

claims.claim: Five-year survival above 90 percent in early disease across high-income countries, driven by screening, endocrine therapy and HER2-targeted drugs.
claims.note: No source on the record covers "across high-income countries"; the record's SEER subtype page says "among those with localized disease, the 5-year relative survival was greater than 92 percent regardless of subtype" (SEER 21, 2016-2022), a US figure.
claims.fixed: Reworded to "Five-year relative survival above 92 percent for localised disease in the United States, whatever the receptor subtype (SEER 21, 2016 to 2022)".

claims.claim: Survival is the same either way and has been for twenty years: NSABP B-06 found a hazard ratio for death of 0.97 (0.83 to 1.14) for lumpectomy with irradiation against mastectomy, Milan I found death from any cause of 41.7 against 41.2 percent at twenty years, and EORTC 10801 found a hazard ratio of 1.11 (0.94 to 1.33) at a median 22.1 years.
claims.note: NSABP B-06 NEJM 2002: HR for death lumpectomy+irradiation vs total mastectomy 0.97 (0.83 to 1.14). Milan I: death from all causes 41.7% (conserving) vs 41.2% (radical mastectomy). EORTC 10801: median 22.1 years, time to death HR 1.11 (0.94-1.33).

claims.claim: NICE NG101 recommendation 1.4.3 offers further surgery when invasive cancer or ductal carcinoma in situ is present at the radial margin (0 mm), and recommendation 1.4.5, new in 2024, considers it when tumour cells lie within 1 mm of but not at the radial margin.
claims.note: NG101 1.4.3 "radial margins ('tumour on ink'; 0 mm). [2018]"; 1.4.5 "within 1 mm of, but not at, the radial margins ... [2024]".

claims.claim: The threshold for invasive cancer was lowered from 2 mm to 1 mm because the evidence could not separate 1 to 2 mm from more than 2 mm on local recurrence, and repeated operations harm appearance and self-image.
claims.note: NG101 2024 rationale: "the evidence could not differentiate between greater than 1 mm to 2 mm compared with greater than 2 mm"; repeated surgeries "negatively affect breast appearance ... view of themselves".

claims.claim: For ductal carcinoma in situ alone the 2 mm threshold is retained (recommendation 1.4.4).
claims.note: NG101 1.4.4: DCIS without invasive cancer, "within 2 mm of, but not at, the radial margins"; rationale "retain the threshold of 2 mm".

claims.claim: NSABP B-32 randomised 5,611 women and found eight-year overall survival of 90.3 percent with sentinel node biopsy alone against 91.8 percent with added clearance (hazard ratio 1.20, 0.96 to 1.50);
claims.note: Lancet Oncol 2010: "5611 women were randomly assigned ... 3989 had pathologically negative SLN"; OS analysed in the 3986 SLN-negative patients: 8-year OS 91.8% (ALND) vs 90.3% (SLN alone), HR 1.20 (0.96-1.50). The sentence applied the SLN-negative analysis to all 5,611.
claims.fixed: Added "in the 3,986 whose sentinel nodes were clear" before the survival figures.

claims.claim: ALMANAC measured the gain, with lymphoedema at one year falling from 13 to 5 percent and sensory loss from 31 to 11 percent.
claims.note: ALMANAC JNCI 2006 at 12 months: lymphedema 5% vs 13%, sensory loss 11% vs 31%.

claims.claim: In selected patients the sentinel node itself can now be omitted: SOUND (tumours up to 2 cm, clear axillary ultrasound) and INSEMA (T1 and T2, breast-conserving surgery) both showed non-inferiority, with axillary recurrence in INSEMA of 1.0 against 0.3 percent.
claims.note: SOUND: BC up to 2 cm and negative axillary ultrasound, non-inferior. INSEMA: T1 or T2, breast-conserving surgery, non-inferior; axillary recurrence 1.0% vs 0.3%.

claims.claim: Micrometastases need nothing further either: IBCSG 23-01 found ten-year disease-free survival of 76.8 percent without clearance against 74.9 percent with it, and lymphoedema of 4 against 13 percent (recommendation 1.4.14).
claims.note: IBCSG 23-01 Lancet Oncol 2018: 10-year DFS 76.8% (no dissection) vs 74.9%; lymphoedema 4% vs 13%. NG101 1.4.14 micrometastases: no further axillary treatment.

claims.claim: For one or two macrometastases, NICE recommendation 1.4.12 offers axillary clearance or axillary radiotherapy and recommendation 1.4.13 asks for a discussion of having neither after breast-conserving surgery with whole-breast radiotherapy and systemic therapy.
claims.note: NG101 1.4.12 "1 or more sentinel lymph node macrometastasis" (clearance or radiotherapy); 1.4.13 "1 or 2 sentinel lymph node macrometastases" after breast-conserving surgery with whole-breast radiotherapy and systemic therapy.

claims.claim: The evidence behind that discussion is Z0011 (ten-year overall survival 86.3 against 83.6 percent) and SENOMAC (five-year recurrence-free survival 89.7 against 88.7 percent in 2,540 patients including mastectomy and T3 disease).
claims.note: Z0011 JAMA 2017: 10-year OS 86.3% vs 83.6%. SENOMAC NEJM 2024: per-protocol 2540, T1 to T3, 5-year RFS 89.7% vs 88.7%. (Mastectomy eligibility is from the trial design; the abstract states T1-T3.)

claims.claim: Where the axilla is treated, AMAROS makes radiotherapy the gentler choice: ten-year axillary recurrence of 1.82 against 0.93 percent, with lymphoedema halved at 11.9 against 24.5 percent.
claims.note: AMAROS JCO 2023: 10-year ARR 0.93% after ALND and 1.82% after ART; lymphedema 24.5% v 11.9% (5-year).

claims.claim: The axilla after chemotherapy given before surgery: Sentinel node biopsy after chemotherapy is unreliable on its own: ACOSOG Z1071 found a false-negative rate of 12.6 percent against a pre-specified threshold of 10 percent.
claims.note: ACOSOG Z1071 JAMA 2013: "FNR of 12.6%"; threshold 10%.

claims.claim: The fix is targeted axillary dissection, marking the biopsied node before chemotherapy and removing that node as well as the sentinel nodes, which brought the false-negative rate to 1.4 percent when combined with sentinel node dissection and 2.0 percent as a formal procedure.
claims.note: Caudle JCO 2016: adding clipped node "reduced the FNR to 1.4%"; "TAD ... 85 patients, with an FNR of 2.0%".

claims.claim: If the nodes are pathologically clear afterwards, NSABP B-51 found that regional nodal irradiation adds nothing (hazard ratio 0.88, 0.60 to 1.28, p=0.51).
claims.note: NSABP B-51 NEJM 2025: "hazard ratio, 0.88; 95% confidence interval, 0.60 to 1.28; P = 0.51" in ypN0 patients.

claims.claim: The Early Breast Cancer Trialists' Collaborative Group overview of 10,801 women in 17 trials found radiotherapy cut the ten-year risk of any first recurrence from 35.0 to 19.3 percent and the fifteen-year risk of breast cancer death from 25.2 to 21.4 percent, with about one death avoided by year fifteen for every four recurrences avoided by year ten.
claims.note: EBCTCG Lancet 2011: 10,801 women in 17 trials; 10-year any first recurrence 35.0% to 19.3%; 15-year breast cancer death 25.2% to 21.4%; one death avoided by year 15 for every four recurrences avoided by year 10.

claims.claim: A boost of 16 Gy to the tumour bed is offered where the risk of local recurrence is high (recommendation 1.13.17): EORTC 22881-10882 found twenty-year recurrence of 12.0 against 16.4 percent with no survival gain and severe fibrosis of 5.2 against 1.8 percent.
claims.note: EORTC 22881 Lancet Oncol 2015: 16 Gy boost; 20-year IBTR 12.0% (boost) vs 16.4%; severe fibrosis 5.2% vs 1.8%; no OS effect. But NICE NG101 1.13.17 offers "an external beam boost" and sets no dose: the sentence attributed the trial's 16 Gy to the NICE recommendation.
claims.fixed: Moved 16 Gy from the NICE clause to the trial: "A boost to the tumour bed is offered ... (recommendation 1.13.17): EORTC 22881-10882, which gave 16 Gy, found ...".

claims.claim: Dose and schedule: In England, 26 Gy in five fractions over one week for partial-breast, whole-breast or chest-wall radiotherapy without nodal irradiation (NICE NG101 recommendation 1.13.13), and 40 Gy in fifteen fractions over three weeks when the regional nodes are treated (recommendation 1.13.16) or where a diagnosis increases radiosensitivity, an implant-based reconstruction has been done, or a three-week course is simply more acceptable (recommendation 1.13.14).
claims.note: NG101 1.13.13 26 Gy in 5 fractions over 1 week without regional nodal irradiation; 1.13.16 40 Gy in 15 fractions with nodal irradiation; 1.13.14 radiosensitivity, implant-based reconstruction, or 3 weeks more acceptable.

claims.claim: The radiobiology came from three British trials: START-A held the treatment time constant and varied the fraction size, START-B established 40 Gy in fifteen, FAST estimated the alpha to beta ratio at 2.7 Gy and so predicted a five-fraction equivalent of 28 Gy, and FAST-Forward tested 26 Gy in five fractions in 4,096 women and found five-year recurrence of 1.4 against 2.1 percent.
claims.note: START Lancet Oncol 2013: START-A 41.6/39 Gy in 13 fractions vs 50 Gy in 25, all over 5 weeks; START-B 40 Gy in 15. FAST JCO 2020: alpha/beta 2.7 Gy, 5-fraction isoeffective 28 Gy. FAST-Forward Lancet 2020: 4096 patients; 5-year IBTR 2.1% after 40 Gy, absolute difference -0.7% for 26 Gy (1.4%).

claims.claim: Deep inspiratory breath hold is used for left-sided cancers to lower the heart dose (recommendation 1.13.2), because major coronary events rise by 7.4 percent per gray of mean heart dose with no threshold.
claims.note: NG101 1.13.2 deep inspiratory breath-hold for left-sided cancer. Darby NEJM 2013: "increased linearly with the mean dose to the heart by 7.4% per gray ... no apparent threshold".

claims.claim: Treating less than the whole breast: Partial-breast radiotherapy is considered for women who have had breast-conserving surgery for invasive cancer excluding lobular type, with clear margins, aged 50 or over with tumours of 3 cm or less, node-negative, oestrogen receptor-positive, HER2-negative, grade 1 to 2, who will take endocrine therapy for at least five years, and it must be given by external beam (NICE NG101 recommendations 1.13.4 to 1.13.6).
claims.note: NG101 1.13.4: excluding lobular type, clear margins, aged 50 and over, tumours 3 cm or less, N0, ER-positive, HER2-negative, grade 1 to 2, endocrine therapy minimum 5 years; 1.13.6 external beam.

claims.claim: IMPORT LOW found five-year local relapse of 0.5 against 1.1 percent with fewer changes in breast appearance, while RAPID, which gave the dose twice a day, was non-inferior on recurrence but had late toxicity of 32 against 13 percent.
claims.note: IMPORT LOW Lancet 2017: 5-year local relapse 1.1% (whole breast) vs 0.5% (partial). RAPID Lancet 2019: late grade >=2 toxicity 32% vs 13%.

claims.claim: Intraoperative radiotherapy during the lumpectomy met its non-inferiority margin in TARGIT-A and had lower mortality from causes other than breast cancer (hazard ratio 0.59, 0.40 to 0.86), but NICE TA501 does not recommend the Intrabeam system for routine commissioning and permits it only on existing machines under NHS England governance.
claims.note: TARGIT-A BMJ 2020: "Mortality from other causes was significantly lower (0.59, 0.40 to 0.86, P=0.005)". NG101 1.13.24/TA501: not recommended for routine commissioning; existing machines with NHS England governance.

claims.claim: The largest trial, NSABP B-39/RTOG 0413, did not establish equivalence: ten-year ipsilateral breast tumour recurrence was 4.6 percent with partial-breast against 3.9 percent with whole-breast radiotherapy, which is why the option is confined to the low-risk group described above rather than offered generally.
claims.note: NSABP B-39 Lancet 2019: 10-year IBTR 4.6% APBI vs 3.9% WBI.

claims.claim: Who can leave radiotherapy out: Women aged 65 and over with clear margins and a very low absolute risk of local recurrence, defined by NICE NG101 recommendation 1.13.7 as T1N0, oestrogen receptor-positive, HER2-negative, grade 1 to 2, who are willing to take endocrine therapy for at least five years.
claims.note: NG101 1.13.7: aged 65 and over, T1N0, ER-positive, HER2-negative, grade 1 to 2, endocrine therapy minimum 5 years.

claims.claim: Recommendation 1.13.8 sets out what must be said: without radiotherapy local recurrence occurs in about 50 women per 1,000 at five years and with it in about 10 per 1,000; overall survival at ten years is the same; and there is no increase in serious late effects from having it in this group.
claims.note: NG101 1.13.8: "about 50 women per 1,000 at 5 years ... about 10 women per 1,000"; OS at 10 years the same; no increase in serious late effects.

claims.claim: CALGB 9343 (aged 70 and over, ten-year locoregional recurrence 10 against 2 percent), PRIME II (aged 65 and over, ten-year local recurrence 9.5 against 0.9 percent) and LUMINA (aged 55 and over with luminal A biology, five-year local recurrence 2.3 percent) are the trials behind it.
claims.note: CALGB 9343 JCO 2013: free from local and regional recurrence at 10 years 98% vs 90%. PRIME II NEJM 2023: 10-year local recurrence 9.5% vs 0.9%. LUMINA NEJM 2023: 5-year recurrence 2.3%.

claims.claim: SUPREMO tested it in intermediate-risk disease treated with modern systemic therapy and found ten-year overall survival of 81.4 against 81.9 percent (hazard ratio 1.04, p=0.80), with chest-wall recurrence of 1.1 against 2.5 percent.
claims.note: SUPREMO NEJM 2025: 10-year OS 81.4% vs 81.9%, HR 1.04, P=0.80; chest-wall recurrence 1.1% vs 2.5%.

claims.claim: NSABP B-51/RTOG 1304 tested the other end of it and was negative: after a complete nodal response to chemotherapy, regional nodal irradiation did not lengthen the invasive breast cancer recurrence-free interval (hazard ratio 0.88, 0.60 to 1.28, p=0.51; event-free estimates 92.7 against 91.8 percent), so a complete response is a reason not to irradiate the nodes.
claims.note: NSABP B-51 NEJM 2025: HR 0.88 (0.60-1.28), P=0.51; point estimates 92.7% vs 91.8%.

claims.claim: The choice between an implant and the woman's own tissue is a real trade: in the Mastectomy Reconstruction Outcomes Consortium, autologous reconstruction gave higher satisfaction with the breasts at two years (7.94 points, 5.68 to 10.20) but roughly double the odds of a complication, while implants failed more often (7.1 against 1.3 percent).
claims.note: MROC JAMA Surg 2018: satisfaction with breasts difference 7.94 (5.68-10.20); flap complication ORs about 1.9-2.05 (SIEA 4.71); failure "EI and DTI techniques, 7.1%; ... DIEP flap, 1.3%" (pTRAM 1.2, fTRAM 2.1, LD 2.8, SIEA 0). 1.3% is the DIEP figure, not autologous reconstruction overall.
claims.fixed: Labelled the comparator: "7.1 percent against 1.3 percent for deep inferior epigastric perforator flaps".

claims.claim: British outcomes after implant reconstruction have been measured and are above the national standards: iBRA found implant loss of 9 percent, infection of 25 percent and return to theatre of 18 percent within three months across 81 units, and Pre-BRA found implant loss of 8.2 percent for the newer pre-pectoral technique.
claims.note: iBRA Lancet Oncol 2019: 81 units; implant loss 9%, return to theatre 18%, infection 25%, above National Quality Standards. Pre-BRA BJS 2022: implant loss 8.2%.

claims.claim: Mesh was used in 65 percent of iBRA reconstructions without randomised evidence;
claims.note: iBRA: "1376 (65%) patients had reconstruction with biological (1133 [54%]) or synthetic (243 [12%]) mesh".

claims.claim: The Early Breast Cancer Trialists' Collaborative Group pooled 4,756 women in ten trials of the same chemotherapy before or after surgery and found no difference in distant recurrence (38.2 against 38.0 percent at fifteen years), breast cancer mortality or death from any cause, with breast conservation achieved in 65 against 49 percent and fifteen-year local recurrence higher after chemotherapy first (21.4 against 15.9 percent, rate ratio 1.37).
claims.note: EBCTCG Lancet Oncol 2018: 4756 women, 10 trials; BCT 65% vs 49%; 15-year local recurrence 21.4% vs 15.9%, rate ratio 1.37; distant recurrence 38.2% vs 38.0%; no difference in breast cancer mortality or death from any cause.

claims.claim: In the Milan trial, 701 women with cancers no larger than 2 cm were assigned between 1973 and 1980 to radical (Halsted) mastectomy or to quadrantectomy followed by radiotherapy; after a median 20 years, death from any cause had occurred in 41.2 percent of the mastectomy group and 41.7 percent of the conserving group (P equals 1.0), and death from breast cancer in 24.3 and 26.1 percent (P equals 0.8).
claims.note: Veronesi NEJM 2002: 701 women, cancers no more than 2 cm, 1973 to 1980; death from all causes 41.7% (conserving) vs 41.2% (radical mastectomy), P=1.0; breast cancer death 26.1% and 24.3%, P=0.8.

claims.claim: In NSABP B-06, 1,851 women were assigned to total mastectomy, lumpectomy alone, or lumpectomy with radiotherapy, and after 20 years there was no significant difference between the three in disease-free, distant-disease-free or overall survival, with a hazard ratio for death of 0.97 (0.83 to 1.14) for lumpectomy with radiotherapy against total mastectomy.
claims.note: Fisher NEJM 2002: 1851 women; no significant differences in DFS, DDFS or OS; HR for death 0.97 (0.83 to 1.14).

claims.claim: What radiotherapy is worth after conserving surgery has been measured: in the EBCTCG meta-analysis of 10,801 women in 17 randomised trials, it cut the 10-year risk of any first recurrence from 35.0 to 19.3 percent and the 15-year risk of breast cancer death from 25.2 to 21.4 percent, with about one breast cancer death avoided by year 15 for every four recurrences avoided by year 10.
claims.note: EBCTCG Lancet 2011 as above: 35.0 to 19.3%, 25.2 to 21.4%, one death per four recurrences.

claims.claim: For a narrow low-risk group NICE offers the choice of leaving it out: NG101 (1.13.7, 1.13.8) says to consider not using radiotherapy for women aged 65 and over with T1N0, ER-positive, HER2-negative, grade 1 to 2 cancer who will take endocrine therapy for at least 5 years, and to tell them that without radiotherapy local recurrence occurs in about 50 women per 1,000 at 5 years against about 10 per 1,000 with it, that overall survival at 10 years is the same, and that there is no increase in serious late effects from having it.
claims.note: NG101 1.13.7 and 1.13.8 as quoted: 65 and over, T1N0, ER+, HER2-, grade 1-2, 5 years endocrine; 50 vs 10 per 1,000 at 5 years; OS at 10 years same; no increase in serious late effects.

claims.claim: How the breast looks and feels: after conserving surgery the treated breast can be smaller, firmer or dented, and NICE's own radiotherapy evidence records more clinician-assessed adverse events at 5 years and more reports of a harder or firmer breast with the one-week schedule, though it judged the differences not clinically important.
claims.note: NG101 2023 rationale: "higher incidence of outcomes related to clinician-assessed adverse events at 5 years and quality-of-life measurements (related to harder or firmer breasts) for people who were given 26 Gy in 5 fractions"; differences "not clinically significant" (with one exception, swollen breasts).

claims.claim: And what recurrence would mean: in the Milan trial, 30 of 352 women treated by quadrantectomy and radiotherapy had a recurrence in the same breast over 20 years, a crude cumulative incidence of 8.8 percent, against 8 local recurrences among 349 after radical mastectomy, 2.3 percent, with no difference in distant metastases;
claims.note: Veronesi NEJM 2002: 30 recurrences in same breast (352 conserving) vs 8 local recurrences (349 radical), crude cumulative incidence 8.8% and 2.3% at 20 years; no significant difference in distant metastases.

claims.claim: NSABP B-06 put in-breast recurrence at 14.3 percent over 20 years with radiotherapy and 39.2 percent without.
claims.note: Fisher NEJM 2002: ipsilateral recurrence 14.3% with irradiation vs 39.2% without.

claims.claim: If a sentinel node turns out to contain cancer, (1.4.12) says to offer further axillary treatment, clearance or radiotherapy, for 1 or more macrometastasis; (1.4.13) says to discuss the benefits and risks of having no further treatment with women who have 1 or 2 macrometastases, have had conserving surgery, and are having whole-breast radiotherapy with systemic therapy; (1.4.14) says not to treat micrometastases further; and (1.4.15) says isolated tumour cells count as node-negative.
claims.note: NG101 1.4.12 "1 or more sentinel lymph node macrometastasis"; 1.4.13 "1 or 2 ... macrometastases", breast-conserving surgery, whole-breast radiotherapy with systemic therapy; 1.4.14 micrometastases; 1.4.15 ITCs node-negative.

claims.claim: In a meta-analysis of 72 studies, the pooled incidence of arm lymphoedema after breast cancer was 16.6 percent, and 21.4 percent when restricted to 30 prospective cohorts, rising over the first two years; it was about four times higher after axillary lymph node dissection (19.9 percent) than after sentinel node biopsy (5.6 percent), and the risk factors with the strongest evidence were extensive surgery and being overweight or obese.
claims.note: DiSipio Lancet Oncol 2013: 72 studies, pooled 16.6%; 21.4% in 30 prospective cohorts; increase up to 2 years; about four times higher after ALND (19.9%) than SLNB (5.6%); strong-evidence risk factors extensive surgery and overweight/obesity.

claims.claim: Radiotherapy to the axilla instead of surgery roughly halves it: in AMAROS, 1,425 sentinel node-positive patients were randomised, and at 5 years lymphoedema affected 24.5 percent after clearance against 11.9 percent after axillary radiotherapy, while at 10 years axillary recurrence was 0.93 against 1.82 percent with no difference in survival.
claims.note: AMAROS JCO 2023: 1,425 randomised; 5-year lymphedema 24.5% (ALND) v 11.9% (ART); 10-year ARR 0.93% vs 1.82%; no OS difference.

claims.claim: Two trials go further and leave the axilla alone: in ACOSOG Z0011, 891 women with 1 or 2 positive sentinel nodes having lumpectomy and whole-breast radiotherapy had 10-year overall survival of 86.3 percent without clearance against 83.6 percent with it, and in SENOMAC, 2,540 patients with 1 or 2 sentinel-node macrometastases, about 90 percent of them having nodal radiotherapy, had 5-year recurrence-free survival of 89.7 against 88.7 percent.
claims.note: Z0011: 891 women, 1 or 2 SLN metastases, lumpectomy and tangential WBI, 10-year OS 86.3% vs 83.6%. SENOMAC: 2540, 1-2 macrometastases, nodal RT 89.9% and 88.4%, 5-year RFS 89.7% vs 88.7%.

claims.claim: What reduces the risk, in NICE's own 2025 words: information before treatment starts in a format to take away, covering risk reduction, early signs, skin changes, how to self-monitor and how to take baseline measurements of the limb (1.14.1); keeping to a healthy weight and keeping the arm moving, because (1.14.3) physical activity does not cause or worsen lymphoedema and may improve quality of life; and skin care, because infection is what tips a vulnerable arm over.
claims.note: NG101 1.14.1 [2018, amended 2025] information list incl. healthy body weight, skincare, self-monitoring, baseline limb measurements; 1.14.3 [2025] "no indication that physical activity causes, or worsens, lymphoedema" and may improve quality of life.

claims.claim: NG101 (1.14.14) says to identify people as high risk before surgery if they have a pre-existing shoulder problem, a BMI over 30, planned axillary node clearance, or planned radiotherapy to the axilla or supraclavicular nodes, (1.14.16) to offer them supervised support with upper limb exercises, and (1.14.19) to refer anyone with a persistent reduction in arm and shoulder mobility to physiotherapy.
claims.note: NG101 1.14.14: pre-existing shoulder conditions, "BMI is over 30 kg/m2", planned axillary node clearance, planned radiotherapy to axilla or supraclavicular nodes; 1.14.16 supervised support; 1.14.19 physiotherapy referral.

claims.claim: NICE NG101 (1.1.5) hands fertility preservation to the NICE fertility guideline, now NG257 (2026), and NG257 (1.53.1) says to discuss it with people preparing for treatment likely to impair their fertility, and that where treatment is urgent the discussion should happen at the earliest possible opportunity.
claims.note: NG101 1.1.5 refers to the NICE fertility guideline; NG257 published 31 March 2026; 1.53.1 [2026] "For people who need urgent treatment, this discussion should take place at the earliest possible opportunity."

claims.claim: Storage is reviewed at least every 5 years and NHS funding continues for people who remain at significant risk (1.53.8).
claims.note: NG257 1.53.8: "Organise follow-ups at least every 5 years ... Offer continued NHS-funded storage for people who remain at continued significant risk".

claims.claim: On timing, Cancer Research UK says collecting and freezing eggs takes about 2 to 3 weeks, that IVF is the most effective method, that letrozole or tamoxifen can be used with lower-dose stimulation, and that IVF is available for some people on the NHS but not everywhere, so the answer varies by where you live.
claims.note: CRUK fertility page: freezing eggs "takes about 2 to 3 weeks"; IVF "currently the most effective way"; letrozole or tamoxifen with lower-dose IVF hormones; "available for some people on the NHS but not in all parts of the country".

claims.claim: In an individual patient-level meta-analysis of 873 patients from five randomised trials, premature ovarian insufficiency occurred in 14.1 percent of those given a GnRH agonist against 30.9 percent of controls (adjusted odds ratio 0.38), and at least one pregnancy after treatment in 10.3 against 5.5 percent, with no significant difference in disease-free or overall survival.
claims.note: Lambertini JCO 2018: 873 patients, five trials; POI 14.1% vs 30.9% (aOR 0.38); pregnancy 10.3% vs 5.5%; no significant DFS or OS difference.

claims.claim: The trial that opened this question, POEMS, randomised 257 premenopausal women with operable hormone receptor-negative breast cancer and found ovarian failure at 2 years in 8 percent on goserelin against 22 percent, with pregnancy in 21 against 11 percent.
claims.note: Moore NEJM 2015: 257 premenopausal women, HR-negative; ovarian failure 8% vs 22% (2 years); pregnancy 21% vs 11%.

claims.claim: The longer-term picture comes from a Danish national survey: of 3,253 women aged 18 to 70 who answered a median of 26 months after surgery, 1,543 (47 percent) reported pain in the treated area, 201 of them severe and 595 moderate; the odds of persistent sensory disturbance were about five times higher after axillary lymph node dissection than after sentinel lymph node dissection (odds ratio 4.97, 3.92 to 6.30) and five times higher in women aged 18 to 39; radiotherapy raised the odds of pain and chemotherapy did not.
claims.note: Gartner JAMA 2009: 3253 of 3754 women aged 18 to 70; "assessed an average of 26 months after surgery" (not a median); 1543 (47%) pain, 201 severe, 595 moderate; sensory disturbance ALND OR 4.97 (3.92-6.30), age 18-39 OR 5.00; radiotherapy OR 1.50 for pain, chemotherapy not.
claims.fixed: Changed "a median of 26 months" to "an average of 26 months".

claims.claim: Only about 1 in 5 of those in pain had spoken to a doctor about it in the previous three months, which is the second half of the problem: it is treatable, and people do not report it because they were never told to expect it.
claims.note: Gartner JAMA 2009: "306 patients (20%) with pain had contacted a physician within the prior 3 months".

claims.claim: In the SCALP randomised trial, 50.5 percent of women cooled during taxane, anthracycline or both kept more than half their hair after the fourth cycle, against none of the controls.
claims.note: SCALP JAMA 2017: hair preservation 48 of 95 (50.5%) with cooling vs 0 of 47; taxane- or anthracycline-based; assessed at cycle 4.

claims.claim: A caveat that belongs beside every one of those numbers: the trials that produced them had few Black participants, and a later phase II study of the Paxman device in Black patients having chemotherapy for stage I to III breast cancer closed early after 15 of a planned 30 participants for lack of efficacy, with hair loss and distress scores rising during cooling and only one participant avoiding significant loss; the authors named hair thickness, hair volume and cap design as the likely reasons.
claims.note: Dilawari Oncologist 2021: planned enrolment of 30 Black patients, stage I-III; 15 enrolled before closure for lack of efficacy; MDS and CADS increased; only one avoided significant hair loss; hair thickness, volume and cap design named.

claims.claim: The Little Princess Trust provides free real-hair wigs to people up to the age of 24.
claims.note: Macmillan hair loss page (on the record): "The Little Princess Trust provides free real-hair wigs to young people up to age 24 who have hair loss as a result of cancer treatment."

claims.claim: NICE NG101 (1.15.1) says to offer annual mammography for 5 years to everyone who has had or is being treated for breast cancer including DCIS, and for women to continue annual mammography past 5 years until they enter the NHS Breast Screening Programme in England or the Breast Test Wales Screening Programme; (1.15.2) not to do mammography of the ipsilateral soft tissues after a mastectomy; and (1.15.3) not to use routine ultrasound or MRI for post-treatment surveillance.
claims.note: NG101 1.15.1 annual mammography for 5 years, continue until NHSBSP/BTWSP entry; 1.15.2 no ipsilateral soft tissue mammography after mastectomy; 1.15.3 no routine US or MRI.

claims.claim: That first rule is under revision: NICE reviewed the guideline on 11 September 2026 and says it will be updating the recommendation on annual mammography, following a surveillance decision taken in June 2026, with no new wording published yet.
claims.note: NG101 overview: "Last reviewed: 11 September 2026. We have reviewed this guideline and will be updating the recommendation on annual mammography. See the June 2026 surveillance decision"; 1.15.1 wording unchanged.

claims.claim: Men have breast tissue and get breast cancer too, about 420 UK cases a year against about 59,000 in women; there is a page for it, and there is no screening programme for men, so a lump behind a man's nipple needs the same appointment (Cancer Research UK)
claims.note: CRUK incidence: "around 59,000 new cases in females and around 420 new cases in males every year (2019, 2021-2022)".

claims.claim: The pathology report carries the histological type, the Nottingham grade with its three component scores, the invasive and whole tumour size in millimetres, the node stage, the excision margins, the receptor results and the assessment of treatment effect where chemotherapy came first (RCPath G148, version 3, November 2024)
claims.note: G148 PDF title page "November 2024", "Version number 3"; contents as listed.

claims.claim: Grades are not expected in equal thirds: the expected ratio of grades 1, 2 and 3 is about 2:3:5 in symptomatic breast cancer and about 3:5:2 in screen-detected breast cancer, so a grade 3 is commoner in a cancer found as a lump than in one found by screening (RCPath G148)
claims.note: G148: "ratios for grades 1, 2 and 3 are approximately 2:3:5 in symptomatic breast cancer and 3:5:2 in screen-detected breast cancer".

claims.claim: TNM 9 was published on 3 July 2025 and UICC recommends it from 1 January 2026.
claims.note: The UICC TNM page returns an empty body to a script; Brierley 2026 (full text read) says the 9th edition "has recently been published" but prints neither 3 July 2025 nor 1 January 2026. No alternative copy read.

claims.claim: For breast the classification is unchanged; the one change clarifies the post-treatment yp classification, basing ypT on the largest continuous focus of residual invasive cancer and recommending that residual cancer burden be reported beside it (Brierley 2026)
claims.note: Brierley IJC 2026 section 8: "The classification remains unchanged. The yp classification is clarified ... ypT category must be based on the largest continuous focus of residual invasive cancer ... residual cancer burden method is recommended".

claims.claim: Because stage does not include grade or the receptors, the UK adds the Nottingham Prognostic Index, grade plus node stage plus 0.2 times the size in centimetres, banded from excellent below 2.4 to poor at 5.4 and above (RCPath G148;
claims.note: G148 Appendix: "NPI = Grade (1 to 3) + node stage (1 to 3) + (invasive carcinoma size in cm x 0.2)"; "<2.4 = Excellent", ">=5.4 = Poor".

claims.claim: Tumour size is less precise than it looks: the national screening programme's quality assurance scheme finds poor agreement between pathologists on size even on prepared slides, and separate deposits 5 mm or more apart are not added together (RCPath G148)
claims.note: G148 8.2.1: "NHSBSP EQA scheme shows poor concordance on tumour size ... on ready-prepared slides"; foci "5 mm or more apart" treated as separate, satellite focus not included in the measurement.

claims.claim: One report gives a hormone receptor answer and a HER2 answer, and the four combinations are unequal: 70.1 percent hormone receptor-positive HER2-negative, 9.3 percent positive for both, 4.0 percent HER2-positive alone and 10.8 percent triple-negative (SEER 21, 2019 to 2023).
claims.note: SEER 21 2019-2023 percent of cases: HR+/HER2- 70.1, HR+/HER2+ 9.29, HR-/HER2+ 3.99, HR-/HER2- 10.78 (unknown 5.5).

claims.claim: A British and an American clinician can therefore give the same tumour a different stage, and PREDICT is explicitly less accurate in women under 30, women over 70, tumours over 50 mm, and has never been validated in men.
claims.note: NG101 1.6.5: less accurate for "women under 30 with ER-positive breast cancer", "women aged 70 and over", "tumours larger than 50 mm", "not been validated in men". The page dropped the ER-positive qualifier.
claims.fixed: Now "women under 30 with oestrogen receptor-positive disease, women aged 70 and over".

claims.claim: On meta-analysis of 39 paired studies, 22.5 percent of oestrogen receptor-positive primaries had become negative in their metastases and 21.3 percent of HER2-positive ones had, with conversion in the other direction too;
claims.note: Schrijver JNCI 2018: 39 studies of paired metastases; positive-to-negative conversion ER 22.5%, HER2 21.3%; negative-to-positive also reported.

claims.claim: No prospective study has shown what treating on the metastasis rather than the primary does to survival, so the commonest decision in relapsed breast cancer rests on a biological argument rather than a trial (Schrijver 2018).
claims.note: Schrijver JNCI 2018 conclusion: "Large prospective studies assessing the impact of receptor conversion on treatment efficacy and survival are needed."

claims.claim: Grade agrees between core biopsy and surgical specimen about 70 percent of the time; the national screening programme's quality assurance scheme finds poor agreement between pathologists on tumour size even on prepared slides; there is no internationally agreed method for scoring oestrogen receptor; and pathologists disagree at the HER2 0 to 1+ boundary that now decides eligibility for an antibody-drug conjugate.
claims.note: G148: "There is moderate, about 70%, agreement of grade on core biopsy with the corresponding surgical specimen"; poor EQA concordance on size.

claims.claim: A systematic review of 97 trials in up to 94,866 participants found multiple studies asking nearly the same question, with patients rarely involved in designing them.
claims.note: npj Breast Cancer 2025 (on the axillary de-escalation term): "97 trials evaluated de-escalation ... in up to 94,866 participants"; "Significant duplication"; "Patients were rarely involved in study design".

claims.claim: LUMINA selected by luminal A biology rather than by age and got a lower recurrence rate than the age-based trials, but the guidelines still key the decision to 65 or 70.
claims.note: LUMINA 5-year recurrence 2.3% vs PRIME II 10-year 9.5%; NG101 threshold 65, CALGB 9343 70.

claims.claim: Hormone receptor-positive, HER2-negative breast cancer is about 70% of all breast cancers and the archetype of a hormone-driven, slow-evolving disease.
claims.note: SEER 21 2019-2023: HR+/HER2- 70.1% of female breast cases.

claims.claim: Oestrogen receptor signalling drives proliferation, so endocrine therapy has been the backbone since tamoxifen (1977) and aromatase inhibitors (1990s); because recurrences can occur 10-20 years after diagnosis, therapy lasts 5-10 years and adherence is a major real-world determinant of outcome.
claims.note: Drugs@FDA NDA017970 (Nolvadex) original approval 1977-12-30; EBCTCG Pan NEJM 2017 (on the late-recurrence term): recurrences "at a steady rate throughout the study period from 5 to 20 years"; MA.17R extends AI to 10 years.

claims.claim: Gene-expression assays (Oncotype DX, MammaPrint) now spare roughly 70% of node-negative and most postmenopausal node-positive patients chemotherapy, while adjuvant CDK4/6 inhibitors (abemaciclib, ribociclib) reduce recurrence in the high-risk minority.
claims.note: TAILORx NEJM 2018 (record trial): 69% had a midrange score of 11-25; the paper's discussion says the assay "may identify up to 85% of women with early breast cancer who can be spared adjuvant chemotherapy". The 70% is the midrange share, not the share spared. RxPONDER: no benefit in postmenopausal women with 1-3 nodes.
claims.fixed: Now "spare up to 85% of node-negative patients (TAILORx)"; TAILORx link added to the record.

claims.claim: Progression is increasingly managed by genotype: ESR1 mutations detected in ctDNA (30-40% after aromatase inhibitors) call for oral SERDs (elacestrant, imlunestrant) or the PROTAC vepdegestrant, and since September 2026 for camizestrant switched in at molecular progression;
claims.note: No source on the record gave the ESR1 share (the esr1-mutation term cites only Wikipedia). Brett et al., Breast Cancer Research 2021 (PMC8365900, full text): "Approximately 20-40% of patients who have received aromatase inhibition (AI) for MBC have ESR1 mutations". Camizestrant date: ASCO Post "On September 4, 2026 ... accelerated approval".
claims.fixed: Changed "30-40%" to "about 20-40% after aromatase inhibitors for metastatic disease" and added Brett 2021 to the record links.

claims.claim: PIK3CA/AKT1/PTEN alterations (about 50%) call for inavolisib, capivasertib, or alpelisib; gedatolisib (2026) works in PIK3CA-wild-type disease.
claims.note: CAPItello-291 NEJM 2023 (record trial): "289 patients (40.8%) had AKT pathway alterations" (PIK3CA, AKT1, PTEN). No record source gives about 50%. Gedatolisib 2026 approval: FDA event 14 July 2026 in drug-depth (VIKTORIA-1), not re-read.
claims.fixed: Changed "about 50%" to "40.8% of patients in CAPItello-291"; CAPItello-291 link added.

claims.claim: After endocrine options are exhausted, antibody-drug conjugates precede chemotherapy: T-DXd for the ~60% with HER2-low or ultralow expression, and the TROP2 ADCs sacituzumab govitecan and datopotamab deruxtecan.
claims.note: No source on the record states that about 60% are HER2-low or ultralow; DESTINY-Breast06 NEJM 2024 reports 713 HER2-low and 153 HER2-ultralow randomised, not a population share. TROP2 ordering against labels was fixed in round 1.
claims.fixed: Removed "~60%": now "T-DXd for HER2-low or ultralow expression".

claims.claim: HR-positive, HER2-negative disease is 70.1 percent of American cases with a known receptor subtype (SEER 21, 2019 to 2023), so, if the same share holds elsewhere, of the order of 1.7 million of the 2,434,087 breast cancers diagnosed worldwide each year (GLOBOCAN 2024).
claims.note: SEER: 70.1054781980336% is the share of all female breast cases, of which 5.5% have unknown subtype; it is not the share "with a known receptor subtype" (that would be about 74%). 1.7 million of 2,434,087 is consistent with GLOBOCAN 2024 (dated).
claims.fixed: Now "70.1 percent of American female breast cancer cases"; same label fixed in breast-core.ts subtypes and two notes.

claims.claim: Most are found early, treated with surgery and endocrine therapy, and spared chemotherapy by genomic assays; five-year relative survival in this group is 95.8 percent, the best of the four receptor boxes (SEER 21, 2016 to 2022).
claims.note: SEER 21 (excluding IL) 2016-2022: HR+/HER2- 95.8%, highest of the four subtypes.

claims.claim: Because it can recur late, it accounts for the majority of the 693,660 annual breast cancer deaths, which is why adjuvant therapy lasts years and tests for late recurrence are a research priority.
claims.note: No source on the record says HR+/HER2- disease accounts for the majority of the 693,660 breast cancer deaths (GLOBOCAN gives deaths without subtype; SEER gives no deaths by subtype).
claims.fixed: Removed the clause; now "Because it can recur late, adjuvant therapy lasts years and tests for late recurrence are a research priority."

claims.claim: Chemotherapy omission for ~70% of node-negative and most postmenopausal node-positive patients using genomic assays (TAILORx, RxPONDER, MINDACT).
claims.note: As item 110: TAILORx "up to 85% ... can be spared"; 69% was the midrange share.
claims.fixed: Changed "~70%" to "up to 85%".

claims.claim: First-line CDK4/6 + endocrine therapy with median OS beyond five years (MONALEESA-2: 63.9 months).
claims.note: MONALEESA-2 NEJM 2022: median OS 63.9 months with ribociclib plus letrozole.

claims.claim: The first ctDNA-triggered treatment switch approved by the FDA (camizestrant, SERENA-6, September 2026), over a negative advisory vote.
claims.note: ASCO Post: "On September 4, 2026, the U.S. FDA granted accelerated approval to camizestrant ... upon detection of ESR1 mutation"; ODAC voted against (record link).

claims.claim: Early stage, deciding on chemotherapy: Genomic assay (Oncotype DX RS ≤25 node-negative or postmenopausal 1-3 nodes;
claims.note: TAILORx: endocrine therapy noninferior for RS 11-25 node-negative, benefit only in women 50 or under with RS 16-25; RxPONDER: no chemotherapy benefit in postmenopausal women with 1-3 nodes and RS 25 or lower.

claims.claim: MammaPrint low risk) → endocrine therapy alone; premenopausal RS 16-25 or high clinical risk → chemotherapy or OFS-based escalation.
claims.note: TAILORx: "some benefit of chemotherapy found in women 50 years of age or younger with a recurrence score of 16 to 25"; RxPONDER premenopausal benefit.

claims.claim: Early stage, adjuvant endocrine therapy: Postmenopausal: aromatase inhibitor 5-10 years (or tamoxifen → AI switch).
claims.note: MA.17R NEJM 2016: AI for 5 years is the treatment of choice; extension to 10 years improved DFS.

claims.claim: Premenopausal: tamoxifen 5-10 years; add OFS (+ AI or tamoxifen) for higher-risk or chemotherapy-treated women (SOFT/TEXT).
claims.note: Record entities: tamoxifen ("ten years is better than five (ATLAS, aTTom)"), SOFT/TEXT (OFS for higher-risk, chemotherapy cohort); NG101 table 5 says OFS "may be most beneficial for people who are at higher risk". NCCN (cited) requires login.

claims.claim: Early stage, high risk: adjuvant CDK4/6: Abemaciclib 2 years for node-positive high-risk (monarchE); ribociclib 3 years for stage II-III including node-negative high-risk (NATALEE).
claims.note: monarchE JCO 2020: abemaciclib 150 mg twice daily for 2 years, node-positive high risk. NATALEE NEJM 2024: ribociclib for 3 years, stage II-III.

claims.claim: Olaparib 1 year if gBRCA (OlympiA).
claims.note: OlympiA NEJM 2021: "1 year of oral olaparib or placebo" in germline BRCA1/2.

claims.claim: Early stage, extended and adjuvant SERD (emerging): Extended AI to 10 years for higher-risk (MA.17R, NSABP B-42); adjuvant giredestrant positive in lidERA (2025, not yet approved);
claims.note: MA.17R NEJM 2016 extends AI to 10 years; lidERA record: presented SABCS December 2025, not yet approved; CT.gov NCT04961996 giredestrant 5 years adjuvant.

claims.claim: For relapse on/within 12 months of adjuvant ET with PIK3CA mutation: inavolisib + palbociclib + fulvestrant (INAVO120).
claims.note: INAVO120 NEJM 2024 (record): eligibility relapse during or within 12 months of adjuvant endocrine therapy, PIK3CA-mutated, inavolisib + palbociclib + fulvestrant.

claims.claim: Metastatic, molecular progression on first line: Serial ctDNA; on emergent ESR1 mutation before radiographic progression, switch AI → camizestrant and continue the CDK4/6 inhibitor (SERENA-6; accelerated approval 4 Sep 2026).
claims.note: ASCO Post: accelerated approval September 4, 2026, ESR1 mutation during AI + CDK4/6 therapy, combination with a CDK4/6 inhibitor.

claims.claim: Metastatic, endocrine-resistant: ADC before chemotherapy: HER2-low or ultralow (~60%): T-DXd (DESTINY-Breast06 chemotherapy-naive;
claims.note: The "(~60%)" share is not in any record source; DESTINY-Breast06 (chemotherapy-naive after endocrine therapy) is right.
claims.fixed: Removed "(~60%)".

claims.claim: Late recurrence: half of relapses occur after year 5 and no test reliably identifies who needs extended or intensified therapy.
claims.note: No record source says half of relapses occur after year 5. EBCTCG Pan NEJM 2017 (late-recurrence term) says "Breast-cancer recurrences occurred at a steady rate throughout the study period from 5 to 20 years"; full text searched, no "half" statement.
claims.fixed: Replaced with "after five years of endocrine therapy, recurrences continue at a steady rate from year 5 to year 20 (EBCTCG, Pan 2017)"; Pan 2017 added to record links.

claims.claim: HER2-low scoring reproducibility at IHC 0/1+ determines T-DXd eligibility for millions of patients.
claims.note: "for millions of patients" has no source on the record; T-DXd eligibility at the 0/1+ boundary applies only in advanced disease.
claims.fixed: Removed "for millions of patients".

claims.claim: Invasive lobular carcinoma is under-represented in trials despite being 10-15% of cases.
claims.note: No source on the HR-positive record; Cancer Research UK invasive lobular page: "Around 15 in every 100 breast cancers (around 15%) are invasive lobular breast cancer."
claims.fixed: Changed "10-15% of cases" to "about 15% of breast cancers (Cancer Research UK)" and added the CRUK page to the record links.

claims.claim: HER2-positive breast cancer (15-20% of cases;
claims.note: DESTINY-Breast12 (Nat Med 2024, record trial) introduction: HER2+ "accounts for between 15% and 20% of all cases of breast cancer"; RCPath G148 gives 13 to 20% of early breast cancer; SEER 13.3%.

claims.claim: The modern curative pathway is response-adapted: neoadjuvant chemotherapy with dual HER2 blockade (or, since 2026, T-DXd followed by THP), surgery, then either antibody completion for patients with a pathologic complete response or an ADC for residual disease (T-DM1 from KATHERINE, now T-DXd from DESTINY-Breast05).
claims.note: Enhertu US label (DailyMed, revised 05/2026): neoadjuvant T-DXd followed by THP and adjuvant for residual invasive disease, Indications 1.1 changed 05/2026. DESTINY-Breast05 NEJM 2026 replaces T-DM1.

claims.claim: Metastatic disease has been transformed twice: by CLEOPATRA's pertuzumab (OS 57 months) and then by trastuzumab deruxtecan, which beat T-DM1 by a wide margin in second line (DESTINY-Breast03) and beat THP in first line (DESTINY-Breast09, PFS 40.7 months; approved 2025).
claims.note: CLEOPATRA Lancet Oncol 2020: median OS 57.1 months. DESTINY-Breast09 NEJM 2025: median PFS 40.7 months vs 26.9; label section 1.2 (first-line with pertuzumab) changed 12/2025. DESTINY-Breast03 PFS HR 0.33.

claims.claim: Brain metastases, which develop in up to half of patients, are now treatable systemically with tucatinib (HER2CLIMB) and T-DXd (DESTINY-Breast12).
claims.note: DESTINY-Breast12 Nat Med 2024 introduction: "As many as 50% of patients with HER2+ advanced/metastatic breast cancer (mBC) develop brain metastases".

claims.claim: HER2CLIMB-05 (tucatinib maintenance) and PATINA (palbociclib maintenance in HR+/HER2+, approved 2026) intensify chemotherapy-free maintenance, and a wave of Chinese HER2 ADCs (trastuzumab rezetecan, BL-M07D1, ARX788, disitamab vedotin) is producing Enhertu-scale results.
claims.note: FDA: "On June 24, 2026, the Food and Drug Administration approved palbociclib (Ibrance ...)" for HR+/HER2+ maintenance (PATINA).

claims.claim: 15-20% of breast cancers (roughly 400,000 cases per year worldwide).
claims.note: 15-20% (DESTINY-Breast12 introduction) of the GLOBOCAN 2024 total of 2,434,087 is about 365,000-487,000, so roughly 400,000 holds, but the figure was presented undated "per year" without naming GLOBOCAN.
claims.fixed: Dated it: "roughly 400,000 of the 2,434,087 new breast cancers GLOBOCAN estimated worldwide for 2024".

claims.claim: Ten-year survival for early-stage disease treated with trastuzumab-based therapy exceeds 80%.
claims.note: Joint NSABP B-31/NCCTG N9831 analysis (JCO 2014, record trial hera-b31-n9831): adding trastuzumab increased "10-year OS rate from 75.2% to 84%".

claims.claim: Ten-year survival above 80% for early disease: the subtype with the poorest outlook in the 1990s is now one of the most treatable.
claims.note: As item 144: 10-year OS 84% with trastuzumab in B-31/N9831.

claims.claim: Response-adapted curative therapy: pCR patients de-escalate, residual disease escalates to an ADC (now T-DXd, iDFS HR 0.47 vs T-DM1).
claims.note: DESTINY-Breast05 NEJM 2026: invasive-disease events or deaths, hazard ratio 0.47 (0.34-0.66) vs T-DM1.

claims.claim: T-DXd across the continuum: neoadjuvant (2026), post-neoadjuvant (2026), first-line metastatic with pertuzumab (2025, PFS 40.7 months), second line, and brain metastases.
claims.note: Enhertu label: neoadjuvant and residual-disease indications (section 1.1 changed 05/2026), first line with pertuzumab (section 1.2 changed 12/2025); DESTINY-Breast09 PFS 40.7 months.

claims.claim: Stage I (≤2-3 cm, node-negative): Surgery then weekly paclitaxel × 12 + trastuzumab × 1 year (APT);
claims.note: APT JCO 2019 (record): node-negative HER2+ tumours 3 cm or less, weekly paclitaxel x 12 with trastuzumab for 1 year; 7-year DFS 93%.

claims.claim: Stage II-III, neoadjuvant: TCHP (docetaxel, carboplatin, trastuzumab, pertuzumab) or anthracycline-taxane + HP; from 2026, T-DXd × 4 → THP (DESTINY-Breast11, pCR 67%).
claims.note: DESTINY-Breast11 Ann Oncol 2026: pCR 67.3% T-DXd-THP vs 56.3% ddAC-THP; label neoadjuvant indication 05/2026.

claims.claim: Post-neoadjuvant, pathologic complete response: Complete 1 year of trastuzumab (± pertuzumab if node-positive at diagnosis); endocrine therapy if HR+; radiation per stage.
claims.note: APHINITY JCO 2021: node-positive cohort "continues to derive clear IDFS benefit from pertuzumab"; "Benefit was not seen in the node-negative cohort"; one year of HER2 therapy.

claims.claim: Post-neoadjuvant, residual invasive disease: T-DXd (DESTINY-Breast05, iDFS HR 0.47 vs T-DM1; approved 2026) replacing T-DM1 (KATHERINE); consider extended adjuvant neratinib for HR+ high-risk.
claims.note: DESTINY-Breast05 NEJM 2026 HR 0.47; Enhertu label adjuvant residual-disease indication 05/2026.

claims.claim: Adjuvant (upfront surgery), node-positive: Chemotherapy + trastuzumab + pertuzumab for 1 year (APHINITY); trastuzumab alone for lower risk;
claims.note: APHINITY: pertuzumab plus trastuzumab for one year; node-positive benefit.

claims.claim: 6 months acceptable where resources are limited (PERSEPHONE).
claims.note: PERSEPHONE Lancet 2019: 6 months non-inferior to 12 months (4-year DFS 89.4% vs 89.8%).

claims.claim: Metastatic, first line: T-DXd + pertuzumab (DESTINY-Breast09, PFS 40.7 months; approved 2025) or taxane + trastuzumab + pertuzumab (CLEOPATRA) followed by maintenance: HP ± tucatinib (HER2CLIMB-05) and, if HR+, endocrine therapy + palbociclib (PATINA, approved 2026).
claims.note: DESTINY-Breast09 NEJM: median PFS 40.7 months; Enhertu label first-line indication changed 12/2025; PATINA FDA approval June 24, 2026.

claims.claim: Metastatic, second line: T-DXd if not used first line (DESTINY-Breast03, PFS HR 0.33 vs T-DM1); tucatinib + trastuzumab + capecitabine, especially with brain metastases (HER2CLIMB).
claims.note: DESTINY-Breast03 updated results (Lancet 2023): median PFS 28.8 vs 6.8 months, "HR 0.33 [95% CI 0.26-0.43]".

claims.claim: Brain metastases: Systemic: tucatinib triplet or T-DXd (DESTINY-Breast12, intracranial ORR 72%); local: stereotactic radiosurgery or surgery for symptomatic or large lesions; whole-brain RT reserved.
claims.note: DESTINY-Breast12 Nat Med 2024 full text: confirmed CNS ORR 71.7% in the brain-metastasis cohort (record result 71.7%).

claims.claim: Cardiac monitoring and survivorship: LVEF every 3 months during anti-HER2 therapy; hold and cardioprotect for declines; anthracycline-free regimens preferred; long-term surveillance for late recurrence in HR+/HER2+.
claims.note: PERSEPHONE registry record (NCT00712140): "Determine cardiac function as assessed by left ventricular ejection fraction every 3 months during treatment".

claims.claim: They share late presentation (jaundice, weight loss) and dependence on surgical resection as the only cure, achievable in a minority, which keeps five-year survival under 20%.
claims.note: The only source on the record is Wikipedia, which gives no overall five-year figure; it says 'For non-resectable cases, the five-year survival rate is ... under 5%, in general' and up to 20-50% after resection of perihilar tumours. 'Under 20%' is not stated.
