claims.fixed: Replaced 'which keeps five-year survival under 20%' with 'without resection, five-year survival is under 5%' (the figure the cited Wikipedia page states).

claims.claim: The systemic landscape was gemcitabine-cisplatin alone from ABC-02 (2010) until TOPAZ-1 (durvalumab, 2022) and KEYNOTE-966 (pembrolizumab, 2023) added PD-(L)1 blockade with a modest median benefit but a doubling of two-year survival.
claims.note: Years correct (ABC-02 NEJM 2010, TOPAZ-1 NEJM Evid 2022, KEYNOTE-966 Lancet 2023). TOPAZ-1: '24-month overall survival rate was 24.9% ... and 10.4%' (a doubling). KEYNOTE-966 abstract reports only median OS 12.7 vs 10.9 months (HR 0.83); the doubling was attributed to both trials.
claims.fixed: Doubling now attributed to TOPAZ-1 only, with its figures (24.9% versus 10.4%); TOPAZ-1 link added to the cancers.ts cholangiocarcinoma record.

claims.claim: What sets biliary cancer apart is its genomic actionability: roughly 40% of intrahepatic tumours carry FGFR2 fusions (pemigatinib, futibatinib), IDH1 mutations (ivosidenib), HER2 amplification or overexpression (zanidatamab, trastuzumab deruxtecan), NRG1 fusions (zenocutuzumab, approved 2026), BRAF V600E, or MSI-high status, so molecular profiling at diagnosis is guideline-mandated.
claims.note: Wikipedia (only source) gives no proportion of actionable alterations. Lowery 2018 (MSK-IMPACT, 195 patients, 78% intrahepatic): 'Genetic alterations with potential therapeutic implications were identified in 47% of patients'. NRG1 approval 2026 confirmed on Bizengri label (revised 05/2026, section 1.3 cholangiocarcinoma).
claims.fixed: Replaced 'roughly 40% of intrahepatic tumours carry' with 'in a 195-patient sequencing series 47% carried an alteration with therapeutic implications (Lowery 2018), among them'; Lowery link added to the cancers.ts record.

claims.claim: About 210,000 cases per year worldwide; incidence of intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma has roughly doubled in Western countries over 30 years; gallbladder cancer is endemic in Chile, northern India, and among Indigenous Americans.
claims.note: Wikipedia (only source) has no worldwide case count and no 'doubled over 30 years'; it says rates are '0.5-2 people per 100,000 per year' in the West, '60 per 100,000 per year' in parts of Thailand, and 'Rates of cholangiocarcinoma within the liver in the Western world have increased.'
claims.fixed: Replaced '210,000 cases per year' and 'roughly doubled over 30 years' with the rates the cited page states and 'has risen in Western countries'.

claims.claim: Genotype-directed therapy in ~40% of patients.
claims.note: Wikipedia (only source) gives no figure. Lowery 2018: 'potential therapeutic implications ... in 47% of patients'.
claims.fixed: Rewrote as '47% of patients in one sequencing series had an alteration with therapeutic implications (Lowery 2018)' and added the source.

claims.claim: Four biomarker-directed drug classes approved (FGFR2, IDH1, HER2, NRG1), plus tumour-agnostic BRAF, MSI-H and NTRK options: ~40% of intrahepatic tumours have an actionable alteration.
claims.note: Approvals verified (FGFR2, IDH1, HER2 labels; NRG1 on Bizengri label 05/2026). '~40% of intrahepatic tumours' not on Wikipedia; Lowery 2018 reports 47% of a mixed (78% intrahepatic) cohort.
claims.fixed: Replaced with 'almost half of cholangiocarcinomas (47% in one series) have an alteration with therapeutic implications'.

claims.claim: Resectable: Margin-negative resection (hepatectomy, Whipple, or radical cholecystectomy) with lymphadenectomy; adjuvant capecitabine 6 months (BILCAP).
claims.note: BILCAP: 'oral capecitabine (1250 mg/m2 twice daily on days 1-14 of a 21-day cycle, for eight cycles)' = 24 weeks, about 6 months.

claims.claim: Advanced, other alterations: Zenocutuzumab (NRG1 fusion, approved 2026); dabrafenib-trametinib (BRAF V600E); pembrolizumab or dostarlimab (MSI-H/dMMR); larotrectinib/entrectinib (NTRK).
claims.note: Bizengri label revised 05/2026: '1.3 Advanced Unresectable or Metastatic NRG1 Fusion-Positive Cholangiocarcinoma'.

claims.claim: FGFR inhibitor resistance (polyclonal kinase-domain mutations) limits benefit to ~7-9 months; sequencing next-generation agents is unproven.
claims.note: Wikipedia gives no PFS. FIGHT-202 full text: 'Median progression-free survival was 6.9 months'; FOENIX-CCA2: 'median progression-free survival was 9.0 months'. Figure consistent with these.
claims.fixed: Figure kept; FIGHT-202 and FOENIX-CCA2 links added to the cancers.ts cholangiocarcinoma record.

claims.claim: Around 200,000 cases a year worldwide, rare in the West and common in parts of Asia and South America; most present late and five-year survival is under 20 percent overall.
claims.note: Cited Wikipedia (Biliary_tract_cancer redirects to Cholangiocarcinoma) and NCI PDQ bile duct patient page give no worldwide count and no overall five-year figure; Wikipedia: unresectable 'under 5%, in general'. GLOBOCAN does not report biliary tract cancer as one site.
claims.fixed: Removed '200,000 cases a year' and 'under 20 percent overall'; now 'for bile duct cancer that cannot be removed five-year survival is under 5 percent'.

claims.claim: Its genome differs from that of the rest of the biliary tree: FGFR2 fusions occur in about 10 to 15 percent, IDH1 mutations in about 15 percent, and BAP1 and ARID1A mutations are common, whereas KRAS and HER2 alterations are less frequent than in extrahepatic disease, so comprehensive sequencing at diagnosis is standard.
claims.note: FIGHT-202 full text: FGFR2 fusions 'occurring in 10-16% of patients' with intrahepatic disease; ClarIDHy: 'IDH1 mutations occur in approximately 13% of patients with intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma' (page said about 15).
claims.fixed: Changed to 'about 10 to 16 percent' and 'about 13 percent'.

claims.claim: For advanced disease gemcitabine with cisplatin (ABC-02, 2010) was the standard for a decade until TOPAZ-1 (2022) added durvalumab and KEYNOTE-966 (2023) added pembrolizumab, each modestly improving survival and producing a tail of long-term responders.
claims.note: ABC-02 NEJM 2010; TOPAZ-1 NEJM Evid 2022 (OS HR 0.80); KEYNOTE-966 Lancet 2023 (OS 12.7 vs 10.9 months). TOPAZ-1 3-year update: 36-month OS 14.6% vs 6.9% (long-term survivors).

claims.claim: After chemotherapy, targeted drugs matched to the tumour's mutation are given: pemigatinib (FIGHT-202, response rate 36 percent) and futibatinib (FOENIX-CCA2, response rate 42 percent) for FGFR2 fusions, and ivosidenib for IDH1 mutations, which in ClarIDHy extended progression-free survival from 1.4 to 2.7 months and gave a survival benefit once crossover was accounted for.
claims.note: FIGHT-202: '38 (35.5%)' responded (36%); FOENIX-CCA2: '43 of 103 patients (42%)'; ClarIDHy: 'median 2.7 months ... vs 1.4 months'.

claims.claim: For unresectable perihilar tumours in primary sclerosing cholangitis or under 3 cm, the Mayo protocol of chemoradiation followed by liver transplantation achieves long-term survival in selected patients and is offered in a few centres.
claims.note: None of the record's sources (TOPAZ-1, HERIZON-BTC-01, Wikipedia Klatskin) states the 3 cm criterion. Darwish Murad 2012: patients 'outside the United Network of Organ Sharing criteria (those with tumor mass >3 cm ...)' had shorter survival; the 3 cm limit applies to all candidates, not only non-PSC tumours.
claims.fixed: Reworded to 'perihilar tumours no larger than 3 cm that are unresectable or arise in primary sclerosing cholangitis' and added the Gastroenterology 2012 link.

claims.claim: HER2-positive tumours respond to zanidatamab, which had a response rate of 41 percent in HERIZON-BTC-01 and gained accelerated FDA approval in 2024, and to trastuzumab deruxtecan; the phase 3 HERIZON-BTC-302 tests zanidatamab in the first line.
claims.note: HERIZON-BTC-01: 'Confirmed objective responses ... in 33 patients in cohort 1 (41.3%)'. Accelerated FDA approval 2024 matches the zanidatamab record.

claims.claim: Hepatocellular carcinoma is the dominant primary liver cancer (~75-85%) and one of the most preventable: HBV vaccination and HCV cure have cut incidence wherever they were deployed.
claims.note: Only source is Wikipedia, which says HCC 'is the most common primary liver cancer' and that in SEER 'HCC accounts for 65% of all cases of liver cancers'; '~75-85%' is not stated.
claims.fixed: Removed '(~75-85%)'; now 'the most common primary liver cancer'.

claims.claim: Lenvatinib matched it (REFLECT), then IMbrave150 made atezolizumab plus bevacizumab the first regimen to beat sorafenib on survival (OS 19.2 vs 13.4 months).
claims.note: IMbrave150 update: 'median OS was 19.2 months ... and 13.4 months with sorafenib'. Lenvatinib REFLECT non-inferiority on record.
claims.fixed: Added the J Hepatol 2022 update link to the cancers.ts hcc record (Wikipedia only before).

claims.claim: HIMALAYA's STRIDE regimen (single-dose tremelimumab plus durvalumab) followed with a doubling of five-year survival (19.6% vs 9.4%), and CheckMate 9DW's nivolumab plus ipilimumab reached a median OS of 23.7 months (approved 2025).
claims.note: HIMALAYA 5-year: 'OS rates at 60 months for STRIDE vs. sorafenib were 19.6% vs. 9.4%'. CheckMate 9DW Lancet 2025: 'median 23.7 months ... vs 20.6'; FDA approval April 2025 per trial record.

claims.claim: Camrelizumab plus rivoceranib (CARES-310, OS 23.8 vs 15.2 months) is approved in China but has received three FDA complete response letters for manufacturing reasons, most recently in July 2026.
claims.note: OS 23.8 vs 15.2 months is the CARES-310 final analysis (quoted in Ahmed 2025 review; primary Lancet 2023 reported PFS). The third CRL is true: OncLive 13 July 2026 'FDA Issues Third CRL for Rivoceranib Plus Camrelizumab ... Over Additional Manufacturing Concerns' (Elevar release 10 July 2026). The hcc record cited only Wikipedia and the trial record only the second CRL.
claims.fixed: Added the OncLive third-CRL link to the cancers.ts hcc record; also corrected the record's history date '23 July' to 'announced 10 July'.

claims.claim: Second-line options after sorafenib (regorafenib, cabozantinib, ramucirumab for AFP ≥400) lack data after immunotherapy, the setting most patients now reach.
claims.note: Wikipedia: 'second-line options like regorafenib, cabozantinib, or ramucirumab (for patients with AFP >400 ng/ml)'.

claims.claim: Three phase 3 trials (EMERALD-1, LEAP-012, EMERALD-3) show that adding immunotherapy and anti-VEGF drugs to TACE prolongs progression-free survival by about 30%, but LEAP-012's final overall-survival hazard ratio of 0.98 shows PFS is a weak surrogate here, and adjuvant atezolizumab-bevacizumab (IMbrave050) lost its early benefit with follow-up.
claims.note: LEAP-012 ClinicalTrials.gov posted results: OS hazard ratio 0.98 (0.76-1.26), PFS HR 0.66; a 2026 meta-analysis of TACE+ICI trials gives PFS HR 0.63. '~30%' is a fair summary of HRs 0.63-0.77.

claims.claim: Roughly 900,000 liver cancer cases a year worldwide (GLOBOCAN), ~80% in Asia and Africa, and largely preventable: HBV vaccination and HCV cure have cut incidence in Taiwan, Japan and Egypt.
claims.note: GLOBOCAN 2022 (repo dataset public/globocan/countries.json): liver 866,136 cases; Asia 607,266 (70.1%) + Africa 73,759 (8.5%) = 78.6%. Presented undated as 'a year'. Served GCO sheet is now GLOBOCAN 2024 (843,045).
claims.fixed: Dated: 'In 2022 GLOBOCAN estimated about 866,000 liver cancer cases worldwide, ~80% in Asia and Africa'.

claims.claim: Deaths are ~800,000 a year, and in the United States the death rate has risen faster than for any other cancer over the past two decades, driven by hepatitis C and fatty liver disease.
claims.note: GLOBOCAN 2022: 758,725 liver cancer deaths (page '~800,000 a year', undated). The US claim 'death rate has risen faster than for any other cancer over the past two decades' is not on the cited Wikipedia page, which says incidence in the US and higher-income countries 'is increasing due to an increase in hepatitis C virus infections' and NASH is 'the fastest growing cause'.
claims.fixed: Now 'GLOBOCAN estimated about 759,000 deaths in 2022, and in the United States and other high-income countries incidence has been rising, driven by hepatitis C and, increasingly, fatty liver disease.'

claims.claim: TACE plus systemic therapy prolongs PFS in intermediate-stage disease in three phase 3 trials, but overall survival is unproven (LEAP-012 OS HR 0.98).
claims.note: LEAP-012 registry results: OS HR 0.98 (95% CI 0.76-1.26).

claims.claim: Very early / early (BCLC 0-A): Ablation (RFA/microwave) for ≤3 cm; resection for preserved liver function; transplantation within Milan or downstaged criteria; radiation segmentectomy as an alternative.
claims.note: BCLC 2022 (bclc-staging ref): 'the survival offered by ablation in patients with HCC ≤3 cm may be competitive with that offered by resection'.

claims.claim: Surveillance imaging every 3-6 months.
claims.note: The row's only ref (imbrave050: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT04102098 and J Hepatol 2026 update) does not state a 3-6 month post-resection imaging interval; the registry record has no imaging schedule.
claims.fixed: Removed 'every 3-6 months'.

claims.claim: Adjuvant therapy after curative resection remains unproven; recurrence is ~70% at five years.
claims.note: Wikipedia: 'Surgical resection is associated with a greater than 60% survival rate at 5 years and a recurrence rate greater than 70%.'

claims.claim: Surveillance uptake is below 25% and ultrasound misses early tumours in obese, steatotic livers;
claims.note: Not on Wikipedia. Wolf 2021 meta-analysis (29 studies, 118,799 patients with cirrhosis): 'pooled estimate for surveillance use of 24.0%'.
claims.fixed: Now 'Surveillance uptake in cirrhosis was 24% in a pooled analysis of 29 studies (Wolf 2021)'; link added to the cancers.ts hcc record.

claims.claim: It causes about one million new cases a year, concentrated in East Asia, Eastern Europe, and Latin America, where Helicobacter pylori infection, salt, and smoking drive incidence; elsewhere two-thirds present with advanced disease, which is why it accounts for 660,000 deaths a year and five-year survival outside screened populations is under 30%.
claims.note: GLOBOCAN 2022: 968,784 cases, 660,175 deaths (undated on page). The record's own SEER source contradicts 'five-year survival outside screened populations is under 30%': US 5-year relative survival '39.8%' (2016-2022); regional 23% + distant 35% = 58% of cases, not two-thirds. NCCN/ESMO/PDQ give no global two-thirds figure.
claims.fixed: Dated the GLOBOCAN figures (2022, about 970,000 and 660,000) and replaced the two-thirds/under-30% clause with the SEER figures (58% spread beyond the stomach; 39.8% five-year relative survival); SEER link added to the gastric record links.

claims.claim: Biology splits by the Lauren classification (intestinal vs diffuse) and the TCGA classes (EBV-positive, MSI, genomically stable, chromosomally unstable), and clinically by three actionable biomarkers: HER2 (~15-20%), PD-L1 (CPS ≥5 in ~60%), and Claudin 18.2 (~38% at the approval threshold), with FGFR2b, MSI, and EBV as further strata.
claims.note: Biomarker prevalences are not in the PDQ or ESMO landing page; the NCCN guideline PDF needs a login. Consistent with trials read: CheckMate 649 randomised 1,581 (CPS ≥5 subgroup 955, 60%, in the paper body); SPOTLIGHT eligibility '≥75% of tumour cells showing moderate-to-strong membranous CLDN18 staining'.

claims.claim: MATTERHORN (2025) added durvalumab to FLOT, the first perioperative immunotherapy with an overall survival benefit (3-year OS 68.6%).
claims.note: MATTERHORN final OS (ESMO 2025, ASCO Post): 'At 36 months ... from 61.9% with placebo to 68.6% with durvalumab', HR 0.78. NEJM 2025.

claims.claim: HER2-negative, PD-L1 CPS ≥5 tumours get nivolumab or pembrolizumab with chemotherapy (CheckMate 649 5-year OS 16% vs 6%);
claims.note: CheckMate 649 5-year (Ann Oncol 2026), CPS ≥5: 'Five-year OS and PFS rates were 16% versus 6% and 10% versus 6%'.

claims.claim: Second line: T-DXd for HER2-positive disease (DESTINY-Gastric04, OS 14.7 vs 11.4 months), ramucirumab + paclitaxel otherwise, and from 2026 the CLDN18.2 ADC sonesitatug vedotin (CLARITY-Gastric 01).
claims.note: DESTINY-Gastric04 NEJM 2025: 'median, 14.7 vs. 11.4 months' correct. CLARITY-Gastric 01 met its OS endpoint (OncLive 27 July 2026, 'Overall survival benefit was statistically significant ... in third-line+ and in the overall second-line+ population'); 'from 2026' presented it as an available second-line option, which no source on the record supports.
claims.fixed: Now 'the CLDN18.2 ADC sonesitatug vedotin improved overall survival after earlier treatment in CLARITY-Gastric 01 (2026)'; OncLive link added to the gastric record.

claims.claim: ~1 million cases per year, the fifth most common cancer; where endoscopic screening finds it early (Korea, Japan) most cases are cured.
claims.note: GLOBOCAN 2022: stomach 968,784 cases, 5th in incidence (repo dataset ranks). Presented undated as 'per year'.
claims.fixed: Dated: 'About 970,000 cases in 2022 (GLOBOCAN), the fifth most common cancer'.

claims.claim: 5-year survival exceeds 60% there, versus under 30% in most of the West, where it is found late; ~660,000 deaths per year, fifth among cancers.
claims.note: 'Under 30% in most of the West' is contradicted by the record's SEER source (US 39.8%, 2016-2022); '>60%' in Korea/Japan is not stated by any source on the record. Deaths: GLOBOCAN 2022 660,175, 5th (undated on page).
claims.fixed: Removed the unsourced 60%/30% comparison; now 'five-year relative survival in the United States is 39.8% (SEER, 2016 to 2022); about 660,000 deaths in 2022, fifth among cancers'.

claims.claim: In the United States, 39.8% of people diagnosed with stomach cancer in 2016-2022 were alive five years later, relative to people of the same age without the disease.
claims.note: SEER: '5-Year Relative Survival 39.8% 2016–2022'.

claims.claim: 32% of cases are found while confined to the stomach, with five-year relative survival of 78.1%; it is 39% for regional disease (23% of cases) and 8.1% for distant disease (35% of cases).
claims.note: SEER: 'Localized 32% 78.1%; Regional 23% 39.0%; Distant 35% 8.1%'.

claims.claim: Perioperative durvalumab + FLOT (MATTERHORN) is the first immunotherapy to improve survival in resectable gastric cancer (FDA November 2025).
claims.note: FDA approval of durvalumab with FLOT announced 25 November 2025 (ASCO Post, AJMC, CancerNetwork); matches the matterhorn record.

claims.claim: Claudin 18.2 is the first target with an antibody, an ADC with OS benefit (CLARITY-Gastric 01, 2026), and an approved CAR-T (satri-cel, China).
claims.note: CLARITY-Gastric 01 met OS (OncLive 27 July 2026: 'marking a first phase 3 OS win for CLDN18.2 ADCs').

claims.claim: Five-year survivors exist with chemo-immunotherapy in PD-L1-rich disease (16% vs 6%, CheckMate 649).
claims.note: CheckMate 649 5-year: OS 16% vs 6% (CPS ≥5).

claims.claim: Prevention and screening: H. pylori eradication reduces incidence; endoscopic screening programmes in Japan and Korea (biennial from age 40-50) detect most cancers at a curable stage.
claims.note: Screening intervals are not stated by the row's refs (chemoprevention, germline-testing records) and the NCCN PDF needs a login. Jun 2017 confirms the Korean programme screens 'individuals 40 years and older'; Japan's interval (2-3 years from 50) was not confirmed in raw text, so the range is left as is.

claims.claim: Early (T1a) disease: Endoscopic submucosal dissection for well-differentiated mucosal tumours ≤2 cm without ulceration (expanded criteria in Japan); otherwise gastrectomy.
claims.note: ESD criteria (≤2 cm, differentiated, no ulceration) are an NCCN statement; the NCCN PDF needs a login and the endoscopic-resection record gives no size criterion.

claims.claim: Resectable stage II-III (Western): Perioperative FLOT + durvalumab (MATTERHORN: OS HR 0.78, pCR 19%) with D2 gastrectomy;
claims.note: MATTERHORN: OS HR 0.78 (0.63-0.96) at ESMO 2025; NEJM 2025: 'pathological complete response was 19.2% in the durvalumab group and 7.2%'.

claims.claim: Resectable stage II-III (Asian practice): D2 gastrectomy then adjuvant S-1 (ACTS-GC) or CAPOX (CLASSIC) for 6-12 months; neoadjuvant approaches increasingly adopted.
claims.note: CLASSIC: 'eight 3-week cycles of oral capecitabine ... plus intravenous oxaliplatin ... for 6 months'. ACTS-GC's one-year S-1 duration was not re-read in raw text (abstract not retrieved), giving the upper end of the range.

claims.claim: Advanced, HER2-positive, first line: Trastuzumab + fluoropyrimidine/platinum + pembrolizumab (KEYNOTE-811, PD-L1 CPS ≥1); zanidatamab + chemotherapy ± tislelizumab after HERIZON-GEA-01 (PFS 12.4 vs 8.1 months; sBLA 2026).
claims.note: HERIZON-GEA-01 (ASCO GI 2026, via OncLive): 'median PFS of 12.4 months (95% CI, 9.8-18.5) vs 8.1 months'; FDA accepted the sBLA with priority review, April 2026.

claims.claim: Advanced, HER2-negative, PD-L1 CPS ≥5 (or ≥1), first line: Nivolumab (CheckMate 649) or pembrolizumab (KEYNOTE-859) or tislelizumab (RATIONALE-305) with FOLFOX or CAPOX; add zolbetuximab if CLDN18.2-positive (sequencing/combination under study).
claims.note: Thresholds match the trials: CheckMate 649 primary population CPS ≥5 (5-year paper); KEYNOTE-859 CPS ≥1/≥10 per record.

claims.claim: Advanced, CLDN18.2-positive (≥75%), HER2-negative, first line: Zolbetuximab + mFOLFOX6 or CAPOX (SPOTLIGHT/GLOW).
claims.note: SPOTLIGHT: 'CLDN18.2-positive (defined as ≥75% of tumour cells showing moderate-to-strong membranous CLDN18 staining)'.

claims.claim: Second line, HER2-positive: Trastuzumab deruxtecan 6.4 mg/kg (DESTINY-Gastric04, OS 14.7 vs 11.4 months) if HER2 persists on re-biopsy or ctDNA.
claims.note: DESTINY-Gastric04 NEJM 2025: 'median, 14.7 vs. 11.4 months; hazard ratio for death, 0.70'. 6.4 mg/kg is the trial dose per record.

claims.claim: Second line, HER2-negative: Ramucirumab + paclitaxel (RAINBOW, OS 9.6 vs 7.4 months);
claims.note: RAINBOW: 'median 9.6 months ... vs 7.4 months, hazard ratio 0.807'.

claims.claim: Third line and beyond: Trifluridine/tipiracil (TAGS, OS 5.7 vs 3.6 months); irinotecan; clinical trials (FGFR2b, CLDN18.2 bispecifics, T-cell engagers).
claims.note: TAGS: 'Median overall survival was 5.7 months ... and 3.6 months in the placebo group'.

claims.claim: Oesophageal cancer is two diseases: squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC, ~85% globally, driven by tobacco, alcohol, hot beverages, and nutritional factors along a belt from Iran through Central Asia to China) and adenocarcinoma (EAC, dominant in the West, arising from Barrett's oesophagus through reflux and obesity).
claims.note: Not in NCCN landing/ESMO/PDQ (PDQ: 'Approximately 30% of esophageal cancers in the United States are squamous cell carcinomas'). Arnold 2020: in 2018 '572 000 new cases ... 482 000 OSCCs' = 84%.
claims.fixed: Figure kept (84% rounds to about 85%); Arnold 2020 link added to the oesophageal record links.

claims.claim: It causes about 510,000 new cases a year (the seventh most common cancer) and, because of late presentation, 445,000 deaths (sixth among cancers); five-year survival is about 20% overall.
claims.note: GLOBOCAN 2022: oesophagus 511,054 cases, ranked 11th in incidence (not 7th), and 445,391 deaths, 7th in mortality (not 6th); the ranks belong to an older edition. Undated. PDQ: 'The 5-year relative survival rate is 21.6%' (US).
claims.fixed: Now 'In 2022 GLOBOCAN estimated about 511,000 new cases (the eleventh most common cancer) and ... 445,000 deaths (seventh among cancers); five-year relative survival in the United States is 21.6%.'

claims.claim: CROSS chemoradiation followed by oesophagectomy gives 10-year survival of 38% versus 25% for surgery alone; perioperative FLOT is the alternative for adenocarcinoma (ESOPEC favoured it).
claims.note: CROSS 10-year (JCO 2021): 'The absolute 10-year overall survival benefit was 13% (38% v 25%)'.

claims.claim: CheckMate 577 added a year of adjuvant nivolumab for residual disease after chemoradiation (DFS 22.4 vs 11.0 months), and SANO showed that patients with a clinical complete response can be watched rather than operated on with non-inferior survival.
claims.note: PDQ: 'The median DFS was 22.4 months ... compared with 11.0 months among patients who received placebo'.

claims.claim: Advanced disease is treated with chemotherapy plus PD-1 blockade: pembrolizumab (KEYNOTE-590, both histologies), nivolumab ± ipilimumab (CheckMate 648, squamous), tislelizumab (RATIONALE-306, squamous PD-L1 ≥1%), and camrelizumab or sintilimab in China.
claims.note: RATIONALE-306 PD-L1 ≥1% US indication per the trial record (OncLive FDA approval); CheckMate 648 primary population tumour-cell PD-L1 ≥1% per PDQ.

claims.claim: In 2026 the EGFR×HER3 bispecific ADC izalontamab brengitecan became the first agent to improve overall survival in second-line ESCC after immunotherapy (PANKU-Esophagus01).
claims.note: PANKU-Esophagus01 interim analysis presented at ASCO 2026 (release 2 June 2026): 'statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvements in overall survival and progression-free survival' after PD-1/PD-L1 plus platinum.

claims.claim: ~510,000 cases per year; ~85% squamous cell carcinoma globally, adenocarcinoma dominant in North America, Western Europe, and Australia.
claims.note: GLOBOCAN 2022: 511,054 cases (undated as 'per year'). ~85% SCC is not on NCCN/ESMO/PDQ; Arnold 2020 gives 482,000 of 572,000 (84%) in 2018.
claims.fixed: Dated to 2022 and sourced the share ('84% in 2018, Arnold 2020'); link added.

claims.claim: 5-year survival is >80% for endoscopically treated early cancers and ~20% overall; ~445,000 deaths per year.
claims.note: '>80% for endoscopically treated early cancers' is not in any source on the record; PDQ gives 21.6% overall and 48.1% at the local stage (US). Deaths: GLOBOCAN 2022 445,391 (undated).
claims.fixed: Replaced with 'Five-year relative survival is 21.6% overall in the United States and 48.1% when found at the local stage; about 445,000 deaths in 2022.'

claims.claim: Chemoradiation before surgery (CROSS) has a durable 13-point 10-year survival gain; organ preservation after complete response is non-inferior (SANO).
claims.note: CROSS: '13% (38% v 25%)' absolute 10-year gain; SANO non-inferior per the sano record.

claims.claim: Adjuvant nivolumab doubles disease-free survival after incomplete response to chemoradiation (CheckMate 577), though OS was not significantly improved.
claims.note: DFS 22.4 vs 11.0 months (PDQ), so DFS doubled; OS not significant at ASCO 2025 final analysis per the checkmate-577 record (HR 0.85). PDQ itself says OS 'have not been published'.

claims.claim: The first bispecific ADC with an OS benefit in second-line ESCC (iza-bren, 2026) gives post-immunotherapy squamous cancer its first targeted option.
claims.note: PANKU-Esophagus01 2026 OS benefit (ASCO 2026 release).

claims.claim: Advanced squamous cell carcinoma, first line: Chemotherapy + pembrolizumab (KEYNOTE-590), nivolumab (CheckMate 648), or tislelizumab (RATIONALE-306, PD-L1 ≥1%); nivolumab + ipilimumab chemotherapy-free option; camrelizumab/sintilimab/toripalimab in China.
claims.note: RATIONALE-306 PD-L1 ≥1% matches the trial record (OS 16.8 vs 9.6 months in PD-L1 ≥1%; US approval restricted to PD-L1 ≥1).

claims.claim: Second line, squamous cell carcinoma: Izalontamab brengitecan after PD-(L)1 + platinum (PANKU-Esophagus01, OS and PFS benefit, 2026; approval pending); otherwise taxane or irinotecan; nivolumab/pembrolizumab if IO-naive.
claims.note: PANKU-Esophagus01: OS and PFS benefit at interim analysis, ASCO 2026; population progressed after PD-1/PD-L1 plus platinum.

claims.claim: The gallbladder is a pear-shaped pouch about 8 cm long under the right lobe of the liver that concentrates and stores bile; it is not essential and people digest normally without it (CRUK, what is gallbladder cancer).
claims.note: CRUK: 'The gallbladder is a small, hollow, pear-shaped pouch about 8cm long. It lies in the upper tummy (abdomen) underneath the right side of the liver.'

claims.claim: Hundal and Shaffer describe it as the commonest biliary tract cancer, 80 to 95 percent of biliary tract cancers in their review, and Roa and colleagues note that most cases are discovered incidentally after cholecystectomy for symptomatic stones.
claims.note: Hundal 2014: 'the most common malignancy of the biliary tract, accounting for 80%-95% of biliary tract cancers'; Roa 2022: 'most GBCs are discovered incidentally following cholecystectomy for symptomatic gallbladder stones'.

claims.claim: World: the IARC gallbladder fact sheet, served today with the GLOBOCAN 2024 estimates, gives 126,384 new cases (22nd commonest cancer, age-standardised rate 1.2 per 100,000) and 92,029 deaths (20th, 0.82 per 100,000) a year, with 72.4 percent of cases in Asia, 10.0 percent in Europe, 8.8 percent in Latin America and the Caribbean and 4.3 percent in Northern America.
claims.note: GCO gallbladder fact sheet, printed 'GLOBOCAN 2024': rank 22, 126 384 cases, ASR 1.2; rank 20, 92 029 deaths, ASR 0.82; Asia 72.4%, Europe 10.0%, Latin America and the Caribbean 8.8%, Northern America 4.3%. Page names the 2024 edition.

claims.claim: The highest national age-standardised incidence on the sheet is Bolivia (6.7 per 100,000, both sexes;
claims.note: GLOBOCAN 2024 sheet: Bolivia (Plurinational State of) (6.7) top incidence, both sexes.

claims.claim: 6.0 in men) and Chile (7.6 per 100,000 in women); the highest regions are South Central Asia, South America and Eastern Asia.
claims.note: GLOBOCAN 2024 sheet: males Bolivia (6.0), females Chile (7.6); top regions South Central Asia, South America, Eastern Asia.

claims.claim: Randi and colleagues (2006) recorded the highest registry rates in women in Delhi (21.5 per 100,000), South Karachi (13.8) and Quito (12.9), high rates in Korea, Japan and parts of central and eastern Europe, and a female to male ratio of about 3.
claims.note: Randi 2006: 'women in Delhi, India (21.5/100,000), South Karachi, Pakistan (13.8/100,000) and Quito, Ecuador (12.9/100,000)... Female-to-male incidence ratios were generally around 3'.

claims.claim: In the United States about 3,700 people a year were diagnosed in 2007 to 2011 (1.13 per 100,000) and 2,000 died (0.62 per 100,000), two thirds of them women, with rates three times higher in American Indian and Alaska Native people (Henley 2015); a 2026 meta-analysis found 3 to 3.5-fold higher incidence in Native American people nationally and 6 to 8.5-fold in the Southwest and Alaska (Kosuru 2026).
claims.note: Henley 2015: 'approximately 3,700 persons ... (rate = 1.13 ...) and 2,000 died (rate = 0.62 ...)', 'Two thirds ... among women', 'three times higher among American Indian and Alaska Native persons'. Kosuru 2026: 3.5- and 3-fold nationally, 6- and 8.5-fold in Alaska and the Southwest.

claims.claim: SEER incidence fell by 1.65 percent a year from 1973 but has been flat since 2002 (Low 2022).
claims.note: Low 2022: 'incidence decreased by 1.65% ... per year since 1973, but has plateaued since 2002'.

claims.claim: In India a Tata Memorial registry of 1,950 patients (2019 to 2022) found 84.6 percent came from, or had migrated from, the Gangetic belt, and 60 percent had metastatic disease at presentation (Patkar 2025); in Pakistan a prospective series of 233 cases was 77 percent women with a mean age of 55 (Malik 2003).
claims.note: Patkar 2025: Jan 2019 to Dec 2022, 1950 patients, 84.6% Gangetic belt or migrants, '60 % had metastatic disease'. Malik 2003: 233 cases, 'women (77%)', 'Mean age was 55 years'.

claims.claim: United Kingdom (Cancer Research UK, drawing on the national registries): 1,288 new cases a year (2019 and 2021 to 2022 average, ICD-10 C23), around 900 in females and 380 in males, under 1 percent of all cancers;
claims.note: CRUK statistics hub: '1,288 new cases of gallbladder cancer each year, 2019, 2021-2022, UK'; incidence page: 'around 900 new cases in females and around 380 new cases in males', 'less than 1% of all new cancer cases'.

claims.claim: 54 percent are diagnosed at 75 or over and rates peak at ages 85 to 89, which account for 13 percent of cases.
claims.note: CRUK: 'more than half (54%) ... aged 75 and over'; 'highest in people aged 85 to 89 ... (13%)'.

claims.claim: Incidence rates have risen by 79 percent since the early 1990s and by 33 percent in the last decade, and are projected to rise a further 43 percent by 2038 to 2040 to about 3,100 cases a year.
claims.note: CRUK: 'increased by around four-fifths (79%) ... since the early 1990s ... a third (33%) in the last decade'; 'projected to increase by 43% between 2024-2026 and 2038-2040, with around 3,100 new cases each year'.

claims.claim: Rates are higher in the Asian and Black ethnic groups than the White group in England (2013 to 2017).
claims.note: CRUK: 'higher in the Asian and Black ethnic groups, compared with the White ethnic group, in England (2013-2017)'.

claims.claim: There are about 810 deaths a year (2022 to 2024), 60 percent at 75 or over; it is the 23rd commonest cause of cancer death (20th in women).
claims.note: CRUK: 'around 810 gallbladder cancer deaths ... (2022-2024)', '(60%) ... aged 75 and over', '23rd most common cause of cancer death', '20th ... in females'.

claims.claim: Mortality rates are 28 percent lower than in the early 1970s but 29 percent higher than a decade ago.
claims.note: CRUK: 'decreased by more than a quarter (28%) ... since the early 1970s, and ... increased by more than a quarter (29%) in the last decade'.

claims.claim: Lifetime risk is about 1 in 210 for females and 1 in 670 for males born in 1961.
claims.note: CRUK: 'nearly 1 in 210 ... for females, and 1 in 670 ... for males born in 1961'.

claims.claim: A UK primary-care cohort found biliary tract cancer incidence rising 4 percent a year in 2000 to 2010 and higher in the most deprived quintile (Keane 2014).
claims.note: Keane 2014: 2000-2010 'BTC by 4% (95% CI 2.00-6.00%)' a year; 'BTC was associated with increasing deprivation (most deprived versus least deprived quintile (OR: 1.45'.

claims.claim: Half of cases in England (2019) were diagnosed after an emergency presentation and 17 percent through an urgent suspected cancer referral; in Northern Ireland 24 percent of staged cases were stage I or II (2015 to 2019); in England in 2022, 21 percent of patients had surgery, 22 percent systemic therapy and 2 percent radiotherapy as part of primary treatment (CRUK main statistics page).
claims.note: CRUK hub: 2019 England '(17%) ... urgent suspected cancer ... (50%) via an emergency presentation'; NI '24% ... early stage (I & II) ... 2015 and 2019'; 'In 2022, 22% ... SACT, 2% ... radiotherapy, and 21% underwent surgery'.

claims.claim: Risk factors, with the evidence: gallstones are the strongest (pooled relative risk 4.9 for a history of benign gallbladder disease, Randi 2006; odds ratio 7.26 for gallbladder cancer in a 2021 meta-analysis of 30 studies, Huang; hazard ratio 7.35 for gallbladder cancer death in 396,720 Koreans followed by ultrasound, Ryu 2016), and larger stones carry more risk (odds ratio 2.4 for stones 2.0 to 2.9 cm and 10.1 for 3 cm or larger versus under 1 cm, Diehl 1983).
claims.note: Randi: pooled RR 4.9 for history of gallstones; Huang 2021: 7 cohort + 23 case-control studies, GBC OR 7.26; Ryu 2016: 396,720 Koreans, HR 7.35; Diehl 1983: OR 2.4 for 2.0-2.9 cm and 10.1 for 3 cm or larger vs under 1 cm.

claims.claim: Porcelain gallbladder: about eight times the risk (CRUK, citing Schnelldorfer), but the 2013 systematic review found cancer in only 6 percent of calcified gallbladders in studies without selection bias against 1 percent in matched controls, and a 2018 cohort observed 90 patients for a mean 3.2 years without a cancer (DesJardins).
claims.note: CRUK: 'around eight times as high ... porcelain gallbladder'; Schnelldorfer 2013: subgroup without selection bias 'only 6 % ... compared to 1 %'; DesJardins 2018: observation group n=90, no malignancy over 'mean of 3.2 ± 3.2 years'.

claims.claim: Gallbladder polyps: about 8 percent of polyps of 10 mm or more are malignant and about 4 percent of polyps reach that size (CRUK, citing Elmasry 2016, whose review found 0.57 percent of 5,482 ultrasound-detected polyps were malignant).
claims.note: CRUK: 'Around 8% of larger (10mm+) gallbladder polyps are malignant ... Around 4% ... are 10mm+'; Elmasry 2016: 'Of the 5482 GBPs reported, malignant GBPs had an incidence of just 0.57%'.

claims.claim: Primary sclerosing cholangitis: 37 percent of explanted gallbladders showed dysplasia and 14 percent adenocarcinoma in one transplant series (Lewis 2007); polyps were seen in 16 percent of 453 patients and the cancer rate among those with a polyp was 8.8 per 1,000 person-years (van Erp 2020).
claims.note: Lewis 2007: 72 gallbladders, 'dysplasia in 27 (37%) ... adenocarcinoma in 10 (14%)'; van Erp 2020: 453 patients, polyp in 16%, 'GBC rate was 8.8 ... per 1000 person-years'.

claims.claim: Chronic Salmonella Typhi carriage: summary relative risk 4.6 for anti-Vi antibodies and 5.0 for bile or stool culture across more than 1,000 cases (Koshiol 2016; pooled 4.8 in Randi 2006).
claims.note: Koshiol 2016 meta-analysis of '>1000 GBC cases': 'summary relative risk was 4.6 ... for anti-Vi and 5.0 ... for bile or stool culture'; Randi: pooled RR 4.8.

claims.claim: Anomalous pancreaticobiliary junction: about seven times the risk in a meta-analysis of case-control studies (CRUK, citing Deng 2011); in a 2025 MRCP series the anomaly was present in 0.44 percent of benign cholecystectomies but 16 percent of gallbladder cancers, an estimated 38-fold higher incidence (Shirai 2025).
claims.note: CRUK: 'around seven times as high ... pancreaticobiliary maljunction'; Shirai 2025: PBM in '0.44% ... of 2046 benign cholecystectomies, 16% ... of gallbladder cancers', '38-fold higher'.

claims.claim: Obesity: 20 percent of UK cases are attributed to overweight and obesity; risk is 22 to 29 percent higher in overweight women and 68 to 78 percent higher in obese women, and 43 to 54 percent higher in obese men (CRUK risk page; relative risk 1.69 for obesity across 14 cohorts, Liu 2016).
claims.note: CRUK: '20% ... caused by overweight and obesity', '22-29% higher in women who are overweight ... 68-78% higher in women who are obese', '43-54% higher in men who are obese'; Liu 2016: obesity RR 1.69, 14 cohorts.

claims.claim: Sex and age: 71 percent of UK patients are women and risk climbs steeply after 75 (CRUK).
claims.note: CRUK patient page: '71 out of 100 people diagnosed ... (71%) are women'; incidence peaks at 85-89 and 54% are 75 or over.

claims.claim: Aflatoxin: exposure markers were found in 32 percent of Shanghai gallbladder cancer patients against 15 percent of gallstone controls, odds ratio 7.61 for the top exposure quartile and a population attributable fraction of 20 percent (Koshiol 2017), with a parallel signal in Chile (Nogueira 2015).
claims.note: Koshiol 2017: AFB1-lysine 'detected in 67 (32%) of 209 ... and 37 (15%) of the 250 controls', fourth vs first quartile 'OR ... 7.61', 'population-attributable fraction ... was 20%' (PMC full text).

claims.claim: Genetics: a family history raises risk about five-fold (CRUK); the Indian genome-wide association study found risk variants at 7q21.12 spanning the bile phospholipid transporter genes ABCB1 and ABCB4 (per-allele odds ratios 1.47 to 1.61) and estimated a sibling relative risk of 3.15 from common variation (Mhatre 2017); in Chile each 1 percent rise in Mapuche ancestry raised risk by about 0.8 percent in a Mendelian randomisation analysis, partly through gallstones (Zollner 2023;
claims.note: CRUK: family history 'around five times as high'; Mhatre 2017: 7q21.12 (ABCB1, ABCB4), per-allele ORs 1.47, 1.61, 1.57, 'sibling relative risk 3.15'; Zollner 2023: 'risk increase of 0.8% per 1% increase in Mapuche ancestry'.

claims.claim: Also on the CRUK list: type 2 diabetes (44 to 49 percent higher), smoking (19 percent higher in current smokers), heavy alcohol (about three times at 50 g or more a day), choledochal cysts and ionising radiation.
claims.note: CRUK risk page: diabetes '44-49% higher', smokers '19% higher', alcohol 'around 3 times higher in people who drink 50g+'.

claims.claim: About 20 percent of UK cases are judged preventable.
claims.note: CRUK: '20% of gallbladder cancer cases in the UK are preventable'.

claims.claim: A large share is found by the pathologist after a cholecystectomy for presumed gallstone disease: 0.25 to 0.89 percent of all cholecystectomy specimens in the series reviewed by Soreide (2019), 0.29 percent of 9,698 in a Danish department (0.08 percent under 60, 0.67 percent over 60;
claims.note: Soreide 2019: '0.25-0.89 per cent of all cholecystectomy specimens'; Lerche-Jorgensen 2025: 9,698 gallbladders, 0.29%, '≤ 60 years ... 0.08%', '> 60 years ... 0.67%' (page says 'under 60' for ≤60).

claims.claim: In the Pakistani series pain was the presenting symptom in 89 percent, weight loss in 42 percent, jaundice in 33 percent and a palpable mass in a quarter (Malik 2003).
claims.note: Malik 2003: 'pain (89%) ... weight loss (42%), and jaundice (33%). One-quarter of patients had a palpable abdominal mass'.

claims.claim: Jaundice usually means the tumour has reached the bile duct or hilar nodes: even among patients without distant spread who were operated on, five-year survival was 21.9 percent with jaundice against 68.3 percent without (Chaudhary 2021, Langenbecks Arch Surg, doi 10.1007/s00423-020-02075-8).
claims.note: Chaudhary 2021: '5-year survival rate of M0 ... GBC patients with jaundice, who underwent resectional surgery, was 21.9%, versus 68.3% in those without jaundice'.

claims.claim: The NHS asks people to seek urgent help for jaundice or for vomiting lasting more than two days, and NICE NG12 (1.2.10) tells GPs to consider an urgent direct-access ultrasound for an upper abdominal mass consistent with an enlarged gallbladder.
claims.note: NHS: urgent GP/111 if 'the whites of your eyes or your skin turn yellow' or 'you're being sick for more than 2 days'; NG12 1.2.10: 'Consider an urgent, direct access ultrasound scan ... upper abdominal mass consistent with an enlarged gall bladder'.

claims.claim: Diagnosis: ultrasound is the first test for a gallbladder mass, wall thickening or polyp, and the joint European polyp guideline keeps it as the primary investigation, with contrast-enhanced or endoscopic ultrasound reserved for expert centres in difficult cases (Foley 2022).
claims.note: Foley 2022 recommendation 1: primary investigation with abdominal ultrasound; contrast-enhanced and endoscopic ultrasound 'may be useful ... in difficult cases' in expert centres.

claims.claim: Contrast CT of chest, abdomen and pelvis stages the tumour and judges resectability (pooled sensitivity 99 percent, specificity 76 percent for resectability;
claims.note: Li 2013: 'Pooled sensitivity was 99% ... pooled specificity was 76%'.

claims.claim: Both are weak at finding involved lymph nodes: CT sensitivity ranged from 25 to 93 percent across studies and MRI pooled sensitivity was 75 percent (de Savornin Lohman 2019).
claims.note: de Savornin Lohman 2019: 'Sensitivity of CT ranged from 0.25 to 0.93'; MRI 'sensitivity 0.75'.

claims.claim: FDG PET-CT is accurate for the primary (sensitivity 96 percent) and for distant metastases (95 percent) but less so for nodes (75 percent), and changes management in a meaningful share of patients (Parida 2021); gallbladder cancers are PET-avid, and PET can spare a futile re-resection (Soreide 2019).
claims.note: Parida 2021: local disease sensitivity 96%, metastatic 95%, nodal 75%; 'changed the management in significant proportion'. Soreide: 'Gallbladder cancers are PET-avid, and PET may ... prevent unnecessary surgery'.

claims.claim: Blood tests include liver function and the tumour markers CA 19-9 and CEA, which are raised more often in cancer than in benign disease but cannot make or exclude the diagnosis and did not predict survival in a 200-patient Indian series (Sinha 2022);
claims.note: Sinha 2022: 200 patients (80 GBC, 120 benign); 'no significant association ... between ... elevated levels of any tumor marker with respect to survival'.

claims.claim: 58 percent of the Pakistani series had a raised CEA (Malik 2003).
claims.note: Malik 2003: '58% had elevated carcinoma embryonic antigen'.

claims.claim: When imaging shows a resectable mass, UK hepatobiliary teams generally do not biopsy through the tumour beforehand: the Liverpool MDT relied on the surgeon's intraoperative assessment with frozen section, which matched final histology in every case but doubled operating time (Chan 2022), and an Imperial College unit runs a single-stage operation in which frozen section decides whether to extend a cholecystectomy to a radical resection (Banh 2024).
claims.note: Chan 2022: 'All frozen sections were congruent with final histopathology but doubled the operating time'; Banh 2024 single-stage frozen-section approach.

claims.claim: Pathology: about 90 percent are adenocarcinomas, which Cancer Research UK divides into non-papillary, papillary and mucinous; squamous cell carcinoma makes up about 5 percent, and adenosquamous carcinoma, small cell (neuroendocrine) carcinoma, sarcoma, neuroendocrine tumours and lymphoma are rare (CRUK types page).
claims.note: CRUK types: 'Around 90 out of every 100 ... are adenocarcinomas'; 'Around 5 out of every 100 ... (around 5%) are squamous'.

claims.claim: Mucinous carcinoma is defined by extracellular mucin in more than half of the tumour and was 2.5 percent of 606 carcinomas (Dursun 2012); adenosquamous carcinoma needs a squamous component above 25 percent and was 5 percent of adenocarcinoma-plus-adenosquamous cases in the National Cancer Database (Murimwa 2021;
claims.note: Dursun 2012: 'only 15 (2.5%) ... (stromal mucin deposition constituting >50% of the tumor)' of 606; Gasparello 2026: 'more than 25% squamous component'; Murimwa 2021: 13,158 patients, '703 (5%) with adenosquamous'.

claims.claim: Gasparello 2026); neuroendocrine carcinoma was 31 of 636 cancers, under 5 percent, in a pathology cohort and 1.6 percent of gallbladder carcinomas in SEER (Reid 2026;
claims.note: Reid 2026: '31 NECs were identified through an analysis of 636 GB cancers'; Cai 2022: 'GB-NEC incidence rate was 1.6% (of all gallbladder carcinomas)'.

claims.claim: Grade runs from 1 (well differentiated) to 3 (poorly differentiated) (CRUK stages and grades).
claims.note: CRUK: 'There are 3 grades of gallbladder cancer – grade 1 to grade 3.'

claims.claim: Early cancers are often invisible to the naked eye: 60 percent of 190 Tis, T1a and T1b tumours were not apparent on gross examination, which is why the AHPBA asks for at least three sections and the cystic duct margin from every routine specimen in high-incidence areas (Roa 2013;
claims.note: Roa 2013: '(114/190; 60%), the tumor was inapparent by gross examination'; Aloia 2015: 'a minimum of three sections and the cystic duct margin' in high-incidence areas.

claims.claim: N2: four or more (the count replaced the 7th edition's anatomical grouping after series such as Shirai 2012 showed 0, 1 to 3 and 4 or more nodes stratified survival).
claims.note: CRUK: 'N2 - means there are cancer cells in 4 or more nearby lymph nodes'; Shirai 2012: 'number of positive nodes (0, 1 to 3, ≥ 4; P <0.001)'.

claims.claim: What each means for surgery: Tis and T1a are cured by the cholecystectomy already done in almost all cases (five-year survival up to 100 percent after cholecystectomy alone, Soreide 2019); from T1b upwards guidelines recommend radical (extended) cholecystectomy with resection of the liver bed and portal lymphadenectomy, though the T1b benefit is contested (meta-analysis of 26 cohorts: better overall survival with extended surgery, hazard ratio 0.48, but no difference in disease-specific survival, Cho 2026; no survival difference in 950 National Cancer Database patients, Rhodin 2024);
claims.note: Soreide: T1a or less 'up to 100 per cent after cholecystectomy alone'; Cho 2026: 26 cohorts, OS HR 0.48, DSS HR 0.73 (NS); Rhodin 2024: 950 NCDB patients, HR 1.23 (NS).

claims.claim: T2b tumours carry more vascular invasion (51 versus 19 percent), perineural invasion (33 versus 8 percent) and nodal spread (40 versus 17 percent) than T2a and roughly twice the hazard of death (Shindoh 2015;
claims.note: Shindoh 2015: '51% vs 19%, 33% vs 8%, and 40% vs 17%'; hepatic side HR 2.7.

claims.claim: Alrawashdeh 2022 meta-analysis of 2,531 patients), so liver resection matters most on the hepatic side;
claims.note: Alrawashdeh 2022: 'Fifteen retrospective studies (2531 patients' , OS HR 2.18 T2b vs T2a.

claims.claim: T4 disease and N2 nodes, or para-aortic node involvement, rarely benefit from resection and are directed to systemic treatment (Aloia 2015).
claims.note: Aloia 2015 says 'Patients with confirmed metastases to N2 nodal stations do not benefit from radical resection and should receive systemic and/or palliative treatments' (N2 there is the 7th-edition nodal station, not the 8th-edition count of 4+ the page defines just before) and that 'preoperatively staged T3 or T4 N1 disease should be considered for clinical trials of neoadjuvant chemotherapy'; it does not say T4 disease rarely benefits from resection.
claims.fixed: Rewrote: 'confirmed spread to the N2 nodal stations of the 7th edition (a location, not the 8th edition's count of four or more) gains nothing from radical resection and is directed to systemic or palliative treatment, and T3 or T4 disease with involved regional nodes should be considered for trials of chemotherapy before surgery (Aloia 2015).'

claims.claim: The 8th edition N split did not improve prognostic performance over the 7th in a 7,743-patient validation (Giannis 2021), and a Korean series found the N category discriminated only when six or more nodes had been examined (Sung 2020), the count the AHPBA asks surgeons to aim for.
claims.note: Giannis 2021: 7743 patients; 8th edition N changes 'failing to improve the prognostic performance'; Sung 2020: survival differences when '≥ 6 examined lymph nodes'; Aloia: 'goal recovery of at least six nodes'.

claims.claim: Polyps: the 2022 ESGAR, EAES, EFISDS and ESGE guideline recommends cholecystectomy for polyps of 10 mm or more; for 6 to 9 mm polyps with a risk factor (age over 60, primary sclerosing cholangitis, Asian ethnicity, or a sessile polyp including focal wall thickening over 4 mm); ultrasound at 6 months, 1 year and 2 years for 6 to 9 mm polyps without risk factors or 5 mm or smaller polyps with one, stopping after 2 years if there is no growth; no follow-up for polyps of 5 mm or less with no risk factors; cholecystectomy if a polyp reaches 10 mm, and discussion if it grows 2 mm or more (Foley 2022).
claims.note: Foley 2022 recommendations 2, 4-7 match (10 mm; 6-9 mm with risk factor: age over 60, PSC, Asian ethnicity, sessile incl. wall thickening > 4 mm; ultrasound at 6 months, 1 year, 2 years; none for ≤5 mm without risk; 2 mm growth).

claims.claim: Cancer Research UK lists anomalous pancreaticobiliary junction and choledochal cysts among the congenital risk factors, and the 38-fold incidence estimated with the maljunction (Shirai 2025) is the argument for removing the gallbladder once it is found.
claims.note: Shirai 2025: '38-fold higher than that in the general population'; CRUK lists pancreaticobiliary maljunction and choledochal cysts.

claims.claim: Prophylactic cholecystectomy has traditionally been advised for porcelain gallbladder (the CRUK patient page says a doctor may suggest it); that advice is now debated because the cancer risk in unselected calcified gallbladders is far lower than once thought and observation caused no cancers in a 90-patient cohort (Schnelldorfer 2013;
claims.note: DesJardins 2018: observation group n = 90, no malignancy over mean 3.2 years; CRUK patient page: doctor 'may suggest that you have surgery'.

claims.claim: For T1b or deeper disease the patient should be referred to a hepatobiliary centre for re-resection, ideally 4 to 8 weeks after the first operation (median survival 40.4 months, against 17.4 months for under 4 weeks and 22.4 months for over 8 weeks in 207 US patients, Ethun 2017), with cross-sectional imaging and often PET-CT in the interval.
claims.note: Ethun 2017: 207 patients; 'between 4 and 8 weeks had the longest median overall survival (group B: 40.4 months) compared with ... early (group A: 17.4 months) or late (group C: 22.4 months)'.

claims.claim: Port-site metastases fell from 18.6 percent before 2000 to 10.3 percent since (Berger-Richardson 2017), and routine excision of port sites has no effect on survival (Soreide 2019).
claims.note: Berger-Richardson 2017: 'decreased from 18.6% prior to 2000 ... to 10.3% since then'; Soreide: 'Routine resection of port sites has no effect on survival'.

claims.claim: A Dutch study found only 53.9 percent of patients eligible for re-resection were referred to a tertiary centre (van Dooren 2024), a gap the UK pathway pages take up.
claims.note: van Dooren 2024: 'Of 243 patients eligible for re-resection ... 131 (53.9%) were referred to a tertiary centre'.

claims.claim: Around 1,300 people a year in the UK, seven in ten of them women and more than half aged 75 or over; rare here, but common where gallstones are common, above all Bolivia, Chile, northern India and Pakistan (Cancer Research UK;
claims.note: CRUK: around 1,300 a year, 71% women, 54% aged 75 or over.

claims.claim: England, people diagnosed 2016 to 2020: around 30 percent survive one year and 11.8 percent survive five years (net survival), similar in men and women and similar to the European average;
claims.note: CRUK patient survival page (England 2016-2020, net survival): 'around 30 out of 100 ... at least 1 year', 'more than 10 out of 100 ... at least 5 years'; professional page: '11.8%', similar by sex and to the European average.

claims.claim: 18.2 percent at ages 15 to 54 against 6.7 percent at 75 to 99.
An older cohort (2009 to 2013) gave 15 percent ten-year survival.
claims.note: CRUK hub: '15% survive gallbladder cancer for 10 or more years, 2009-2013, England'.

claims.claim: Cancer Research UK quotes the US SEER programme for people diagnosed 2013 to 2019 instead: more than 65 percent five-year relative survival for localised disease, almost 30 percent for regional disease, and almost 5 percent for distant disease, with the caution that US health care and data collection differ from the UK.
claims.note: CRUK patient survival page: SEER 2013-2019, localised 'more than 65%', regional 'almost 30%', distant 'almost 5%', with the UK caveat.

claims.claim: Two further figures qualify the averages: cancers confined to the mucosa (T1a or less) had five-year survival of up to 100 percent after cholecystectomy alone in the series reviewed by Soreide, and 190 early (Tis, T1a, T1b) carcinomas from a high-incidence region had 92.3 percent five-year and 90.4 percent ten-year survival (Roa 2013).
claims.note: Soreide: 'up to 100 per cent after cholecystectomy alone'; Roa 2013: 190 early carcinomas, 'Overall actuarial survival was 92.3 % at 5 years and 90.4 % at 10 years'.

claims.claim: In a SEER cohort of 2,433 patients diagnosed 2010 to 2015, 82 percent of whom had surgery, median survival was 19 months and five-year survival 28.8 percent (Zhu 2020).
claims.note: Zhu 2020: 2433 SEER patients 2010-2015, surgery 82.1%, 'overall median survival time ... 19 months and the 5-year survival rate was 28.8%'.

claims.claim: Where it is found matters more than any drug: the same tumour has a five-year survival near 100 percent as a T1a incidental finding and under 5 percent once it has spread (Soreide 2019;
claims.note: Soreide: T1a 'up to 100 per cent'; CRUK quoting SEER: distant 'almost 5%'.

claims.claim: Incidental cancers are rising with the volume of cholecystectomies; the evidence now favours re-resection 4 to 8 weeks after the first operation, PET-CT beforehand, and no routine port-site excision.
claims.note: Ethun 2017 (4 to 8 weeks); Soreide (PET, port sites).

claims.claim: The joint European polyp guideline (2022) gives ultrasound-based rules by polyp size and risk factor, replacing ad hoc surveillance.
claims.note: Foley et al., Eur Radiol 2022 (published 2022).

claims.claim: TP53 (47 to 63%), CDKN2A/B loss (14 to 21%), ERBB2 (14 to 16%, split roughly 8% amplification and 4% mutation), KRAS (7 to 11%), PIK3CA (about 11%), ARID1A (13 to 25%), SMAD4 (21 to 38%, prognostic), CTNNB1 (about 6%), ELF3 (about 9%), STK11 (about 9%, prognostic), MDM2 amplification (about 12%) and CCNE1 amplification (about 9%) define the disease;
claims.note: Giraldo 2022: 'TP53 63% and CDKN2A 21% ... ERBB2 15% and KRAS 11%'; Li 2014: TP53 47.1%, KRAS 7.8%; Mondaca 2024: ERBB2 14% (8% amplification, 4% mutation). Recount of cBioPortal gbc_mskcc_2022 by API matched the page exactly (TP53 154/244, ARID1A 50, SMAD4 52, CTNNB1 15, ELF3 21, STK11 22, PIK3CA 26, MDM2 amp 29, CCNE1 amp 22).

claims.claim: IDH1 (0.4%), FGFR2 fusions (none deposited) and NTRK fusions (about 0.4%) are rare, the mirror image of intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma.
claims.note: Molecular table (cBioPortal gbc_mskcc_2022): IDH1 1 of 244 (0.4%), no FGFR2 fusion deposited, one NTRK1 fusion patient of 233 (about 0.4%); Giraldo: 'No recurrent structural variants were identified'.

claims.claim: About a third of patients carry something actionable (Giraldo 2022) and 22% a top-tier alteration (Cowzer 2026).
claims.note: Giraldo 2022: actionable alterations 'identified in 35% of patients'; Cowzer 2026: level 1/2 alteration in 'gallbladder 22%'.

claims.claim: Indian patients present a decade earlier with less ARID1A, SMAD4 and CDKN2A but the same 15% ERBB2 (Suryavanshi 2025);
claims.note: Suryavanshi 2025: 'diagnosed nearly a decade earlier', 'ERBB2 (15%...)'; table cites lower ARID1A, SMAD4 (7%), CDKN2A (9%).

claims.claim: Chilean tumours show lower TP53 and high TSC2 and NOTCH1 on a small panel series (Erices 2025) and a comparable ERBB2 rate to the United States (Mondaca 2024);
claims.note: Erices 2025: 56 tumours, 'TP53 (30%), TSC2 (29%), and NOTCH1 (27%)'; Mondaca 2024: ERBB2 'comparable between the two cohorts (15% v 9%; P = .42)'.

claims.claim: Chinese exomes put the ErbB pathway in 36.8% (Li 2014).
claims.note: Li 2014: 'ErbB signaling ... affecting 36.8% (21/57) of the GBC samples'.

claims.claim: Most cancers arise through flat metaplasia, dysplasia and carcinoma in situ over 10 to 15 years (Roa 1996, 2006); a minority through adenomas and intracholecystic papillary-tubular neoplasms, which carry invasive cancer in 55% but a better outlook (Adsay 2012).
claims.note: Roa 1996: 'the period required to progress from dysplasia to advanced gallbladder carcinoma would be around 15 years'; Roa 2006 age gradient 51.9 to 62.9 years; Adsay 2012: 'Overall, 55% of the cases had an associated invasive carcinoma'.

claims.claim: Chronic Salmonella Typhi carriage raises risk four to five fold and the bacterium transforms predisposed cells through MAPK and AKT signalling (Koshiol 2016, Scanu 2015).
claims.note: Koshiol 2016: summary RR 4.6 and 5.0; Scanu 2015: 'activation of MAPK and AKT pathways ... is critical to both ignite and sustain transformation'.

claims.claim: PD-L1 on tumour cells at a 1% cut-off is 14.7% in Western and 23% in Indian series, and higher PD-L1 marks poorly differentiated tumours with shorter survival (Albrecht 2021, Neyaz 2018); poor-survival transcriptomic subtypes are defined by myeloid suppressor cells, desmoplasia, hypoxia and T-cell dysfunction (Nepal 2021).
claims.note: Albrecht 2021: 'PD-L1 in a subset of 14.7% GBC patients at a TPS cut-off of 1%'; Neyaz 2018: 'Tumour cells expressed PD-L1 in 23.0% of cases'.

claims.claim: MSI-high (0.6 to 2.5%) and TMB-high are rare, and the first-line immunotherapy approvals were unselected.
claims.note: Molecular table: MSIsensor-unstable 6 of 244 (2.5%) in cBioPortal gbc_mskcc_2022; 0.6% (2 of 170) in Suryavanshi 2025.

claims.claim: A comprehensive panel at diagnosis captures ERBB2 copy number and mutations, MSI, TMB, BRAF, NTRK and repair genes in one run, and plasma panels found a therapeutically relevant alteration in 55% of advanced biliary patients (Mody 2019).
claims.note: Mody 2019: 'therapeutically relevant alterations were observed in 76 patients (55%)'.

claims.claim: Germline testing is warranted because 11% of biliary patients carried a predisposing repair-gene variant (Wardell 2018).
claims.note: Wardell 2018: deleterious germline mutations 'detected in 11% (16/146) of BTC patients'.

claims.claim: T1b, T2 or T3 (incidental or suspected before surgery): Radical (extended) cholecystectomy: resection of the liver bed (wedge or segments IVb and V) with portal lymphadenectomy, bile duct resection only when the cystic duct margin is positive; re-resection 4 to 8 weeks after an incidental diagnosis; port sites not routinely excised.
claims.note: Ethun 2017: 4 to 8 weeks; Aloia 2015 (row guideline): bile duct resection only when needed for R0; Soreide: port-site resection no survival effect.

claims.claim: Unresectable or metastatic disease, first line: Gemcitabine and cisplatin with durvalumab (TOPAZ-1, in which 25 percent of patients had gallbladder cancer;
claims.note: Imfinzi US label (TOPAZ-1): 'primary tumor location was ICCA 56%, ECCA 18% and GBC 25%'.

claims.claim: Polyps and precursors (prevention): Cholecystectomy for polyps of 10 mm or more, or 6 to 9 mm with a risk factor; ultrasound surveillance at 6, 12 and 24 months otherwise; no follow-up for polyps of 5 mm or less without risk factors (ESGAR, EAES, EFISDS and ESGE 2022).
claims.note: Foley 2022 recommendations 2, 4, 5 and 6.

claims.claim: Newly diagnosed advanced disease: HER2 and genomic testing: HER2 testing (immunohistochemistry and in situ hybridisation) and a tumour gene panel at diagnosis of advanced disease: about one in ten gallbladder cancers is HER2-positive on staining and about one in seven carries a HER2 gene change, and zanidatamab is licensed (MHRA, February 2026) and NICE-recommended (TA1153, May 2026) for HER2-positive biliary cancer after chemotherapy; mismatch repair, BRAF V600E and NTRK results open tumour-agnostic options.
claims.note: 'About one in ten ... HER2-positive on staining' is one Italian resected series by the trial rule (Angerilli 2026: 9.4% of 53); other series give 12.8% (Roa 2014, breast scoring, 187 Chilean) and 31.3% (Hiraoka 2020, gastric scoring, 80 Japanese). One in seven gene change matches Mondaca 14% / Giraldo 15%. MHRA approval published 19 Feb 2026 (GOV.UK); NICE TA1153 published 07 May 2026.
claims.fixed: Now 'between about one in ten and one in three gallbladder cancers is HER2-positive on staining, depending on the series and the scoring rule, and about one in seven carries a HER2 gene change'.

claims.claim: HER2-positive (IHC 3+ or amplified), after first-line therapy: Zanidatamab (HERIZON-BTC-01: 41 percent response, 53 percent gallbladder cancer;
claims.note: HERIZON-BTC-01: confirmed ORR 41.3% (cohort 1); Ziihera label: 'Fifty-three percent of patients had gallbladder cancer'. NICE TA1153 published 07 May 2026; MHRA 19 Feb 2026. Note: the UK licence and TA1153 define HER2-positive as IHC 3+ only, narrower than the row's 'IHC 3+ or amplified'.

claims.claim: FDA 2024, EU 2025, MHRA February 2026, NICE TA1153 May 2026) or trastuzumab deruxtecan for IHC 3+ (DESTINY-PanTumor02 biliary cohort 45 percent response;
claims.note: Enhertu label DESTINY-PanTumor02 table: 'Biliary Tract Cancer 22 45.5 (24.4, 67.8)' (IHC 3+). Dates per records.

claims.claim: Other actionable alterations (rare in gallbladder cancer): BRAF V600E: dabrafenib with trametinib (ROAR biliary cohort 51 percent response;
claims.note: ROAR: 'investigator-assessed overall response was achieved by 22 (51%...) of 43 patients'.

claims.claim: Second line, no actionable target: FOLFOX with active symptom control (ABC-06, UK: overall survival 6.2 versus 5.3 months; gallbladder cancer eligible); liposomal irinotecan with fluorouracil is an NCCN option on NIFTY but was negative in NALIRICC and is not commissioned in the UK; trials preferred (SEVILLA ivonescimab versus FOLFOX at UCL;
claims.note: ABC-06: 'median overall survival of 6.2 months ... versus 5.3 months'; SEVILLA registry: UNICANCER phase 2, UK site University College London.

claims.claim: Palliation of obstruction and symptoms: Biliary drainage by ERCP metal stent, percutaneous transhepatic drainage for hilar block or failed ERCP, or EUS-guided drainage (non-inferior to ERCP with fewer complications in a 125-patient randomised trial); duodenal stent or gastrojejunostomy for gastric outlet obstruction by expected survival (SUSTENT); opioids with coeliac plexus block for visceral pain; paracentesis or tunnelled catheter for ascites; early integrated palliative care.
claims.note: Paik 2018: 125 patients randomised, technical success 93.8% vs 90.2% (noninferiority), fewer adverse events (6.3% vs 19.7%).

claims.claim: Ultrasound first for a mass, wall thickening or polyp; endoscopic or contrast-enhanced ultrasound in expert centres for difficult cases (Foley 2022)
claims.note: Foley 2022 recommendation 1 (ultrasound first; contrast-enhanced or endoscopic ultrasound in expert centres for difficult cases).

claims.claim: FDG PET-CT before any radical or re-resection, accurate for the primary and for distant spread, less so for nodes (Parida 2021)
claims.note: Parida 2021: primary 96%, metastatic 95%, nodal 75%.

claims.claim: A needle biopsy is usually avoided when the mass looks resectable; surgeons rely on imaging and intraoperative frozen section, and biopsy when the disease is unresectable and drug treatment is planned (Chan 2022;
claims.note: Chan 2022 (frozen section matched final histology).

claims.claim: T2b: on the hepatic (liver) side, which spreads to nodes and vessels more often and roughly doubles the risk of death (Shindoh 2015;
claims.note: Shindoh 2015: hepatic side HR 2.7, higher vascular, perineural and nodal spread; Alrawashdeh HR 2.18.

claims.claim: Whether T1b tumours need radical re-resection: no randomised trial exists, meta-analyses of retrospective cohorts disagree on disease-specific benefit, and the largest international series found five-year disease-specific survival of 93.7 versus 95.5 percent after simple versus extended cholecystectomy in 237 patients (Kim 2018); bile duct excision and port-site policy rest on the same kind of series.
claims.note: Kim 2018 (JHBPS): 14 centres, 237 qualifying patients, 5-year DSS 'similar between SC and EC patients (93.7% vs. 95.5%'.

claims.claim: How much liver to remove for T2 disease: a 2023 meta-analysis found better one-year disease-free survival but worse three-year overall survival and more complications with anatomical segment IVb and V resection than with a wedge, and two meta-analyses suggest peritoneal-side (T2a) tumours may not need the liver resection at all.
claims.note: Chen 2023: 1-year DFS higher with segment IVb/V resection (RR 1.07), 3-year OS lower (RR 0.90), more complications (RR 1.90).

claims.claim: The highest-incidence populations are the least sequenced: 23 Chilean patients in the largest comparative HER2 series and 56 Chilean tumours in the first landscape paper, against 244 samples from New York.
claims.note: Mondaca 2024: '237 from MSK and 23 from PUC'; Erices 2025: 56 Chilean tumours; Giraldo 2022: 244 samples.

claims.claim: HER2 heterogeneity and loss at progression (Cowzer 2026) mean a positive biopsy does not guarantee benefit and a single diagnostic test may not describe the relapsed tumour.
claims.note: Only figure is the year; Cowzer et al., Clin Cancer Res 2026.

claims.claim: Neoadjuvant chemotherapy for incidental gallbladder cancer is untested: GAIN closed after 68 of 333 planned patients and OPT-IN will not report before 2028.
claims.note: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT03673072 (GAIN): completed 2024-10-10, actual enrolment 68; protocol paper: 'A total of N = 333 patients'. NCT04559139 (OPT-IN): primary completion 2028-07-01 (estimated).

claims.claim: HER2 positivity in gallbladder cancer ranges from 9 percent (Italian resected series scored by the HERIZON-BTC-01 rule, Angerilli 2026) through 13 percent (Chile, breast scoring, Roa 2014) to 31 percent (Japan, gastric scoring, Hiraoka 2020) depending on cohort and scoring rule, so the size of the zanidatamab-eligible population in the UK is uncertain.
claims.note: Angerilli 2026: GBC HER2 positivity 9.4% by HERIZON-BTC-01 criteria; Roa 2014: 12.8% by CAP/ASCO breast criteria (187 Chilean); Hiraoka 2020: '31.3% of GBC' by gastro-oesophageal guidelines.

claims.claim: Second-line evidence is thin: FOLFOX adds a month, liposomal irinotecan has one positive and one negative trial, and the UK's randomised second-line option is a single phase 2 (SEVILLA) at one site.
claims.note: ABC-06 median OS 6.2 vs 5.3 months (about one month); SEVILLA is a phase 2 with one UK site (University College London) on the registry.

claims.claim: Prevention in high-incidence regions: Chile's prophylactic cholecystectomy programme has run since 2006 without an evaluable design; typhoid carriers have never been offered a trial.
claims.note: Samaniego Sanhueza et al., Rev Med Chile 2024 (a paper on the record's history): 'In 2006, the Chilean Ministry of Health included cholelithiasis (patients aged 35-49) and treatment with cholecystectomy within the Explicit Health Guarantees (GES) program.'

claims.claim: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma is the most common aggressive lymphoma, about 30% of all non-Hodgkin lymphoma, with a median age around 65.
claims.note: No record source gives '30% of NHL' (Lymphoma Action: 'most common type of non-Hodgkin lymphoma'; HMRN, not on this record, puts DLBCL at 2,373 of 4,961 NHL). Median age: Wikipedia 'median age of diagnosis at ~70 years'; Lymphoma Action 'Most people diagnosed with DLBCL are 65 or over'.
claims.fixed: Removed '30% of NHL' and 'median age around 65'; now 'most people diagnosed are 65 or over' (Lymphoma Action).

claims.claim: It is curable: R-CHOP (rituximab plus cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin, vincristine, prednisone) cures roughly 60% of patients, more with low IPI and fewer with high-risk features (IPI 3-5, double-hit MYC/BCL2 rearrangement, activated B-cell origin, TP53 loss).
claims.note: POLARIX NEJM: 'only 60% of patients are cured with R-CHOP'; Wikipedia: 'more than half of all patients with DLBCL can be cured'.

claims.claim: Frontline therapy stood still for twenty years until POLARIX (2022) showed that replacing vincristine with the CD79b ADC polatuzumab vedotin improves progression-free survival (5-year 64.9% vs 59.1%), and frontMIND (Lancet 2026) showed tafasitamab plus lenalidomide added to R-CHOP improves PFS in IPI 3-5 disease (HR 0.75); epcoritamab plus R-CHOP (EPCORE DLBCL-2) and golcadomide plus R-CHOP (GOLSEEK-1) follow.
claims.note: POLARIX 5-year: 'PFS rates of 64.9% ... and 59.1%'; frontMIND Lancet 2026: 'HR 0.75 [0.59-0.96]'.

claims.claim: For the 30-40% who relapse, the sequence has been rebuilt around T-cell redirection: CD19 CAR-T (axi-cel, liso-cel) beats salvage chemotherapy and transplant for relapse within a year (ZUMA-7 with an overall survival benefit;
claims.note: POLARIX: 'only 60% of patients are cured with R-CHOP'; frontMIND: 'Approximately 40% of patients with high-risk DLBCL are not cured'.

claims.claim: Off-the-shelf CD20×CD3 bispecifics (glofitamab, epcoritamab, mosunetuzumab, odronextamab) give complete remissions in about 40% of heavily pretreated patients, and chemotherapy-free doublets such as mosunetuzumab-polatuzumab (SUNMO) beat salvage chemotherapy.
claims.note: Epcoritamab dose expansion (JCO 2023, linked on the record's bispecific step-up term): 'complete response rate was 38.9%' after a median of three prior lines.

claims.claim: EPCORE DLBCL-1 (2026) improved PFS but not overall survival against chemotherapy;
claims.note: Genmab topline release (read via Wayback copy; live page refuses scripts): PFS 'HR: 0.74'; 'OS of HR: 0.96 ... did not reach statistical significance'.

claims.claim: ~150,000 new cases a year worldwide; ~25,000 in the US; median age 65; about 60% cured with first-line therapy.
claims.note: No record source states ~150,000 worldwide or ~25,000 US; Wikipedia: 'annual incidence of 7-8 cases per 100,000 people per year in the US and UK', median ~70; Lymphoma Action: 'Just under 5,500 people are diagnosed with DLBCL each year in the UK', 'Most ... are 65 or over'.
claims.fixed: Burden rewritten to the cited figures: incidence 7-8 per 100,000 (US and UK), just under 5,500 UK diagnoses a year, most 65 or over; 60% cure kept.

claims.claim: CD19 CAR-T is second-line standard for early relapse, with an overall survival benefit in ZUMA-7 (4-year OS 54.6% vs 46.0%).
claims.note: ZUMA-7 OS paper: 'estimated 4-year overall survival was 54.6% and 46.0%'.

claims.claim: Four CD20×CD3 bispecifics approved or conditionally approved worldwide give ~40% complete remissions off the shelf; chemotherapy-free doublets (mosun-pola) beat salvage chemotherapy.
claims.note: Epcoritamab CR 38.9% after >=2 lines (JCO 2023); approvals: COLUMVI 15 Jun 2023, EPKINLY 19 May 2023 (Drugs@FDA).

claims.claim: A MYC rearrangement with BCL2, with or without BCL6, is a separate WHO entity and usually moves a patient off R-CHOP; rates in 442 unselected cases were 8.8% for MYC, 13.5% for BCL2 and 28.7% for BCL6.
claims.note: Figures correct per Horn et al. Blood 2013: 'Rearrangements of MYC, BCL2, and BCL6 were detected in 8.8%, 13.5%, and 28.7%' of 442, but that paper was not on the dlbcl record.
claims.fixed: Added Horn 2013 (and Johnson 2012) as links on the dlbcl patch in lymphoma-molecular.ts; text unchanged.

claims.claim: Co-expression of MYC and BCL2 protein without rearrangement, about 21% of cases, is prognostic and is not the same thing.
claims.note: Johnson et al. JCO 2012: 'Concurrent expression (MYC positive/BCL2 positive) was present in 21% of patients' (training cohort); not previously on the dlbcl record.
claims.fixed: Added Johnson 2012 as a link on the dlbcl patch; text unchanged.

claims.claim: CD20 on essentially every case, CD19 on the same cells and retained when CD20 is lost, CD79b on more than 95% and chosen because it internalises and can carry a payload, and CD3 as the handle for the bispecific antibodies.
claims.note: 'CD79b on more than 95%' has no source on the record; the antigen card cites Davis 2010 (BCR signalling), which does not give it. POLARIX says CD79b is 'ubiquitously expressed on the surface of malignant B cells'.
claims.fixed: 'more than 95%' replaced by 'almost every case'.

claims.claim: Limited stage (I-II, non-bulky): R-CHOP × 4 with PET-guided omission of radiation (FLYER, S1001): 4 cycles if interim PET negative; involved-site radiotherapy if PET positive.
claims.note: FLYER (four cycles) and S1001 PET-adapted approach; no other figure.

claims.claim: Advanced stage, IPI 0-1: R-CHOP × 6 (or Pola-R-CHP); consider 4 cycles plus 2 rituximab in young low-risk patients (FLYER).
claims.note: FLYER: 'four cycles of R-CHOP plus two doses of rituximab' non-inferior in young favourable patients.

claims.claim: Advanced stage, IPI 2-5: Pola-R-CHP × 6 (POLARIX) or R-CHOP × 6; tafasitamab + lenalidomide + R-CHOP (frontMIND) pending approval for IPI 3-5;
claims.note: POLARIX six cycles in IPI 2-5; frontMIND enrolled high-intermediate/high-risk (IPI 3-5) and is not yet approved.

claims.claim: Primary refractory or relapse within 12 months: CD19 CAR-T (axi-cel or liso-cel) preferred over salvage chemotherapy and transplant (ZUMA-7, TRANSFORM); bridging therapy while manufacturing; bispecific ± chemotherapy if CAR-T unavailable.
claims.note: ZUMA-7 and TRANSFORM: refractory or relapsed within 12 months.

claims.claim: Late relapse (>12 months), transplant-eligible: Salvage chemotherapy (R-ICE, R-DHAP, R-GemOx) → high-dose therapy and autologous transplant if chemosensitive;
claims.note: Twelve-month split as in ZUMA-7/TRANSFORM eligibility; no other figure.

claims.claim: The IPI (age over 60, stage III or IV, more than one extranodal site, performance status 2 or worse, raised LDH) sets the risk group, and the CNS-IPI adds kidney or adrenal involvement to estimate the risk of relapse in the brain.
claims.note: IPI (NEJM 1993): age, stage, LDH, performance status, extranodal sites; CNS-IPI (JCO 2016, on the CNS prophylaxis term): 'IPI factors in addition to involvement of kidneys and/or adrenal glands'.

claims.claim: Limited stage (I to II), non-bulky, low risk: four cycles, and often no radiotherapy: Four cycles of R-CHOP with two extra doses of rituximab, rather than six cycles, for patients aged 18 to 60 with stage I or II disease, normal LDH, performance status 0 to 1 and no mass of 7.5 cm or more.
claims.note: FLYER: 'aged 18-60 years, with stage I-II disease, normal serum lactate dehydrogenase concentration, ECOG performance status 0-1, and without bulky disease (maximal tumour diameter <7.5 cm)'.

claims.claim: FLYER randomised 588 such patients and found three-year progression-free survival of 96 per cent with the four-cycle arm, non-inferior to six cycles, and with fewer adverse events recorded in the four-cycle group (294 haematological and 1,036 non-haematological events against 426 and 1,280).
claims.note: FLYER: '592 patients were enrolled ... 295 ... and 297 were assigned'; 'Four patients ... withdrew ... so 588 patients were included in the intention-to-treat analysis'. 96%, AE counts 294/1036 vs 426/1280 correct.
claims.fixed: 'randomised 588' -> 'randomised 592 such patients (588 analysed)'.

claims.claim: Radiotherapy is not given routinely; an involved-site 30 to 40 Gy field is added where the end-of-treatment PET is positive, or for a bulky or skeletal site.
claims.note: FLYER: 'No radiotherapy was planned except for testicular lymphoma'; no source on the row or record gives the 30-40 Gy dose.
claims.fixed: Removed '30 to 40 Gy'.

claims.claim: Advanced stage, IPI 0 to 1: R-CHOP for six cycles: Six cycles of R-CHOP every 21 days.
claims.note: FLYER/CALGB 50303: R-CHOP cycles 'repeated every 21 days'.

claims.claim: This has been the reference regimen since rituximab was added to CHOP in 2002, and every attempt to improve on it in this risk group has failed: DA-EPOCH-R was no better and more toxic in Alliance/CALGB 50303 (491 patients, progression-free survival hazard ratio 0.93, febrile neutropenia 35.0 against 17.7 per cent), and obinutuzumab in place of rituximab was no better in GOYA (1,418 patients, hazard ratio 0.92).
claims.note: CALGB 50303: '491 eligible', 'hazard ratio, 0.93', 'febrile neutropenia (35.0% v 17.7%)'; GOYA (on the failed-and-negative term): 'N = 1,418', 'stratified hazard ratio was 0.92'.

claims.claim: POLARIX, which established polatuzumab vedotin in place of vincristine, enrolled only patients with IPI 2 to 5, so there is no randomised evidence for pola-R-CHP in IPI 0 to 1 disease.
claims.note: POLARIX enrolled 'intermediate-risk or high-risk' (IPI 2-5) only.

claims.claim: Advanced stage, IPI 2 to 5: pola-R-CHP or R-CHOP, and where polatuzumab did and did not win: Six cycles of polatuzumab vedotin with rituximab, cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin and prednisone (pola-R-CHP), or six cycles of R-CHOP.
claims.note: POLARIX: 'six cycles of either pola-R-CHP or R-CHOP'.
