claims.claim: POLARIX randomised 879 previously untreated patients aged 18 to 80 with IPI 2 to 5: two-year progression-free survival 76.7 against 70.2 per cent (hazard ratio 0.73) and five-year progression-free survival 64.9 against 59.1 per cent (hazard ratio 0.77).
claims.note: POLARIX: '879 patients', '18 to 80', '76.7% ... vs. 70.2% at 2 years; stratified hazard ratio ... 0.73'; 5-year: 'HR 0.77', '64.9% ... and 59.1%'.

claims.claim: Overall survival has not separated: the five-year figures are 82.3 against 79.5 per cent, hazard ratio 0.85, not significant.
claims.note: HR 0.85 (0.63-1.15), not significant, confirmed in the JCO 2025 text; the 5-year OS rates 82.3/79.5 are not in the abstract or body text (Kaplan-Meier figure 2B only, not machine-readable). Left as is.

claims.claim: So polatuzumab prevents some relapses without yet being shown to prevent deaths, and the prespecified subgroup analyses suggested the benefit sat with activated B-cell subtype and with IPI 3 to 5 rather than with germinal centre or IPI 2 disease.
claims.note: POLARIX 5-year: 'favorable 5-year survival rates with Pola-R-CHP in high-risk subgroups, including activated B-cell DLBCL and International Prognostic Index score 3-5'; 'patients with IPI score 2, may be too small'.

claims.claim: The newer option is tafasitamab and lenalidomide added to R-CHOP for IPI 3 to 5. frontMIND randomised 899 such patients and reported two-year progression-free survival 71.1 against 62.9 per cent (hazard ratio 0.75).
claims.note: frontMIND: '899 were randomly allocated', '2-year progression-free survival rates of 71.1% ... versus 62.9%', 'HR 0.75'.

claims.claim: High-grade B-cell lymphoma with MYC and BCL2 rearrangements (double-hit), and MYC with BCL6: Dose-adjusted EPOCH-R rather than R-CHOP, with central nervous system-directed treatment, on the basis of consistent retrospective series rather than a randomised trial; there has never been one, because the entity is uncommon and was only separated out in 2016.
claims.note: WHO 2016 revision (Swerdlow, Blood 2016): 'High-grade B-cell lymphoma, with MYC and BCL2 and/or BCL6 translocations: New category'; true, but no source on the record carried it.
claims.fixed: Added Swerdlow 2016 as a link on the dlbcl treatment patch; text unchanged.

claims.claim: Older or frail patients: R-mini-CHOP and the comprehensive geriatric assessment: Attenuated R-CHOP (R-mini-CHOP), typically at 50 per cent of the cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin and vincristine doses, is standard for patients over about 80 and for frail patients of any age, and is given with the intention to cure rather than to palliate.
claims.note: No source on the row or record (NCI PDQ page has no R-mini-CHOP content) supports '50 per cent of the doses' or 'over about 80'.
claims.fixed: Removed the 50 per cent and 'over about 80' figures; now 'with reduced doses ... standard for the oldest patients'.

claims.claim: A pre-phase of prednisolone with or without one dose of vincristine for a week before cycle 1 improves performance status and reduces early deaths.
claims.note: No source on the row or record describes the pre-phase schedule (one dose of vincristine, a week).
claims.fixed: Removed 'one dose' and 'for a week'.

claims.claim: Central nervous system prophylaxis: who is offered it, and the evidence against it: Relapse in the brain or spinal fluid occurs in roughly 2 to 5 per cent of patients overall and in about 10 per cent of those with a high CNS-IPI.
claims.note: CNS-IPI (JCO 2016): 2-year CNS rates '0.6%', '3.4%' and '10.2%' (high risk); weighted overall about 3%.

claims.claim: In 1,162 adults across 21 United States academic centres who all received single-route prophylaxis, central nervous system relapse occurred in 5.7 per cent, with no difference between intrathecal (5.4 per cent) and systemic high-dose methotrexate (6.8 per cent), and the observed rate matched the rate predicted from CNS-IPI alone.
claims.note: Blood 2022: '1162 adult patients across 21 US academic centers', 'Sixty-four patients (5.7%) had CNS relapse', 'IT and HD-MTX recipients (5.4% vs 6.8%', expected vs observed '5.8% vs 5.7%'.

claims.claim: ZUMA-7 randomised 359 patients with large B-cell lymphoma refractory to, or relapsing within twelve months of, first-line therapy to axicabtagene ciloleucel or to salvage chemotherapy with autologous transplant in responders: median event-free survival 8.3 against 2.0 months (hazard ratio 0.40) and four-year overall survival 54.6 against 46.0 per cent (hazard ratio 0.73).
claims.note: ZUMA-7: 180+179 randomised, 'median event-free survival was 8.3 months ... and 2.0 months', 'hazard ratio ... 0.40'; OS paper 54.6% vs 46.0%, HR 0.73.

claims.claim: TRANSFORM randomised 184 transplant-eligible patients to lisocabtagene maraleucel or the same standard of care: complete response 74 against 43 per cent, progression-free survival hazard ratio 0.400, with grade 3 cytokine release syndrome in 1 per cent and grade 3 neurological events in 4 per cent.
claims.note: TRANSFORM Blood 2023: 'N = 184', 'CR rate was 74% for liso-cel vs 43%', 'HR = 0.400', 'Grade 3 cytokine release syndrome and neurological events occurred in 1% and 4%'.

claims.claim: BELINDA, with tisagenlecleucel and a longer manufacturing interval, was negative (event-free survival hazard ratio 1.07), which is why product and pathway speed are treated as part of the treatment rather than a detail of it.
claims.note: BELINDA NEJM: 'hazard ratio for event or death ... 1.07'; 52-day manufacturing interval.

claims.claim: With gemcitabine and oxaliplatin, STARGLO reported median overall survival 25.5 against 12.9 months for rituximab-GemOx (hazard ratio 0.62).
claims.note: STARGLO Lancet 2024: 'median 25.5 months [18.3-NE] vs 12.9 months ... HR 0.62'. Note: the starglo trial entity links PIIS0140-6736(24)02565-4, which does not resolve on Crossref; the paper's DOI is 10.1016/S0140-6736(24)01774-4.

claims.claim: This is one of the places where England is ahead of the United States: NICE TA1113 allows glofitamab with gemcitabine and oxaliplatin for relapsed or refractory diffuse large B-cell lymphoma not otherwise specified after one line of treatment in adults who are not eligible for an autologous transplant, while glofitamab's only American indication remains the accelerated approval of 15 June 2023 for disease after two or more lines.
claims.note: NICE TA1113 1.1: glofitamab-GemOx for DLBCL NOS when 'they have had 1 line of treatment only, and they are not eligible for an autologous stem cell transplant'; Drugs@FDA COLUMVI original approval 2023-06-15.

claims.claim: EPCORE DLBCL-1 randomised 552 transplant-ineligible patients against investigator's choice of R-GemOx or bendamustine-rituximab and improved progression-free survival (hazard ratio 0.74) without improving overall survival (hazard ratio 0.96).
claims.note: Genmab topline release: 'The global study enrolled 483 patients'; ClinicalTrials.gov NCT04628494 actual enrolment 483. HR 0.74 (PFS) and 0.96 (OS) correct. 552 is not in any source read (the trial entity carries enrolled: 552).
claims.fixed: 'randomised 552' -> 'enrolled 483'.

claims.claim: Mosunetuzumab with polatuzumab vedotin in SUNMO gave progression-free survival 11.5 against 3.8 months for R-GemOx (hazard ratio 0.41), overall response 70 against 40 per cent and complete response 51 against 24 per cent.
claims.note: SUNMO JCO 2025: 'median PFS ... 11.5 months ... v 3.8 months; hazard ratio ... 0.41', 'ORR ... (70% v 40%', 'complete response rates of 51% and 24%'.

claims.claim: Polatuzumab with rituximab, gemcitabine and oxaliplatin in POLARGO improved overall survival, 19.5 against 12.5 months (hazard ratio 0.6), in 255 transplant-ineligible patients.
claims.note: POLARGO JCO 2026 (row link): '255 patients', 'hazard ratio, 0.6', 'median OS of 19.5 months ... versus 12.5 months'.

claims.claim: Loncastuximab tesirine alone (LOTIS-2: response 48 per cent, complete response 24 per cent).
claims.note: LOTIS-2: 'overall response rate 48.3%'; 35 of 145 complete (24%).

claims.claim: Tafasitamab with lenalidomide (L-MIND: response 60 per cent, complete response 43 per cent), which suits someone who wants an outpatient oral-and-infusion regimen.
claims.note: L-MIND: '48 (60%) ... had an objective response: 34 (43%) ... complete response'.

claims.claim: Brentuximab vedotin with lenalidomide and a rituximab product, approved in the United States on 11 February 2025 on the ECHELON-3 trial, for people after two or more lines who are not eligible for an autologous transplant or for CAR-T.
claims.note: Drugs@FDA ADCETRIS BLA125388 efficacy supplement approved 2025-02-11.

claims.claim: Third line and beyond, including relapse after CAR-T: If CAR-T has not been given and the patient is fit, it is given now: ZUMA-1 reported an objective response of 82 per cent and complete response 54 per cent in refractory large B-cell lymphoma, with 42 per cent still in response at a median 15.4 months.
claims.note: ZUMA-1: 'objective response rate was 82%, and the complete response rate was 54%. With a median follow-up of 15.4 months, 42% ... continued to have a response'.

claims.claim: End-of-treatment PET-CT, reported on the five-point Deauville scale, decides whether treatment is complete: scores 1 to 3 are a complete metabolic response, 4 to 5 need biopsy of the residual site before any further treatment, because inflammation and brown fat both light up.
claims.note: Lugano classification: PET-CT response on the 5-point scale; Deauville 1-3 complete metabolic response.

claims.claim: Primary refractory disease (~10-15%) still has poor outcomes even with CAR-T;
claims.note: No source on the record gives a 10-15% primary refractory rate.

claims.claim: Polatuzumab vedotin prevents relapses in first-line diffuse large B-cell lymphoma without a proven survival gain: POLARIX gave five-year progression-free survival of 64.9 against 59.1 per cent but overall survival of 82.3 against 79.5 per cent, hazard ratio 0.85, not significant.
claims.note: 64.9 vs 59.1 and HR 0.85 NS confirmed (JCO 2025); the OS rates 82.3/79.5 appear only in figure 2B. Left as is.

claims.claim: Older and frail patients are systematically under-represented: POLARIX capped enrolment at 80 and required performance status 0 to 2, so the evidence for the commonest presentation of this lymphoma, a person in their late seventies or eighties, rests on single-arm and retrospective work.
claims.note: POLARIX: 'Patients 18 to 80 years of age'; baseline ECOG 0-1 and 2 only.

claims.claim: It is the name given to every cancer of the lymphatic system that is not Hodgkin lymphoma, and it covers scores of separate diseases whose only shared feature is the cell they come from: the tables of the 2022 WHO classification list more than sixty mature B-cell, T-cell and NK-cell entities: a lymphocyte, one of the white blood cells that run the immune system.
claims.note: Lymphoma Action (record link): 'There are over 60 different types of lymphoma'; WHO 2022 classification on the record.

claims.claim: In the United Kingdom the B-cell side is about 95 per cent of lymphoma diagnoses and the T-cell and NK-cell side about 5 per cent (Haematological Malignancy Research Network, 5,796 lymphomas in a population of nearly four million).
claims.note: HMRN BJC 2015: 'Mature B-cell malignancies, which comprise around 94.7% (N=5488) of the total ... T-cell subtypes (N=308)'; population 'nearly 4 million'.

claims.claim: Lymphoma is mostly a disease of later life: the median age at diagnosis in the HMRN population was 67.2 years for all lymphomas together and 69.1 years for the non-Hodgkin group, with men diagnosed younger than women and at higher rates at almost every age.
claims.note: HMRN Table 1: all lymphomas median age 67.2; non-Hodgkin 69.1; males younger; 'males tended to be diagnosed at younger ages and have significantly ... higher incidence rates'.

claims.claim: But the family spans every age, and different subtypes dominate different ages: Burkitt lymphoma and Hodgkin lymphoma are the common lymphomas of childhood and early adult life, while above 60 the diffuse large B-cell, marginal zone and follicular subtypes account for more than 80 per cent of diagnoses.
claims.note: HMRN: 'in those aged 60 years or more, diffuse large B-cell, marginal-zone and follicular lymphomas accounted for over 80% of diagnoses'; Hodgkin and Burkitt dominate under 15.

claims.claim: Cancer Research UK estimates that about 3 per cent of UK cases are preventable, which is the honest counterpart to the fact that most people did nothing to cause this.
claims.note: CRUK: '3% of non-Hodgkin lymphoma cases are preventable, UK, 2015'.

claims.claim: Lugano kept the descriptive language of the Ann Arbor system that preceded it, agreed at a meeting in Ann Arbor, Michigan in 1971 for Hodgkin's disease, which is why a report in 2026 may still say Ann Arbor stage IIA and mean the same thing.
claims.note: Committee on Hodgkin's Disease Staging Classification, Cancer Research 1971 (PMID 5121694).

claims.claim: The International Prognostic Index, built in 1993 from 2,031 patients with aggressive lymphoma treated across 16 institutions, counts five: age over 60, stage III or IV, a raised lactate dehydrogenase, a performance status of 2 or worse, and more than one site outside the lymph nodes.
claims.note: IPI NEJM 1993: '16 institutions and cooperative groups', 'In 2031 patients of all ages', five factors.

claims.claim: Follicular lymphoma has its own version (FLIPI), mantle cell lymphoma has MIPI, and the nodal T-cell lymphomas have the Prognostic Index for T-cell lymphoma, built from 385 patients in 2004.
claims.note: PIT Blood 2004: 'we retrospectively analyzed 385 cases'.

claims.claim: Rituximab, approved in 1997, was the first antibody ever licensed for a cancer, and adding it to chemotherapy raised both the proportion of people whose diffuse large B-cell lymphoma went away and the proportion still alive years later; the trial and its figures are on that page.
claims.note: Drugs@FDA RITUXAN BLA103705 original approval 1997-11-26.

claims.claim: CAR-T cell therapy, in which a patient's own T cells are collected, engineered to recognise CD19 and given back, was approved for relapsed large B-cell lymphoma in 2017 and now cures a proportion of people whose disease had come back after chemotherapy.
claims.note: ZUMA-1 (on the record) led to the 2017 approval of axicabtagene ciloleucel for relapsed large B-cell lymphoma.

claims.claim: Bispecific antibodies, which grip a lymphoma cell with one arm and a T cell with the other, arrived in 2023 and do a related job without the manufacturing wait.
claims.note: Drugs@FDA: COLUMVI (glofitamab) 2023-06-15, EPKINLY (epcoritamab) 2023-05-19 for large B-cell lymphoma.

claims.claim: About 13,747 new cases and 5,100 deaths a year in the United Kingdom, where 64.6 per cent of people are alive ten years later (Cancer Research UK); an estimated 79,320 new cases and 19,970 deaths in the United States in 2026, 3.8 per cent of all new cancer diagnoses, with five-year relative survival of 74.3 per cent for 2016 to 2022 (SEER); and about 544,000 cases and 260,000 deaths worldwide in 2020 (GLOBOCAN).
claims.note: CRUK: '13,747 new ... cases', '5,100 ... deaths', '64.6% survive ... 10 or more years'; SEER: 'Estimated New Cases in 2026 79,320', '% of All New Cancer Cases 3.8%', 'Estimated Deaths in 2026 19,970', '74.3% 2016-2022'; GLOBOCAN 2020 fact sheet: 544 352 cases, 259 793 deaths (dated 2020; two newer editions exist, listed for the 2024 round).

claims.claim: With that said: in the United Kingdom, 64.6 per cent of people diagnosed with non-Hodgkin lymphoma are alive ten years later (Cancer Research UK), and in the United States five-year relative survival was 74.3 per cent for 2016 to 2022, up from about 47 per cent in the mid-1970s (SEER).
claims.note: CRUK 64.6% at 10 years; SEER 74.3% for 2016-2022 and 47.98% for 1975.

claims.claim: In the UK population series that reports survival by subtype, five-year relative survival ran from 86.5 per cent in follicular lymphoma and 87.9 per cent in extranodal marginal zone lymphoma, through 54.8 per cent in diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, to 31.4 per cent in mantle cell lymphoma and 45.4 per cent across the T-cell lymphomas as a group; those figures are for people diagnosed between 2004 and 2012 and followed to 2014, so they predate the bispecific antibodies, CAR-T and the newer mantle cell regimens, and they understate what is achieved today in several subtypes.
claims.note: HMRN Table 3 relative survival: FL 86.5, extranodal MZL 87.9, DLBCL 54.8, mantle cell 31.4, T-cell 45.4; 'diagnosed over the period 2004-2012 and followed-up through to March 2014'.

claims.claim: The 9p24.1 amplicon carries both PD-1 ligand genes and JAK2, which induces them further, and 97% of 108 classical Hodgkin lymphomas carried concordant alterations of the two loci.
claims.note: Roemer JCO 2016: 'Ninety-seven percent of all evaluated cHLs had concordant alterations' of 108; correct, but not on the NHL record.
claims.fixed: Added Roemer 2016, Ansell 2015, Hiraga 2009, Woyach 2014 and Blombery 2019 as links on the NHL hub patch; text unchanged.

claims.claim: PD-1 blockade gave an objective response in 20 of 23 heavily pre-treated patients; outside Hodgkin lymphoma and the mediastinal group, single-agent checkpoint blockade in B-cell lymphoma does very little.
claims.note: Ansell NEJM 2015: 'An objective response was reported in 20 patients (87%)' of 23; not on the NHL record.
claims.fixed: Added Ansell 2015 as a link on the NHL hub patch.

claims.claim: Anti-CD20 is defeated by transcriptional loss of CD20, found in 5 of 19 rebiopsied relapses; covalent BTK inhibitors by BTK C481S, answered by a non-covalent inhibitor, and by PLCG2 gain of function, which no BTK inhibitor can reach; venetoclax by BCL2 G101V, which lowers drug affinity about 180-fold and appears months before progression;
claims.note: Hiraga Blood 2009: 'Of those 19, 5 (26.3%) ... CD20 protein-negative'; Blombery Cancer Discov 2019: 'Gly101Val reduces the affinity of BCL2 for venetoclax by ~180-fold'. Neither was on the NHL record.
claims.fixed: Added Hiraga 2009 and Blombery 2019 (and Woyach 2014) as links on the NHL hub patch.

claims.claim: A person whose large B-cell lymphoma relapses in 2026 has a realistic second and third chance of cure, which was not true in 2015.
claims.note: Second-line CAR-T (ZUMA-7 2022) and bispecific approvals (2023) postdate 2015.

claims.claim: The 2022 classifications moved several diseases from being a descriptive label to being a genetically defined entity: high-grade B-cell lymphoma with MYC and BCL2 rearrangements, the large B-cell lymphomas of immune-privileged sites, mediastinal grey zone lymphoma.
claims.note: WHO 2022 and ICC 2022 classifications on the record.

claims.claim: Hepatitis B reactivation: test surface antigen and core antibody before any anti-CD20 antibody and give entecavir or tenofovir prophylaxis, which in a randomised trial cut reactivation from 30 to 6.6 per cent against lamivudine.
claims.note: JAMA 2014 (on the hepatitis B term): 'HBV reactivation (6.6% vs 30%'.

claims.claim: The Lugano classification (2014), which modified the Ann Arbor system of 1971: stage I, one lymph node region; stage II, two or more on the same side of the diaphragm; stage III, both sides; stage IV, diffuse involvement of an organ outside the lymphatic system.
claims.note: Lugano 2014: 'A modification of the Ann Arbor descriptive terminology will be used'; Ann Arbor 1971.

claims.claim: Bulk is recorded separately: a single mass of 10 cm or more, or more than a third of the width of the chest, which changes treatment in several subtypes.
claims.note: NCI PDQ: Lugano bulk in HL 'greater than one-third of the thoracic diameter ... or a mass >10 cm'; DLBCL '10 cm is recommended'.

claims.claim: The same is true of CD20: the only series that looked found 5 of 19 rebiopsied relapses had lost the antigen, which means the denominator for every other patient is unknown and a second anti-CD20 drug is often given without checking the target is still there.
claims.note: Hiraga 2009: 5 of 19 rebiopsied; correct but not on the NHL record.
claims.fixed: Added Hiraga 2009 as a link on the NHL hub patch.

claims.claim: Five-year relative survival in the UK population series was 45.4 per cent across T-cell lymphomas against 68.8 per cent across B-cell lymphomas.
claims.note: HMRN: 'B-cell ... and T-cell lymphomas ... 68.8% ... and 45.4%'.

claims.claim: The gap between Schmitz in 2018 and a randomised trial that assigns treatment by LymphGen subtype is the clearest unfinished business in the disease.
claims.note: Schmitz NEJM 2018 (574 biopsies; MCD, BN2, N1, EZB).

claims.claim: Adult T-cell leukaemia/lymphoma has had exactly one controlled trial, opened in 1998 with 118 patients, and the regimen that makes extranodal NK/T-cell lymphoma treatable rests on a 38-patient single-arm study.
claims.note: JCOG9801 (NCT00145002, phase 3, start 1998-08): 'A total of 118 patients were enrolled'; SMILE: '38 eligible patients'. But 'exactly one controlled trial' is wrong: a randomised phase 2 of mLSG15 with or without mogamulizumab in newly diagnosed aggressive ATL was published (Br J Haematol 2015, doi 10.1111/bjh.13338).
claims.fixed: 'exactly one controlled trial' -> 'one phase 3 trial'.

claims.claim: Classical Hodgkin lymphoma is a B-cell cancer in which rare, giant Reed-Sternberg cells (about 1% of the mass) recruit an inflammatory microenvironment and hide behind amplified PD-L1.
claims.note: No record source gives '1% of the mass'; Roemer 2016: 'small numbers of malignant Reed-Sternberg cells within an extensive ... infiltrate'.
claims.fixed: 'about 1% of the mass' -> 'a small minority of the cells in the node'.

claims.claim: It peaks in young adults and again after 55, is staged with PET-CT and the Lugano system, and is cured in more than 85% of patients overall and in over 90% of early-stage disease.
claims.note: Peaks correct (Wikipedia: 'young adulthood (age 15-35) and ... over 55'). 'Cured in more than 85% overall and over 90% early-stage' turns survival into cure: SEER gives five-year relative survival 89.3%; Lymphoma Action 'Most people are cured'.
claims.fixed: Cure clause now 'most patients are cured: in the US, five-year relative survival is 89%'.

claims.claim: Two ADC- and immunotherapy-based regimens then replaced ABVD for advanced disease: brentuximab vedotin-AVD (ECHELON-1, overall survival benefit) and, from March 2026, nivolumab-AVD (SWOG S1826, PFS HR 0.45 versus BV-AVD, neuropathy halved, children and adults together).
claims.note: S1826 NEJM: HR 0.45; patients 'at least 12 years'; PMC text: neuropathy 29% vs 56%; FDA label (3/2026) nivolumab+AVD for 12 years and older.

claims.claim: In Europe, GHSG HD21's PET-guided BrECADD matches escalated BEACOPP's ~94% PFS with far less toxicity.
claims.note: HD21 Lancet 2024: 4-year PFS '94.3% ... for BrECADD and 90.9% ... for eBEACOPP'; treatment-related morbidity 42% vs 59%. BrECADD did not 'match eBEACOPP's ~94%'; eBEACOPP was 91%.
claims.fixed: Now 'BrECADD gave 94% four-year PFS against 91% for escalated BEACOPP, with less treatment-related morbidity (42% against 59%)'.

claims.claim: About 84,500 new cases and 19,500 deaths a year worldwide (GLOBOCAN 2024); about 8,900 new cases are expected in the US in 2026, with age peaks at 20-30 and over 55.
claims.note: GLOBOCAN 2024 fact sheet: 84 495 cases, 19 515 deaths (correct); SEER 2026 estimate 8,920 (correct). Age peaks: Wikipedia 'young adulthood (age 15-35) and ... over 55', Lymphoma Action '15 and 34, or over 60'; '20-30' is not in any cited source.

claims.claim: More than 85% are cured, so the research agenda is curing with less toxicity.
claims.note: 'More than 85% are cured' rests on survival, not cure (SEER 5-year relative survival 89.3%); Lymphoma Action: 'Most people are cured'.
claims.fixed: 'More than 85% are cured' -> 'Most are cured'.

claims.claim: In the US, five-year relative survival is 89% (SEER, 2016 to 2022).
claims.note: SEER: '5-Year Relative Survival 89.3% 2016-2022'.

claims.claim: Nivolumab-AVD is the new frontline standard for advanced disease (S1826: 2-year PFS 92%, neuropathy halved), approved March 2026 for ages 12 and up.
claims.note: S1826: '2-year progression-free survival was 92%'; neuropathy 29% vs 56%; Opdivo label recent changes 3/2026, ages 12 and older.

claims.claim: Two intensive but de-toxified European options: PET-guided BrECADD (HD21) achieves ~94% 5-year PFS with 40% less morbidity than eBEACOPP.
claims.note: HD21: PFS is 4-year (94.3%), not 5-year; morbidity 42% vs 59% (relative risk 0.72, about 29% lower, not 40%).
claims.fixed: Now '~94% 4-year PFS with less treatment-related morbidity than eBEACOPP (42% against 59%)'.

claims.claim: Radiotherapy is disappearing from advanced-stage care (<1% in S1826) and being minimised in early stage.
claims.note: S1826: 'Overall, 7 patients received radiation therapy' of 994 randomised.

claims.claim: PD-1 blockade is the most effective single agent in any lymphoma relapse (ORR ~70%), and beat brentuximab head to head (KEYNOTE-204).
claims.note: CheckMate 205: 'objective response rate was 69%'; KEYNOTE-204: PFS 13.2 vs 8.3 months, 'hazard ratio 0.65'.

claims.claim: Cure rates above 90% in young patients shift the research agenda to late effects and to older adults.
claims.note: HD21 (adults up to 60): 4-year PFS 94.3%; Wikipedia: survival 97% under age 20.

claims.claim: 97% of 108 cases carried concordant alterations of the two ligand loci, with amplification in 36% and copy gain in 56%.
claims.note: Roemer 2016: 97%, 'copy gain, 56%', 'amplification, 36%'; correct but not on the Hodgkin record.
claims.fixed: Added Roemer 2016, Ansell 2015, Roemer 2018, Steidl 2011 and Steidl 2010 as links on the Hodgkin patch in lymphoma-molecular.ts.

claims.claim: PD-1 blockade gave an objective response in 20 of 23 heavily pre-treated patients.
claims.note: Ansell 2015: 20 of 23 (87%); not on the Hodgkin record.
claims.fixed: Added Ansell 2015 as a link on the Hodgkin patch.

claims.claim: What predicts a complete remission on a checkpoint inhibitor is MHC class II, not class I, on the Reed-Sternberg cells, which points at a CD4 T cell as the effector and makes CIITA rearrangement, present in 15% of cases, an escape route as well as a cause.
claims.note: Roemer 2018: 'HRS cell expression of MHC class II was predictive for complete remission'; Steidl 2011: CIITA breaks in 'classical Hodgkin lymphoma (cHL) (15%)'. Not on the Hodgkin record.
claims.fixed: Added Roemer 2018 and Steidl 2011 as links on the Hodgkin patch.

claims.claim: The infiltrate carries prognosis of its own: more CD68-positive macrophages meant shorter progression-free survival, more relapse after autologous transplant and shorter disease-specific survival in an independent cohort of 166 patients, outperforming the International Prognostic Score.
claims.note: Steidl NEJM 2010: 'independent cohort of 166 patients', CD68+ macrophages and shorter PFS, relapse after transplant and disease-specific survival, outperforming the IPS. Not on the Hodgkin record.
claims.fixed: Added Steidl 2010 as a link on the Hodgkin patch.

claims.claim: Advanced stage: Nivolumab-AVD (2026) or BV-AVD;
claims.note: FDA Opdivo label (recent change 3/2026): nivolumab with AVD for previously untreated stage III-IV cHL.

claims.claim: Early stage, favourable (I-II): ABVD × 2 + involved-site radiotherapy 20 Gy (HD10), or PET-adapted omission of radiotherapy after 3 cycles if PET-negative (RAPID, HD16) accepting ~5% lower PFS;
claims.note: HD16 omitted radiotherapy after two cycles (PET-2), not three, and cost 7.3 percentage points of 5-year PFS (93.4 vs 86.1); three cycles applies to RAPID only. HD10 two cycles + 20 Gy correct.
claims.fixed: Now 'omission ... if PET-negative (after 3 cycles in RAPID, 2 in HD16) accepting lower PFS (7.3 points at five years in HD16)'.

claims.claim: Early stage, unfavourable (I-II bulky or risk factors): ABVD × 4 + ISRT 30 Gy, or escalated BEACOPP × 2 + ABVD × 2 + RT (HD14/HD17 PET-guided); nivolumab- or BV-containing regimens in trials.
claims.note: NCI PDQ Hodgkin: HD17 PET-guided radiotherapy after two cycles; 30-36 Gy to involved regions; four cycles ABVD in H10.

claims.claim: Advanced stage (III-IV), age ≤60: Nivolumab-AVD × 6 (S1826; approved March 2026, no routine radiotherapy) or BV-AVD × 6 with G-CSF (ECHELON-1); in Europe PET-guided BrECADD × 4-6 (HD21) or eBEACOPP;
claims.note: FDA approval 3/2026 (label); ECHELON-1 six cycles with G-CSF prophylaxis recommended; HD21 four or six cycles.

claims.claim: Advanced stage, age >60: Nivolumab-AVD (S1826 included older adults with less toxicity than BV-AVD); sequential brentuximab → AVD → brentuximab; avoid bleomycin;
claims.note: S1826 older-patient analysis (JCO 2025): 99 eligible patients 60 and older; less toxicity with N-AVD than BV-AVD.

claims.claim: Survivorship: Lifelong surveillance for cardiac disease (anthracycline, mediastinal RT), breast cancer screening from 8 years after chest RT in women, thyroid and lung checks, fertility counselling before therapy.
claims.note: 'From 8 years after chest RT' is not in the cited gov.uk protocol or the Lymphoma Action late-effects page (which say women treated with breast radiotherapy before 36 are invited earlier and more often).
claims.fixed: 'from 8 years after chest RT' -> 'early breast cancer screening in women who had chest RT'.

claims.claim: EORTC counts a large mediastinal mass, age 50 or over, a raised sedimentation rate and four or more nodal areas.
claims.note: NCI PDQ Hodgkin lists the GHSG-type factors (large mediastinal mass, extranodal disease, raised ESR, three or more nodal areas); no record source states the EORTC criteria (age 50, four or more areas).
claims.fixed: EORTC clause softened to 'a similar list that also counts age and sets the threshold for nodal areas differently'.

claims.claim: And the interim PET after two cycles, scored 1 to 5 on the Deauville scale, which is used to intensify treatment in patients who have not responded and to reduce it in those who have.
claims.note: RATHL/H10/HD16: PET after two cycles on the 5-point Deauville scale.

claims.claim: RATHL showed that bleomycin can be dropped from cycles 3 to 6 in patients whose PET after two cycles is negative, with three-year progression-free survival of 85.7 per cent for continued ABVD against 84.4 per cent for AVD, which removed lung toxicity from most patients' treatment.
claims.note: RATHL: 3-year PFS '85.7%' ABVD vs '84.4%' AVD.

claims.claim: EORTC H10 showed the reverse direction: in patients whose early PET was positive, switching from ABVD to escalated BEACOPP with involved-node radiotherapy raised five-year progression-free survival from 77.4 to 90.6 per cent (hazard ratio 0.42).
claims.note: EORTC H10: 'In ePET-positive patients, 5-year PFS improved from 77.4% ... to 90.6% ... (hazard ratio [HR], 0.42'.

claims.claim: The long-term German Hodgkin Study Group series of 471 patients with the nodular lymphocyte-predominant subtype makes the arithmetic plain: ten-year overall survival was 92.1 per cent, second cancers occurred in 10.2 per cent, and of 43 deaths only 10 were from the lymphoma, against 20 from second cancers and 13 from conditions possibly related to treatment.
claims.note: Eichenauer JCO 2020: 471 patients; 10-year OS 92.1%; second malignancy 48 (10.2%); 43 deaths, 10 NLPHL, 20 second malignancies, 13 non-malignant treatment-related.

claims.claim: Follow-up therefore includes cardiovascular risk assessment, thyroid function after neck or upper mediastinal radiotherapy, echocardiography at intervals, active smoking cessation support, and, in England, automatic referral into the NHS breast screening programme's very high risk pathway for women who had radiotherapy to breast tissue for Hodgkin or non-Hodgkin lymphoma between the ages of 10 and under 36.
claims.note: gov.uk protocol: 'those receiving radiotherapy to breast tissue during treatment for Hodgkin and non-Hodgkin lymphoma between the ages of 10 and under 36 years'.

claims.claim: Older patients (>60) have roughly half the cure rate and double the toxicity; the best regimen for them is unsettled.
claims.note: No record source gives 'half the cure rate and double the toxicity' for patients over 60 (PDQ: older patients 'may have more treatment-related morbidity and mortality').
claims.fixed: Now 'lower cure rates and more treatment-related toxicity'.

claims.claim: The ~10-15% with primary refractory or early-relapsing disease still need transplant; those failing PD-1 blockade have few options beyond allogeneic transplant.
claims.note: No record source gives a 10-15% primary refractory/early relapse rate.
claims.fixed: '~10-15%' -> 'The minority'.

claims.claim: The consequences of PD-1 blockade given to a 20-year-old who will live another sixty years are unknown, and the trials that made it a first-line standard have a few years of follow-up in a disease whose main late harms appear after twenty.
claims.note: Illustrative ages; S1826 median follow-up 2.1 years; late harms rising after decades (Schaapveld NEJM 2015, 40-year follow-up).

claims.claim: Every attempt to omit radiotherapy from early-stage Hodgkin lymphoma on the strength of a negative interim scan has cost tumour control: 7.3 percentage points in HD16 and a failure to demonstrate non-inferiority in either risk group of EORTC H10.
claims.note: HD16: 'difference 7.3%'; H10: 'For both F and U groups, noninferiority of ABVD only ... could not be demonstrated'.

claims.claim: The late-effect figures that justify de-escalation come from patients treated up to 2000 with mantle fields.
claims.note: Schaapveld NEJM 2015: 'Patients had received treatment between 1965 and 2000'; mantle-field irradiation.

claims.claim: Follicular lymphoma (FL) is an indolent germinal-centre B-cell lymphoma defined by t(14;18) BCL2 overexpression in ~85% and frequent CREBBP, KMT2D and EZH2 mutations.
claims.note: No source on the FL record gives '~85%' for t(14;18) (Lymphoma Research Foundation, Lymphoma Action and NCI pages checked).
claims.fixed: 'in ~85%' -> 'in most cases'. The record's tldr repeats 'about 85%' and was not in scope.

claims.claim: Median survival now exceeds 15-20 years, so the questions are when to treat, how to avoid over-treatment, and how to manage the ~20% who progress within 24 months (POD24) and the 2-3% per year who transform to DLBCL.
claims.note: 'Median survival now exceeds 15-20 years' unsourced (NCI PDQ, not on this record, says 8 to 15 years); Lymphoma Action: 'Most people live with follicular lymphoma for many years'. POD24 ~20% (Casulo, on the POD24 term) and transformation '2 to 3 people in every 100 ... each year' (Lymphoma Action) correct.
claims.fixed: 'Median survival now exceeds 15-20 years' -> 'Most people now live with it for many years'.

claims.claim: Relapsed disease has the richest menu in lymphoma: lenalidomide-rituximab (AUGMENT), CD20×CD3 bispecifics (mosunetuzumab 2022, epcoritamab 2024, odronextamab EU), CD19 CAR-T (axicabtagene 2021, tisagenlecleucel 2022, lisocabtagene 2024), zanubrutinib-obinutuzumab (ROSEWOOD, 2024) and radioimmunotherapy historically.
claims.note: Drugs@FDA: LUNSUMIO 2022-12-22, EPKINLY FL supplement 2024-06-26, BRUKINSA FL supplement 2024-03-07; FDA Breyanzi approval letter 15 May 2024; axi-cel 2021 and tisa-cel 2022 FL approvals not separately re-read.

claims.claim: Follicular lymphoma is the second most common non-Hodgkin lymphoma in the West (~20% of NHL; about 3-4 per 100,000 per year), median age ~65.
claims.note: ~20% consistent with LRF ('20 to 30 percent of all NHL'); '3-4 per 100,000' and 'median age ~65' had no source on the record. HMRN: FL crude incidence 3.23 per 100,000, median age 64.9.
claims.fixed: Added HMRN (BJC 2015) to the FL record links; burden now 'about 3.2 per 100,000 a year and the median age at diagnosis 65' in a UK population series.

claims.claim: CAR-T gives durable remissions in heavily pretreated FL (ZUMA-5 ~50% progression-free at 4 years) and is being tested against bispecifics.
claims.note: No source on the record gives ~50% progression-free at 4 years for ZUMA-5 (the linked Lancet Oncology paper has 17.5 months' follow-up: ORR 92%, CR 74% across FL and MZL).
claims.fixed: Replaced with the linked paper's figures: 'overall response 92% and complete response 74% across follicular and marginal zone lymphoma'.

claims.claim: KMT2D was mutated in 89% of follicular lymphomas in the discovery series, CREBBP or EP300 in about 41%, and EZH2 at Tyr646 in 7.2%.
claims.note: Morin Nature 2011: '89% of FL cases had somatic mutations in MLL2' (KMT2D); Pasqualucci Nature 2011: 'about 39% of DLBCL and 41% of follicular lymphoma'; Morin Nat Genet 2010: EZH2 Tyr641 in '7.2% of FLs'. Correct, but none was on the FL record.
claims.fixed: Added Tsujimoto 1985, Morin 2011, Pasqualucci 2011 and Morin 2010 as links on the FL patch in lymphoma-molecular.ts.

claims.claim: Limited stage (I-II): Involved-site radiotherapy 24 Gy (FoRT); rituximab alone or observation in selected cases.
claims.note: FoRT: '24 Gy in 12 fractions is the more effective radiation schedule ... standard of care'.

claims.claim: Advanced, high burden (GELF criteria): Bendamustine-rituximab or bendamustine-obinutuzumab (GALLIUM), R-CHOP, or lenalidomide-rituximab (RELEVANCE); anti-CD20 maintenance 2 years (PRIMA).
claims.note: PRIMA: '2 years of rituximab maintenance'; GALLIUM and RELEVANCE entities.

claims.claim: Relapsed (≥2 lines): Lenalidomide-rituximab (AUGMENT);
claims.note: AUGMENT (relapsed after at least one prior therapy); '>=2 lines' reads as second line onward. No other figure.

claims.claim: Stage I and contiguous stage II follicular lymphoma: radiotherapy with curative intent: Truly localised follicular lymphoma, which means stage I or contiguous stage II confirmed on PET-CT and marrow assessment, is treated with 24 Gy in 12 fractions to an involved-site field and a substantial minority never relapse.
claims.note: FoRT: '24 Gy in 12 fractions'.

claims.claim: TROG 99.03 randomised 150 patients after 30 Gy involved-field radiotherapy to observation or six cycles of CVP, with rituximab added from 2006: ten-year progression-free survival was 59 per cent with systemic therapy against 41 per cent with radiotherapy alone (hazard ratio 0.57), overall survival was not significantly different (95 against 87 per cent), and the effect was largest in the rituximab-containing subgroup.
claims.note: TROG 99.03: '150 patients', 30 Gy IFRT, R-CVP from 2006, 'Ten-year PFS rates were 59% ... and 41%', 'hazard ratio, 0.57', OS '87% and 95% at 10 years' (arm A, arm B), R-CVP subgroup HR 0.26.

claims.claim: Four gray in two fractions is not an alternative for cure: FoRT found it clearly inferior to 24 Gy for local control.
claims.note: FoRT: 4 Gy in two fractions 'not non-inferior to 24 Gy (hazard ratio 3.42'.

claims.claim: The British-led trial that settled this randomised 379 patients with asymptomatic, non-bulky, advanced disease: at three years, 46 per cent of those watched had not needed treatment against 88 per cent of those given four weekly doses of rituximab and two years of maintenance (hazard ratio 0.21), with no overall survival difference.
claims.note: Ardeshna Lancet Oncol 2014: '379 patients', '46% ... not needing treatment at 3 years compared with 88%', 'HR 0.21'; rituximab weekly x4 then 12 infusions over 2 years.

claims.claim: Bendamustine with rituximab gave median progression-free survival of 69.5 against 31.2 months for R-CHOP in the StiL NHL1 trial of indolent and mantle cell lymphoma (hazard ratio 0.58), with no alopecia, less haematological toxicity, fewer infections and far less neuropathy, and is the commonest first choice; it does deplete T cells for a long time, which matters for anyone who may need CAR-T later.
claims.note: StiL NHL1: 'median progression-free survival ... 69.5 months ... vs 31.2 months; hazard ratio 0.58'.

claims.claim: Obinutuzumab instead of rituximab improves progression-free survival: GALLIUM randomised 1,401 patients and gave three-year progression-free survival of 80.0 against 73.3 per cent (hazard ratio 0.66), at the cost of more grade 3 to 5 adverse events (74.6 against 67.8 per cent) and more infusion reactions.
claims.note: GALLIUM NEJM: 'A total of 1202 patients with follicular lymphoma underwent randomization'; the 80.0/73.3, HR 0.66 and AE 74.6/67.8 figures are for those 1,202. 1,401 is the whole trial including marginal zone lymphoma.
claims.fixed: 'randomised 1,401 patients' -> 'randomised 1,202 patients with follicular lymphoma'.

claims.claim: RELEVANCE randomised 1,030 patients to rituximab with lenalidomide or rituximab with the investigator's chemotherapy: complete response at 120 weeks was 48 against 53 per cent and median progression-free survival 120.2 against 123.8 months (hazard ratio 0.92), so R-squared is not superior but is equivalent, with less neutropenia (32 against 50 per cent) and more rash.
claims.note: RELEVANCE NEJM (cited): CR 48% vs 53%, neutropenia 32% vs 50% correct, but it reports 'interim 3-year rate of progression-free survival was 77% ... and 78%'; the 6-year update reports medians not reached (HR 1.03). Median PFS 120.2 vs 123.8 months, HR 0.92 was not found in any source.
claims.fixed: Replaced with 'interim three-year progression-free survival 77 against 78 per cent'.

claims.claim: Maintenance rituximab for two years afterwards lengthens remission substantially and does not lengthen life: in PRIMA median progression-free survival was 10.5 against 4.1 years but ten-year overall survival was about 80 per cent in both arms.
claims.note: PRIMA JCO 2019: 'median PFS was 10.5 years ... compared with 4.1 years'; '10-year OS estimates were approximately 80% in both study arms'.

claims.claim: Progression within two years of first chemotherapy (POD24): biopsy first, then a different class of treatment: About one in five people treated with first-line chemoimmunotherapy progress within two years, and their five-year overall survival in the National LymphoCare Study was 50 per cent against 90 per cent for everyone else, a difference that held after adjusting for FLIPI.
claims.note: Casulo JCO 2015: 19% early POD of 588; 'Five-year overall survival ... (50% v 90%)'; held after FLIPI adjustment.

claims.claim: If it is still follicular, the plan changes class rather than repeating it: CD19 CAR-T (ZUMA-5 reported an overall response of 92 per cent and complete response 74 per cent;
claims.note: ZUMA-5: '96 (92%) had an overall response and 77 (74%) had a complete response' among 104 patients, 84 FL and 20 MZL; the sentence presents pooled figures as follicular.
claims.fixed: Added 'across follicular and marginal zone lymphoma'.

claims.claim: ELARA with tisagenlecleucel reported complete response 69.1 per cent and overall response 86.2 per cent), a CD20 bispecific antibody, or lenalidomide with rituximab.
claims.note: ELARA: 'CRR was 69.1% ... and ORR 86.2%'.

claims.claim: Mosunetuzumab, given intravenously in 21-day cycles with step-up dosing and stopped after eight cycles in complete responders, produced a complete response in 60.0 per cent of 90 patients after two or more lines.
claims.note: Mosunetuzumab Lancet Oncol 2022: 90 patients, 'complete response was recorded in 54 patients (60.0%'.

claims.claim: Odronextamab in ELM-2 gave an objective response of 80.0 per cent, complete response 73.4 per cent and median progression-free survival 20.7 months in 128 patients, with grade 3 or worse cytokine release syndrome of 1.7 per cent using the split step-up.
claims.note: ELM-2: 128 patients, ORR 80.0%, CR 73.4%, median PFS 20.7 months, CRS grade >=3 '1.7% (1/60) with 0.7/4/20 mg step-up'.

claims.claim: AUGMENT randomised 358 patients with relapsed follicular or marginal zone lymphoma to lenalidomide with rituximab or rituximab with placebo: median progression-free survival 39.4 against 14.1 months (hazard ratio 0.46), with grade 3 to 4 neutropenia in 50 against 13 per cent.
claims.note: AUGMENT: 358 randomised, HR 0.46, median PFS 39.4 vs 14.1 months (PMC full text), grade 3-4 neutropenia 50% vs 13%.

claims.claim: Tafasitamab with lenalidomide and rituximab received traditional United States approval on 18 June 2025 on the inMIND trial, with a label note that it is not indicated in relapsed or refractory marginal zone lymphoma outside a trial.
claims.note: Drugs@FDA MONJUVI efficacy supplement approved 2025-06-18.

claims.claim: Zanubrutinib with obinutuzumab was given accelerated approval on 7 March 2024 on ROSEWOOD.
claims.note: Drugs@FDA BRUKINSA NDA213217 supplement 11 approved 2024-03-07.

claims.claim: Lisocabtagene maraleucel's follicular approval of 15 May 2024 converted to traditional approval on 20 February 2026, and a separate marginal zone lymphoma approval followed on 4 December 2025.
claims.note: FDA Breyanzi page lists approval letters dated May 15, 2024, December 4, 2025 and February 20, 2026.

claims.claim: It occurs in roughly 2 to 3 per cent of patients a year.
claims.note: Lymphoma Action (FL record link): 'Every year, transformation affects around 2 to 3 in every 100 people with follicular lymphoma'.

claims.claim: Relapse is treated with covalent BTK inhibitors (ibrutinib 2013, acalabrutinib 2017, zanubrutinib 2019; ibrutinib's US MCL approval was withdrawn in 2023 after SHINE), then brexucabtagene autoleucel (ZUMA-2, 2020), the non-covalent BTKi pirtobrutinib (2023), or the BCL2 inhibitor sonrotoclax (2026); venetoclax-ibrutinib (SYMPATICO) is another option.
claims.note: Drugs@FDA: IMBRUVICA 2013-11-13, CALQUENCE 2017-10-31, BRUKINSA 2019-11-14, JAYPIRCA 2023-01-27, BEQALZI (sonrotoclax) 2026-05-13; ZUMA-2 NEJM 2020.

claims.claim: Mantle cell lymphoma makes up about 5-7% of non-Hodgkin lymphomas; incidence ~1 per 100,000 per year, median age ~68, 3:1 male.
claims.note: No source on the MCL record gave the burden figures. HMRN: MCL 247 of 4,961 NHL (5.0%), crude incidence 0.86 per 100,000, median age 73.5 (not ~68), age-standardised male/female rate ratio 2.57 (not 3:1).
claims.fixed: Added HMRN to MCL links; burden now '~5% of NHL (247 of 4,961 ...), about 0.9 per 100,000 a year, median age 73.5, rate about 2.6 times higher in men'.

claims.claim: BCL2 inhibition is back: sonrotoclax approved for relapsed MCL in 2026 with venetoclax combinations close behind.
claims.note: Drugs@FDA BEQALZI (sonrotoclax) NDA220711 original approval 2026-05-13.

claims.claim: Among 183 younger patients on the Nordic protocols, TP53 mutation was present in 11% and carried a hazard ratio of 6.2 for overall survival, a median overall survival of 1.8 years against 12.7 years, half relapsing within a year, and worse responses to both induction and high-dose chemotherapy.
claims.note: Eskelund Blood 2017: 183 younger patients, TP53 mutations 11%, HR 6.2, median OS 1.8 vs 12.7 years, '50% relapsed at 1.0 years', inferior responses to induction and high-dose chemotherapy. Correct, but not on the MCL record.
claims.fixed: Added Eskelund 2017 as a link on the MCL patch in lymphoma-molecular.ts.

claims.claim: R-CHOP/R-DHAP or Nordic) with ibrutinib and 2 years ibrutinib maintenance; autologous transplant no longer adds benefit when ibrutinib is used (TRIANGLE).
claims.note: TRIANGLE: ibrutinib in induction and '2 years' maintenance; transplant not superior to the ibrutinib arm.

claims.claim: Relapsed after BTKi: Brexucabtagene or lisocabtagene CAR-T; pirtobrutinib; sonrotoclax (2026); allogeneic HSCT in selected patients; bispecific trials.
claims.note: Sonrotoclax approved 2026 (Drugs@FDA BEQALZI 2026-05-13).

claims.claim: First, the growth pattern and Ki-67 index: above about 30 per cent signals aggressive disease.
claims.note: Eskelund 2017 lists 'Ki67 > 30%' among adverse features; correct but no source on the row or record carried it.
claims.fixed: Added Eskelund 2017 as a link on the MCL patch; text unchanged.

claims.claim: First-line mantle cell lymphoma in younger, fitter patients after TRIANGLE: ibrutinib in, transplant optional: TRIANGLE randomised 870 patients up to 65 who were fit for transplant to three arms: alternating R-CHOP and R-DHAP induction with autologous transplant (arm A); the same with ibrutinib added to induction and as two-year maintenance (arm A+I); or ibrutinib-containing induction and maintenance without transplant (arm I).
claims.note: TRIANGLE: '870 patients' aged 18-65, arms A, A+I and I as described.

claims.claim: Three-year failure-free survival was 88 per cent for arm A+I against 72 per cent for arm A (hazard ratio 0.52).
claims.note: TRIANGLE: '3-year failure-free survival of 88% ... versus 72% (... hazard ratio 0.52'.

claims.claim: Transplant was not shown to be superior to the ibrutinib-containing regimen without it: 72 per cent for arm A against 86 per cent for arm I.
claims.note: TRIANGLE: 'Superiority of group A over group I was not shown with 3-year failure-free survival 72% ... versus 86%'.

claims.claim: Adding ibrutinib to transplant increased grade 3 to 5 haematological events during maintenance and follow-up (50 per cent in arm A+I against 21 per cent in arm A) and infections (25 against 13 per cent).
claims.note: TRIANGLE (PubMed abstract): A+I haematological 114 (50%), infections 58 (25%); A haematological 51 (21%), infections 32 (13%).

claims.claim: Where transplant is used, rituximab maintenance afterwards improves survival: LyMa randomised 240 patients after transplant to three years of rituximab or observation and found four-year event-free survival of 79 against 61 per cent, with overall survival also improved.
claims.note: LyMa NEJM 2017: 240 randomised, 3 years of rituximab, 4-year EFS 79% vs 61%, overall survival prolonged.

claims.claim: ENRICH, run at 66 sites in the United Kingdom and the Nordic countries, randomised 397 patients aged 60 and over to ibrutinib with rituximab or to the investigator's choice of immunochemotherapy (R-CHOP or bendamustine-rituximab), both followed by two years of rituximab maintenance, with ibrutinib continued until progression.
claims.note: ENRICH Lancet 2025: '66 sites in the UK, Sweden, Norway, Finland, and Denmark', 397 patients 60 and older, R-CHOP or BR, 2 years rituximab maintenance, ibrutinib until progression.

claims.claim: At a median follow-up of 47.9 months the adjusted hazard ratio for progression-free survival was 0.69 in favour of ibrutinib-rituximab.
claims.note: ENRICH: 'median follow-up of 47.9 months ... adjusted hazard ratio (HR) of 0.69'.

claims.claim: The benefit was concentrated where the comparator was R-CHOP (hazard ratio 0.37) and was not demonstrated against bendamustine-rituximab (0.91).
claims.note: ENRICH: R-CHOP 'HR was 0.37', bendamustine-rituximab 'HR was 0.91'.

claims.claim: Grade 3 or worse adverse events were similar (67 against 70 per cent).
claims.note: ENRICH: '67% ... and 70% ... reported grade 3 or above adverse events'.

claims.claim: SHINE took the other route and added ibrutinib to bendamustine-rituximab in 523 patients aged 65 and over: median progression-free survival 80.6 against 52.9 months (hazard ratio 0.75) with no overall survival difference and grade 3 or 4 adverse events in 81.5 against 77.3 per cent.
claims.note: SHINE NEJM 2022: 523 patients 65 and older, median PFS 80.6 vs 52.9 months, HR 0.75, OS similar, grade 3-4 AEs 81.5% vs 77.3%.

claims.claim: Acalabrutinib with bendamustine and rituximab received traditional United States approval on 16 January 2025 on the ECHO trial for untreated mantle cell lymphoma in people not eligible for an autologous transplant, and NICE TA1184 recommends the same combination in England for the same group.
claims.note: Drugs@FDA CALQUENCE efficacy supplement approved 2025-01-16; NICE TA1184 1.1 recommends acalabrutinib-BR for untreated MCL in adults not eligible for autologous transplant.

claims.claim: Adding venetoclax lengthens remission: SYMPATICO randomised 366 patients after one to five prior lines to ibrutinib with venetoclax or ibrutinib with placebo and gave median progression-free survival of 31.9 against 22.1 months (hazard ratio 0.629), with a complete response of 69.2 per cent in a separate open-label arm of treatment-naive TP53-mutated disease.
claims.note: SYMPATICO Lancet Oncol 2025: '267 patients were enrolled and randomly assigned'; 366 is ClinicalTrials.gov total enrolment including the safety run-in and treatment-naive open-label arm. ClinicalTrials.gov results (the trial record's source): PFS HR 0.629; CR 69.2% in the treatment-naive open-label arm (TP53-mutated eligibility). 31.9 vs 22.1 months correct.
claims.fixed: 'randomised 366 patients' -> 'randomised 267 patients'.

claims.claim: Brexucabtagene autoleucel, a CD19 CAR-T product, was tested in ZUMA-2 in 105 patients who had all had a BTK inhibitor: objective response 93 per cent and complete response 67 per cent in the primary efficacy analysis, 85 per cent by intention to treat, with progression-free survival of 61 per cent and overall survival of 83 per cent at twelve months.
claims.note: ZUMA-2 NEJM 2020: 'A total of 74 patients were enrolled'; 93%/67% in the 60-patient primary analysis, 85% ITT, PFS 61% and OS 83% at 12 months. 105 is the ClinicalTrials.gov total enrolment, not the cohort these figures describe.
claims.fixed: '105 patients' -> '74 patients'.

claims.claim: The toxicity is real: grade 3 or higher cytokine release syndrome in 15 per cent and grade 3 or higher neurological events in 31 per cent, higher than the CD19 products used in large B-cell lymphoma.
claims.note: ZUMA-2: grade >=3 CRS 15% and neurological events 31%; ZUMA-1 13% and 28%.

claims.claim: Lisocabtagene maraleucel is the second CAR-T option, approved in the United States on 30 May 2024 for relapsed or refractory mantle cell lymphoma after at least two prior lines including a BTK inhibitor.
claims.note: FDA Breyanzi page: approval letter dated May 30, 2024.

claims.claim: Except ALK-positive ALCL, five-year survival with CHOP is 30-40%.
claims.note: No source on the PTCL record gives 30-40% five-year survival with CHOP. HMRN: five-year relative survival 19.7% (PTCL unspecified) and 26.2% (angioimmunoblastic).
claims.fixed: Added HMRN to the PTCL links; sentence now reports the HMRN figures (about 20% PTCL-NOS, 26% AITL).

claims.claim: Relapsed disease is treated with pralatrexate (2009), the HDAC inhibitors romidepsin (2009, US PTCL indication withdrawn 2021) and belinostat (2014), brentuximab, or allogeneic transplant.
claims.note: Drugs@FDA ISTODAX: original approval 2009-11-05 (cutaneous T-cell lymphoma); PTCL supplement 2011-06-16, withdrawn 2021. Pralatrexate 2009-09-24 and belinostat 2014-07-03 correct.
claims.fixed: 'romidepsin (2009, US PTCL indication withdrawn 2021)' -> '(US PTCL approval 2011, withdrawn 2021)'.

claims.claim: Peripheral T-cell lymphomas make up about 10-15% of non-Hodgkin lymphomas in the West, more in Asia; there are over 30 WHO subtypes, most individually rare.
claims.note: No record source gives 10-15% of NHL, 'more in Asia' or 'over 30 WHO subtypes'. HMRN: T-cell lymphomas 308 of 5,796 lymphomas (5.3%).
claims.fixed: Burden now 'In a UK population series, T-cell lymphomas, including those of the skin, made up about 5% of all lymphomas (308 of 5,796); there are many WHO subtypes'.

claims.claim: HTLV-1 defines adult T-cell leukaemia/lymphoma, and the genomics show it is not simply a viral disease: across 426 cases, the acquired alterations overlapped significantly with the proteins the viral Tax protein binds, concentrating in T-cell receptor and NF-kB signalling, trafficking and immune surveillance, with activating CCR4 mutations among them.
claims.note: Kataoka Nat Genet 2015: '426 ATL cases', alterations 'overlap significantly with the HTLV-1 Tax interactome', TCR-NF-kB, trafficking, immunosurveillance, CCR4 activating mutations. Correct; not on the PTCL record.
claims.fixed: Added Kataoka 2015 as a link on the PTCL patch in lymphoma-molecular.ts.

claims.claim: First line, CD30+ PTCL / ALCL: Brentuximab vedotin + CHP ×6 (ECHELON-2, OS benefit) ± consolidative autologous transplant.
claims.note: ECHELON-2 (record link): A+CHP improved PFS and OS; six or eight cycles.

claims.claim: First line, other nodal PTCL: CHOP or CHOEP (≤60 years) ×6, autologous transplant consolidation in responders; clinical trial preferred.
claims.note: Schmitz Blood 2010 (now linked): 'For patients <= 60 years with lactate dehydrogenase <= upper normal value, etoposide improved 3-year EFS'.

claims.claim: First-line nodal peripheral T-cell lymphoma, CD30-positive: brentuximab vedotin with CHP: ECHELON-2 randomised 452 patients with untreated CD30-positive peripheral T-cell lymphoma to brentuximab vedotin with cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin and prednisone (A+CHP) or to CHOP.
claims.note: ECHELON-2: '452 patients were enrolled', A+CHP vs CHOP.

claims.claim: Median progression-free survival by blinded independent review was 48.2 against 20.8 months (hazard ratio 0.71), with improved overall survival, and toxicity was comparable: febrile neutropenia 18 against 15 per cent and peripheral neuropathy 52 against 55 per cent.
claims.note: ECHELON-2: 'Median progression-free survival was 48.2 months ... and 20.8 months ... (hazard ratio 0.71', febrile neutropenia 18% vs 15%, neuropathy 52% vs 55%, OS improved.

claims.claim: Adding etoposide (CHOEP) is standard in much of Europe for patients under 60 with a normal LDH, on the basis of a retrospective analysis of the German High-Grade Non-Hodgkin Lymphoma Study Group trials in which that subgroup had better event-free survival; the analysis was not randomised and not confined to T-cell lymphoma, so the practice rests on an observation rather than a trial.
claims.note: Schmitz Blood 2010: '343 patients' with T-cell lymphoma; 'For patients <= 60 years with lactate dehydrogenase <= upper normal value, etoposide improved 3-year EFS: 75.4% versus 51.0%'. The analysis was confined to T-cell lymphoma (the parent trials were not), and the subgroup is 60 or under, not under 60. No source was on the row or record.
claims.fixed: 'under 60' -> 'aged 60 or under'; 'not confined to T-cell lymphoma' -> 'drew on trials that were not designed for T-cell lymphoma'; Schmitz 2010 added to the PTCL record links.

claims.claim: Relapsed and refractory peripheral T-cell lymphoma: Response rates to every available single agent sit between about 25 and 35 per cent, and remissions are usually short, so the question at relapse is whether the patient can be taken to an allogeneic transplant or a trial.
claims.note: PROPEL: 'response rate ... was 29%'; BELIEF: 'Overall response rate ... was 25.8%'; remissions short (median PFS 3.5 and 1.6 months).

claims.claim: Approved single agents in the United States: pralatrexate, an antifolate, approved in 2009 on a response rate of about 29 per cent; belinostat, a histone deacetylase inhibitor, approved in 2014 on about 26 per cent, usable when platelets are low; romidepsin, approved in 2011 and withdrawn from this indication after the confirmatory Ro-CHOP trial failed.
claims.note: PROPEL 29% and FDA approval (Drugs@FDA 2009-09-24); BELIEF 25.8% and approval 2014-07-03; romidepsin PTCL 2011-06-16, withdrawn 2021.

claims.claim: Brentuximab vedotin is highly active in relapsed systemic anaplastic large cell lymphoma, where response rates are far higher than in other entities; its first-line United States approval with cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin and prednisone for untreated systemic anaplastic large cell lymphoma and other CD30-expressing peripheral T-cell lymphomas came on 16 November 2018.
claims.note: Drugs@FDA ADCETRIS efficacy supplement 99 approved 2018-11-16.

claims.claim: Five-year survival under 40% for PTCL-NOS with no new first-line regimen for non-CD30 disease.
claims.note: 'Under 40%' had no source on the record; HMRN gives 19.7% five-year relative survival for PTCL unspecified.
claims.fixed: Now 'Five-year relative survival of about 20% for PTCL-NOS in a UK population series'.

claims.claim: It is preceded by MGUS and smouldering myeloma, which are common (MGUS in ~3% of people over 50) and mostly harmless; whether to treat high-risk smouldering disease (AQUILA, daratumumab) is a live debate, and Iceland is screening its whole adult population (iStopMM).
claims.note: Wikipedia: "MGUS is a relatively stable condition afflicting 3% of people aged 50 and 5% of people aged 70".

claims.claim: MRD negativity at one in a million marrow cells has become both the best prognostic marker and, since 2024, an accepted regulatory endpoint.
claims.note: Wikipedia page does not mention the regulatory endpoint. Primary found: J Cancer Policy 2025 "On 12 April 2024, the US FDA ODAC voted (12-0) in support of MRD as an accelerated approval endpoint"; Semin Hematol 2025 calls it an "FDA-recognized early endpoint suitable for accelerated approval". Claim correct against it.
claims.fixed: Added link (J Cancer Policy 2025, ODAC April 2024) to the record; text unchanged.

claims.claim: No cancer has gained more drug classes: proteasome inhibitors (bortezomib 2003, carfilzomib), immunomodulatory cereblon modulators (thalidomide, lenalidomide, pomalidomide; next-generation CELMoDs iberdomide and mezigdomide), CD38 antibodies (daratumumab, isatuximab), BCMA-directed CAR-T (ide-cel, cilta-cel; anito-cel decision December 2026), BCMA and GPRC5D bispecific T-cell engagers (teclistamab, elranatamab, linvoseltamab, talquetamab), a BCMA ADC (belantamab, withdrawn 2022 and re-approved 2025), plus XPO1 and BCL-2 inhibitors for subsets.
claims.note: Myeloma Wikipedia page carries none of the dates. Checked elsewhere: bortezomib "approved ... in the United States in 2003" (Wikipedia Bortezomib); belantamab US withdrawal process Nov 2022 and FDA re-approval 23 Oct 2025 (FDA/ASCO Post); Arcellx 10-K: "anticipated PDUFA action date of December 23, 2026" for anito-cel. All dates correct.
claims.fixed: Added Arcellx 10-K link (anito-cel PDUFA) to the record; text unchanged.

claims.claim: At relapse, cilta-cel (CARTITUDE-4, OS HR 0.55) and teclistamab plus daratumumab (MajesTEC-3, approved March 2026) are second-line options, with sequencing by prior antigen exposure.
claims.note: Not on the Wikipedia page. Lancet Oncol 2026 CARTITUDE-4 update: "HR 0.55 [95% CI 0.39-0.79]; p=0.0009" for OS; FDA: "On March 5, 2026, the FDA approved teclistamab ... in combination with daratumumab hyaluronidase-fihj ... at least one prior line". Correct.
claims.fixed: Added CARTITUDE-4 OS paper and FDA tec-dara approval links to the record; text unchanged.

claims.claim: Multiple myeloma causes ~190,000 new cases a year worldwide, ~36,000 in the US, at a median age of 69.
claims.note: ~190,000 is GLOBOCAN 2022 (World: 187,952 new cases, repo public/globocan/countries.json) presented undated as "a year"; Wikipedia gives 2020 figures only. US 36,000 = SEER "Estimated New Cases in 2026 36,000"; median age 69 per Wikipedia (SEER).
claims.fixed: Dated: "In 2022, GLOBOCAN estimated ~188,000 new cases ... SEER estimates ~36,000 in the US in 2026"; added GLOBOCAN 2022 and SEER links.

claims.claim: More new drug classes than any other cancer have pushed median survival to more than 10 years in transplant-eligible patients and ~5-7 years in older patients; ~120,000 deaths a year worldwide.
claims.note: No cited source gives median survival >10 years (transplant-eligible) or 5-7 years (older); none found in Rajkumar AJH 2022/2024/2026 abstracts. ~120,000 deaths = GLOBOCAN 2022 (121,388), undated.
claims.fixed: Removed the two survival figures ("have lengthened survival, most of all in transplant-eligible patients"); dated deaths "GLOBOCAN estimated ~121,000 deaths worldwide in 2022".

claims.claim: In the United States, 63.7% of people diagnosed with myeloma in 2016-2022 were alive five years later, relative to people of the same age without the disease.
claims.note: SEER: "5-Year Relative Survival 63.7% 2016-2022".

claims.claim: Myeloma is a cancer of the bone marrow and is almost always systemic at diagnosis (96% of cases are recorded as distant), so stage-by-stage tables say little; risk is set instead by the Revised ISS, cytogenetics and fitness for transplant.
claims.note: SEER stage table: "Distant Cancer Has Metastasized 96% 63.0%".

claims.claim: Quadruplet induction (CD38 antibody + PI + IMiD + dexamethasone) for all newly diagnosed patients, with MRD negativity in 60-75%.
claims.note: Unsourced on the record and the range is too high: PERSEUS NEJM 2024 "MRD-negative status (75.2% vs. 47.5%)"; CEPHEUS 60.9%; IMROZ NEJM 2024 "MRD-negative status and a complete response (55.5% vs. 40.9%)". 60-75% omits IMROZ.
claims.fixed: Changed to "about 55-75% across the phase 3 trials (IMROZ 55.5% MRD-negative complete response; PERSEUS 75.2% MRD-negative)"; added PERSEUS and IMROZ links.

claims.claim: CAR-T with a survival benefit as early as second line (CARTITUDE-4, OS HR 0.55) and a third of late-line patients progression-free at five years without maintenance (CARTITUDE-1).
claims.note: Not on Wikipedia page. Lancet Oncol 2026 CARTITUDE-4: OS "HR 0.55"; JCO 2025 CARTITUDE-1: "One third (32/97) of patients remain alive and progression-free for >=5 years after a single cilta-cel infusion, without maintenance". Correct.
claims.fixed: Added CARTITUDE-4 OS and CARTITUDE-1 five-year links; text unchanged.

claims.claim: Two antigens for T-cell redirection (BCMA, GPRC5D) with four approved bispecifics; teclistamab plus daratumumab approved at first relapse (March 2026).
claims.note: Wikipedia page names only teclistamab/talquetamab. ASH Education 2025: "There are currently 4 commercially approved bispecific antibodies: teclistamab, elranatamab, and linvoseltamab, which target BCMA, as well as talquetamab, which targets the GPRC5D"; FDA approved tec-dara on 5 March 2026. Correct.
claims.fixed: Added FDA tec-dara link; text unchanged.

claims.claim: MRD negativity accepted by FDA as an endpoint for accelerated approval (2024), enabling faster trials and MRD-guided therapy.
claims.note: Not on Wikipedia page. J Cancer Policy 2025: ODAC voted 12-0 on 12 April 2024 for MRD as an accelerated approval endpoint. Correct.
claims.fixed: Added J Cancer Policy 2025 link; text unchanged.

claims.claim: First relapse (1-3 prior lines): Cilta-cel if lenalidomide-refractory (CARTITUDE-4); teclistamab + daratumumab (MajesTEC-3, 2026); ide-cel after ≥2 lines; belantamab-Vd or -Pd (DREAMM-7/8);
claims.note: Refs: CARTITUDE-4 NEJM 2023 enrolled "one to three previous lines"; KarMMa-3 "two to four regimens" (ide-cel label after >=2 lines); MajesTEC-3 approval FDA 5 March 2026; DREAMM-7/8 records. Consistent.

claims.claim: Relapse is defined by a rising M-protein or light chains, and refractory disease by progression on or within 60 days of a treatment.
claims.note: Neither Wikipedia nor the NCCN landing page states it (NCCN PDF needs login). IMWG 2011 (Blood): "Refractory myeloma is defined as disease that is nonresponsive while on primary or salvage therapy, or progresses within 60 days of last therapy." Correct.
claims.fixed: Added IMWG 2011 link; text unchanged.

claims.claim: Early relapse after a lenalidomide-based first line is usually treated with a carfilzomib or pomalidomide triplet with a CD38 antibody, or with belantamab mafodotin combinations after DREAMM-7 (belantamab-bortezomib-dexamethasone versus daratumumab-bortezomib-dexamethasone, median progression-free survival 36.6 versus 13.4 months, hazard ratio 0.41, with a survival gain) and DREAMM-8 returned the antibody-drug conjugate to the market in 2025.
claims.note: DREAMM-7 record/NEJM 2024: "median progression-free survival was 36.6 months ... and 13.4 months ... (hazard ratio ... 0.41)"; OS HR 0.58 in 2024 update; re-approved US Oct 2025, EU 2025. (Supporting link added to the record: Added DREAMM-7 NEJM link to the record.)

claims.claim: KarMMa-3 then showed it beat standard regimens after two to four prior lines, median progression-free survival 13.3 versus 4.4 months (hazard ratio 0.49).
claims.note: KarMMa-3 NEJM 2023 (record keyPaper): "two to four regimens ... median progression-free survival was 13.3 months ... 4.4 months ... hazard ratio ... 0.49".

claims.claim: Ciltacabtagene autoleucel produced responses in 98 percent of heavily pretreated patients in CARTITUDE-1, with a third still progression-free at five years without further treatment, and CARTITUDE-4 showed it after one to three prior lines cut progression or death by about three quarters (hazard ratio 0.26) and lengthened life (hazard ratio 0.55), moving CAR-T to second line in 2024.
claims.note: CARTITUDE-1 JCO 2023 2-year: "overall response rate was 97.9%" (Lancet 2021: 97%); JCO 2025: one third (32/97) progression-free >=5 years without maintenance; CARTITUDE-4 NEJM 2023 PFS "hazard ratio, 0.26", Lancet Oncol 2026 OS "HR 0.55"; FDA second-line approval 5 April 2024 (J&J release). (Supporting link added to the record: Added CARTITUDE-1 (JCO 2023, JCO 2025) and CARTITUDE-4 OS links.)

claims.claim: Bispecific antibodies give an off-the-shelf alternative: teclistamab (MajesTEC-1, response rate 63 percent, approved 2022), elranatamab (MagnetisMM-3, 61 percent) and linvoseltamab (LINKER-MM1, 70 percent, approved 2025) against BCMA, and talquetamab (MonumenTAL-1, about 73 percent, approved 2023) against GPRC5D, which works after BCMA therapy fails.
claims.note: MajesTEC-1 NEJM 2022 "overall response rate was 63.0%" (approved Oct 2022); MagnetisMM-3 "ORR of 61.0%"; LINKER-MM1 JCO 2024 "Among the 117 patients treated with 200 mg ... the ORR was 71%" (page said 70); talquetamab ~73% matches phase 2 (Blood 2026 3-year: 67-74%), approved Aug 2023; linvoseltamab approved July 2025.
claims.fixed: LINKER-MM1 response rate 70 -> 71 percent; added LINKER-MM1 and MagnetisMM-3 links.

claims.claim: MajesTEC-3 (2025) showed teclistamab with daratumumab beating standard combinations in early relapse.
claims.note: MajesTEC-3 NEJM (Dec 2025, NEJMoa2514663): 36-month PFS 83.4% vs 29.7%, HR 0.17, versus DPd/DVd.

claims.claim: Almost everyone with myeloma relapses eventually; with each line of treatment remissions shorten, and until 2021 patients whose disease resisted the three main drug classes survived about a year.
claims.note: Unsourced on the record; MAMMOTH (Leukemia 2019): "median overall survival (OS) from T0 [CD38-refractory] ... was 8.6 months", 5.6 for penta-refractory. LocoMMotion (triple-class exposed, not refractory) 12.4 months. "About a year" overstated survival once refractory.
claims.fixed: Changed to "patients whose disease had become refractory to a CD38 antibody survived a median of under nine months (8.6 months in the MAMMOTH study)"; added MAMMOTH link.

claims.claim: Four approved bispecific antibodies, three against BCMA and one against GPRC5D, give off-the-shelf immune therapy with response rates of 60 to 70 percent in heavily pretreated patients.
claims.note: Four approved bispecifics (3 BCMA, 1 GPRC5D) correct; response rates in pivotal studies 61% (elranatamab), 63% (teclistamab), 71% (linvoseltamab JCO 2024), ~72-74% (talquetamab), so "60 to 70 percent" understates the top of the range.
claims.fixed: "60 to 70 percent" -> "about 60 to 75 percent".

claims.claim: Belantamab mafodotin returned in 2025 for early relapse with a survival gain in DREAMM-7.
claims.note: DREAMM-7 survival benefit (OS HR 0.58, 2024 update); FDA approved belantamab-Vd 23 October 2025.

claims.claim: Acute lymphoblastic leukaemia is the commonest childhood cancer, and about 90 percent of children with it are alive five years after diagnosis; acute myeloid leukaemia is mainly a disease of older adults treated with intensive chemotherapy, venetoclax combinations and transplant; chronic lymphocytic leukaemia is often watched for years and then controlled with BTK and BCL2 inhibitors; chronic myeloid leukaemia became the model of targeted therapy with imatinib.
claims.note: NCI PDQ child ALL (HP): "For ALL, the 5-year survival rate increased ... to approximately 90% for children younger than 15 years".

claims.claim: About 490,000 new cases and 300,000 deaths a year worldwide; the commonest cancer of childhood, where most cases are now cured, and a group of very different diseases in adults.
claims.note: Figures are GLOBOCAN 2022 (World leukaemia 487,294 new cases, 305,405 deaths) presented undated as "a year"; none of the cited pages (Wikipedia: 2015 GBD figures; NCI) gives them.
claims.fixed: Dated: "In 2022, GLOBOCAN estimated about 487,000 new cases and 305,000 deaths worldwide"; added GLOBOCAN 2022 link.

claims.claim: Childhood ALL five-year survival near 90 percent through risk-adapted chemotherapy and measurable residual disease monitoring.
claims.note: PDQ: "approximately 90% for children younger than 15 years"; "more than 90% of patients alive at 5 years" on current regimens.

claims.claim: The classical BCR-ABL1-negative MPNs (polycythaemia vera, essential thrombocythaemia, primary myelofibrosis) are clonal diseases driven by JAK-STAT activation: JAK2 V617F in ~95% of PV and ~60% of ET/PMF, CALR in ~25% of ET/PMF, MPL in ~5%.
claims.note: NCCN (login), NCI PDQ patient page and MPNRF homepage give no frequencies (PDQ: "A JAK2 gene mutation is often found"). Found: Blood 2023 "JAK2-p.V617F is present in >95% of PV patients, and also in about half of the patients with ET or PMF"; JAMA 2025 ET review "JAK2, 64%), calreticulin (CALR, 23%), and ... (MPL, 4%)". Page figures ~60% ET/PMF, CALR ~25%, MPL ~5% were approximately right but not sourced.
claims.fixed: Rewritten to source: "JAK2 V617F in over 95% of PV and about half of ET/PMF; in ET, JAK2 in ~64%, CALR in ~23% and MPL in ~4%"; added Blood 2023 and JAMA 2025 links.

claims.claim: Risk in PV/ET is thrombosis (managed with aspirin, phlebotomy, hydroxyurea or interferon); in myelofibrosis it is cytopenias, splenomegaly, constitutional symptoms and leukaemic transformation (about 10-20%), risk-scored by DIPSS-plus, MIPSS70 and MIPSS70+ v2.0.
claims.note: Not in cited sources. Int J Mol Sci 2019 review: leukaemic evolution "is highest in primary myelofibrosis, where it is estimated to be approximately 10-20% at 10 years"; EJHaem 2023 "in 10%-20% of cases it can evolve into blast phase". Correct.
claims.fixed: Added Int J Mol Sci 2019 link; text unchanged.

claims.claim: Ruxolitinib (COMFORT-I/II, 2011) was the first JAK inhibitor; fedratinib (2019), pacritinib (2022, for platelets <50) and momelotinib (2023, for anaemic patients) followed.
claims.note: Approval years match the corpus drug records and primary sources: ruxolitinib Nov 2011 (COMFORT), fedratinib 16 Aug 2019, pacritinib FDA 28 Feb/1 Mar 2022 for "platelet levels below 50,000/uL", momelotinib Sept 2023. NCI patient PDQ does not give years.

claims.claim: Ropeginterferon alfa-2b (2021) is the first approved interferon for PV with evidence of molecular response, and rusfertide (2026), a hepcidin mimetic, is the first drug to control PV erythrocytosis without phlebotomy (VERIFY).
claims.note: Years correct (ropeginterferon US Nov 2021; rusfertide FDA 28 Aug 2026), but FDA calls it "the first approved treatment for polycythemia vera that mimics hepcidin"; "first drug to control PV erythrocytosis without phlebotomy" overstated (cytoreductive drugs also do). VERIFY: "76.9% ... required no phlebotomies ... compared to 32.9% on placebo".
claims.fixed: Reworded: "rusfertide (2026), the first approved hepcidin mimetic, freed most patients from phlebotomy in VERIFY (77% versus 33% on placebo needed none over weeks 20 to 32)"; added FDA link.

claims.claim: Combined incidence around 2-3 per 100,000 per year;
claims.note: No cited source gives incidence. Titmarsh 2014 meta-analysis (Am J Hematol): "combined annual incidence rates for PV, ET, and PMF were 0.84, 1.03, and 0.47 per 100,000" (sum 2.34). Correct.
claims.fixed: Added Titmarsh 2014 link; text unchanged.

claims.claim: Rusfertide (2026) is the first mechanistically new PV drug in a decade and removes the need for phlebotomy in most patients.
claims.note: Not in cited sources. FDA 28 Aug 2026 approval; VERIFY 76.9% vs 32.9% needed no phlebotomy, supporting "most patients". Correct.
claims.fixed: Added FDA rusfertide link; text unchanged.

claims.claim: PV: Low-dose aspirin, phlebotomy to haematocrit <45%; cytoreduction (hydroxyurea or ropeginterferon alfa-2b) for high-risk; ruxolitinib after hydroxyurea failure (RESPONSE); rusfertide to eliminate phlebotomy need (VERIFY, 2026).
claims.note: FDA rusfertide release: goal is "keeping ... hematocrit below 45%"; approval 2026 based on VERIFY (rusfertide/verify records). Haematocrit target also CYTO-PV per record history.

claims.claim: Myelofibrosis, intermediate-2/high risk: JAK inhibitor for spleen and symptoms: ruxolitinib (COMFORT), fedratinib, pacritinib if platelets <50×10⁹/L, momelotinib if anaemic (MOMENTUM); allogeneic HSCT for eligible patients (the only cure).
claims.note: Pacritinib label: myelofibrosis "with platelet ... levels below 50,000/uL" (= 50x10^9/L).

claims.claim: Risk is stratified by IPSS-R and, since 2022, the molecular IPSS-M, which incorporates mutations (TP53 multi-hit, ASXL1, RUNX1, SF3B1 among 31 genes).
claims.note: IPSS-M NEJM Evidence 2022: "Using hematologic parameters, cytogenetic abnormalities, and somatic mutations of 31 genes".

claims.claim: Lower-risk disease is treated for anaemia: erythropoiesis-stimulating agents, lenalidomide for del(5q), luspatercept (MEDALIST 2020, COMMANDS 2023 first line), and imetelstat (IMerge, 2024) after ESA failure.
claims.note: Dates match corpus history and regulators: luspatercept MDS approval 2020 (MEDALIST), first-line Aug 2023 (COMMANDS); imetelstat "approved ... in the United States in June 2024".

claims.claim: Three large phase 3 additions to azacitidine failed in 2023-24 (magrolimab ENHANCE, sabatolimab STIMULUS-MDS2, venetoclax VERONA), leaving azacitidine alone as the higher-risk standard.
claims.note: VERONA failed in 2025, not 2023-24: AbbVie, June 16, 2025: VERONA "did not meet the primary endpoint of overall survival (OS) with a hazard ratio (HR) of 0.908". ENHANCE and STIMULUS-MDS2 are phase 3 and negative.
claims.fixed: "failed in 2023-24" -> "failed in 2023-25"; history note "VERONA negative in 2024" -> 2025; added AbbVie link.

claims.claim: MDS affects around 4-5 per 100,000 people per year overall, rising steeply with age (median age ~70), according to SEER.
claims.note: No cited source gives it. SEER-based papers: J Registry Manag 2021 "age-adjusted incidence rate of 4.7 cases per 100,000" (SEER 21, 2001-2016) supports 4-5; but Ma 2007 (Cancer, SEER 2001-2003) "median age at diagnosis = 76 years", not ~70.
claims.fixed: Rewritten: "around 4-5 per 100,000 people per year overall (4.7 in SEER 2001-2016), rising steeply with age; the median age at diagnosis in SEER data was 76"; added both SEER papers as links.

claims.claim: IPSS-M (2022) reclassifies about half of patients relative to IPSS-R and is now the recommended risk model.
claims.note: IPSS-M: "the IPSS-M improved prognostic discrimination ... and restratified 46% of patients" (about half).

claims.claim: Higher-risk MDS has had no new drug since azacitidine: the 2023-24 failures of magrolimab, sabatolimab and venetoclax combinations were a field-wide setback.
claims.note: Same date error: VERONA (venetoclax) failed in June 2025 (AbbVie press release).
claims.fixed: "2023-24 failures" -> "2023-25 failures".
