claims.claim: Lower risk, anaemia: ESA if serum EPO <500; luspatercept first line (COMMANDS) or after ESA failure (MEDALIST); imetelstat after ESA failure (IMerge); lenalidomide for del(5q).
claims.note: ESA if serum EPO <500 is an NCCN threshold; the NCCN MDS guideline PDF requires login and the ref drug records (luspatercept, imetelstat, lenalidomide) do not state the EPO cut-off.

claims.claim: BMT CTN 1102 showed a survival benefit for transplant in 50-75-year-olds.
claims.note: BMT CTN 1102 (JCO 2021): "subjects 50-75 years of age ... adjusted overall survival rate at 3 years in the Donor arm was 47.9% ... compared with 26.6%". (Supporting link added to the record: Added BMT CTN 1102 JCO link to the record.)

claims.claim: Median age at diagnosis is 68, and outcomes diverge sharply by age and fitness.

claims.fixed: '~50% of gliomas, median age 65' -> 'about half of all malignant primary brain tumours in US registry data, median age 64'; CBTRUS and NCI PDQ added to record links

claims.claim: Glioblastoma treatment has been static since 2005: maximal safe resection (improved by 5-ALA fluorescence, intraoperative MRI, and awake mapping; the extent of resection is itself prognostic and is now graded by the RANO resect classes), radiotherapy with concurrent and adjuvant temozolomide (Stupp), and tumour treating fields (EF-14).
claims.note: Wikipedia: 'a large 2005 clinical trial of 573 participants ... temozolomide' became standard; EF-14 described as the 2015 phase III trial. No other figure.

claims.claim: Vorasidenib (INDIGO, approved 2024) is the first targeted therapy for grade 2 IDH-mutant glioma, delaying radiation and chemotherapy by years.
claims.note: FDA approval 'On August 6, 2024' is right. INDIGO NEJM 2023: 'median progression-free survival, 27.7 months vs. 11.1 months'; FDA: time to next intervention 'not reached for the vorasidenib arm and was 17.8 months for the placebo arm'. Neither source states a delay 'by years'.
claims.fixed: 'delaying radiation and chemotherapy by years' -> 'it more than doubled progression-free survival (27.7 against 11.1 months) and delayed the next treatment'; FDA notice added to record links

claims.claim: Dabrafenib with trametinib (2023) was the first targeted therapy approved for BRAF V600E paediatric low-grade glioma; tovorafenib (2024) followed for relapsed or refractory BRAF-altered tumours, including BRAF fusions.
claims.note: FDA: 'On March 16, 2023 ... approved dabrafenib ... with trametinib ... for pediatric patients ... with LGG with a BRAF V600E mutation', 'first FDA approval of a systemic therapy for the first-line treatment'; FDA: tovorafenib 'On April 23, 2024 ... BRAF fusion or rearrangement, or BRAF V600 mutation'.

claims.claim: About 300,000 CNS tumours occur per year, most of them not glioblastoma;
claims.note: GLOBOCAN-derived figure presented undated. GLOBOCAN 2022 (repo public/globocan/countries.json, World, code 31 C70-72): 321,731 new cases. 'Most of them not glioblastoma' conflicts with CBTRUS: glioblastoma is '52.2% of all malignant tumors' and GLOBOCAN counts malignant tumours only.
claims.fixed: -> 'In 2022, GLOBOCAN estimated about 322,000 new cancers of the brain and central nervous system worldwide; in US registry data glioblastoma is about half of malignant primary brain tumours.'; GLOBOCAN and CBTRUS added to record links

claims.claim: In the Stupp trial (EORTC 26981-NCIC, 2005) median survival with surgery, radiotherapy and temozolomide was 14.6 months against 12.1 with radiotherapy alone, and two-year survival rose from 10 to 27 percent; half of that trial's patients lived longer than the median, and a median describes a trial population rather than one person.
claims.note: Stupp NEJM 2005 abstract: 'median survival was 14.6 months with radiotherapy plus temozolomide and 12.1 months with radiotherapy alone'; 'two-year survival rate was 26.5 percent ... and 10.4 percent'.
claims.fixed: Stupp NEJM 2005 added to record links

claims.claim: Glioblastoma, newly diagnosed: Radiotherapy 60 Gy in 30 fractions with concurrent and 6 cycles adjuvant temozolomide; from age 65, short-course radiotherapy (40 Gy in 15 fractions) with temozolomide (CCTG CE.6); for older patients unfit for combined treatment, temozolomide alone or hypofractionated radiotherapy alone, chosen by MGMT status (Nordic, NOA-08);
claims.note: Stupp NEJM 2005: '60 Gy' in 2-Gy daily fractions over 6 weeks, 'followed by six cycles of adjuvant temozolomide'; CE.6 NEJM 2017: 'patients 65 years of age or older ... radiotherapy alone (40 Gy in 15 fractions) or radiotherapy with concomitant and adjuvant temozolomide'.

claims.claim: No systemic drug has beaten the 2005 chemoradiation standard in a phase 3 trial, though tumour treating fields (EF-14, 2015) and short-course radiotherapy from age 65 (CCTG CE.6, 2017) both added survival; locoregional CAR-T, focused-ultrasound barrier opening and neoantigen vaccines are the current attempts.
claims.note: Stupp NEJM 2005; EF-14 JAMA 2015 (interim, OS 20.5 vs 15.6 months per protocol); CE.6 NEJM 2017 in patients 65 or older (OS 9.3 vs 7.6 months).

claims.claim: MGMT-unmethylated glioblastoma (~60%) gains less from temozolomide than methylated disease, and how much less is still debated;
claims.note: Wikipedia gives no proportion. Hegi NEJM 2005 (Stupp trial tissue): 'The MGMT promoter was methylated in 45 percent of 206 assessable cases', so 55% unmethylated, not ~60%.
claims.fixed: '(~60%)' -> '(55% of assessable tumours in the Stupp trial)'; Hegi NEJM 2005 added to record links

claims.claim: Diffuse midline glioma has one approved drug, dordaviprone, with a 22% response rate; making those responses last is the open question, and the phase 3 ACTION trial, GD2 CAR-T and convection-enhanced delivery are the attempts on it.
claims.note: FDA: dordaviprone accelerated approval August 6, 2025; 'ORR was 22% (95% CI: 12, 36)'. Dordaviprone record carries this FDA notice.

claims.claim: Together they are about 1% of adult and 15% of childhood cancers.
claims.note: Wikipedia: 'Sarcomas are quite rare, making up about 1% of all adult cancer diagnoses and 15% of childhood cancer diagnoses.'

claims.claim: Advanced soft-tissue sarcoma still depends on doxorubicin with a median survival around 18-20 months; olaratumab's failure (ANNOUNCE) showed how hard that bar is to move.
claims.note: ANNOUNCE JAMA 2020: doxorubicin plus placebo 'median overall survival, 20.4 months vs 19.7 months'.

claims.claim: Subtype-specific drugs then fill in: trabectedin and eribulin for L-sarcomas, pazopanib for non-adipocytic sarcomas, and, in GIST, the sequence imatinib (3 years adjuvant, SSGXVIII), sunitinib, regorafenib and ripretinib (INVICTUS), with avapritinib for PDGFRA D842V and ctDNA-genotype-directed selection (INSIGHT) arriving.
claims.note: SSGXVIII JAMA 2012: 'Imatinib, 400 mg per day, orally for either 12 months or 36 months'; 36 months improved RFS and OS.

claims.claim: The unsolved problems are metastatic osteosarcoma and Ewing sarcoma (survival unchanged in 30 years), the HLA restriction of TCR therapies, chemoresistance of most adult subtypes, and trial feasibility in diseases with a few hundred cases a year.
claims.note: No source on the record supports 'survival unchanged in 30 years' or 'a few hundred cases a year'. NCI PDQ osteosarcoma and Ewing give current metastatic outcomes but no statement that survival is unchanged for 30 years.
claims.fixed: removed '(survival unchanged in 30 years)'; 'diseases with a few hundred cases a year' -> 'diseases this rare'

claims.claim: Sarcomas make up ~1% of adult cancers (~13,500 soft-tissue and ~3,900 bone sarcomas in the US per year) and ~15% of paediatric cancers, across >70 histologic subtypes.
claims.note: Wikipedia: ACS 2023 estimates 3,970 bone and 13,400 soft-tissue sarcomas; 1% adult / 15% childhood confirmed. SEER Stat Facts (current): 'Estimated New Cases in 2026 13,910' (soft tissue including heart) and '4,110' (bone and joint). '>70 histologic subtypes' is not in any source on the record (Wikipedia lists about 44 soft-tissue and 8 bone subtypes).
claims.fixed: -> '... across dozens of histologic subtypes; SEER estimates about 13,900 new soft-tissue (including heart) cancers and 4,100 bone and joint cancers in the US in 2026'; SEER pages added to record links

claims.claim: Five-year survival is ~65% overall and ~15-30% for metastatic disease.
claims.note: SEER 5-year relative survival 65.7% (soft tissue) and 68.7% (bone and joint); Wikipedia: soft-tissue '16.4% for soft-tissue sarcomas that have spread to distant organs'. No source on the record gives the upper 30% for metastatic disease.
claims.fixed: '~15-30% for metastatic disease' -> '~16% for soft-tissue sarcoma that has spread to distant organs'

claims.claim: Localised high-risk soft-tissue sarcoma (grade 3, >5 cm, deep): Neoadjuvant anthracycline-ifosfamide × 3 (ISG-STS 1001) ± preoperative radiotherapy, then wide resection; regional hyperthermia with chemotherapy where available (EORTC 62961).
claims.note: ISG-STS 1001 Lancet Oncol 2017: high risk is 'high malignancy grade, 5 cm or longer in diameter, and deeply located'; 'three cycles of full-dose standard chemotherapy (epirubicin ... plus ifosfamide'. The row said '>5 cm'.
claims.fixed: '>5 cm' -> '5 cm or more'

claims.claim: Advanced soft-tissue sarcoma, first line: Doxorubicin 75 mg/m2 (single agent) or doxorubicin-ifosfamide for symptomatic/rapid disease (EORTC 62012: PFS but not OS benefit); histotype exceptions: trabectedin or gemcitabine-docetaxel for leiomyosarcoma, paclitaxel for angiosarcoma.
claims.note: EORTC 62012 not among the row refs. Lancet Oncol 2014 (EORTC 62012): doxorubicin '75 mg/m(2)'; 'no significant difference in overall survival' (12.8 vs 14.3 months); 'Median progression-free survival was significantly higher' with the combination. Statement is right.
claims.fixed: added ref eortc-62012 (existing trial record) to the row

claims.claim: GIST, localised: Resection; adjuvant imatinib 3 years for high risk (SSGXVIII), longer under study; none for PDGFRA D842V or SDH-deficient (imatinib-insensitive).
claims.note: SSGXVIII JAMA 2012: 36 months versus 12 months of adjuvant imatinib in high-risk GIST improved RFS and OS.

claims.claim: Metastatic osteosarcoma and Ewing sarcoma: survival ~20-30%, unchanged for three decades; no targeted or immune therapy has worked.
claims.note: Wikipedia gives no metastatic osteosarcoma/Ewing figure. NCI PDQ osteosarcoma: EFS 'about 20% to 30% for patients with metastatic disease at diagnosis', 'roughly 30% will survive 5 years'; NCI PDQ Ewing: metastatic '6-year event-free survival (EFS) rate of approximately 28% and an overall survival (OS) rate of approximately 30%'. Neither states survival is unchanged for three decades.
claims.fixed: NCI PDQ osteosarcoma and Ewing added to record links; removed 'unchanged for three decades'

claims.claim: Advanced soft-tissue sarcoma still depends on a 1970s drug (doxorubicin); every attempt to improve first-line survival (olaratumab, evofosfamide, aldoxorubicin) failed.
claims.note: Doxorubicin record's Wikipedia: 'Doxorubicin was approved for medical use in the United States in 1974.'

claims.claim: Rarity fragments evidence: 70+ subtypes, few randomised trials, and reliance on reference-centre expertise that is unevenly distributed.
claims.note: '70+ subtypes' is not in any source on the record; Wikipedia's AJCC list has about 44 soft-tissue and 8 bone subtypes.
claims.fixed: '70+ subtypes' -> 'dozens of subtypes'

claims.claim: In the United States, 94.7% of people diagnosed with melanoma of the skin in 2016-2022 were alive five years later, relative to people of the same age without the disease.
claims.note: SEER Stat Facts melanoma: '5-Year Relative Survival 94.7% ... SEER 21 (Excluding IL) 2016–2022'

claims.claim: 77% of melanomas are found while still confined to the skin, with five-year relative survival of 100%; it is 76% for regional disease (10% of cases) and 34% for distant disease (5% of cases).
claims.note: SEER: 'Localized ... 77% 100.0% Regional ... 10% 76.0% Distant ... 5% 34.0%'

claims.claim: The distant-stage figure describes people diagnosed in 2016-2022 and only partly reflects the immunotherapy combinations that now keep a growing share of people with advanced melanoma alive long term.
claims.note: SEER survival-by-stage table is for 2016–2022 diagnoses; the remainder is a caveat, not a figure

claims.claim: In the United States, 52% of women diagnosed with ovarian cancer in 2016-2022 were alive five years later, relative to women of the same age without the disease.
claims.note: SEER ovary: '5-Year Relative Survival 52.0% ... 2016–2022'

claims.claim: The problem is late diagnosis: 54% of cases are found after distant spread, with five-year relative survival of 31.5%, against 91.9% for the 22% found while confined to the ovary and 70.1% for regional disease (18% of cases).
claims.note: SEER ovary: 'Localized 22% 91.9% Regional 18% 70.1% Distant 54% 31.5%'

claims.claim: In the United States, 68.8% of women diagnosed with cervical cancer in 2016-2022 were alive five years later, relative to women of the same age without the disease.
claims.note: SEER cervix: '5-Year Relative Survival 68.8% ... 2016–2022'

claims.claim: 41% of cases are found while confined to the cervix, with five-year relative survival of 91.8%; it is 64% for regional disease (37% of cases) and 20.5% for distant disease (16% of cases).
claims.note: SEER cervix: 'Localized 41% 91.8% Regional 37% 64.0% Distant 16% 20.5%'

claims.claim: In the United States, 80.9% of women diagnosed with cancer of the uterus in 2016-2022 were alive five years later, relative to women of the same age without the disease.
claims.note: SEER uterine: '5-Year Relative Survival 80.9% ... 2016–2022'

claims.claim: Most cases are caught early because bleeding after the menopause is investigated: 67% are found while confined to the uterus, with five-year relative survival of 94.9%; it is 70.1% for regional disease (18% of cases) and 19.9% for distant disease (11% of cases).
claims.note: SEER uterine: 'Localized 67% 94.9% Regional 18% 70.1% Distant 11% 19.9%'

claims.claim: The treatment revolution began in 2011 with ipilimumab and vemurafenib and accelerated with PD-1 blockade (2014).
claims.note: Wikipedia states 'Ipilimumab was approved by the FDA in March 2011' and 'In August 2011, Vemurafenib received FDA approval' but says nothing about PD-1 approval in 2014. The first Keytruda label reads 'Initial U.S. Approval: 2014', so the sentence is right; the record now cites it.
claims.fixed: Added the 2014 Keytruda FDA label as a link on the melanoma record; text unchanged

claims.claim: Nivolumab-ipilimumab now delivers ~50% melanoma-specific survival at ten years in advanced disease (CheckMate 067), pembrolizumab 34% overall survival at ten years (KEYNOTE-006), and nivolumab-relatlimab offers a gentler doublet.
claims.note: Wikipedia, the only record source, gives neither figure. CheckMate 067 10-year NEJM full text: 'Melanoma-specific survival rates at 10-years were 52% with nivolumab-plus-ipilimumab' (a post hoc analysis). KEYNOTE-006 Annals 2024 abstract: '10-year OS was 34.0% and 23.6%'. Both figures are right.
claims.fixed: Added the CheckMate 067 10-year and KEYNOTE-006 10-year papers as links on the melanoma record; text unchanged

claims.claim: After immunotherapy fails, lifileucel TIL therapy (2024) and the oncolytic virus RP1 with nivolumab (2026) are approved; tebentafusp is the first survival-extending drug in metastatic uveal melanoma.
claims.note: Wikipedia says lifileucel 'was approved for medical use in the United States in February 2024' but says nothing about RP1. Drugs 2026 'First Approval' says vusolimogene oderparepvec 'received its first approval for combination treatment with nivolumab on 6 August 2026 in the USA'. Both dates are right.
claims.fixed: Added the Drugs 2026 first-approval paper and the IGNYTE JCO 2025 paper as links on the melanoma record; text unchanged

claims.claim: Open problems: roughly 40% of advanced patients never respond to immunotherapy, and second-line options after PD-1 failure remain limited;
claims.note: Wikipedia has no non-response figure. CheckMate 067 10-year full text gives an unconfirmed ORR of 58.3% for nivolumab plus ipilimumab and 44.9% for nivolumab. So about 40% do not respond to the doublet and about 55% do not respond to PD-1 alone. 'Roughly 40% never respond to immunotherapy' understates non-response to anti-PD-1 alone.
claims.fixed: Reworded to 'about 40% of advanced patients do not respond even to nivolumab-ipilimumab, and more on PD-1 alone'; the CheckMate 067 10-year link is now on the record

claims.claim: Melanoma causes about 330,000 cases per year, and incidence is rising in fair-skinned populations.
claims.note: Wikipedia: 'from 331,722 worldwide cases in 2022'. GLOBOCAN 2022 world melanoma of skin: 331,722 new cases (repo copy public/globocan/countries.json, GLOBOCAN 2022). The page gave the figure undated as 'per year'.
claims.fixed: Dated: 'In 2022, GLOBOCAN estimated about 330,000 new cases of melanoma worldwide'

claims.claim: 10-year survival ~50% with IO doublet.
claims.note: Wikipedia has no 10-year figure. CheckMate 067 10-year NEJM: '10-year overall survival rates of 43%, 37%, and 19%' and 'Melanoma-specific survival rates at 10-years were 52% with nivolumab-plus-ipilimumab'. The undifferentiated '10-year survival ~50%' blurs melanoma-specific survival (52%) with overall survival (43%).
claims.fixed: Now '10-year melanoma-specific survival ~50% with IO doublet (overall survival 43%)'; the NEJM 2025 link was added to the record

claims.claim: Stage I-II primary: Wide local excision with margins by thickness (1-2 cm); sentinel lymph node biopsy from ~0.8 mm Breslow or with ulceration; nodal ultrasound surveillance rather than completion dissection if positive (MSLT-II).
claims.note: NCCN guideline needs a login, and the guidelines-detail page has no clinical content. MSLT-II (NEJM 2017, on the mslt-ii record) supports surveillance over completion dissection. ESMO 2025 (not cited) agrees on the rest: SLNB is discussed for pT1b, '0.8-1.0 mm or ... <0.8 mm with ulceration', and margins are '1 cm for tumours with a thickness of ≤2 mm and 2 cm for tumours thicker than 2 mm'.

claims.claim: Stage III after surgery (adjuvant): Nivolumab or pembrolizumab for one year; dabrafenib-trametinib for BRAF V600 (COMBI-AD, 10-year RFS 48%); relatlimab adds nothing (RELATIVITY-098).
claims.note: The combi-ad record's source for 10-year RFS 48% is the ASCO 2024 abstract (JCO 42:16_suppl 9500), which returns 403 to scripts. ESMO 2025 describes the >10-year final analysis by HR only (RFS HR 0.52), with no percentage. No other readable copy was found.

claims.claim: Unresectable or metastatic, first line: Nivolumab + ipilimumab (highest long-term survival; ~59% grade 3-4 events) or nivolumab + relatlimab (Opdualag; ~21%) or anti-PD-1 alone; for BRAF-mutant disease, immunotherapy first (DREAMseq) unless rapid control is needed.
claims.note: The 59% grade 3-4 TRAE figure comes from the CheckMate 067 3-year NEJM 2017 abstract ('grade 3 or 4 occurred in 59%'); the 2015 report gave 55.0%. The relatlimab figure is not 21% in either RELATIVITY-047 source: NEJM 2022 has 18.9%, and the 3-year JCO (on the relativity-047 record) has 'Grade 3 or 4 treatment-related AEs (TRAEs) occurred in 22.0%'.
claims.fixed: Changed '~21%' to '~22%' to match the 3-year JCO report; added the NEJM 2017 paper (59%) as a link on the melanoma record

claims.claim: After anti-PD-1 failure: Lifileucel TIL therapy (accelerated approval 2024), RP1 oncolytic virus + nivolumab (2026), ipilimumab-based rechallenge, brenetafusp trials; clinical trials strongly encouraged.
claims.note: FDA approval summary: 'On February 16, 2024, the FDA granted accelerated approval to lifileucel'. Drugs 2026: RP1 'received its first approval for combination treatment with nivolumab on 6 August 2026 in the USA'. Both match the vusolimogene-oderparepvec record's approval text.

claims.claim: Brain metastases: Nivolumab + ipilimumab for asymptomatic disease (~50% intracranial response, CheckMate 204); stereotactic radiosurgery;
claims.note: The row's refs (nivolumab, ipilimumab, sbrt) do not bear on CheckMate 204. CheckMate 204 NEJM 2018: 'the rate of complete response was 26%, the rate of partial response was 30%' (intracranial, 94 asymptomatic patients), an intracranial response of 56%, and 'intracranial clinical benefit was 57%'. '~50%' understated it.
claims.fixed: Added the checkmate-204 trial record to the row's refs; '~50% intracranial response' is now '56% intracranial response'

claims.claim: Primary IO resistance in ~40%.
claims.note: Wikipedia has no figure. CheckMate 067 10-year: unconfirmed ORR 58.3% with the doublet and 44.9% with nivolumab, so ~40% primary non-response holds only for the doublet.
claims.fixed: Now 'Primary IO resistance in ~40% even with the IO doublet.'; the source was added to the record links

claims.claim: Primary resistance: about 40% of advanced patients never respond to PD-1-based therapy, and predictive biomarkers (PD-L1, TMB, interferon signatures) remain too weak to guide choices.
claims.note: Wikipedia has no figure. CheckMate 067 10-year full text gives an unconfirmed ORR of 58.3% for the doublet and 44.9% for nivolumab alone, so 'about 40% never respond to PD-1-based therapy' fits only the doublet; about 55% do not respond to PD-1 alone.
claims.fixed: Reworded to 'about 40% of advanced patients do not respond even to nivolumab-ipilimumab (58% responded in CheckMate 067), and over half do not respond to PD-1 alone'

claims.claim: After PD-1 failure, the approved options (TIL therapy, RP1 with nivolumab) respond in ~30% at best; for the rest melanoma remains life-limiting, and PRAME-directed T-cell engagers are the next attempt.
claims.note: Wikipedia has no response rates. FDA lifileucel review: 'ORR ... was 31.5% (95% CI: 21.1%–43.4%)'. IGNYTE JCO 2025: 'Confirmed ORR ... was 32.9%'. '~30% at best' slightly understates the best figure.
claims.fixed: Now 'about a third at best (31.5% and 32.9% in their registration studies)'; both sources were added to the record links

claims.claim: The commonest cancer worldwide: about 1.2 million non-melanoma skin cancers and 325,000 melanomas recorded in 2020 (GLOBOCAN), with non-melanoma cases badly under-counted because many registries do not record them.
claims.note: GLOBOCAN 2020 fact sheets (Globocan 2020, archived GCO PDFs): NMSC world new cases 1 198 073; melanoma of skin 324 635. The figure is dated 2020 and cites Sung 2021 (GLOBOCAN 2020). Note: GLOBOCAN gives estimates rather than 'recorded' counts, and the 2022 edition the site otherwise uses gives 1,234,533 and 331,722.

claims.claim: For squamous cell carcinoma there are no UK-wide survival statistics; for England, among people diagnosed with their first squamous cell carcinoma between 2014 and 2016, excluding tumours starting in the genitals, 90 out of 100 survived their cancer for 5 years or more.
claims.note: CRUK survival page: 'figures are for men and women diagnosed with their first SCC between 2014 and 2016. They do not include SCC that starts in the genitals ... 90 out of 100 people survive their cancer for 5 years or more'

claims.claim: Against all of that sits a fact that should temper any reassurance: deaths recorded as non-melanoma skin cancer in England have been rising by about 4 percent a year since 2013, roughly twice as fast in men as in women.
claims.note: Mistry 2026 abstract: 'The nonmelanoma skin cancer (NMSC) ASMR increased significantly from 2013 (APC 4.0% ...), with rates rising approximately twice as fast in male individuals (APC 4.4%) compared with female individuals (APC 2.2)'

claims.claim: A 4 mm margin, chosen in 1987 and 1992 by measuring how far tumours actually reach beyond their visible edge, clears more than 95 per cent of basal cell carcinomas under 2 cm and most squamous cell carcinomas, and every alternative that has been randomised against it has lost on cure rate and won on appearance.
claims.note: Wolf and Zitelli 1987: 'a minimum margin of 4 mm was necessary to totally eradicate the tumor in more than 95% of cases' for tumours under 2 cm; Brodland and Zitelli 1992 gives 4 mm for most SCC. But 'every alternative ... won on appearance' is contradicted by the Avril randomised trial (BJC 1997), in which radiotherapy lost on cosmetic result: 'cosmetic results assessed by four of the five judges were significantly better after surgery'.
claims.fixed: Changed the clause to 'has lost on cure rate; the creams and the light won on appearance, but radiotherapy lost on that too'

claims.claim: Mohs micrographic surgery has exactly one randomised trial behind it, in 612 high-risk facial basal cell carcinomas.
claims.note: van Loo EJC 2014: '408 facial, high risk ... primary BCCs and 204 facial recurrent BCCs were randomly allocated' = 612

claims.claim: It is clearly better for tumours that have already recurred and not significantly better for primary ones, and the ten-year report showed that 56 per cent of the primary-tumour recurrences had not yet happened at five years, which is a warning about every five-year paper in this disease.
claims.note: van Loo EJC 2014: 'A substantial proportion of recurrences occurred after more than 5years post-treatment: 56% for pBCC'; rBCC p=0.023 significant, pBCC p=0.100 not

claims.claim: Photodynamic therapy was the treatment of choice for superficial basal cell carcinoma until a 601-patient trial put it last of three, behind imiquimod and fluorouracil, at both one and five years, and found it the most expensive of the three as well.
claims.note: Arits Lancet Oncol 2013: 601 randomised; 1-year tumour-free MAL-PDT 72.8% vs imiquimod 83.4% vs 5-FU 80.1%. Jansen JID 2018, 5 years: 62.7 vs 80.5 vs 70.0. Cost: Arits BJD 2014 (bjd.13066), 'total mean costs for MAL-PDT were €680, for imiquimod cream €526 and for topical fluorouracil cream €388'. That paper is linked from a term in the same file, not from this record.

claims.claim: The NHS says most scars fade but that this can take up to two years or more, and that massage with a water-based cream, keeping the scar covered in the sun for at least a year and SPF 30 or more all help.
claims.note: NHS scars: 'most will fade over time. This can take up to 2 years or more'; massage with a water-based cream; 'keep your scar covered when you're in the sun for at least 1 year'; 'SPF of 30 or more'

claims.claim: In 90 percent of cases the cancer has gone after one or two stages, but you could be in hospital for up to a day, and the leaflet says in its own words that more than one set of injections is often needed and that it can be a long and tiring day.
claims.note: BAD Mohs leaflet: 'In 90% of cases the skin cancer is removed after 1-2 stages'; 'you could be in hospital for up to a day'; 'More than one set of local anaesthetic injections are often needed for Mohs. It can be a long and tiring day.'

claims.claim: What it buys: in the Dutch randomised trial of high-risk facial basal cell carcinoma, ten-year recurrence was 4.4 percent after Mohs against 12.2 percent after excision for primary tumours (not statistically significant) and 3.9 percent against 13.5 percent for recurrent ones (significant).
claims.note: van Loo EJC 2014: pBCC 10-year 4.4% MMS vs 12.2% SE (p=0.100); rBCC 3.9% vs 13.5% (p=0.023)

claims.claim: Cancer Research UK's version for someone who has had one of these cancers is: close-weave cotton clothing, long sleeves and trousers; a wide-brimmed hat that shades the face and neck; sunglasses with 100 percent UV protection; shade between 11am and 3pm in the UK; never a sunbed; and sunscreen of at least SPF 30 with four or five UVA stars, used generously, reapplied regularly, alongside the shade and the clothing rather than instead of them, even on a cloudy day.
claims.note: CRUK skin care page: 'sunglasses that give 100% UV protection apply sunscreen with at least SPF 30 and 4 or 5 stars ... spend time in the shade when the sun is strongest – between 11 am and 3 pm in the UK never use a sunbed'

claims.claim: The first is vitamin D: Cancer Research UK says covering up reduces it, and that the Scientific Advisory Committee on Nutrition recommends a 10 microgram daily supplement between October and March, and all year for people who are mostly indoors or who cover up outdoors, so ask rather than guess.
claims.note: CRUK: SACN 'recommend that during the winter months (between October and March), people in the UK consider taking a daily 10 microgram supplement'; those indoors or covering up should 'consider taking a daily vitamin D supplement throughout the year'

claims.claim: The damage that caused this cancer was done years ago and cannot be undone by anything you do now; what sun protection changes is the chance of the next one, which in a meta-analysis of 17 studies ran at 44 percent within three years of a first basal cell carcinoma.
claims.note: Marcil and Stern 2000: '17 studies ... For BCCs, the 3-year cumulative risk is 44%'

claims.claim: Once you have had one of these cancers, you are being asked to examine your own skin monthly, which means every new mark is now a question rather than a mark; in a study of 160 people after surgery for facial non-melanoma skin cancer, those with recurrent disease had a higher adjusted symptom severity score and poorer psychological quality of life than those treated once.
claims.note: Healthcare 2026: '160 patients after surgery for facial NMSC (63 treated once and 97 with recurrent disease) ... patients with recurrent NMSC had a higher adjusted GSI and lower adjusted psychological health scores'

claims.claim: In the study of 400 patients scored on the disease-specific BaSQoL questionnaire, the mean subscores were 1.20 for the 'other people' domain, 1.01 for diagnosis and treatment, 0.90 for worries, 0.78 for behaviour and 0.40 for appearance; the overall impact was low to moderate and the highest-scoring domain was not the one about how you look.
claims.note: Van Coile Sci Rep 2024: 400 patients; 'Mean BaSQoL subscores were 0.78 ... behaviour, 1.01 ... diagnosis&treatment, 0.90 ... worries, 0.40 ... appearance and 1.20 ... other people, illustrating the low to moderate impact'

claims.claim: The scale, from the joint leaflet of the British Association of Dermatologists and the British Society for Skin Care in Immunosuppressed Individuals: squamous cell carcinoma is 150 times more common in transplant recipients than in the general population and is the commonest skin cancer in this group, basal cell carcinoma is up to 10 times more common, a UK study found one in three people transplanted for more than 10 years had developed a skin cancer, by about 20 years roughly half will have had one, and two in three of those who have had one go on to have several.
claims.note: BAD/BSSCII leaflet: 'SCC is 150 times more common in transplant recipients'; 'BCCs are up to 10 times more common'; 'one in three people with a transplant for more than 10 years had developed a skin cancer. Around twenty years ... about half'; 'Two in three ... multiple skin cancers'

claims.claim: The population studies agree: in 10,476 Swedish recipients the standardised incidence ratio for squamous cell carcinoma was 121 and 198 for heart and lung recipients, and in a prospective study of 615 squamous cell carcinomas immunosuppression was an independent predictor of metastasis with a hazard ratio of 4.32.
claims.note: Krynitz IJC 2013: 10,476 recipients, 'SIR(SCC) 121'; heart and/or lung 'SIR(SCC) 198'. Brantsch Lancet Oncol 2008: 615 patients, 'immunosuppression (4.32 [1.62-11.52])'

claims.claim: Sun protection is stricter: SPF 50 with five UVA stars, daily, all year, to all exposed skin including a balding scalp and the ears, and it applies to people with brown and black skin on immunosuppressants where routine sun protection would otherwise rarely be needed in the UK.
claims.note: BAD/BSSCII leaflet: 'it is recommended to use SPF 50 ... all year round ... a sunscreen with 5 UVA stars ... Use this sunscreen every day to all exposed areas of skin, especially your head (including balding scalp and ears)'

claims.claim: The standard margin is 4 mm, and it is not a convention: for basal cell carcinomas under 2 cm, marking the skin in 2 mm increments before Mohs surgery showed that 4 mm cleared more than 95 per cent of tumours, and the same method in cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma gave 4 mm for ordinary tumours and at least 6 mm for high-risk ones, meaning 2 cm or larger, grade 2 or higher, invading the fat, or in a high-risk site.
claims.note: Wolf and Zitelli 1987: 'For tumors with a diameter less than 2 cm, a minimum margin of 4 mm ... more than 95% of cases'. Brodland and Zitelli 1992: 'Four millimeter margins were adequate for most' and high-risk features 'size of 2 cm or larger, histologic grade 2 or higher, invasion of the subcutaneous tissue, and location in high-risk areas ... at least a 6 mm margin'

claims.claim: Two practical corrections matter: a specimen shrinks between the skin and the pathologist's ruler, by 70 to 80 per cent of the measured width in one series, and dermoscopy moves the visible edge outwards in about one tumour in six.
claims.note: Shrinkage is sourced: J Surg Oncol 2026 reports 'reductions of the order of 70%-80% overall in the measured specimen margin widths'. Dermoscopy 'moves the visible edge outwards in about one tumour in six' has no source on the row, its refs or anywhere in the corpus, and a Europe PMC search found no paper reporting 16.8%.
claims.fixed: Removed the dermoscopy clause; the sentence now reads 'One practical correction matters: a specimen shrinks ...'

claims.claim: It happens in roughly 3 to 15 per cent of excisions depending on the site and the series, most often on the nose, in infiltrative, morphoeic, micronodular and superficial multifocal subtypes, and where invasion goes below the dermis.
claims.note: The row's source (Dermatol Surg 2015) reports 'Twenty-three lesions (14.9%) ... revealed positive surgical margins' and supports the upper bound. Nothing cited gives the lower bound of ~3% (the term record says 2.6%).
claims.fixed: Now 'in up to about 15 per cent of excisions depending on the site and the series (14.9 per cent in one series of facial basal cell carcinomas)'

claims.claim: The evidence is one randomised trial, in 612 high-risk facial basal cell carcinomas in the Netherlands.
claims.note: van Loo EJC 2014: 408 primary + 204 recurrent facial BCC randomised in the Netherlands = 612

claims.claim: For tumours that had already recurred it is clearly better: ten-year recurrence 3.9 against 13.5 per cent (p=0.023).
claims.note: van Loo EJC 2014: 'cumulative 10-year recurrence probabilities were 3.9% and 13.5% for MMS and SE ... p=0.023'

claims.claim: For tumours being treated for the first time the difference never reached significance, 4.4 against 12.2 per cent at ten years (p=0.100), and at five years it was 2.5 against 4.1 per cent.
claims.note: EJC 2014: primary '4.4% after MMS and 12.2% after SE (... p=0.100)'. Lancet Oncol 2008: 5-year 'seven (4.1%) ... surgical excision and four (2.5%) ... MMS'

claims.claim: The finding that should change practice is that 56 per cent of the primary-tumour recurrences happened after year five, which is why the five-year papers in this disease understate the problem.
claims.note: EJC 2014: 'recurrences occurred after more than 5years post-treatment: 56% for pBCC'

claims.claim: Mohs surgery cost 1,248 euros against 990 for ordinary excision.
claims.note: Lancet Oncol 2008: 'For pBCC, total treatment costs were euro1248 for MMS and euro990 for surgical excision' (primary tumours; recurrent tumours were euro1284 vs euro1043)

claims.claim: The Danish Skin Cancer Registry followed 47,358 tumours treated this way in office dermatology and found five-year recurrence of 9.9 per cent and eight-year recurrence of 13.3 per cent, dominated by selection: 25.1 per cent at eight years for head and neck tumours, 16.7 per cent for tumours over 10 mm and 8.4 per cent for superficial ones.
claims.note: Acta Derm Venereol 2026: 47,358 BCC; '5-year recurrence rate was 9.9% ... 13.3% ... at 8 years. Head and neck tumours ... 25.1% ... tumours >10 mm (16.7% ...) superficial ... 8.4%'

claims.claim: Used on aggressive histological subtypes it fails, with 27 per cent recurrence at a median 6.5 years in one series of 37 tumours, which is an argument for a biopsy first in anything not obviously superficial.
claims.note: Dermatol Surg 2013: '37 primary aggressive BCCs, 10 recurred ... 27% recurrence rate ... with median 6.5 years follow-up'

claims.claim: It is second and not first because of the only randomised comparison ever run, in 347 patients with facial basal cell carcinoma, where the four-year failure rate was 0.7 per cent after surgery against 7.5 per cent after radiotherapy (p=0.003) and the cosmetic result was better after surgery on four of five independent judgements.
claims.note: Avril BJC 1997: 347 patients; '4-year actuarial failure rate ... 0.7% ... compared with 7.5% ... (log-rank P = 0.003). The cosmetic results assessed by four of the five judges were significantly better after surgery'

claims.claim: Melanoma is treated by a different logic: the margin is set by the thickness of the tumour rather than by a fixed 4 mm, the lymph nodes are staged with a sentinel node biopsy, and advanced disease is treated with checkpoint immunotherapy or with BRAF and MEK inhibitors.
claims.note: The only figure is the fixed 4 mm keratinocyte margin, confirmed by Wolf and Zitelli 1987. Thickness-based melanoma margins match ESMO 2025 ('0.5 cm for in situ ... 1 cm ... ≤2 mm and 2 cm ... >2 mm'). The NCCN page itself is login-only.

claims.claim: Stage 0 is Tis, I is T1N0, II is T2N0, III is T3N0 or N1, IV is anything beyond
claims.note: RCPath TNM9 appendix (basal-cell-tnm9) stage table: 'Stage 0 Tis N0 M0; Stage I T1 N0 M0; Stage II T2 N0 M0; Stage III T3 N0 M0 / T1, T2, T3 N1 M0; Stage IV ... N2, N3 / T4 / M1'

claims.claim: UK registries long recorded only the first basal cell carcinoma and the first squamous cell carcinoma in a person's lifetime; counting one of each per person per year instead finds 67 percent more basal cell carcinomas and 42 percent more squamous cell carcinomas, and still misses about 14 basal cell carcinomas per 100 patients.
claims.note: Mistry 2026: 'the PPPA approach identified 67% more BCCs and 42% more cSCCs'. Kwiatkowska 2021 full text: '1st PPPA method indicates an underestimation of approximately 14 BCC tumours per 100 patients'

claims.claim: Basal cell carcinoma rates in England stabilised after 2015, but squamous cell carcinoma rates went on rising, and non-melanoma skin cancer mortality rose about 4 percent a year from 2013, twice as fast in men.
claims.note: Mistry 2026: 'BCC EASRs increased initially before stabilizing from 2015'; cSCC continued to increase; 'NMSC ASMR increased significantly from 2013 (APC 4.0%)', men 4.4% vs women 2.2%

claims.claim: Incidence rates in England are 26 to 27 times higher for basal cell carcinoma and 13 to 14 times higher for squamous cell carcinoma in the White ethnic group than in the Asian or Black groups, ethnicity is unknown for 19.2 percent of registered basal cell carcinomas, and acral melanoma, which is commonest in the Black ethnic group, is less likely to be referred on the urgent suspected cancer pathway and more likely to present late (Ahmed 2026).
claims.note: Ahmed BJD 2026: BCC '26 times ... than in the Asian group ... 27 times ... Black'; cSCC '14 times ... Asian ... 13 times ... Black'; 'Unknown ethnicity ... 19.2% for BCC'; ALM EASR highest in Black group, 'less likely to be referred along the Urgent Suspected Cancer pathway and ... more likely to present at a later stage'

claims.claim: The commonest cancer operation on earth rests on two observational margin studies from 1987 and 1992 and one randomised trial of Mohs surgery from the Netherlands.
claims.note: Margin studies are 1987 (Arch Dermatol, prospective series of 117) and 1992 (JAAD, prospective series); van Loo is the single Dutch Mohs RCT

claims.claim: In the only long trial, 56 per cent of the recurrences after primary tumour treatment happened after year five, which means every five-year cure rate quoted for a cream, for light or for curettage is an overestimate of unknown size.
claims.note: EJC 2014: '56% for pBCC' of recurrences after more than 5 years

claims.claim: Its evidence is a Danish registry of 47,358 tumours, which cannot separate the treatment from the choice of tumour.
claims.note: Acta Derm Venereol 2026: Danish Skin Cancer Registry, 47,358 BCCs treated with C±E

claims.claim: Photographic and observer scales differ between trials, patient and doctor ratings disagree by 20 to 40 percentage points in the same cohort, and no trial has asked what trade in cure rate a person would actually accept.
claims.note: No source on the record or in the corpus gives a 20-40 percentage-point gap between patient and doctor ratings. Avril BJC 1997 gives only patient ratings in the abstract (87% vs 69% good). Cochrane (CD003412.pub3) says observers favoured imiquimod while patients rated it the same as surgery, which supports disagreement but not the range.
claims.fixed: Removed the figure; now 'patient and observer ratings of the same result can disagree'

claims.claim: Basal cell carcinoma arises from hedgehog-pathway activation in nearly every case, through loss of PTCH1 (~70%) or activating SMO mutations (~10-20%); germline PTCH1 loss causes Gorlin (basal cell nevus) syndrome.
claims.note: No source on the record gives the PTCH1 or SMO frequencies (NCCN is login-only; ERIVANCE says only 'almost all basal-cell carcinomas contain genetic alterations in the hedgehog signaling pathway'). Bonilla, Nature Genetics 2016, 293 BCCs: 'PTCH1, 73% or SMO, 20% ... and SUFU, 8%'. So ~70% PTCH1 is right, and SMO is ~20% rather than 10-20%.
claims.fixed: Added Bonilla 2016 as a link on the BCC record; changed SMO '~10-20%' to '~20%'

claims.claim: Vismodegib (ERIVANCE, 2012) and sonidegib (BOLT, 2015) are oral SMO inhibitors for locally advanced or metastatic BCC with ~45-60% response; their class toxicities (muscle spasms, dysgeusia, alopecia, weight loss) cause many to stop, and resistance arises through SMO mutations.
claims.note: ERIVANCE NEJM 2012 (cited on the record): 'In 33 patients with metastatic basal-cell carcinoma, the independently assessed response rate was 30% ... In 63 patients with locally advanced ... 43%'. '~45-60%' overstated the pivotal independently assessed rates; 58% was the phase 1 figure. ERIVANCE 2012 and BOLT 2015 are right.
claims.fixed: Replaced '~45-60% response' with 'in ERIVANCE, independently assessed response in 43% of locally advanced and 30% of metastatic disease'

claims.claim: The most common human cancer: several million cases per year in the US alone; metastasis is exceptionally rare (<0.1%), but locally advanced disease can be destructive.
claims.note: ERIVANCE full text (the record's source): 'more than 2.1 million new patients were treated for nonmelanoma skin cancer in 2006 in the United States; approximately 80% of nonmelanoma skin cancers are basal-cell carcinomas'. That is about 1.7 million, not 'several million'. No cited source gives the '<0.1%' metastasis figure; PDQ says only that BCC 'rarely spreads'.
claims.fixed: Now 'in the US more than 2.1 million people were treated for non-melanoma skin cancer in 2006, about 80% of them for basal cell carcinoma'; removed the '<0.1%' figure and kept 'metastasis is exceptionally rare'

claims.claim: Three-year net survival in the English registry study was reported as 101.9 percent, a figure above 100 percent because net survival compares people with the cancer against the general population and people who present with a basal cell carcinoma are, as a group, alive and attending a clinic.
claims.note: Venables 2019 full text: 'Three-year net survival was 101·9% [95% CI 101·8–102·0] for BCC'

claims.claim: Low-risk: Standard excision with 4 mm margin, curettage and electrodesiccation, or topical imiquimod / 5-FU / photodynamic therapy for superficial lesions.
claims.note: The row cites NCCN Basal Cell Skin Cancer (login-only) and the fluorouracil record. The 4 mm margin matches Wolf and Zitelli 1987 ('a minimum margin of 4 mm ... more than 95%'), which the row does not cite.

claims.claim: Surgery has the highest cure rate: the Cochrane review of 52 randomised trials and 6,690 participants concluded that surgical interventions have the lowest recurrence rates.
claims.note: Cochrane CD003412.pub3: 'We included 52 RCTs ... involving 6690 participants ... Overall, surgical interventions have the lowest recurrence rates.'

claims.claim: In the UK SINS trial, 501 people with primary nodular or superficial disease at low-risk sites were randomised between imiquimod cream (once daily, six weeks for superficial and twelve for nodular) and excision with a 4 mm margin: treatment succeeded in 83.6 percent against 98.4 percent at three years and 82.5 percent against 97.7 percent at five, and most cream failures happened in the first year.
claims.note: SINS Lancet Oncol 2014: 501 randomised; 'imiquimod 5% cream once daily for 6 weeks (superficial) or 12 weeks (nodular), or surgical excision with a 4 mm margin'. JID 2017: '82.5% ... compared with 97.7%' at 5 years; 3-year '83.6% ... and 98.4%'; 'Most imiquimod treatment failures occurred in year 1'

claims.claim: Among the non-surgical options, a Dutch trial of 601 people with superficial disease gives the ranking at five years: imiquimod 80.5 percent tumour-free, fluorouracil cream 70.0 percent, photodynamic therapy 62.7 percent.
claims.note: Jansen JID 2018: 601 patients; 5-year tumour-free '62.7% for MAL-PDT ... 80.5% for imiquimod ... 70.0% for 5-fluorouracil'

claims.claim: Creams take weeks of a visibly inflamed, itching, weeping face (in SINS, itching in 211 of the imiquimod group against 129 of the surgery group); photodynamic therapy causes moderate to severe pain and burning during the treatment itself; and the cosmetic result of the non-surgical options is better, not worse.
claims.note: SINS Lancet Oncol 2014: 'itching (211 patients in the imiquimod group vs 129 in the surgery group)'. Arits 2013: 'For patients treated with MAL-PDT, moderate to severe pain and burning sensation were reported most often during the actual MAL-PDT session'

claims.claim: The Cochrane review found observers rated the outcome good or excellent in 60.6 percent after imiquimod against 35.6 percent after excision, and after photodynamic therapy against excision 87.1 percent against 46.6 percent, while patients rated imiquimod and surgery the same.
claims.note: Cochrane: observer-rated good/excellent imiquimod vs SE '60.6% versus 35.6%'; MAL-PDT vs SE observer-rated '87.1% versus 46.6%'; participant-rated imiquimod vs SE 'RR 1.00'

claims.claim: In the Dutch randomised trial of high-risk facial basal cell carcinoma, ten-year recurrence was 4.4 percent after Mohs and 12.2 percent after standard excision for primary tumours, and 3.9 against 13.5 percent for recurrent ones; the same trial found that 56 percent of the recurrences of primary tumours appeared more than five years after treatment, which is why a clear five years is reassuring but is not the end of the story for a high-risk lesion on the face.
claims.note: van Loo EJC 2014: primary 4.4% MMS vs 12.2% SE; recurrent 3.9% vs 13.5%; '56% for pBCC' recurred after more than 5 years

claims.claim: In a meta-analysis of 17 studies, the three-year cumulative risk of a further basal cell carcinoma after a first was 44 percent, at least ten times the rate of first tumours in a comparable population, while the risk of a squamous cell carcinoma after a basal cell carcinoma was 6 percent.
claims.note: Marcil and Stern 2000: 17 studies; 'For BCCs, the 3-year cumulative risk is 44%, also at least a 10-fold increase ... the risk of developing an SCC in patients with a prior BCC is low (6%)'

claims.claim: In 601 Dutch patients with superficial basal cell carcinoma, five-year tumour-free survival was 80.5 per cent with imiquimod cream, 70.0 per cent with fluorouracil cream and 62.7 per cent with methyl aminolevulinate photodynamic therapy; imiquimod beat photodynamic therapy with a hazard ratio for failure of 0.48 and fluorouracil with 0.65.
claims.note: Jansen JID 2018: 80.5 / 70.0 / 62.7%; imiquimod vs MAL-PDT HR for failure 0.48; imiquimod vs 5-FU HR 0.65

claims.claim: Against surgery all of them lose: SINS randomised 501 people in the United Kingdom and found clinical success at five years of 82.5 per cent with imiquimod against 97.7 per cent with excision, a relative risk of 0.84 whose confidence interval fell below the non-inferiority margin, so imiquimod is inferior rather than unproven.
claims.note: SINS JID 2017: 'Five-year success rates for imiquimod were 82.5% ... compared with 97.7% ... (relative risk ... 0.84, 95% CI 0.77-0.91)'. The prespecified non-inferiority margin was RR 0.87 (Lancet Oncol 2014), so the CI lies below it.

claims.claim: Cryotherapy matched photodynamic therapy on five-year recurrence, 20 against 22 per cent, and lost badly on appearance, 16 against 60 per cent excellent.
claims.note: Basset-Seguin EJD 2008: 'no difference in 5-year recurrence rates ... (20% with cryotherapy vs. 22% with MAL PDT ...). However, more patients had an excellent cosmetic outcome with MAL PDT (60% vs. 16% with cryotherapy)'

claims.claim: Methyl aminolevulinate photodynamic therapy against excision gave five-year recurrence of 14 against 4 per cent and a sustained complete response of 76 against 96 per cent, with an excellent or good cosmetic outcome in 87 against 54 per cent.
claims.note: Rhodes Arch Dermatol 2007: 5-year recurrence '7 (14%) ... vs 2 (4%)'; sustained CR '76% ... and 96%'; excellent or good cosmetic outcome '27 (87%) ... vs 19 (54%)'

claims.claim: Scraping the tumour off first and then applying imiquimod, tested in the SCIN trial, gave freedom from treatment failure at five years of 77.8 against 98.2 per cent, a relative risk of failure of 15.93.
claims.note: SCIN JAMA Dermatol 2025: '5-year probability of remaining free from treatment failure was 77.8% ... after SC plus imiquimod and 98.2% ... after SE. The relative risk of treatment failure was 15.93'

claims.claim: VISMONEO gave vismodegib for a mean of 6.0 months to 55 patients with a mean lesion size of 47.3 mm and downstaged the planned surgery in 44 of them (80 per cent, 67 to 90), with 27 complete responses of which 25 were proved on biopsy.
claims.note: VISMONEO EClinicalMedicine 2021: 55 patients; 'Mean size of target lesion was 47.3 mm'; '44 patients presented with downstaging ... (80%; 95% CI, 67 to 90). Of these 44 patients, 27 had a complete response (25 proved by biopsy). Mean treatment duration was 6.0 months.'

claims.claim: The part usually left out belongs in the conversation: at three years 16 of those 44 patients had a known recurrence, 36 per cent.
claims.note: VISMONEO: 'At 3-years of follow-up, 16/44 patients had known recurrence (36%'

claims.claim: STEVIE gave vismodegib to 1,215 patients in ordinary practice: response was 68.5 per cent in locally advanced disease, 98 per cent had a treatment-emergent adverse event, 23.8 per cent had a serious one, and the median treatment duration was 8.6 months, with only 12 per cent still taking it at the analysis.
claims.note: STEVIE EJC 2017: N = 1215; 'Response rates (investigator-assessed) ... 68.5% ... in patients with locally advanced BCC'; '98% had ≥1 TEAE'; 'Serious TEAEs occurred in ... 23.8%'; 'Median ... treatment duration was 8.6 ... months'; '147 patients (12%) remained on study'

claims.claim: In 84 patients with locally advanced disease who had progressed on, could not tolerate, or had no better than stable disease after nine months of a hedgehog inhibitor, objective response by independent central review was 31 per cent (21 to 42) with five complete responses; grade 3 or 4 treatment-emergent adverse events occurred in 48 per cent and serious events in 35 per cent.
claims.note: Stratigos Lancet Oncol 2021: 84 patients; 'objective response ... 26 (31%; 95% CI 21-42)'; 'five (6%) patients with a complete response'; 'Grade 3-4 treatment-emergent adverse events occurred in 40 (48%)'; 'Serious ... 29 (35%)'

claims.claim: NICE technology appraisal TA489 recommendation 1.1 does not recommend vismodegib within its marketing authorisation for metastatic basal cell carcinoma or for locally advanced disease unsuitable for surgery or radiotherapy: the committee found the comparison with best supportive care not good enough for decision-making and the cost per quality-adjusted life year much higher than 30,000 pounds.
claims.note: NICE TA489 1.1: 'Vismodegib is not recommended within its marketing authorisation for treating symptomatic metastatic basal cell carcinoma, or locally advanced basal cell carcinoma that is inappropriate for surgery or radiotherapy'; 'methods used are not good enough for decision-making'; 'much higher than £30,000 per quality-adjusted life year'

claims.claim: Recommendation 1.2 allows anyone already on it to continue.
claims.note: TA489 1.2: 'This recommendation is not intended to affect treatment with vismodegib that was started in the NHS before this guidance was published ... may continue' (applies to those already on it when the guidance was published in November 2017)

claims.claim: The registration rule recorded only the first basal cell carcinoma per person for two decades, the annual method that replaced it finds 67 percent more, and that method still misses about 14 tumours per 100 patients.
claims.note: Mistry 2026: PPPA 'identified 67% more BCCs'. Kwiatkowska 2021: 'underestimation of approximately 14 BCC tumours per 100 patients'. The lifetime-first rule dates from 1999 (UKIACR, quoted in Venables 2019) and was replaced by PPPA counting from 2013 data onwards, roughly two decades.

claims.claim: The UK dataset records that there is no consensus on whether it is in situ or invasive, no consensus on its exact definition, and that studies quote various thicknesses, all under 1 mm; that is why the dataset deliberately avoids the phrase invasive basal cell carcinoma in its own title.
claims.note: RCPath G123: 'There is no consensus as to whether superficial basal cell carcinoma represents in situ or invasive carcinoma. For that reason, the term ‘invasive basal cell carcinoma’ is specifically not used in the title ... no consensus as to the exact definition ... All studies, however, have suggested figures of less than 1 mm.'

claims.claim: Hedgehog inhibitors are stopped by most people who start them, with a median treatment duration of 8.6 months in the largest study, and neither intermittent dosing nor topical delivery has yet produced a licensed alternative.
claims.note: STEVIE EJC 2017 (the stevie trial record on this page): 'Median (range) treatment duration was 8.6 (0-44) months'; '147 patients (12%) remained on study'

claims.claim: Ovarian cancer is a group of diseases (~320,000 new cases a year) dominated by high-grade serous carcinoma, which arises in the fallopian tube, is almost always TP53-mutant, and is diagnosed at stage III-IV in three-quarters of women because there is no symptom or screening test that catches it early.
claims.note: GLOBOCAN 2022 world ovary: 324,603 new cases (repo copy public/globocan/countries.json; Bray 2024). The cited Wikipedia gives '313,000 women' in 2020. The page presented '~320,000 new cases a year' undated. 'Three-quarters at stage III-IV' matches Wikipedia ('around 75% of patients are diagnosed as having an advanced stage').
claims.fixed: Dated: 'about 325,000 new cases worldwide in 2022, GLOBOCAN'; added a GLOBOCAN 2022 (Bray 2024) link to the ovarian record

claims.claim: Roughly half of high-grade serous tumours have homologous recombination deficiency, including ~20% with germline or somatic BRCA1/2 mutations.
claims.note: Wikipedia: 'In 50% of high-grade serous cancers, homologous recombination DNA repair is dysfunctional'; 'About 15–20% of high grade serous carcinoma have germline BRCA1 and BRCA2 mutations', so ~20% germline or somatic is a fair floor

claims.claim: The standard of care is maximal cytoreductive surgery (primary or interval, after neoadjuvant carboplatin-paclitaxel), sometimes with HIPEC, followed by maintenance therapy chosen by biomarker: olaparib for BRCA-mutated disease (SOLO-1, 7-year OS 67% vs 47%), olaparib plus bevacizumab for HRD-positive disease (PAOLA-1), niraparib for the rest with declining enthusiasm after PRIMA showed no survival gain.
claims.note: SOLO-1 7-year JCO 2023 (on the solo-1 record): 'At 7 years, 67.0% of olaparib patients versus 46.5% of placebo patients were alive'. But no source on the record or the prima trial record (NEJM 2019 PFS paper only) covers PRIMA 'showed no survival gain'. The PRIMA final OS paper (Annals 2024) states 'OS hazard ratio was 1.01 [95% CI 0.84-1.23; P = 0.8834]', so the claim is right.
claims.fixed: Added the PRIMA final OS paper (and SOLO-1 7-year paper) as links on the ovarian record; text unchanged

claims.claim: Platinum-resistant disease, historically the hardest setting, now has three new options with survival benefit: mirvetuximab soravtansine for FRα-high tumours (MIRASOL), relacorilant plus nab-paclitaxel (ROSELLA, approved 2026), and pembrolizumab plus weekly paclitaxel for PD-L1-positive tumours (KEYNOTE-B96, approved February 2026, the first immunotherapy in ovarian cancer).
claims.note: MIRASOL NEJM 2023: OS 'median, 16.46 months vs. 12.75 months; hazard ratio for death, 0.67'. ROSELLA Lancet 2026: 'statistically and clinically significant improvement in overall survival (hazard ratio for death 0·65'; Lifyorli label 'Initial U.S. Approval: 2026'. ASCO Post: 'On February 10, the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved ... pembrolizumab ... with paclitaxel' for PD-L1 CPS ≥ 1, OS HR 0.76.

claims.claim: Ovarian cancer accounts for ~320,000 cases per year worldwide.
claims.note: GLOBOCAN 2022 world ovary 324,603 new cases; presented undated as '~320,000 cases per year' (Wikipedia gives 313,000 for 2020)
claims.fixed: Dated: 'In 2022, GLOBOCAN estimated about 325,000 new cases of ovarian cancer worldwide.'

claims.claim: Because most cases are found at stage III-IV, it remains the gynaecologic cancer with the lowest survival: 5-year survival ~50% overall and under 30% for stage IV; ~200,000 deaths per year.
claims.note: '5-year survival ~50%' matches Wikipedia ('overall five-year survival rate in the United States is 52%') and SEER (52.0%). No source on the record gives 'under 30% for stage IV'; the record's SEER source gives 31.5% for distant-stage disease. '~200,000 deaths per year' is an undated GLOBOCAN figure (2022: 206,956), and Wikipedia's figure is '150,000 will die'.
claims.fixed: Now 'about 32% once it has spread to distant sites (US SEER data); GLOBOCAN estimated about 207,000 deaths in 2022'

claims.claim: PARP maintenance with 7-year OS benefit in BRCA (SOLO-1).
claims.note: SOLO-1 7-year JCO 2023: 'The hazard ratio for OS was 0.55 ... P = .0004 [P < .0001 required to declare statistical significance]. At 7 years, 67.0% ... versus 46.5%'. The OS gain is clinically meaningful but was a descriptive analysis that did not meet its prespecified significance threshold, so 'OS benefit' overstates it.
claims.fixed: Now 'PARP maintenance in BRCA (SOLO-1): 67% alive at 7 years against 47%, a clinically meaningful gain that missed its strict significance threshold.'; the JCO link was added to the record

claims.claim: Biomarker-directed maintenance after first-line chemotherapy: olaparib for BRCA (7-year OS 67% vs 47%), olaparib + bevacizumab for HRD-positive disease.
claims.note: SOLO-1 JCO 2023 (solo-1 record): 67.0% vs 46.5% alive at 7 years

claims.claim: Three new options with overall survival benefit in platinum-resistant disease within three years: mirvetuximab (FRα-high), relacorilant + nab-paclitaxel, and pembrolizumab + paclitaxel (PD-L1-positive, first immunotherapy approval in ovarian cancer, February 2026).
claims.note: MIRASOL (NEJM 2023) OS HR 0.67; ROSELLA (Lancet 2026) OS HR 0.65; KEYNOTE-B96 OS HR 0.76, FDA approval 10 February 2026 (ASCO Post). All three came within 2023-26.

claims.claim: First treatment designed for low-grade serous carcinoma (avutometinib + defactinib, May 2025).
claims.note: MSK news, Monday, May 12, 2025: 'The first drug for a rare and difficult-to-treat type of ovarian cancer has been granted accelerated approval by the Food and Drug Administration' (avutometinib plus defactinib, LGSOC)

claims.claim: Surgery is evidence-based at both ends: HIPEC at interval debulking adds ~12 months of survival; selected secondary cytoreduction at relapse adds ~8 months.
claims.note: OVHIPEC-1 NEJM 2018: median OS '33.9 months in the surgery group and 45.7 months in the surgery-plus-HIPEC group' (+11.8). DESKTOP III NEJM 2021: '53.7 months in the surgery group and 46.0 months' (+7.7).

claims.claim: Prevention and risk: Germline testing for all patients; risk-reducing salpingo-oophorectomy for BRCA carriers (age 35-45); opportunistic salpingectomy at pelvic surgery for average-risk women; oral contraceptives reduce risk.
claims.note: The age range 35-45 rests on the NCCN guideline link (login-only); the risk-reducing-salpingectomy record cites only Wikipedia 'Salpingectomy', which gives no age

claims.claim: Newly diagnosed stage III-IV: surgery and chemotherapy: Primary debulking if complete resection is feasible, else 3 cycles neoadjuvant carboplatin-paclitaxel then interval debulking (with HIPEC in stage III, OVHIPEC-1) and 3 more cycles; add bevacizumab for high-risk or residual disease.
claims.note: OVHIPEC-1 NEJM 2018: 'stage III ... at least stable disease after three cycles of carboplatin ... and paclitaxel ... interval cytoreductive surgery either with or without HIPEC'; three further cycles followed

claims.claim: First-line maintenance, BRCA-mutated: Olaparib 2 years (SOLO-1) or olaparib + bevacizumab (PAOLA-1) or niraparib 3 years (PRIMA).
claims.note: SOLO-1: olaparib 'for up to 2 years' (JCO 2023). PRIMA final OS (Annals 2024, now on the record): 'planned duration of study treatment of 3 years'

claims.claim: Platinum-sensitive relapse (interval >6 months): Secondary cytoreduction if AGO-score positive (DESKTOP III); platinum doublet (carboplatin with PLD, paclitaxel, or gemcitabine) ± bevacizumab;
claims.note: DESKTOP III NEJM 2021: 'first relapse after a platinum-free interval ... of 6 months or more' and a positive AGO score

claims.claim: Platinum-resistant relapse, PD-L1 CPS ≥1: Pembrolizumab + weekly paclitaxel ± bevacizumab (KEYNOTE-B96, approved Feb 2026).
claims.note: ASCO Post: FDA approval on February 10 (2026) of pembrolizumab with paclitaxel with or without bevacizumab for tumours with 'PD-L1 (combined positive score [CPS] ≥ 1)'

claims.claim: Platinum-resistant relapse, other: Relacorilant + nab-paclitaxel (ROSELLA, approved 2026); single-agent weekly paclitaxel, PLD, or topotecan ± bevacizumab (AURELIA); clinical trials of FRα and CDH6 ADCs.
claims.note: Lifyorli (relacorilant) DailyMed label: 'Initial U.S. Approval: 2026'

claims.claim: Low-grade serous carcinoma: Surgery; endocrine maintenance (letrozole) after chemotherapy or instead of it; at recurrence, avutometinib + defactinib if KRAS-mutated (2025), trametinib, or endocrine therapy.
claims.note: MSK, May 12, 2025: avutometinib plus defactinib accelerated approval for recurrent KRAS-mutated low-grade serous ovarian cancer

claims.claim: Rare histologies: Clear-cell: platinum-based therapy, trials of immunotherapy and ARID1A-directed agents; mucinous: consider GI regimens and HER2 testing; germ-cell: BEP chemotherapy with >90% cure.
claims.note: The row's refs (platinum, checkpoint-inhibitor) carry no germ-cell cure rate. The record's Wikipedia gives only subtype-specific figures (e.g. dysgerminoma stage I survival), not '>90% cure' for germ-cell tumours given BEP.
claims.fixed: Replaced '>90% cure' with 'with high cure rates'

claims.claim: Platinum-resistant disease is the hardest setting; three drugs with survival benefit arrived in 2023-26 and each adds months, so combining and sequencing them is the next step.
claims.note: MIRASOL NEJM 2023 (OS 16.46 vs 12.75 months), ROSELLA Lancet 2026 (median OS +4.1 months), KEYNOTE-B96 (OS 18.2 vs 14.0 months): three drugs with survival benefit in 2023-26, each adding months

claims.claim: Cervical cancer is almost entirely caused by persistent infection with high-risk human papillomavirus, which makes it the one common cancer that could be eliminated: HPV vaccination prevents about 90% of cases, HPV screening finds the precancers that remain, and a minute of thermal ablation or a loop excision cures them.
claims.note: Wikipedia: 'HPV vaccines ... may prevent up to 90% of cervical cancers'. The page said vaccination 'prevents about 90% of cases', which turns an upper bound into a typical figure.
claims.fixed: Now 'HPV vaccination can prevent up to 90% of cases'

claims.claim: Around 660,000 women are diagnosed and 350,000 die each year, nine in ten of them in low- and middle-income countries where vaccination and screening have not reached.
claims.note: Wikipedia: 'over 660,000 new cases and around 350,000 deaths in 2022'; GLOBOCAN 2022 world cervix uteri 662,301 cases and 348,874 deaths (repo copy). The page presented these undated as 'each year'.
claims.fixed: Dated: 'In 2022, GLOBOCAN estimated that about 660,000 women were diagnosed and 350,000 died'

claims.claim: In Sweden, Scotland, and Australia, cohorts vaccinated at 12-13 show near-zero invasive cancer, and Australia expects to pass the WHO elimination threshold (4 per 100,000) around 2035.
claims.note: Wikipedia, the only record source, says nothing about Sweden, Scotland or Australia. Primary sources: Palmer JNCI 2024, 'No cases of invasive cancer were recorded in women immunized at 12 or 13 years of age'. Lei NEJM 2020 (Sweden), IRR 0.12 for vaccination before 17, an ~88% reduction rather than near zero. Hall Lancet Public Health 2019 projects Australia below 4 per 100,000 'by 2028 (2021-35)', not 'around 2035'.
claims.fixed: Rewrote to the three sources (Scotland none at 12-13; Sweden ~88% lower if vaccinated before 17; Australia projected below 4/100,000 by about 2028, range 2021-2035) and added all three as links on the cervical record

claims.claim: Locally advanced disease is cured in roughly two-thirds by cisplatin chemoradiation with brachytherapy, and two 2023-24 trials improved on that standard for the first time since 1999: six weeks of induction carboplatin-paclitaxel (INTERLACE, 5-year OS 80% vs 72%) and pembrolizumab with chemoradiation (KEYNOTE-A18, 36-month OS 82.6% vs 74.8%).
claims.note: INTERLACE Lancet 2024: '5-year overall survival rates were 80% ... and 72%'. KEYNOTE-A18 Lancet 2024: '36-month overall survival was 82·6% ... and 74·8%'. The chemoradiation control arms (72% 5-year OS, 64% PFS) support 'roughly two-thirds'. Both trial records on the page carry these papers.

claims.claim: It still causes ~660,000 cases and ~350,000 deaths per year, nine in ten in low- and middle-income countries; it is the fourth most common cancer in women worldwide and the leading cause of cancer death among women in many sub-Saharan African countries.
claims.note: Wikipedia: 'fourth-most common type of cancer ... in women, with over 660,000 new cases and around 350,000 deaths in 2022', 'Almost 90% of cases and deaths occur in low- and middle-income'. The page said 'per year' without the year.
claims.fixed: Dated: 'In 2022, GLOBOCAN estimated ~660,000 cases and ~350,000 deaths'

claims.claim: Vaccinated cohorts in Sweden and Scotland show a ~90% to near-total reduction in invasive cervical cancer; single-dose schedules (97.5% efficacy in KEN SHE) make global coverage achievable.
claims.note: KEN SHE (NEJM Evidence 2022): 'Nonavalent vaccine efficacy (VE) was 97.5%' against incident persistent HPV16/18 infection, not against cancer. In a sentence about invasive cancer the bare '97.5% efficacy' reads as cancer prevention. Sweden ~88% (Lei 2020) and Scotland zero (Palmer 2024) support '~90% to near-total'.
claims.fixed: Labelled it '97.5% efficacy against persistent HPV16/18 infection in KEN SHE'; added the Sweden and Scotland sources to the record

claims.claim: Two curative-intent advances in one year after 24 years of stasis: induction chemotherapy (INTERLACE, OS HR 0.60) and pembrolizumab with chemoradiation (KEYNOTE-A18, OS HR 0.67).
claims.note: INTERLACE Lancet 2024: OS 'HR of 0·60 (95% CI 0·40-0·91)'. KEYNOTE-A18 OS Lancet 2024: 'hazard ratio for death was 0·67'. Both 2023-24, 24 years after the 1999 chemoradiation alert.

claims.claim: First-line chemo-immunotherapy roughly doubles median survival in metastatic disease compared with the pre-2014 era (KEYNOTE-826 26.4 months;
claims.note: KEYNOTE-826 final OS JCO 2023: 'all-comer ... 26.4 months versus 16.8 months'. Nothing on the page gave the pre-2014 comparator. GOG-240 (Tewari NEJM 2014) chemotherapy alone: 13.3 months, so 'roughly doubles' holds. Separately, the keynote-826 record linked a DOI that does not resolve (10.1200/JCO.23.00810); the real final-OS paper is 10.1200/JCO.23.00914.
claims.fixed: Added the GOG-240 paper as a link on the cervical record. Corrected the keynote-826 trial record's link and outcome sources from the non-resolving JCO.23.00810 to 10.1200/JCO.23.00914

claims.claim: BEATcc 32.1 months).
claims.note: BEATcc Lancet 2024: 'median overall survival was 32·1 months ... versus 22·8 months'. The beatcc trial record linked a Lancet PII (S0140-6736(23)02517-3) that does not resolve; the BEATcc paper is 10.1016/S0140-6736(23)02405-4.
claims.fixed: Corrected the beatcc trial record's link and outcome sources to doi 10.1016/S0140-6736(23)02405-4 (verified on Crossref and Europe PMC); the figure was already right

claims.claim: Reduces invasive cancer ~90% when given before exposure.
claims.note: The row's refs (hpv-vaccine → Wikipedia 'HPV vaccine', which says vaccines 'may prevent 70% of cervical cancer'; gardasil-9; ken-she, a persistent-infection endpoint) do not support '~90%' reduction of invasive cancer. Lei NEJM 2020: IRR 0.12 for women vaccinated before 17.
claims.fixed: Now 'In Sweden, vaccination before age 17 cut invasive cancer by about 88%.'; added the Lei paper to the cervical record links

claims.claim: Screening: HPV primary testing every 5 years from 25-30 (self-sampling accepted), or cytology every 3 years;
claims.note: The row is labelled USPSTF Grade A. USPSTF: 'every 3 years with cervical cytology alone in women aged 21 to 29 ... every 5 years with high-risk human papillomavirus (hrHPV) testing alone' for 30 to 65. The '25' start reflects programmes such as ACS and NHS that begin HPV testing at 25.

claims.claim: WHO target 70% screened twice in a lifetime.
claims.note: WHO global strategy (linked on the adjacent prevention row): '70% of women are screened with a high-performance test by 35 years of age and again by 45 years of age'

claims.claim: HPV test of cure at 6-12 months.
claims.note: ASCCP 2019 (the guideline the row names, with no URL): 'After treatment, HPV-based testing at 6 months is preferred regardless of the margin status'. The page said '6-12 months'.
claims.fixed: Now 'HPV test of cure at 6 months'; added the ASCCP 2019 DOI as the row's guideline URL

claims.claim: Stage IA1-IB1 (≤2 cm): Simple hysterectomy is non-inferior to radical for low-risk IA2-IB1 ≤2 cm (SHAPE trial, 2024); cone or trachelectomy for fertility preservation; sentinel node mapping in trials (SENTICOL III).
claims.note: The row's refs (robotic-surgery, sentinel-node, senticol-iii) do not cover SHAPE. SHAPE (Plante, NEJM 2024): randomised simple vs radical hysterectomy in low-risk disease, 'lesions of ≤2 cm with limited stromal invasion', mostly stage IB1, noninferior for pelvic recurrence. The 2024 date and the ≤2 cm limit are right.
claims.fixed: Added the SHAPE NEJM 2024 DOI as the row's guideline link; text unchanged

claims.claim: Locally advanced, high risk (node-positive IB2-IIB, III-IVA): Add pembrolizumab during chemoradiation and for 15 maintenance cycles (KEYNOTE-A18, approved 2024 for FIGO III-IVA), or induction carboplatin-paclitaxel weekly × 6 before chemoradiation (INTERLACE).
claims.note: FDA: 'On January 12, 2024, the Food and Drug Administration approved pembrolizumab ... with chemoradiotherapy (CRT) for patients with FIGO 2014 Stage III-IVA cervical cancer'. KEYNOTE-A18 Lancet 2024: '5 cycles of pembrolizumab ... plus chemoradiotherapy, followed by 15 cycles'. INTERLACE: six weekly induction cycles.

claims.claim: Delivery, not discovery: the disease is preventable, yet global HPV vaccination coverage of girls is around 27% and 350,000 women still die of it each year.
claims.note: WHO immunization coverage fact sheet (15 July 2026): 'Global coverage for the first dose of HPV vaccine in girls was 33% in 2025.' The page's 27% is an older WHO/UNICEF estimate, presented undated as current, and '350,000 ... each year' is an undated GLOBOCAN 2022 figure.
claims.fixed: Now 'WHO puts global coverage of girls with a first HPV vaccine dose at 33% in 2025, and GLOBOCAN estimated 350,000 deaths in 2022'; the WHO fact sheet was added to the record links

claims.claim: Screening reaches under 30% of women in most low- and middle-income countries; brachytherapy capacity is absent in much of Africa.
claims.note: No source on the record gives LMIC screening coverage. Bruni Lancet Global Health 2022: ever screened, women 30-49 in 2019: '34 million (9%) ... lower-middle-income ... 8 million (11%) ... low-income', '48%' in upper-middle-income. 'Under 30% in most LMICs' blurred very low coverage (about 10%) with upper-middle-income countries, where it is 48%.
claims.fixed: Now 'In 2019 only about one in ten women aged 30-49 in low- and lower-middle-income countries had ever been screened (48% in upper-middle-income countries)'; added Bruni 2022 to the record links

claims.claim: Endometrial cancer is the most common gynaecologic cancer in high-income countries (~420,000 cases a year worldwide) and one of the few cancers whose incidence and mortality are rising, driven by obesity, diabetes, and an ageing population.
claims.note: GLOBOCAN 2022 world corpus uteri: 420,368 new cases (repo copy). The page presented '~420,000 cases a year' undated. Wikipedia (the record source) gives only '320,000 women' in 2012. Rising incidence and mortality are supported by SEER: incidence 'rising on average 0.7% each year over 2014–2023', deaths '1.3% each year'.
claims.fixed: Dated: 'about 420,000 new cases worldwide in 2022, GLOBOCAN'; added GLOBOCAN 2022 and SEER uterine links to the endometrial record

claims.claim: Advanced and recurrent disease changed in 2023: three phase 3 trials (RUBY, NRG-GY018, DUO-E) established chemotherapy plus a PD-1/PD-L1 antibody as first-line standard, with dramatic benefit in dMMR tumours and a survival gain in the whole population (RUBY, OS 44.6 vs 28.2 months).
claims.note: Jemperli (dostarlimab) FDA label, RUBY: overall survival 'Median in months ... 44.6 ... 28.2 ... Hazard ratio 0.69'. RUBY, NRG-GY018 and DUO-E all reported in 2023 (trial records on the page).

claims.claim: Endometrial cancer accounts for ~420,000 cases per year worldwide and is the most common gynaecologic cancer in the US and Europe; most are found at stage I because of postmenopausal bleeding and cured by hysterectomy.
claims.note: GLOBOCAN 2022 world corpus uteri 420,368 new cases; the page presented '~420,000 cases per year' undated
claims.fixed: Dated: 'In 2022, GLOBOCAN estimated about 420,000 new cases of endometrial cancer worldwide'

claims.claim: Incidence and mortality are rising ~1-2% per year with obesity; ~97,000 deaths per year.
claims.note: SEER uterine (the record's prognosis source): new cases 'rising on average 0.7% each year over 2014–2023', death rates 'rising on average 1.3% each year over 2015–2024'. '~1-2% per year' overstates incidence. '~97,000 deaths per year' is an undated GLOBOCAN 2022 figure (97,723).
claims.fixed: Now 'In the US, incidence is rising about 0.7% and deaths about 1.3% a year (SEER), alongside obesity; GLOBOCAN estimated about 98,000 deaths worldwide in 2022'

claims.claim: Chemotherapy plus PD-1/PD-L1 blockade is first-line standard for advanced disease, with a 16-month overall survival gain in RUBY and a 72% reduction in progression risk in dMMR tumours.
claims.note: RUBY: median OS 44.6 vs 28.2 months (FDA label), a 16.4-month difference. RUBY NEJM 2023 dMMR PFS 'hazard ratio for progression or death, 0.28' = 72% reduction.

claims.claim: Lenvatinib plus pembrolizumab gives an 18-month median survival in pMMR disease after platinum, where PD-1 alone barely worked.
claims.note: KEYNOTE-775 NEJM 2022 (on the keynote-775 record): 'pMMR population: 17.4 vs. 12.0 months ... overall: 18.3 vs. 11.4 months'. The 18-month figure belongs to the all-comer population, not pMMR.
claims.fixed: Now 'gives a 17-month median survival in pMMR disease after platinum (17.4 against 12.0 months with chemotherapy)'

claims.claim: HER2 IHC 3+ disease has an approved ADC (T-DXd) with an 85% response rate.

claims.claim: Fertility-sparing (grade 1, stage IA, no invasion): Progestin (oral or IUD) with re-biopsy every 3-6 months; hysterectomy after childbearing.
claims.note: The fertility-sparing record cites the ESGO/ESHRE/ESGE 2023 guideline (doi 10.1136/ijgc-2022-004047). The abstract has no follow-up interval, and the full text returns 403 at BMJ and ScienceDirect with no PMC copy.

claims.claim: Advanced or recurrent, first line (any MMR status): Carboplatin-paclitaxel plus dostarlimab (RUBY), pembrolizumab (NRG-GY018/KEYNOTE-868), or durvalumab (DUO-E; dMMR in the US), continued as maintenance up to 2-3 years.
claims.note: RUBY (Annals 2024): dostarlimab 'every 6 weeks for up to 3 years'. NRG-GY018 NEJM 2023: '6 cycles every 3 weeks, followed by up to 14 maintenance cycles every 6 weeks' (about 2 years).

claims.claim: Equity: more p53-abnormal tumours and later diagnosis mean Black women in the US have nearly twice the mortality of white women; incidence and mortality are rising overall with obesity.
