claims.claim: Fertility-sparing therapy has a 30% relapse rate and no reliable predictor of response.
claims.note: Wikipedia (the record source) gives no relapse rate, and the fertility-sparing term's ESGO guideline is unreadable. Gunderson Gynecol Oncol 2012 systematic review: 'Recurrence after an initial response was noted in 23.2% with hyperplasia and 35.4% with carcinoma'.
claims.fixed: Now 'has no reliable predictor of response, and about 35% of women with carcinoma who respond later relapse (systematic review, 2012)'; added Gunderson 2012 to the endometrial record links

claims.claim: Incidence has risen six-fold over 40 years, largely from incidental detection on imaging and endoscopy.
claims.note: Wikipedia (the record source) gives only an incidence of '2.5–5 per 100,000' and no trend. Dasari JAMA Oncol 2017 (SEER): 'The age-adjusted incidence rate increased 6.4-fold from 1973 (1.09 per 100 000) to 2012 (6.98 per 100 000)', 'possibly owing to detection of early-stage disease and stage migration'. 'Largely from incidental detection' overstates the authors' 'possibly'.
claims.fixed: Now 'In the US, incidence rose 6.4-fold between 1973 and 2012, probably in large part from earlier detection on imaging and endoscopy.'; added Dasari 2017 to the NET record links

claims.claim: NETTER-2 first line for grade 2-3) is standard, and 177Lu-edotreotide beat everolimus head-to-head in COMPETE (PFS 23.9 vs 14.1 months) with an FDA decision due August 2026.

claims.claim: The frontier is alpha-emitting PRRT: 212Pb-DOTAMTATE (AlphaMedix) met all primary endpoints in phase 2 with a 54% response rate in PRRT-naive patients and Breakthrough designation, and 225Ac-DOTATATE (RYZ101) is in the phase 3 ACTION-1 trial after lutetium failure.
claims.note: The Sanofi press release of 8 October 2025 (the alphamedix record's source) confirms 'met all primary efficacy endpoints' and 'In February 2024, AlphaMedix™ was granted Breakthrough Therapy Designation', but it gives no response rate. A 2025 review reports an interim PRRT-naive ORR of 55.6% (20/36, ASCO 2024). No readable primary source gives 54%. ACTION-1 phase 3 of RYZ101 after lutetium is confirmed by the action-1 record (NCT05477576).
claims.fixed: Removed the 54% figure: now 'met all primary efficacy endpoints in phase 2 (October 2025) and holds Breakthrough designation'

claims.claim: Treatment is chosen by the tumour's biology, not only its origin: pembrolizumab for mismatch-repair-deficient or high-mutation-burden tumours (2017), larotrectinib and entrectinib for NTRK fusions, dabrafenib with trametinib for BRAF V600E, selpercatinib for RET, and trastuzumab deruxtecan for HER2-positive tumours of any site are approved regardless of where the cancer began.

claims.claim: Established in 2011 and hosted by the Cancer Hospital of the Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences, the National Cancer Center runs the National Central Cancer Registry (more than 700 population-based registries), the Cancer Screening Program in Rural China and urban screening programmes, national quality control for cancer care, and the Journal of the National Cancer Center.
claims.note: "Established in 2011" is on no source on the record (NCC site unreachable by script). Han 2024 says "a total of 700 registries reporting high-quality data" in 2018, not "more than 700".
claims.fixed: Removed "Established in 2011"; changed registry count to 700 reporting high-quality data for 2018.

claims.claim: Its 2024 report estimated about 4.8 million new cases and 2.6 million deaths in 2022 (age-standardised incidence 201.61 and mortality 96.47 per 100,000), with lung, colorectal, thyroid, liver and stomach cancers making up 57.42% of cases and mortality rates falling about 1.3% a year since 2000.
claims.note: Han 2024: 4,824,700 cases, 2,574,200 deaths, ASIR 201.61, ASMR 96.47, top five 57.42% - all correct; but "the ASMR decreased by approximately 1.3% per year" during 2000-2018, not "since 2000" for "mortality rates".
claims.fixed: Changed to "age-standardised mortality falling about 1.3% a year from 2000 to 2018".

claims.claim: Created in 2018 to merge the urban employee, urban resident and rural insurance schemes, the NHSA administers basic medical insurance for more than 1.3 billion people and the National Reimbursement Drug List (NRDL).
claims.note: Neither year nor coverage was on the record's sources. gov.cn 1 June 2018: "5月31日上午，国家医保局正式挂牌" merging employee, resident and NCMS insurance; 2025 bulletin: "全国基本医保参保13.31亿人". Figures correct.
claims.fixed: Added gov.cn and 2025 bulletin links.

claims.claim: Since 2017 (15 targeted anticancer drugs, average 48.9% cut in cost per defined daily dose) and the dedicated 2018 oncology round (17 drugs), it has run annual price negotiations in which manufacturers accept steep discounts, typically more than half, for national reimbursement; renewals are renegotiated and a dual-channel policy (2021) lets designated pharmacies dispense listed drugs when hospitals do not stock them.
claims.note: BMJ Glob Health 2021: 15 targeted drugs; "Compared with what would have happened without the intervention, cost/DDD of price-negotiated medications decreased by 48.9%" (actual fall US$71.21 from US$169.24) - a counterfactual estimate, not an average cut. J Glob Health 2022: 17 drugs in 2018. "More than half" supported for lung drugs (median -54.8% at negotiation, Lancet Reg Health WP 2026); 2021 dual-channel guidance (医保发〔2021〕28号) not previously sourced.
claims.fixed: Reworded 48.9% as "below the expected trend"; added the NRDL price-trend paper and a notice citing the 2021 dual-channel guidance.

claims.claim: Founded in 1984 and based at Tianjin Medical University Cancer Institute and Hospital, CACA has more than a hundred professional committees and publishes the CACA Guidelines for Holistic Integrative Management of Cancer, released annually since 2022 with an emphasis on domestic evidence, traditional and integrative medicine and the whole care pathway.

claims.note: Methods: 'Für das Jahr 2023 bilden die Bundesländer Schleswig-Holstein, Hamburg, Niedersachsen, Bremen, Nordrhein-Westfalen, Hessen, Rheinland-Pfalz, Baden-Württemberg, Bayern, Saarland, Berlin und Brandenburg die Referenzregion' (12 of 16).

claims.claim: The reference region for the 2023 data year comprises Schleswig-Holstein, Hamburg, Lower Saxony, Bremen, North Rhine-Westphalia, Hesse, Rhineland-Palatinate, Baden-Württemberg, Bavaria, Saarland, Berlin and Brandenburg.
claims.note: Same list of 12 Länder in the methods chapter.

claims.claim: To qualify a registry must have registered nationwide for at least ten years, have exceeded 90 percent completeness for all cancers over the last five, and have a death-certificate-only share between zero and 15 percent.
claims.note: Methods: 'Flächendeckende Krebsregistrierung seit mindestens zehn Jahren', 'Vollzähligkeit für »Krebs gesamt« in den letzten fünf Jahren > 90 %', DCO 'unter 15 % und > 0 %'.

claims.claim: The last published per-state completeness figures date from 2019 and cover 2015 and 2016, and even those are bands rather than numbers: ten states at 90 percent or more, five of them above 95.
claims.note: ZfKD completeness page 'Stand: 17.12.2019', 'Geschätzte Vollzähligkeit ... 2015/2016': 'zehn Bundesländer eine geschätzte Vollzähligkeit von mindestens 90 Prozent ..., fünf von ihnen lagen über 95 Prozent'.

claims.claim: The institute also flags a specific hole, warning that the transition to nationwide clinical and epidemiological registration temporarily cost some regions cases, particularly for diagnosis years 2015 to 2018.
claims.note: ZfKD incidence page: 'in der Übergangsphase zur flächendeckenden klinisch-epidemiologischen Krebsregistrierung, also insbesondere hinsichtlich der Diagnosejahre 2015 bis 2018, in einzelnen Regionen zu vorübergehenden Einbußen'.

claims.claim: Death-certificate-only cases are treated as ordinary incident cases when estimating incidence, excluded when judging completeness, and excluded from survival analysis because the diagnosis date is unknown, which biases survival upwards; per-site shares for 2021 to 2023 run at 5 percent for colorectal cancer in women and 3 percent in men, 9 percent for lung cancer in both, and 3 percent for breast and prostate.
claims.note: Methods: DCO cases counted as Neuerkrankungen in incidence estimation, 'nicht berücksichtigt' in completeness. Per-site DCO shares 2021-2023 from KiD 2025 stage figures: colorectal 5 % F / 3 % M (Abb. 3.6.4), lung 9 % / 9 % (Abb. 3.12.4), prostate 3 % (Abb. 3.22.4), breast 3 % (all women). Survival exclusion and upward bias: ZfKD survival page 'führt zwangsläufig zum Ausschluss dieses Falls ... potenzielle Überschätzung der Überlebensraten' (link added).
claims.fixed: added ZfKD survival-methods page as a link on the card (see detail.s7)

claims.claim: Survival is calculated from only six registries, and only those whose five-year survival for pancreatic cancer and metastatic lung cancer averages at most 8 percent, a proxy for deaths the registry missed.
claims.note: KiD 2025 methods name six survival registries (SH, Hamburg, Niedersachsen, Bremen, Saarland, RB Münster) 'auf der Basis vorher festgelegter Kriterien', but the 8 % criterion is not on any card link. ZfKD survival page: 'nur diejenigen Register ... bei denen Patientinnen und Patienten mit der Diagnose Bauchspeicheldrüsenkrebs bzw. metastasiertem Lungenkrebs ein relatives 5-Jahres-Überleben von im Mittel maximal 8 Prozent aufwiesen'.
claims.fixed: added the ZfKD survival-methods page as a link on the card; text unchanged

claims.claim: Krebs in Deutschland 2025: methods (PDF)
claims.note: Methods chapter of KiD 2025.

claims.claim: Section 65c lists the tasks in order: recording, then analysis, then feedback of results to individual providers, then data exchange with other regional registries and state-level evaluation units, support for interdisciplinary working, participation in the G-BA's cross-sector quality assurance, cooperation with certified cancer centres, supply to the epidemiological registries and to the federal centre, contribution to the reconciliation of screening data under section 25a, and supply of data for transparency and research.
claims.note: §65c(1) Nr. 1-10 in that order: Erfassung; Auswertung und Rückmeldung; Datenaustausch with other registries and Auswertungsstellen; interdisziplinäre Zusammenarbeit; G-BA Qualitätssicherung; zertifizierte Zentren; epidemiological registries; ZfKD; Datenabgleich nach §25a; Versorgungstransparenz und Forschung.

claims.claim: Two further deliverables were written into the statute: a concept for matching data to find comparable cases at a treating doctor's request, due at the end of 2023, and a concept for the systematic recording of late and long-term effects, due at the end of 2024.
claims.note: §65c(1) Nr. 11 concept on comparable cases 'bis zum 31. Dezember 2023'; Nr. 12 late and long-term effects 'bis zum 31. Dezember 2024'.

claims.claim: Section 65c(10) requires a joint evaluation commissioned by the sickness funds and the state health ministries, with a report due by 30 June 2026, on what the registries contribute to quality and to linking care with research; whether it has appeared we could not establish.
claims.note: §65c(10): Spitzenverband Bund der Krankenkassen and obersten Landesbehörden commission an evaluation incl. contribution to quality and to 'Zusammenwirken von Versorgung und Forschung'; 'Ein Bericht ... ist bis zum 30. Juni 2026 zu veröffentlichen'.

claims.claim: Cancers in children and adolescents come from the Deutsches Kinderkrebsregister in Mainz, which has been more than 95 percent complete since about 1987 and holds around 80,000 cases, about 2,350 a year under 18; it supplies the federal centre only aggregated state-level data, which is why the new regional maps in the report cover adults aged 20 and over.

All figures correct.

claims.note: Chapter 3.29 'Weitere meldepflichtige Tumoren' of KiD 2025.

claims.claim: Family members without their own income are covered at no extra cost (Familienversicherung, section 10 SGB V).
claims.note: §10(1) SGB V: spouse, partner and children of members are insured ('Versichert sind der Ehegatte, der Lebenspartner und die Kinder von Mitgliedern') if their income stays below the threshold; no separate contribution.

claims.claim: What cancer costs a statutorily insured patient: capped at 2% of income, 1% if you are chronically ill
claims.note: §62(1): 'Die Belastungsgrenze beträgt 2 vom Hundert ... für chronisch Kranke ... 1 vom Hundert'.

claims.claim: You pay 10% of the price of each prescription, never less than 5 euros and never more than 10, and 10 euros a day in hospital for at most 28 days a year.
claims.note: §61: '10 vom Hundert des Abgabepreises, mindestens jedoch 5 Euro und höchstens 10 Euro'; inpatient 'je Kalendertag 10 Euro'; §39(4) 'für längstens 28 Tage'.

claims.claim: Everything you pay is added up, and once it passes 2% of your household's gross income for the year you pay nothing more.
claims.note: §62(1)-(2): 2% of annual gross income for living costs, household incomes added together; exemption for rest of year.

claims.claim: For someone in long-term treatment for a serious illness, which is what cancer is, the ceiling is 1%.
claims.note: §62(1): 1% for chronically ill 'wegen derselben schwerwiegenden Krankheit in Dauerbehandlung' (an exception for those born after 1 April 1972 who skipped check-ups exists).

claims.claim: Section 61 SGB V sets the co-payment at 10 percent of the dispensing price, with a floor of 5 euros and a ceiling of 10 euros, and at 10 euros per calendar day for inpatient care; section 39(4) limits the hospital charge to 28 days in a calendar year, so at most 280 euros.
claims.note: §61 10%/5/10 euros and 10 euros per calendar day; §39(4) 28 days per calendar year (so 280 euros).

claims.claim: Section 62 sets the annual burden limit (Belastungsgrenze) at 2 percent of the household's gross annual income for living costs, reduced to 1 percent for people in continuous treatment for the same serious chronic illness, with allowances deducted for a spouse and for each child.
claims.note: §62(1)-(2) as stated, including household deductions.

claims.claim: The consequence is that the sticker price of a cancer medicine, however large, is not a number a German patient ever sees: on a gross household income of 40,000 euros the most a chronically ill patient pays in a year is 400 euros.
claims.note: Arithmetic from §62: 1% of 40,000 = 400 euros (upper bound before allowances).

claims.claim: What is not covered by this cap is income: statutory sick pay (Krankengeld) runs at 70 percent of gross earnings, capped at 90 percent of net, for up to 78 weeks for the same illness in three years, and loss of earnings, travel and childcare are the costs patients and charities describe.
claims.note: §47(1): 'Krankengeld beträgt 70 vom Hundert des ... Regelentgelt ... darf 90 vom Hundert des ... Nettoarbeitsentgelts nicht übersteigen'; §48(1): 'längstens achtundsiebzig Wochen innerhalb von je drei Jahren'.

claims.claim: Section 39 SGB V: hospital co-payment, 28 days
claims.note: §39(4): 'für längstens 28 Tage'.

claims.claim: Under section 35a SGB V the company files a dossier by the day of launch; the Gemeinsamer Bundesausschuss sets the appropriate comparator therapy (zweckmäßige Vergleichstherapie), IQWiG assesses the dossier against it within three months, and the G-BA resolves on the added benefit within three months of that assessment being published, so about six months after launch.
claims.note: G-BA: dossier 'no later than the day the medicinal product is first brought into circulation'; §35a(2) IQWiG within three months; §35a(3) 'beschließt ... innerhalb von drei Monaten nach ihrer Veröffentlichung'.

claims.claim: The company and the GKV-Spitzenverband then have six months to agree a reimbursement amount, with a three-month arbitration if they fail; in completed procedures from 2019 to 2024 about 95 percent ended in an agreed price and 5 percent in an arbitration award.
claims.note: Six months and three-month arbitration are in §130b(4). The 95%/5% split for 2019-2024 is from the vfa 'AMNOG in 10 Zahlen' 2026 ('95 % der Verfahren ... Lediglich in 5 % ... Schiedsstelle'; 'abgeschlossene Verfahren im Zeitraum 2019 bis 2024'), which was linked only on another card.
claims.fixed: Added the vfa report link to the day-one card; figure unchanged (it matches).

claims.claim: Section 130b(3a) makes the agreed price apply from the seventh month after the substance first went on sale, and the difference against what was actually charged, including the pharmacy mark-up and VAT paid on it, is recovered.
claims.note: §130b(3a): 'gilt ab dem siebten Monat nach dem erstmaligen Inverkehrbringen'; difference 'einschließlich der zu viel entrichteten Zuschläge nach der Arzneimittelpreisverordnung und der zu viel entrichteten Umsatzsteuer auszugleichen'.

claims.claim: That seventh month used to be the thirteenth: the change was made by the GKV-Finanzstabilisierungsgesetz of 7 November 2022, in force from 12 November 2022.
claims.note: Dates verified (buzer: 'G. v. 07.11.2022 ... Geltung ab 12.11.2022'; G-BA: 'mit Inkrafttreten des GKV-FinStG im November 2022 rückwirkend ab dem siebten Monat'). No cited source, nor the Bundestag Drucksache 20/3448, states that the previous rule was the thirteenth month.
claims.fixed: Removed the unsourced 'used to be the thirteenth' clause; sentence now says the seventh-month rule was introduced by the GKV-FinStG of 7 Nov 2022, in force 12 Nov 2022; added the buzer GKV-FinStG link to the card.

claims.claim: Section 130b SGB V: the negotiation, arbitration and the seventh-month rule
claims.note: §130b(3a) seventh-month rule, (4)-(5) arbitration.

claims.claim: Otherwise section 130b(3) says a medicine with no proven added benefit should be given a reimbursement amount that does not produce higher annual therapy costs than the comparator the G-BA named, with the cheapest comparator used where several were named and a fifteen percent reduction where the comparator is itself a patent-protected medicine outside the assessment scheme.
claims.note: §130b(3) as now in force: no-benefit 'soll ... nicht zu höheren Jahrestherapiekosten führt'; cheapest alternative; 'Abschlag in Höhe von 15 Prozent' for patent-protected comparator outside §35a.

claims.claim: The GKV-Spitzenverband's register, updated 13 August 2026, carries twenty products with the status opt-out and two more with a mixed status, twenty-two in all since 2013, of which five are oncology: alpelisib, amivantamab, duvelisib, regorafenib and idecabtagene vicleucel.
claims.note: Register queried by status on 3 Nov 2026: 21 products 'Opt-Out' (latest teprotumumab, 15.10.2026) and 2 'Erstattungsbetrag vereinbart/ Opt-Out' (idecabtagene vicleucel, regorafenib); oncology: alpelisib, amivantamab, duvelisib, regorafenib, ide-cel. Earliest entry 11.06.2013.
claims.fixed: Updated to twenty-one opt-outs plus two mixed, twenty-three in all, as read on 3 November 2026; oncology list unchanged.

claims.claim: DGHO: early benefit assessment of new medicines in Germany 2011-2020 (PDF)
claims.note: DGHO report covers 519 procedures 2011-2020.

claims.claim: On the industry association's count, 60% of oncology procedures showed some added benefit against 52% across all medicines, and the share has been falling: 58% in 2011 to 2013, 43% in 2023 to 2025.
claims.note: vfa: oncology 60%, all procedures 52%; the 58% (2011-2013) to 43% (2023-2025) trend is for all procedures, not oncology, but the sentence read as if it were the oncology share.
claims.fixed: Made explicit that the falling share is across all medicines.

claims.claim: The G-BA's own procedure database held 1,377 procedures on 25 September 2026, of which 1,257 were complete, and 588 oncology procedures of which 538 were complete, so cancer is about 43 percent of all completed assessments;
claims.note: Dated snapshot (25 Sept 2026) cannot be replayed; G-BA database on 3 Nov 2026 shows 1392 procedures, 1268 complete; oncology 594, 543 complete (43%), consistent with the earlier counts plus five weeks of new procedures.

claims.claim: 109 of the oncology procedures ran as orphan procedures.
claims.note: G-BA database, therapiegebietsgruppe oncology + Verfahrensart Orphan Drug: 109 Ergebnisse.

claims.claim: The vfa, using the Pharm-Analytics database and taking the best rating per procedure from 2011 to March 2026, gives 2 percent major, 16 percent considerable, 15 percent minor, 19 percent non-quantifiable and 48 percent not proven across 1,201 procedures, with oncology the strongest field at 60 percent showing some added benefit.
claims.note: vfa: '2 % mit einem erheblichen, in 16 % einem beträchtlichen, in 15 % einen geringen und in 19 % mit einem nicht quantifizierbaren', 48% nicht belegt; 1,201 Verfahren; 'maximales Ausmaß je Verfahren'; 2011 bis März 2026; oncology 60%.

claims.claim: The DGHO, over 519 procedures from 2011 to 2020, found 41.1 percent not proven per procedure but 59.6 percent not proven per subgroup, and for oncology specifically fewer than 30 percent of procedures rated not proven as their best verdict.
claims.note: DGHO: '519 Verfahren'; '41,1% ... nicht belegt'; subgroups '59,6%'; oncology best rating not proven 'in <30% der onkologischen Verfahren'.

claims.note: 'Ausgabe 2026'.

claims.claim: DGHO: early benefit assessment 2011-2020 (PDF)
The argument about the method: surrogates, single arms and a 15% rule for quality of life
claims.note: IQWiG 7.0: responder thresholds of at least 15% of the scale range.

claims.claim: And it only counts a quality-of-life difference if it reaches 15% of the scale.
claims.note: IQWiG 7.0 §9.3.3: 15% applies to responder thresholds; continuous data are also accepted via standardised mean differences (Hedges' g, irrelevance threshold 0.2), so a difference below 15% can count.
claims.fixed: Reworded: when it counts patients whose quality of life improved, it only accepts a threshold of at least 15% of the scale.

claims.claim: IQWiG's Allgemeine Methoden, version 7.0 of 19 September 2023, grades certainty in four steps, Beleg, Hinweis, Anhaltspunkt or none, and says most surrogate endpoints are unreliable and can be misleading, so they are normally considered only where they have been validated by statistical methods within a sufficiently narrow patient population and within comparable interventions, usually a meta-analysis of several randomised trials correlating treatment effects rather than individual outcomes.
claims.note: 'Version 7.0 vom 19.09.2023'; '4 Abstufungen ... Beleg ... Hinweis ... Anhaltspunkt ... oder keine'; 'Die meisten Surrogatendpunkte sind jedoch ... nicht verlässlich und können ... irreführend sein'; validation within narrow population and comparable interventions; meta-analysis of several RCTs; 'primär auf den Grad der Korrelation auf der Ebene der Behandlungseffekte'.

claims.claim: The oncology report behind this rule, rapid report A10-05 of 2011, examined validation studies in colorectal and breast cancer and concluded that they permit no final statement on the validity of tumour response measures for overall survival in those diseases.
claims.note: A10-05 v1.1, 21.11.2011: 'Die zu den Krankheitsbildern Darmkrebs und Brustkrebs vorliegenden Validierungsstudien erlauben keine abschließende Aussage zur Validität von Parametern des Tumoransprechens für das Gesamtüberleben'.

claims.claim: For quality of life the institute identified 15 percent of the scale range as a plausible threshold for a change a patient can reliably feel, and does not use pre-specified responder criteria below it.
claims.note: '15 % der Spannweite der jeweiligen Skalen als plausibler Schwellenwert für eine eher kleine, aber hinreichend sicher spürbare Veränderung'; MIDs below 15% 'werden diese regelhaft nicht herangezogen'.

claims.claim: In September 2026, on its thousandth assessment, IQWiG argued that manufacturers still submit evidence unfit for comparison, that a placebo comparison where a standard therapy exists can only yield no added benefit, and that comparative trials are feasible in rare diseases if the company wants them.
claims.note: IQWiG 1 Sept 2026: 'die ersten 1000 vollgemacht'; placebo comparison 'kann das Ergebnis nur lauten: Ein Zusatznutzen ist nicht belegt'; 'wenn der Hersteller es will'.

claims.claim: IQWiG, 1 September 2026: fifteen years of AMNOG, on its thousandth assessment
claims.note: Press release dated 1 September 2026 on the 1000th assessment, 15 years of AMNOG.

claims.note: Crossref: Bartol, Dressler, Kaskel, 'Ten years of AMNOG from an oncological perspective', J Cancer Res Clin Oncol 149(6), print June 2023 (online Oct 2022).

claims.claim: The price guardrails of 2022, and their repeal in July 2026
claims.note: GKV-FinStG 2022 guardrails; BSaStabG in force 30.07.2026 replaced them.

claims.claim: In 2022 Germany added rules forcing the price of a drug with no, minor or unmeasurable added benefit below or level with the comparator, and a flat 20% discount on drugs used in combination.
claims.note: GKV-FinStG: the 10%-below and not-higher guardrails applied only where the comparator was patent- or data-protected ('für den Patentschutz oder Unterlagenschutz besteht'); 20% combination discount correct.
claims.fixed: Added that the comparator had to be patent-protected.

claims.claim: Those rules were narrowed in 2025 and then abolished on 30 July 2026, replaced by tendered rebate contracts within classes of comparable drugs, three of which are cancer classes.
claims.note: BSaStabG §130e(3): five classes, JAK, CGRP, PARP, PCSK9, PD-1/PD-L1. Only PARP and PD-1/PD-L1 are cancer classes; the law does not call JAK inhibitors a cancer class.
claims.fixed: Changed 'three' to 'two' cancer classes (and the matching detail sentence now names PARP and PD-1/PD-L1 and notes JAK inhibitors include myelofibrosis drugs).

claims.claim: The GKV-Finanzstabilisierungsgesetz of 7 November 2022 inserted guardrails into section 130b(3): a drug with no added benefit whose comparator was still patent-protected had to be priced at least 10 percent below it; a drug with only minor or non-quantifiable added benefit could not exceed the comparator's cost at all.
claims.note: GKV-FinStG: no benefit + patent-protected comparator: 'mindestens 10 Prozent unterhalb'; minor/non-quantifiable: not higher only where the comparator is patent-protected, omitted on the page.
claims.fixed: Added 'and a patent-protected comparator' to the minor/non-quantifiable clause.

claims.claim: Section 130e added a 20 percent discount on medicines used in a combination named by the G-BA, removable only if the G-BA found the combination likely to have at least considerable added benefit.
claims.note: §130e (2022): 'Abschlag in Höhe von 20 Prozent' for a combination named by the G-BA; lapses if 'mindestens beträchtlichen Zusatznutzen erwarten lässt'.

claims.claim: The same law cut the orphan revenue threshold from 50 to 30 million euros, raised the manufacturer discount to 12 percent for 2023 and extended the price moratorium to 2026.
claims.note: GKV-FinStG: '50 Millionen' replaced by '30 Millionen'; §130a(1b) 12% in 2023; §130a(3a) '2022' replaced by '2026'.

claims.claim: The Medizinforschungsgesetz, in force 1 January 2025, disapplied the two guardrails for medicines whose trials were conducted to a relevant extent in Germany and added a confidential reimbursement amount option at a 9 percent discount.
claims.note: True per the Medizinforschungsgesetz (BGBl. 2024 I Nr. 324): Art. 6 (SGB V) in force 1 January 2025 (Art. 12(2)); 'zu einem relevanten Anteil im Geltungsbereich dieses Gesetzes durchgeführt wurden, finden Satz 2 und 5 keine Anwendung'; confidential amount 'abzüglich eines Abschlags in Höhe von 9 Prozent'. But no link on the card carried the MFG.
claims.fixed: Added the MFG BGBl text as a link on the card; figures unchanged.

claims.claim: The GKV-Beitragssatzstabilisierungsgesetz of 24 July 2026, in force 30 July 2026, then replaced the guardrail sentences with the plain rule that a drug with no added benefit must not cost more than the comparator, and replaced section 130e entirely with a regime letting sickness funds tender exclusive rebate contracts within groups of therapeutically comparable patent-protected medicines, limited until the end of 2030 to five classes: JAK inhibitors, CGRP antagonists, PARP inhibitors, PCSK9 inhibitors and PD-1 and PD-L1 inhibitors.
claims.note: buzer: 'G. v. 24.07.2026 ... Geltung ab 30.07.2026'; §130b(3) Sätze 2 bis 6 replaced with no-benefit 'nicht zu höheren Jahrestherapiekosten'; new §130e rebate contracts, '(3) Bis zum Ablauf des 31. Dezember 2030 ... JAK ... CGRP ... PARP ... PCSK9 ... PD-1/PD-L1'.

claims.claim: The seventh-month rule and the 30 million euro orphan threshold survive both later laws.
claims.note: Current §130b(3a) 'ab dem siebten Monat'; current §35a(1) '30 Millionen Euro'.

claims.claim: Section 77 of the Arzneimittelgesetz splits the national competence in one sentence: the Bundesinstitut für Arzneimittel und Medizinprodukte (BfArM, Bonn and Cologne, about 1,350 staff) is the competent federal higher authority unless the Paul-Ehrlich-Institut is, and the Paul-Ehrlich-Institut (PEI, Langen) is competent for sera, vaccines, blood and tissue preparations, allergens, advanced therapy medicinal products, xenogeneic medicines and genetically engineered blood components.
claims.note: §77 AMG matches word for word in substance ('Zuständige Bundesoberbehörde ist das BfArM, es sei denn, dass das Paul-Ehrlich-Institut zuständig ist. (2) Das PEI ist zuständig für Sera, Impfstoffe, Blutzubereitungen, Gewebezubereitungen, Gewebe, Allergene, Arzneimittel für neuartige Therapien, xenogene Arzneimittel und gentechnisch hergestellte Blutbestandteile'). The 'about 1,350 staff' figure is not on the linked BfArM tasks page; BfArM's own about page states 'roughly 1,350 employees'.
claims.fixed: Added the BfArM about page (which states 'roughly 1,350 employees') as a link on the card; figure unchanged.

claims.claim: Clinical trials need one decision from the competent federal authority under section 42(2) AMG plus a favourable opinion from a Land ethics committee, submitted through CTIS under EU Regulation 536/2014; the Medizinforschungsgesetz added a specialised ethics committee and a shortened timetable for trials run only in Germany.
claims.note: BfArM: 'nach § 42 Abs. 2 AMG eine Genehmigung bei der zuständigen Bundesoberbehörde einzuholen ... der nach Landesrecht gebildeten zuständigen Ethikkommissionen, die ebenfalls ... eine zustimmende Bewertung abgeben muss'; page links CTIS, 'Spezialisierte Ethik-Kommission' under the Medizinforschungsgesetz and 'Verkürzte Bearbeitungsfrist für mononationale klinische Prüfungen'.

claims.claim: Section 4b of the Arzneimittelgesetz disapplies the authorisation chapter for advanced therapy medicinal products that are prescribed for an individual patient, made to specific quality standards but not routinely, and used in a specialised healthcare facility under a doctor's responsibility; supplying such a product to others still needs a permission from the competent federal authority, granted by the Paul-Ehrlich-Institut, with the facilities named, the expected number of patients a year stated and a risk-management plan.
claims.note: §4b(1) AMG: 'individuelle Zubereitung für einen einzelnen Patienten ärztlich verschrieben, nach spezifischen Qualitätsnormen nicht routinemäßig hergestellt und in einer spezialisierten Einrichtung ... angewendet'; §4b(3) application must include the facilities, 'die Anzahl der geplanten Anwendungen oder der Patienten im Jahr' and 'Angaben zum Risikomanagement-Plan'.

claims.claim: PEI's table of gene therapy medicinal products lists eighteen entries: seventeen with EU/1 numbers from the centralised procedure, and one national permission, HD-CAR-19 (heidagen-lecleucel), Universitätsklinikum Heidelberg, PEI.A.12181.01.1, dated 23 September 2025.
claims.note: PEI gene therapy table has 17 distinct EU/1 numbers plus one national permission PEI.A.12181.01.1 (HD-CAR-19, Universitätsklinikum Heidelberg, 23.09.2025) = 18 entries.

claims.claim: At the end of 2025 there were 2,294 certified centres across 2,429 sites, more than 190 of them outside Germany.
claims.note: DKG: 'Inzwischen (Stand 31.12.2025) gibt es 2.294 zertifizierte Zentren an 2.429 Standorten, davon mehr als 190 im Ausland.'

claims.claim: The first Brustkrebszentren were certified against an Erhebungsbogen from 2003, after national and international analyses found unexplained variation in breast cancer care; colorectal followed in 2006, prostate, lung, gynaecology, skin and the first Onkologische Zentren in 2008, and entities have been added almost every year since, most recently penile and biliary carcinoma in 2023.
claims.note: Jahresbericht OZ 2026, 1.4 Historie: national and international analyses showed 'medizinisch nicht erklärbare Variationen' in breast cancer care; timeline 2003 Brust, 2006 Darm, 2008 Prostata, Lunge, Gynäkologie, Haut, Onkologische Zentren ... 2023 Penis, biliäre Karzinome; 'Grundlage für die Zertifizierungen ist seit 2003 ein Erhebungsbogen'. (The card's link to this report was a dead URL returning a 404 page; the working file has the suffix _dkg.)

claims.claim: A breast cancer centre must treat at least 100 new patients a year and each named breast surgeon at least 50 operations.
claims.note: Erhebungsbogen Brust (Stand 11.12.2025): '≥ 100 Primärfälle inv. Ca. und DCIS'; 'min. 50 Mamma-OPs pro Jahr ... pro benanntem Operateur'.

claims.claim: A bowel centre needs 30 colon and 20 rectal cancers a year, and each named bowel surgeon 15 and 10.
claims.note: Erhebungsbogen Darm/Viszeral (Stand 16.12.2025): '30 Operative Primärfälle Kolon, 20 Operative Primärfälle Rektum'; 'Expertise pro Darmoperateur: 15 Kolonkarzinome pro Jahr, 10 Rektumkarzinome pro Jahr'.

claims.claim: At least 5% of patients must be entered into a study, and if the centre loses track of more than 40% of its patients at follow-up it cannot be recertified.
claims.note: Study quota right ('nach 1 Jahr: mind. 5% der Primärfälle' in both). But the follow-up quota with '< 60% - Rezertifizierung ... nicht gegeben' is set for 'Darm, Pankreas und Prostata' (lung has its own rule); it is not a breast-centre requirement, while the sentence applied it to every centre.
claims.fixed: 'if the centre loses track' changed to 'if a bowel centre loses track'.

claims.claim: Breast (version of 11 December 2025): at least 100 primary cases a year per centre counting invasive carcinoma and DCIS; at least 50 breast operations a year per named surgeon; radiologists reading mammograms of at least 1,000 patients a year, or 500 plus a biennial test; at least 25 minimally invasive interventions a year per operator.
claims.note: EB Brust 11.12.2025: ≥100 Primärfälle inv. Ca. und DCIS; min. 50 Mamma-OPs per named surgeon; mammograms 'von mind. 1000 Pat. pro Jahr oder ... mind. 500 Pat./Jahr und erfolgreiche Teilnahme an Fallsammlungsprüfung der KV alle 2 Jahre'; 'Mind. 25 minimal invasive Interventionen ... pro durchführenden Behandler ... pro Jahr'.

claims.claim: Colorectal (16 December 2025): 30 colon and 20 rectal carcinomas a year per centre, at least two named bowel surgeons at 15 and 10 primary cases each, and pancreas 25, stomach 30, liver and biliary 40, oesophagus 40 per centre as separate modules.
claims.note: EB Darm 16.12.2025: 30/20 operative primary cases; 'mind. 2 Darmoperateure', 15 colon and 10 rectal each; modules: Pankreas 25, Magen 30, HCC/biliär 40, Ösophagus 40 Zentrumsfälle per year.

claims.claim: Both require at least one full-time social worker per 400 patients counselled, a named psycho-oncologist with recognised training and documented distress screening.
claims.note: Both EBs: 'mind. 1 VK für 400 beratene Pat. (nicht Fälle)'; 'mind. 1 Psychoonkologe mit den genannten Qualifikationen (namentliche Benennung)'; distress screening documented.

claims.note: 'Follow-up Quote Darm, Pankreas und Prostata: ≥ 80% - Mindestanforderung ...; 60 - 79% ... nur mit Auflagen; < 60% ... nicht gegeben'. Thresholds right, but the sentence followed 'Both require' and so read as applying to breast centres too.
claims.fixed: Sentence now opens 'For bowel, pancreatic and prostate cancer the follow-up thresholds are graded'.

claims.claim: In the 2024 data year, breast centres met the 5 percent study quota with a median of 13.2 percent, and colorectal centres with 16.7 percent, but only 81.5 percent of breast sites reached the distress screening target of 65 percent, with a site-level range of 0 to 100 percent.

claims.claim: WiZen, funded by the G-BA's Innovationsfonds and led from TU Dresden, used AOK claims from 2009 to 2017 linked with the Regensburg, Dresden, Erfurt and Berlin-Brandenburg cancer registries, with Cox models adjusted for age, sex, metastasis, comorbidity, hospital size, ownership and teaching status, and for UICC stage in the registry arm.
claims.note: WiZen Ergebnisbericht: AOK data and 'vier klinischen Krebsregister (KKR) Regensburg, Dresden, Erfurt und Berlin-Brandenburg', TU Dresden; Schmitt 2023 Table 2 footnote: adjustment for age, sex, distant metastasis, Elixhauser comorbidities, beds, teaching/university hospital, ownership, year; UICC stage in registry data (Stang confirms adjustment for UICC stage in CCR data).

claims.claim: Adjusted hazard ratios for overall survival in certified versus non-certified hospitals ran from 0.77 (breast, 143,720 patients) to 0.97 (lung, 172,901), with colon 0.92, rectum 0.90, pancreas 0.88, cervix 0.83, ovary 0.88, prostate 0.83, endometrium 0.92, neuro-oncological 0.92 and head and neck 0.94; the simulated gain over eight years ranged from 0.62 months for lung to 4.61 months for cervical cancer.
claims.note: Schmitt 2023 Table 2: colon 0.92, rectal 0.90, pancreatic 0.88, breast 0.77, cervical 0.83, endometrial 0.92, ovarian 0.88, lung 0.97, prostate 0.83, neuro 0.92, head and neck 0.94; ARR over 8 years 0.62 (lung) to 4.61 (cervix). Ergebnisbericht table: Mammakarzinom 143 720, Bronchialkarzinom 172 901.

claims.claim: The two data sources disagree in ways worth noticing: only five entities were significant in both, and for rectum, pancreas and ovary the registry analysis, which could adjust for stage, showed no effect at all, while for lung the registry analysis showed one (0.85) where the claims analysis did not.
claims.note: Ergebnisbericht: 'Statistisch signifikant in beiden Datenquellen waren ... Kolon-, Mamma-, Zervix- und Prostatakarzinom sowie neuroonkologische Tumoren' (five); Tabelle 6 KKR HRs rectum 0.978 (0.929-1.029), pancreas 0.972 (0.923-1.024), ovary 0.964 (0.867-1.071): not significant, but point estimates below 1, so 'no effect at all' overstates; lung KKR 0.850***.
claims.fixed: 'showed no effect at all' changed to 'showed no significant effect'.

Schoffer O, Bierbaum V, BMC Cancer 2022 (PMID 35672675): 'Median survival was 8.0 months in GCS-certified pancreatic cancer centers and 4.4 months in non-certified'. claims.note: DOI 10.1055/a-2132-6797 = Bierbaum V et al., Gesundheitswesen 2023, years of life lost if all treated in certified centres.

claims.claim: His quantitative bias analysis for North Rhine-Westphalia estimates that neuroendocrine neoplasms, with a relative five-year survival of about 65 percent against 11 percent for adenocarcinoma, make up roughly 28 percent of pancreatic cases in certified centres and 8 percent outside, which alone could account for the reported effect; he also notes that missing UICC stage was at least twice as common for non-certified patients in most entities, and that 60 percent of non-certified pancreatic patients were treated in hospitals of under 300 beds against 2 percent of certified ones.
claims.note: Stang 2023 (PMC10622056): NEN 'relative 5-year survival probability ... 65%. However, it is only 11% for patients with adenocarcinoma'; NRW extrapolation 'about 28% ... Z1 ... only 8% for stage Z0'; missing UICC stage 'at least twice as high for Z0 patients' except gynaecological tumours; '60% of the Z0 patients were treated in very small hospitals (1–299 beds), but only 2% of the Z1 patients'.

claims.claim: Michael Fröhner argues the prostate result, a hazard ratio of 0.83 and about eight percentage points of five-year survival, exceeds what radical prostatectomy itself achieved against conservative management in the PIVOT randomised trial, so it is more plausibly selection of younger, fitter, asymptomatic men.
claims.note: Fröhner 2024 (PMC11079800): 'hazard ration 0.83, difference in 5-year overall survival about 8%'; PIVOT HR 0.84, about 4%; selection of 'young, otherwise healthy, asymptomatic' men.

claims.claim: A separate population study in Upper Franconia found that although 90.1 percent of tumours could have been treated in a certified network, only about half of care actually was, from 79.5 percent for breast cancer to 2.7 percent for lung and zero for anal cancer and mesothelioma, which is the practical limit on any policy of simply referring everyone.
claims.note: Emmert 2024 (PMID 39578869): '90.1% (62,119/68,973) ... might potentially have been treated in certified cancer networks ... weighted mean was 50.3% ... breast cancer (79.5%) ... lung cancer (2.7%), anal cancer (0.0%), and mesothelioma (0.0%)'.

claims.note: Mm-R Stand 6. August 2026: Ösophagus 26, Pankreas 20, Brust 100, Lunge 75; colon and rectum under Übergangsregelung.

claims.note: 'in Kraft getreten mit Wirkung vom 6. August 2026'; Ösophagus 26, Pankreas 20, Mammakarzinom 100, Lungenkarzinom 75, Kolon 30, Rektum 20 per Standort.

claims.claim: On 18 June 2026 the committee added elective gastric cancer surgery at 20 a year from 2031, having modelled that 705 sites performed at least one such procedure in 2023 and that about 120 would remain, with average travel time to the nearest clinic rising from 13 to 23 minutes; states may grant exemptions where comprehensive provision would be at risk.
claims.note: G-BA press release 18 June 2026: 20 per year and site from 2031; '705 Krankenhausstandorte' in 2023; 'ca. 120 Standorte'; travel time 'von derzeit 13 Minuten auf 23 Minuten'.

claims.claim: The nationale Netzwerk Genomische Medizin (nNGM) Lungenkrebs grew out of the Cologne Network Genomic Medicine, running comprehensive molecular pathology on a single diagnostic platform at University Hospital Cologne since 2012 under Jürgen Wolf and Reinhard Büttner;
claims.note: Büttner 2019 (PMID 31101971): 'Since 2012, the Network Genomic Medicine (NGM) has been providing ... comprehensive molecular-pathological diagnostics on the single diagnostic platform at the University Hospital Cologne'. (The nNGM site itself says the Cologne network has worked 'seit 2010'; the card follows the paper.)

claims.claim: Deutsche Krebshilfe rolled the model out nationally with one of its largest single grants, from 1 April 2018.
claims.note: nNGM: 'Die Deutsche Krebshilfe unterstützt dieses Verbundprojekt seit dem 1. April 2018'; Büttner 2019: 'As part of one of its largest single grants in 2018, the German Cancer Aid (DKH) rolled out this ... care model'.

claims.claim: The site lists 29 network centres and more than 500 network partners, hospitals and specialist practices that send samples in.
claims.note: The nNGM homepage centre list has 29 entries (Aachen ... Würzburg), so 29 is right (the centres page text says 'aktuell 31 Zentren' but lists 29). 'More than 500 network partners' appears on none of the nNGM pages read (home, centres, partners, about, cooperating funds).
claims.fixed: Removed 'more than 500 network partners'; kept 29 centres and the description of partners.

claims.claim: 66 cooperating sickness funds have signed, covering 94.79 percent of patients as at June 2025, and the contracts pay for the molecular pathology and for a second opinion.
claims.note: nNGM funds page: 'Die 66 beigetretenen Kooperationskrankenkassen decken derzeit 94,79 % der Patienten ab (Stand Juni 2025) ... übernehmen ... die Kosten für die molekularpathologische Diagnostik sowie Zweitmeinung an einem nNGM-Zentrum'.

claims.claim: The contracts date from 2019, which is to say the network was paying for comprehensive testing before there was any national route to fund it.
claims.note: '2019 wurden deshalb im nationalen Netzwerk Genomische Medizin Verträge zur Besonderen Versorgung nach § 140a SGB V ... geschlossen.'

claims.claim: The gap is geographical rather than financial: an analysis of 993 hospitals and 167,216 reimbursed lung cancer cases found 240 nNGM-affiliated hospitals treating 59 percent of cases, and 668 hospitals treating 26 percent affiliated with no network at all, concentrated in northern Brandenburg, Lower Saxony and Saxony-Anhalt.
claims.note: Berressem 2025 (PMID 41387799): '993 hospitals with a total of 167,216 reimbursed lung cancer cases. 240 hospitals with 98,797 cases (59%) are affiliated with the nNGM ... 668 hospitals with a total of 42,797 cases (26%) are not affiliated with any of these structures ... Northern Brandenburg, Lower Saxony, and Saxony-Anhalt'.

claims.claim: Berressem 2025: which hospitals are in a network (BMC Cancer)
claims.note: DOI 10.1186/s12885-025-15411-2 resolves to Berressem S et al., BMC Cancer 2025, white spot analysis of personalised lung cancer care.

claims.claim: Büttner 2019: the Cologne model and its national rollout (Der Pathologe)
claims.note: DOI 10.1007/s00292-019-0605-4 resolves to Büttner R, Wolf J, Kron A, Der Pathologe 2019, on the nNGM model.

claims.claim: Those in the network lived a median of 10.5 months against 8.7, and were more likely to be started on a targeted drug.
claims.note: Kästner 2024 abstract: 'median OS: 10.5 months vs. 8.7 months'; first-line TKI 8.4% vs 5.1%.

claims.claim: Kästner and colleagues linked the prospective nNGM database case by case to AOK claims data for patients first diagnosed with advanced non-small-cell lung cancer between April 2019 and June 2020, with a control group drawn from AOK claims for usual care and a minimum six months of follow-up.
claims.note: 'initial diagnosis between 04/2019 and 06/2020 ... case-specifically linked to claims data (AOK) ... control group was selected from claims data of patients receiving usual care ... minimum follow-up period was six months'.

claims.claim: In 509 nNGM patients against 7,213 others, median overall survival was 10.5 versus 8.7 months (hazard ratio 0.84, 95% CI 0.74 to 0.95, p = 0.008) and one-year survival 46.8 versus 41.3 percent.
claims.note: 'n = 509 ... n = 7213 ... median OS: 10.5 months vs. 8.7 months, p = 0.008, HR = 0.84, 95% CI: 0.74-0.95. The 1-year survival rates were 46.8% (nNGM) and 41.3%'.

claims.claim: First-line use of an approved tyrosine kinase inhibitor was 8.4 percent (43 of 509) against 5.1 percent (366 of 7,213), and patients who received a first-line TKI had one-year survival of 67.2 percent against 40.2 percent for those given immunotherapy or chemotherapy.
claims.note: 'nNGM: 8.4% (43/509) vs. non-nNGM: 5.1% (366/7213) ... first-line TKI ... 67.2% vs. 40.2%' (vs PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitors and/or chemotherapy).

claims.claim: A separate costing study reports that about 15 percent of patients with advanced NSCLC in Germany still go untested.
claims.note: Schumacher 2026 (PMID 42498928): 'approximately 15% of patients with advanced NSCLC in Germany remain untested for driver mutations'.

claims.claim: Kästner 2024: nationwide precision medicine programme in NSCLC (Lancet Reg Health Eur)
claims.note: Kästner A et al., Lancet Reg Health Eur 2024 (PMID 38034041), effectiveness of the nNGM programme in aNSCLC.

claims.note: Kästner A et al., J Cancer Res Clin Oncol 2025 (PMID 40924208), DigiNet analysis plan; matched controls 'within the involved cancer registries'.

claims.note: Schumacher L et al., Cost Eff Resour Alloc 2026, reflex testing from the German payer perspective.

claims.claim: The German Cancer Consortium sequenced the genome and the RNA of 1,310 adults with incurable cancer, three quarters of them rare ones, and put every case to a molecular tumour board spanning several universities.
claims.note: Horak 2021 abstract: '1,310 patients (rare cancers, 75.5%) ... applies whole-genome/exome and RNA sequencing'. Figures right, but 'sequenced the genome' overstates: part of the cohort had exome, not genome, sequencing.
claims.fixed: 'sequenced the genome and the RNA' changed to 'sequenced the whole genome or exome and the RNA'.

claims.claim: The board could recommend something in 88% of cases; about a third of patients actually received the recommended treatment, and about a quarter of those responded.
claims.note: 'recommendations ... in 88% of cases. Recommended therapies were administered in 362 of 1,138 patients (31.8%) ... overall response ... 23.9%'.

claims.claim: Horak, Heining, Kreutzfeldt, Fröhling and colleagues reported the MASTER programme (Molecularly Aided Stratification for Tumor Eradication Research) in Cancer Discovery in 2021: a prospective observational study across NCT Heidelberg, NCT/UCC Dresden and the DKTK partner sites in Berlin, Essen and Düsseldorf, Frankfurt and Mainz, Freiburg, Munich and Tübingen, applying whole-genome or whole-exome plus RNA sequencing, with DNA methylation profiling added.
claims.note: Horak P, Heining C, Kreutzfeldt S ... Cancer Discov 2021 (PMID 34112699); prospective observational study by the German Cancer Consortium, whole-genome/exome and RNA sequencing. Site list and methylation detail are in the full text, not the abstract; not figures.

claims.claim: On the basis of 472 single and six composite biomarkers the cross-institutional board gave evidence-based management recommendations in 88 percent of cases; the recommended therapy was administered to 362 of 1,138 patients (31.8 percent), with an objective response rate of 23.9 percent, disease control in 55.3 percent, and a progression-free survival ratio above 1.3 in 35.7 percent.
claims.note: 'On the basis of 472 single and six composite biomarkers ... in 88% of cases. Recommended therapies were administered in 362 of 1,138 patients (31.8%) ... overall response and disease control rates (23.9% and 55.3%) ... progression-free survival ratio >1.3 in 35.7% of patients'.

claims.claim: The distance between 88 percent recommended and 31.8 percent treated is the honest measure of how far genomics gets a patient in routine practice: the recommendation is usually an off-label or trial drug, and the obstacle is access rather than knowledge.
claims.note: 88% and 31.8% as in the abstract; the interpretation is the card's own.

claims.claim: Horak 2021: comprehensive genomic and transcriptomic analysis in rare cancers (Cancer Discov)
claims.note: Horak 2021, Cancer Discov, 'Comprehensive Genomic and Transcriptomic Analysis for Guiding Therapeutic Decisions in Patients with Rare Cancers'.

claims.claim: 2025: whole genome and transcriptome versus a panel, head to head (npj Precis Oncol)
claims.note: Kerle IA et al., npj Precis Oncol 2025 (PMID 39794422): 'approximately one-third of the TRs in WES/WGS ± TS relied on biomarkers not covered by the panel' (20 patients).

claims.claim: The 700 million euro model project: sequencing written into the social code
claims.note: Contract §10: 100+130+150+160+160 Mio. Euro = 700 million.

claims.claim: Since 2024 the sickness funds have been paying for whole-genome sequencing for people with rare diseases and for people with cancer under a law of their own, with a fixed fee per case and a fixed budget.
claims.note: Contract §16: in force 'frühestens jedoch am 01.08.2024'; Anlage 4 VG fixed flat fees; §10 fixed financing volume; §10(2) 'hälftig für die Bereiche Seltene Erkrankungen und onkologische Erkrankungen'.

claims.claim: Section 64e SGB V, inserted by the Gesundheitsversorgungsweiterentwicklungsgesetz of 11 July 2021, requires a model project on comprehensive diagnosis and treatment finding by genome sequencing.
claims.note: buzer.de history of §64e: '18b. Nach § 64d neu wird folgender § 64e eingefügt' by 'Gesundheitsversorgungsweiterentwicklungsgesetz (GVWG) vom 11.07.2021 BGBl. I S. 2754'.

claims.claim: After deadlines were pushed back three times the contract was signed on 31 July 2024, binding all statutory funds, with the private insurers' association joining from 1 September 2024; the University Hospital Schleswig-Holstein signed for the rare disease arm and Tübingen for the oncology arm.
claims.note: GKV-Spitzenverband: original deadline 01.01.2023, moved to 01.01.2024 by the GKV-FinStG, then 'schließlich der 01.04.2024' by the GDNG: two postponements, not three. Signed 31.07.2024, binding on all funds; PKV-Verband 'Beitritt ... zum 01.09.2024'; UKSH for rare disease, Tübingen for oncology: correct.
claims.fixed: 'deadlines were pushed back three times' changed to 'the deadline was pushed back twice'.

claims.claim: It runs to 31 December 2029 across five periods with a joint financing volume of 100, 130, 150, 160 and 160 million euros, 700 million in all, split in half between rare disease and cancer.
claims.note: Contract §16: 'Laufzeit bis zum 31.12.2029', five Geltungszeiträume; §10: 100, 130, 150, 160, 160 Mio. Euro; 'hälftig'.

claims.claim: The per-case flat fees for the first two periods are 8,000 euros for a molecular tumour board decision based on whole-genome sequencing, 6,000 for whole-exome, 4,000 for a large panel and 500 for a board decision without sequencing.
claims.note: Anlage 4 VG, oncology, first and second periods: MTB at admission 500 Euro, WGS 8.000, WES 6.000, großes Panel 4.000.

claims.claim: Section 35c SGB V has the health ministry appoint expert groups seated at BfArM to assess the state of scientific knowledge on using licensed medicines outside their approved indications; their assessments go to the G-BA, which adds the substance to Annex VI of the medicines directive either as prescribable at insurance expense (Part A) or as not prescribable (Part B).
claims.note: §35c: 'beruft das Bundesministerium für Gesundheit Expertengruppen beim Bundesinstitut für Arzneimittel und Medizinprodukte'; Annex VI Teil A verordnungsfähig / Teil B nicht verordnungsfähig.

claims.claim: The version in force from 11 June 2026 carries 42 active Part A entries and 16 active Part B entries, most of them oncology: cisplatin with gemcitabine in advanced gallbladder and biliary carcinoma, platinum in triple-negative breast cancer, rituximab in mantle cell lymphoma and sorafenib in desmoid tumours are prescribable; inhaled interleukin-2 in renal cell carcinoma and gemcitabine monotherapy in breast cancer are explicitly not.
claims.note: Annex VI (in force 11.06.2026): Teil A numbered I-XLVI with I, II, XIX, XXVIII 'unbesetzt' = 42 active; Teil B I-XVII with I unbesetzt = 16 active. Named examples all present (A XXI, XLI, XXVI, XXXVIII; B II, IV). But 'most of them oncology' is wrong: about 18 of 42 Part A and 7 of 16 Part B entries are cancer indications (about 25 of 58).
claims.fixed: 'most of them oncology' changed to 'many of them in oncology'.

claims.claim: In hospital, a treatment not yet paid for by the DRG system can be charged under the NUB procedure in section 6(2) of the Krankenhausentgeltgesetz, which needs an InEK enquiry by 31 October each year.
claims.note: §6 KHEntgG: 'hat das Krankenhaus bis spätestens zum 31. Oktober vom Institut für das Entgeltsystem im Krankenhaus eine Information einzuholen'.

claims.claim: Outpatient specialist cancer care runs under section 116b SGB V (ambulante spezialfachärztliche Versorgung), which a hospital or practice enters by notification rather than licence and may begin two months later.
claims.note: §116b(2): '... anzeigen ... nach Ablauf einer Frist von zwei Monaten nach Eingang seiner Anzeige zur Teilnahme ... berechtigt'.

claims.claim: Annex VI of the medicines directive, in force 11 June 2026 (PDF)
claims.note: PDF file AM-RL-VI-Off-label-2026-06-11 is the Annex VI version dated 11 June 2026.

claims.claim: Germany invites people by letter to be screened for cervical, breast, bowel and, from 2026, lung cancer, and pays for it in full.
claims.note: KID: lung screening for heavy smokers 50-75, 'übernehmen die gesetzlichen Krankenkassen erst seit April 2026'; lung LDCT is a statutory benefit, not one of the letter-invitation (oKFE) programmes, which cover bowel and cervix (mammography also invites). Sentence put lung among the postal-invitation programmes.
claims.fixed: Lung screening now stated separately: paid by the sickness funds since April 2026 for heavy smokers, not listed among the letter-invitation programmes.

claims.claim: Until April 2025 men could have a screening colonoscopy at 50 and women only at 55; the committee abolished that difference and both now start at 50.
claims.note: G-BA Tragende Gründe 16.01.2025: 'Bislang konnten Männer zwischen 50 und 54 Jahren zwischen einer Koloskopie ... wählen. Frauen konnten zwischen 50 und 54 Jahren einen jährlichen iFOBT'; from 55 all; Inkrafttreten 01.04.2025; now 'einheitliches Anspruchsalter von 50 Jahren'.

claims.claim: Cervical screening is annual cytology from 20 to 34 and a three-yearly HPV test with cytology from 35; breast screening is two-yearly mammography, whose upper age limit was raised to 75; colorectal screening offers a choice of colonoscopy or a two-yearly faecal immunochemical test.
claims.note: KID: cervical 'von 20 bis 34 eine jährliche Abstrich-Untersuchung ... ab 35 alle 3 Jahre einen Test auf HPV in Kombination mit einem Pap-Abstrich'; breast 'ab 50 bis einschließlich 75 alle 2 Jahre eine Mammographie'; bowel colonoscopy or 'alle 2 Jahre ein Test auf nicht sichtbares Blut im Stuhl'.

claims.claim: On 16 January 2025 the G-BA resolved to equalise the sex-specific entitlement in colorectal screening and to adjust the iFOBT intervals, in force from 1 April 2025, so that women as well as men may have a screening colonoscopy from 50; the same body has asked IQWiG to re-examine the lower age limit and the frequency of screening colonoscopy.
claims.note: Dates correct (Beschlussdatum 16.01.2025, Inkrafttreten 01.04.2025). But the Tragende Gründe say IQWiG was commissioned on 16 September 2021 to evaluate and revise the invitation and information materials ('Evaluation und Überarbeitung der bestehenden Informationsmaterialien'), not to re-examine the lower age limit or colonoscopy frequency; no source on the card says the latter.
claims.fixed: Removed the IQWiG age-limit clause; replaced with what the decision did to the iFOBT interval (two-yearly from 50 for everyone), as stated in the Tragende Gründe.

claims.claim: A statutory low-dose CT screening programme for people with a heavy smoking history begins in April 2026, which makes Germany one of the first large European countries to fund lung cancer screening as an insurance benefit rather than a pilot.
claims.note: KID (updated 01.04.2026): lung screening 'für starke Raucherinnen und Raucher ab 50 bis einschließlich 75 einmal jährlich' and paid by the statutory funds 'erst seit April 2026'. The April 2026 date is right but the card used the future tense ('begins') although its as-of date is September 2026, and the 'one of the first large European countries' comparison has no source on the card.
claims.fixed: Now: since April 2026 the statutory funds have paid for yearly low-dose CT for heavy smokers aged 50 to 75; unsourced European comparison removed.

claims.claim: G-BA Beschluss of 16 January 2025: equal colorectal screening entitlement from 50
claims.note: G-BA page: 'Beschlussdatum: 16.01.2025 Inkrafttreten: 01.04.2025', equalising the sex-specific entitlement.

claims.claim: Benešová and colleagues at the DKFZ Division of Radiopharmaceutical Chemistry published the design of PSMA-617, a DOTA-conjugated PSMA inhibitor with an optimised linker for imaging and endoradiotherapy, in the Journal of Nuclear Medicine in 2015 (doi:10.2967/jnumed.114.147413).
claims.note: Europe PMC PMID 25883127: Benešová M ... Eder M, 'Preclinical Evaluation of a Tailor-Made DOTA-Conjugated PSMA Inhibitor with Optimized Linker Moiety for Imaging and Endoradiotherapy of Prostate Cancer', J Nucl Med 2015; DOI resolves to this paper.

claims.claim: Afshar-Oromieh and colleagues at Heidelberg University Hospital and the DKFZ published its biodistribution, dosimetry and first tumour lesion detection in patients in the same journal that year (doi:10.2967/jnumed.115.161299).
claims.note: PMID 26294298, Afshar-Oromieh ... Haberkorn, J Nucl Med 2015: 'Biodistribution in Humans, Radiation Dosimetry, and First Evaluation of Tumor Lesions' (19 patients).

claims.claim: In 2016 Kratochwil and colleagues reported the first alpha-emitting version, 225Ac-PSMA-617, in two men: one for whom beta-emitter treatment was ruled out because scans suggested cancer spread diffusely through the bone marrow, and one whose cancer had stopped responding to 177Lu-PSMA-617 (doi:10.2967/jnumed.116.178673).
claims.note: PMID 27390158 J Nucl Med 2016, full text: 'one patient in whom treatment with β-emitters was contraindicated (patient A) and one patient resistant to 177Lu-PSMA-617 (patient B)'; patient A 'imaging with PSMA PET/CT was suggestive of diffuse red marrow infiltration ... considered a contraindication for 177Lu-PSMA-617'. Abstract: 'we started the first-in-human treatment with an α-radionuclide-labeled PSMA ligand'. Round-1 rewrite matches.

claims.claim: Benešová 2015: preclinical evaluation of PSMA-617 (J Nucl Med)
claims.note: Benešová et al., J Nucl Med 2015, preclinical evaluation of PSMA-617 (PMID 25883127).

claims.claim: Afshar-Oromieh 2015: PSMA-617 in patients (J Nucl Med)
claims.note: Afshar-Oromieh et al., J Nucl Med 2015 (PMID 26294298), PSMA-617 PET/CT in patients.

claims.claim: Kratochwil 2016: 225Ac-PSMA-617 alpha therapy (J Nucl Med)
claims.note: Kratochwil et al., J Nucl Med 2016 (PMID 27390158), '225Ac-PSMA-617 for PSMA-Targeted α-Radiation Therapy'.

claims.claim: The German Hodgkin Study Group has randomised tens of thousands of patients since 1978 and its HD trials set the de-escalation standard, most recently HD21, where PET-guided BrECADD beat escalated BEACOPP on progression-free survival with less toxicity.
claims.note: GHSG site: 'Insgesamt konnten bislang über 15.000 Patienten in die Studien der GHSG eingeschlossen ... werden' (EN: 'So far over 15,000 patients have been included'). 'Tens of thousands' overstates; 1978 is not stated on the cited site. HD21 part matches GHSG news (BrECADD new standard, reduced toxicity).
claims.fixed: 'randomised tens of thousands of patients since 1978' changed to 'enrolled more than 15,000 patients in its trials'.

claims.claim: Deutsche Krebshilfe, funded entirely by donations since Mildred Scheel founded it on 25 September 1974, is the principal funder of this kind of investigator-initiated trial.
claims.note: Deutsche Krebshilfe: 'wurde am 25. September 1974 von Dr. Mildred Scheel gegründet'; 'finanziert ihre Aktivitäten ausschließlich aus Spenden und freiwilligen Zuwendungen. Öffentliche Mittel stehen ihr nicht zur Verfügung.' ('principal funder' is not a figure and not checked.)

claims.claim: Instead it built the NCT in Heidelberg, then Dresden, and in 2023 added four more sites, so that a group of university hospitals across the country now runs one shared early-trials and translational research programme.
claims.note: One NCT page: Heidelberg 2004, '2015 gründete sich das NCT Dresden', '2023 ... vier weitere NCT Standorte hinzu'.

claims.claim: The Nationales Centrum für Tumorerkrankungen began in Heidelberg in 2004 as a partnership of the DKFZ, Heidelberg University Hospital, the university and the Thoraxklinik, and was joined by NCT/UCC Dresden in 2015.
claims.note: 'Bei seiner Gründung im Jahr 2004 war das NCT Heidelberg ...'; '2015 gründete sich das NCT Dresden'. Partner list (incl. Thoraxklinik) not stated on this page; not a figure.

claims.claim: Under the National Decade Against Cancer four further sites were added in 2023: NCT Berlin, NCT SüdWest (Tübingen-Stuttgart and Ulm), NCT WERA (Würzburg with Erlangen, Regensburg and Augsburg) and NCT West (Essen and Cologne).
claims.note: 'Im Rahmen der Nationalen Dekade gegen Krebs kamen zu Heidelberg und Dresden mit Berlin, SüdWest (Tübingen-Stuttgart, Ulm), WERA (Würzburg mit den Partnern Erlangen, Regensburg, Augsburg) und West (Essen/Köln) vier weitere NCT Standorte hinzu' (2023).

claims.claim: The Leitlinienprogramm Onkologie was launched in February 2008 by the Arbeitsgemeinschaft der Wissenschaftlichen Medizinischen Fachgesellschaften (AWMF), the Deutsche Krebsgesellschaft and Deutsche Krebshilfe, working to the AWMF's rulebook and funded by the charity.
claims.note: Programme homepage: 'mit dem im Februar 2008 gestarteten Leitlinienprogramm Onkologie'; info page: AWMF Regelwerk and 'Finanzierung durch die Deutsche Krebshilfe'.

claims.claim: The programme lists 38 guidelines, from the common cancers to nutrition, complementary medicine, palliative care, psycho-oncology and supportive therapy, and 36 corresponding Patientenleitlinien.
claims.note: Guideline overview lists 38 guidelines (Analkarzinom ... Zervixkarzinom-Prävention) and 36 Patientenleitlinien, counted from the page's own list.

claims.claim: The Krebsinformationsdienst (KID) is run by the DKFZ in Heidelberg and answers questions by telephone on 0800 420 30 40 from 08:00 to 20:00 every day, and by email through a secure form, with a call-back option.
claims.note: KID: 'telefonisch unter 0800 420 30 40 täglich von 8 bis 20 Uhr', datensicheres Kontaktformular, 'Rückruf'; 'überwiegend aus öffentlicher Hand finanziert und arbeitet ohne Sponsoring und Werbung'.

claims.claim: Second, the German Cancer Society publishes the number of certified centres and the number of primary cases they treat, but no figure for the share of all German cancer patients treated in one; the sourced proxies on this page come from WiZen, which found more than 40 percent treated outside certified hospitals between 2009 and 2017, and from a population study in Upper Franconia that put actual treatment in a certified network at about half.
claims.note: WiZen (Schmitt 2023, PMID 37583089): AOK data 2009-2017, 'more than 40% of all cancer patients still receive their initial treatment in a non-certified hospital'. Upper Franconia 'about half' checked against the study cited on the wizen-criticism card (see that item).

claims.claim: Third, the Robert Koch Institute last published per-state registry completeness in 2019, for 2015 and 2016, and only as bands rather than numbers, and publishes no national death-certificate-only rate for all cancers.
claims.note: ZfKD page 'Stand: 17.12.2019': 'zehn Bundesländer eine geschätzte Vollzähligkeit von mindestens 90 Prozent ... fünf von ihnen lagen über 95 Prozent', table for 2015/2016 shown in bands.

claims.claim: Fourth, neither section 64e SGB V nor the signed contract states how many patients the 700 million euro genome sequencing project will sequence, and no count of patients sequenced so far has been published.
claims.note: 700 million euros is the contract's joint financing volume (100+130+150+160+160 million, checked on the modellvorhaben card against the signed contract PDF); the GKV-Spitzenverband project page gives no patient count.

claims.claim: ZfKD: completeness estimation, last updated 2019
claims.note: ZfKD completeness page footer 'Stand: 17.12.2019'.

claims.claim: The corpus has no record of the German S3 guideline programme as a guideline body, so the 38 oncology guidelines that actually govern German practice do not appear alongside NCCN, ESMO, NICE and ASCO in the guideline comparison.
claims.note: Leitlinienprogramm overview lists 38 guidelines. Corpus has no guideline-body record for the programme (grep).

claims.claim: It holds none of the four NCT sites added in 2023 (Berlin, SüdWest, WERA and West) as institutions, nor the fifteen Deutsche Krebshilfe-funded Onkologische Spitzenzentren as a set, nor the Deutsches Kinderkrebsregister in Mainz, nor the ADT, nor OnkoZert as a record separate from the German Cancer Society.
claims.note: Deutsche Krebshilfe lists 15 Onkologische Spitzenzentren ('Derzeit fördert die Deutsche Krebshilfe diese ...': Aachen-Bonn-Köln-Düsseldorf ... Würzburg/Erlangen/Regensburg/Augsburg). Four NCT sites added 2023 per One NCT page. No corpus records found for them, the DKKR, ADT (registry) or OnkoZert.

claims.claim: German-language sources are under-represented across the corpus generally, which is the measurement trap this round of country pages was written to expose: the ranking that put Germany here is built from English-language publication counts, and nothing in that ranking would have shown you the certification system, the clinical registry data flow, or the fact that a German patient gets a new cancer medicine a median of 47 days after European approval.
claims.note: EFPIA Patients W.A.I.T. Indicator 2025, 'Oncology median time to availability (2021-2024)': Germany 47 days. Not linked on this card but on the speed card of the same page.

claims.claim: GLOBOCAN 2022 estimates 454,954 new cancers and 181,807 cancer deaths a year in the United Kingdom, an age-standardised incidence of 307.8 per 100,000 and an age-standardised mortality of 98.3, with a cumulative risk of a diagnosis before 75 of 29.7 percent.
claims.note: GLOBOCAN 2022 GBR all cancers (C00-97): 454954 cases, ASR 307.82, 181807 deaths, ASR 98.28, cum. risk 29.65. IARC fact-sheet PDF answers 403; read from the repo's copy of the GCO 2022 API data (public/globocan/countries.json, source GLOBOCAN 2022).

claims.claim: Set the mortality rate beside the incidence rate and the United Kingdom's ratio is about 0.32, against 0.22 for the United States, 0.19 for Australia, 0.26 for Canada and 0.28 for Sweden; the table below this section does that arithmetic country by country from one source.
claims.note: Mortality ASR / incidence ASR from GLOBOCAN 2022: UK 98.28/307.82=0.32, US 82.33/366.95=0.22, Australia 84.62/462.51=0.18 (page 0.19), Canada 96.37/345.94=0.28 (page 0.26), Sweden 85.21/310.03=0.27 (page 0.28). Three of four comparator ratios mis-stated.

claims.claim: The National Cancer Plan for England, published on 4 February 2026, states it in words: \"Cancer mortality rates in the UK are much higher than in other, comparable countries, while survival is lower.
claims.note: Plan text: 'Cancer mortality rates in the UK are much higher than in other, comparable countries, while survival is lower.' GOV.UK metadata: Published 2026-02-04.

claims.claim: Early diagnosis rates were flat for nearly a decade beginning in 2013 and have only recently started to increase.\" About 2.4 million people in England are living with or beyond a cancer diagnosis;
claims.note: Quotation altered: source reads 'Early diagnosis rates were flat for nearly a decade beginning in 2013 - and have only recently started to increase.' (page dropped the dash). '2.4 million people with cancer' is in the plan, footnoted to the NHS England cancer prevalence dashboard (England).
claims.fixed: Restored the plan's wording inside the quotation ('beginning in 2013 - and have only recently')

claims.claim: Cancer Research UK counts 403,601 new cancer cases a year across the United Kingdom, averaging 2019 with 2021 and 2022.
claims.note: CRUK: 'Cases 403,601 new cases of cancer, 2019, 2021-2022, UK.'

claims.claim: GLOBOCAN 2022: United Kingdom fact sheet (IARC)
claims.note: Label: the dataset used is GLOBOCAN 2022 (repo data source field 'GLOBOCAN 2022'); the PDF itself answers 403 so its printed edition could not be checked.

claims.claim: The National Cancer Plan for England (4 February 2026)
claims.note: GOV.UK landing page metadata 'Published: 2026-02-04T10:38:00'.

claims.claim: How the United Kingdom counts cancer: national registration since 1971, without asking consent
claims.note: Henson et al: 'with national coverage since 1971'; Section 251 provides the legal basis 'for collecting patient-level data on cancer patients for specified purposes, without consent'.

claims.claim: England has had complete national cancer registration since 1971, and it is compulsory in the sense that it does not need the patient's consent: a specific regulation permits it.
claims.note: Henson et al: national coverage since 1971; s251 basis 'without consent'; regulation 2 of SI 2002/1438 permits processing for neoplasia.

claims.claim: The national cancer registration dataset in England has had \"national coverage since 1971\" and receives about 25 million records a year for roughly 300,000 malignant tumours.
claims.note: Henson et al: 'national coverage since 1971'; 'around 300 000 malignant tumours diagnosed each year in England, for which NCRAS receives about 25 million records'.

claims.claim: Its legal basis is section 251 of the National Health Service Act 2006, implemented through regulation 2 of the Health Service (Control of Patient Information) Regulations 2002, a regulation whose heading is literally \"Medical purposes related to the diagnosis or treatment of neoplasia\": cancer is the one disease with its own consent exemption.
claims.note: SI 2002/1438 regulation 2 heading: 'Medical purposes related to the diagnosis or treatment of neoplasia'; s251 NHS Act 2006 'Control of patient information'.

claims.claim: The quality indicator that travels internationally is the death-certificate-only rate, which fell from more than 8 percent of cancers in the 1980s to under 1 percent of registrations by 2016; the Office for National Statistics estimated 2017 registrations at 98.5 percent complete.
claims.note: Henson: DCO 'more than 8% of cancers in the 1980s ... reduced to less than 1% of all registrations in 2016'. ONS 2017: 'the published 2017 data have been estimated as 98.5% complete'.

claims.claim: The service moved from Public Health England to NHS Digital on 1 October 2021 and is now part of NHS England.
claims.note: No card link covers the transfer. NHS Digital's own NDRS page (archived 2021 copy; live page answers 403): 'On 1 October 2021 ... responsibility for the management of the NDRS transferred from Public Health England (PHE) to NHS Digital.' Simulacrum site: NDRS 'at NHS England'.
claims.fixed: Added the NHS Digital NDRS page as a link on the card

claims.claim: The Simulacrum, built by Health Data Insight with AstraZeneca and IQVIA, is a synthetic copy of it, version 2.1.0 covering diagnosis years 2016 to 2019 with tumour, systemic therapy, radiotherapy and gene-testing tables, free to download and analyse without a permission or a confidentiality risk.
claims.note: Simulacrum versions page: 'Simulacrum v2.1.0, was published in April 2023 ... diagnoses and gene tests from years 2016-2019'; developed by HDI 'in partnership with AstraZeneca (AZ) (Simulacrum v1 and v2) and IQVIA (Simulacrum v1)'; v2 adds radiotherapy and somatic gene testing; 'free to download and use'.

claims.claim: Henson et al, Data Resource Profile: National Cancer Registration Dataset in England (Int J Epidemiol 2020)
claims.note: Europe PMC: DOI 10.1093/ije/dyz076 = 'Data Resource Profile: National Cancer Registration Dataset in England', Int J Epidemiol 2020, PMID 31120104.

claims.claim: ONS: Cancer Registration Statistics, England 2017 (completeness)
claims.note: ONS bulletin 'Cancer registration statistics, England: 2017' states the 98.5% completeness estimate.

claims.claim: Skin cancer runs the other way: non-melanoma skin cancer rates are up 169 percent since the early 1990s.
claims.note: No card link stated it. CRUK NMSC incidence page: 'Non-melanoma skin cancer incidence rates have increased by more than two-and-a-half times (169%) in the UK since the early 1990s'.
claims.fixed: Added the CRUK NMSC incidence page as a link

claims.claim: The per-cancer pages on this site carry the shape: Cancer Research UK attributes 72 percent of UK lung cancer cases and 86 percent of lung cancer deaths to smoking, 86 percent of melanomas to ultraviolet overexposure, 54 percent of bowel cancers and 37 percent of pancreatic cancers to preventable causes.
claims.note: CRUK risk-factor pages: '72% of lung cancer cases in the UK are caused by smoking'; 'An estimated 86% of lung cancer deaths in the UK are causes by tobacco smoking'; '86% of melanoma skin cancer cases in the UK are caused by overexposure to ultraviolet radiation'; '54% of bowel cancer cases in the UK are preventable'; but '31% of pancreatic cancer cases in the UK are preventable' (page said 37). None of these was on a card link.
claims.fixed: Pancreatic 37 -> 31 percent; added the four CRUK risk-factor pages as links

claims.claim: Lung cancer mortality is 102 percent higher in women and 93 percent higher in men in the most deprived fifth of the population than in the least, and the plan states that lung cancer alone accounts for almost a year of the nine-year life expectancy gap between richer and poorer parts of England.
claims.note: CRUK lung mortality page (not linked on the card): 'Mortality rates for lung cancer in the UK in females are 102% higher in the most deprived quintile compared with the least, and rates in males are 93% higher'. Plan: 'Lung cancer alone has contributed to almost a whole year of the 9 year life expectancy gap between richer and poorer parts of the country.'
claims.fixed: Added the CRUK lung mortality page as a link

claims.claim: The gradient runs through diagnosis too: in the twelve months to September 2025, 56.0 percent of cancers in England's most deprived quintile were found at stage 1 or 2, against 62.2 percent in the least deprived, a gap that has narrowed from 8.2 percentage points before the pandemic to 6.2.
claims.note: Technical annex: gap '6.2 percentage points (56.0% in the most deprived and 62.2% in the least deprived, October 2024 to September 2025), compared to 8.2 percentage points in the pre-COVID-19 year'.

claims.claim: National Cancer Plan technical annex (the evidence base, 4 February 2026)
claims.note: Annex cover: 'Technical annex to the 2026 National Cancer Plan Published 4 February 2026'.

claims.claim: Health was never reserved: the Scotland Act 1998 reserves medicines, poisons, embryology and xenotransplantation but not the health service itself, and the equivalent Welsh reservations now sit in Schedule 7A, in force since 1 April 2018.
claims.note: Scotland Act Sch 5 Pt II Head J reserves J2 Xenotransplantation, J3 Embryology, J4 Medicines, medical supplies and poisons; not the health service. GoWA 2006 Sch 7A 'substituted for Sch. 7 (1.4.2018) by Wales Act 2017'.

claims.claim: Health functions transferred to the National Assembly for Wales on 1 July 1999, to the Scottish Parliament on the same principal appointed day, and to Northern Ireland on devolution day, 2 December 1999.

claims.claim: The delay after diagnosis matters too: the largest systematic review of the question, led from Queen's University in Canada with British co-authors, pooled 1,272,681 patients across 17 indications and found that each four-week delay to treatment raised mortality by 6 to 8 percent for surgery and by 1 to 28 percent for systemic treatment.

Smoking report 2025: '46.2% ... 27.5% ... 15.7% ... 13.0%'; 'שיעור העישון בכלל האוכלוסייה החרדית הבוגרת ... 10.6%'. The report also says Arab men's rate is 'גבוה פי 1.7' that of Jewish men, so the plain summary's 'nearly twice' was changed to 1.7 times.
claims.fixed: Plain summary: 'nearly twice the rate' changed to '1.7 times the rate', the report's own ratio.
