claims.claim: Dagan et al., BNT162b2 mRNA Covid-19 vaccine in a nationwide mass vaccination setting (NEJM 2021)
claims.note: Dagan N et al., NEJM 2021.

claims.claim: Feinstein et al., short-term breast cancer risk prediction in 1,039,212 Maccabi members (Clin Breast Cancer 2025)
claims.note: Feinstein O et al., Clin Breast Cancer 2025, 1,039,212 members.

claims.claim: Pantanowitz et al., AI for prostate cancer diagnosis on biopsies, developed and deployed with Maccabi (Lancet Digit Health 2020)
claims.note: Pantanowitz L et al., Lancet Digit Health 2020 (authors include Maccabi's Shalev V).

claims.claim: How Japan counts cancer: a compulsory national register since 2016
claims.note: Registry download page: '全国がん罹患データ（2016年～2023年）'; registry is based on the cancer registration act (法律に基づいて).

claims.claim: The Act on Promotion of Cancer Registration put a single national register in place of the patchwork of regional registries that preceded it; its first year of data is 2016.
claims.note: First year of national registry data 2016: '全国がん罹患データ（2016年～2023年）'.

claims.claim: Every medical institution that treats cancer notifies 26 items to the prefecture, which deduplicates and forwards to the National Cancer Center; about 850 designated hospitals additionally keep a 105-item hospital-based registry of their own cases.
claims.note: 'がん診療を行うすべての医療機関では26項目を都道府県に届け出ます…合わせて105項目' and 'がん診療連携拠点病院等の約850の病院では…院内がん登録'.

claims.claim: The 2023 diagnosis year, published in March 2026, records 993,469 new cancers: 556,059 in men and 437,406 in women, a crude rate of 798.9 per 100,000.
claims.note: '2023年に新たに診断されたがんは993,469例（男性556,059例、女性437,406例）'; '人口あたりの罹患率は798.9 例 (人口10万対)' (crude, correctly labelled); history '2026年03月23日 罹患データを2023年に更新'.

claims.claim: Deaths are counted separately in the vital statistics: 384,111 cancer deaths in 2024, published in January 2026.
claims.note: '2024年にがんで死亡した人は384,111人'; '2026年01月07日 死亡データを2024年に更新'.

claims.claim: Five-year relative survival for the 2018 diagnosis cohort, published in July 2026, is 64.8 percent overall, 63.2 percent in men and 66.8 percent in women.
claims.note: '5年相対生存率は男女計で64.8 ％（男性63.2 ％、女性66.8 ％）'; '2026年07月22日 生存率データを2018年に更新'.

claims.claim: GLOBOCAN's estimate for Japan in 2022, which the table below renders, is 1,005,157 cases and 426,278 deaths, with an age-standardised incidence of 267.1 and mortality of 78.6 per 100,000: a lower age-standardised incidence than the United States on a far older population.
claims.note: Names GLOBOCAN 2022. Repo GLOBOCAN 2022 data (public/globocan/countries.json) JPN all cancers: [1005157, 267.08, 426278, 78.63]; USA ASR incidence 366.95. Card has no GLOBOCAN link of its own; the page's GLOBOCAN table carries the source.

claims.claim: The registry's 2023 diagnosis year records 104,864 stomach cancers, 71,135 in men and 33,729 in women, and 37,867 stomach cancer deaths in 2024.
Liver and intrahepatic bile duct cancer accounts for 32,673 diagnoses and 22,465 deaths, against 103,424 breast cancers and 16,005 breast cancer deaths.
claims.note: Liver figures on the linked liver page ('32,673例', '22,465人'), but breast figures ('103,424例', '16,005人') are on the breast page, which the card did not link. Figures correct.
claims.fixed: Added the ganjoho breast statistics page to the card's links.

claims.claim: Colorectal cancer is the largest single site with 154,039 diagnoses and 54,416 deaths; lung follows with 123,989 and 75,569; prostate has risen to 102,094 diagnoses; pancreatic cancer causes 41,235 deaths on 47,540 diagnoses.
claims.note: Colorectal on linked page ('154,039例', '54,416人'); lung ('123,989例', '75,569人'), prostate ('102,094例') and pancreas ('47,540例', '41,235人') only on their own ganjoho pages, not linked. Figures correct.
claims.fixed: Added ganjoho lung, prostate and pancreas statistics pages to the card's links.

claims.claim: Five-year relative survival for the 2018 cohort separates them sharply: prostate 95.7 percent, breast 89.7, colorectal 69.9, stomach 66.1, lung 39.3, liver 35.2, pancreas 13.2.
claims.note: Survival: prostate 95.7, breast 89.7 (女性のみ), lung 39.3, pancreas 13.2 on unlinked site pages; colorectal 69.9, stomach 66.1, liver 35.2 on linked pages. All figures correct.
claims.fixed: Added the missing site pages to the card's links.

claims.claim: Stomach cancer survival of 66.1 percent, in a disease usually written about as lethal, is a statement about when it is found rather than about how it is treated.
claims.note: Stomach page: '５年相対生存率 （2018年診断例） 66.1 %'.

claims.claim: Across all cancers 46 percent are confined to the organ they started in when they are diagnosed.
claims.note: xlsx 最新データ（進行度別）: 全部位 限局 割合 46.02%.

claims.claim: For stomach cancer it is 57 percent, and nine in ten of those people are alive five years later.
claims.note: xlsx: 胃 限局 割合 57.28%, 相対生存率 93.97%. 'nine in ten of those people are alive' presents a relative survival ratio as the share alive.
claims.fixed: Reworded: 'their five-year survival, measured against people of the same age without cancer, is 94 percent'.

claims.claim: The registry publishes five-year relative survival by clinical extent for the 2018 diagnosis cohort, excluding death-certificate-only cases, second primaries, in-situ disease and cases of unknown age or address.
claims.note: xlsx note *1 excludes DCO, 第2がん以降, 上皮内がん, 年齢不詳, 住所不明 (also non-malignant, unknown sex, 100+).

claims.claim: For all sites, 46.0 percent were localised (survival 91.2 percent), 23.0 percent regional (62.2), 18.9 percent distant (19.4) and 12.1 percent unknown.
Stomach cancer is the outlier: 57.3 percent localised (94.0 percent survival), 18.2 percent regional (50.4), 18.1 percent distant (7.0).
Lung cancer, which has only a chest radiograph behind it, is the mirror image: 31.3 percent localised and 38.8 percent distant.
claims.note: xlsx 肺: 限局 31.34, 遠隔 38.84.

claims.note: countries.json JP works 2021 4929, 2025 4604.

claims.note: countries.json JP trials 9840 (ClinicalTrials.gov query.locn).

claims.claim: The highly cited share, 2.84 percent against 4.35 percent for the United States, partly reflects a publication culture that puts a great deal of clinical work in Japanese-language and Japanese-domiciled journals that index and cite differently.
claims.note: countries.json citedHigh/total: JP 657/23161 = 2.84%; US 5051/115990 = 4.35%.

claims.claim: The guidance was issued on 31 March 2008 and has been amended eight times, most recently on 24 December 2025.
claims.note: Header '平成20年3月31日' then eight amendments, last '令和７年12月24日一部改正'.

claims.claim: Stomach screening is a questionnaire plus either barium photofluorography or upper endoscopy, the person's choice where both are offered, from age 50, every two years, with two long-standing concessions: barium may be offered from 40, and may be done annually.
claims.note: '５０歳以上…ただし、胃部エックス線検査については、当分の間、４０歳以上'; '２年に１回…当分の間、胃部エックス線検査を年１回実施しても差し支えない'; '受診者は…いずれかを選択'.

claims.claim: Cervical screening is a questionnaire, inspection, cervical cytology and bimanual examination from 20 every two years, or, as an alternative in the current text, HPV testing alone from 30 every five years with cytology as a triage test on a positive result and a follow-up test the next year for HPV-positive, cytology-negative women.
claims.note: '問診、視診、子宮頸部の細胞診及び内診'; '２０歳以上'; HPV検査単独法 '３０歳以上', '５年に１回', 'トリアージ検査陰性となった場合に翌年度追跡検査'.

claims.claim: Lung screening is a questionnaire and chest radiography from 40, annually; the current text lists no sputum cytology.
claims.note: '肺がん検診の検診項目は、質問…、胸部エックス線検査とする' (no sputum cytology); '４０歳以上'; '年１回'.

claims.claim: Breast screening is a questionnaire and mammography from 40 every two years, and explicitly does not recommend clinical breast examination.
claims.note: '質問…及び乳房エックス線検査'; '視触診は推奨しない'; '４０歳以上の女性'; '２年に１回'.

claims.claim: Bowel screening is a questionnaire and a two-day immunochemical faecal occult blood test from 40, annually.
claims.note: '問診及び便潜血検査'; '免疫便潜血検査２日法'; '４０歳以上'; '年１回'.

claims.claim: A combined screen is offered at the milestone ages of 40 and 50.
claims.note: '総合がん検診については…４０歳及び５０歳の者を対象'.

claims.claim: Each programme names the age band it most wants to reach, 40 to 69 in most cases, while requiring that anyone eligible be offered a slot every year.
claims.note: '受診を特に推奨する者を４０歳以上６９歳以下' (lung, bowel, breast; stomach 50-69, cervix 20-69); '受診機会を必ず毎年度設ける'.

claims.claim: About half of Japanese adults aged 40 to 69 have had each screen in the period it covers.
claims.note: Survey figures range from 36.5% (women, stomach, 1 yr) to 53.7% (men, stomach, 2 yr); cervical band is 20-69, stomach 2-yr band 50-69. 'About half … aged 40 to 69' overstates and mislabels ages.
claims.fixed: Reworded to 'Between about a third and a half of Japanese adults in each target age group have had each screen…, depending on the test and on sex.'

claims.claim: That is short of the government's own target of 60 percent, and it has barely moved across the 2016, 2019 and 2022 surveys.
claims.note: Plan: '受診率60％を目指す'; survey: 'いずれのがん検診においても、受診した者の割合は概ね横ばい' across 2016/2019/2022.

claims.claim: The 2022 Comprehensive Survey of Living Conditions, which asks people rather than counting municipal records and so includes workplace and opportunistic screening, found that in the previous year 47.5 percent of men and 36.5 percent of women aged 40 to 69 had a stomach screen, 53.2 and 46.4 percent a lung screen and 49.1 and 42.8 percent a bowel screen.

Over the previous two years 53.7 percent of men and 43.5 percent of women aged 50 to 69 had a stomach screen, 43.6 percent of women aged 20 to 69 a cervical screen and 47.4 percent of women aged 40 to 69 a breast screen.
claims.note: '過去２年間では「胃がん検診」…男が 53.7％、女が 43.5％…「子宮がん（子宮頸がん）検診」は 43.6％、「乳がん検診」は 47.4％'; ages 50-69, 20-69, 40-69.

claims.claim: The Fourth Basic Plan to Promote Cancer Control sets 60 percent uptake for every guideline-based screen and 90 percent attendance at the follow-up examination when a screen is positive.
claims.note: '指針に基づく全てのがん検診において、受診率60％を目指す…精密検査受診率 90％を目指す'.

claims.claim: The National Cancer Center's gastric screening guideline, 2014 edition, gives grade B to upper gastrointestinal radiography and grade B to upper endoscopy, both defined as having reasonable evidence of a reduction in mortality, and recommends endoscopy from 50 at an interval of two to three years.
claims.note: '胃X線検査： 推奨グレードB'; '胃内視鏡検査： 推奨グレードB'; '死亡率減少効果を示す相応な証拠'; '検診対象は50歳以上が望ましく、検診間隔は2~3年'.

claims.claim: The 2005 edition had graded endoscopy I, insufficient evidence; the upgrade to B came with the 2014 edition, and the guideline page names as its confirming evidence a Korean nested case-control study in 16.6 million people.
claims.note: 2005 edition: '胃内視鏡検査…推奨グレードI'; page cites Jun et al., Gastroenterology 2017; abstract: cohort of 16,584,283.

claims.claim: That study is worth reading closely, because it separates the two tests Japan offers: against never being screened, the odds of dying of gastric cancer were 0.53 (95 percent confidence interval 0.51 to 0.56) for endoscopic screening and 0.98 (0.95 to 1.01) for the upper gastrointestinal series, and the endoscopy benefit deepened with each additional screen.
claims.note: Abstract: 'ORs of death from gastric cancer were 0.53 (95% CI, 0.51-0.56) for upper endoscopy and 0.98 (95% CI, 0.95-1.01) for UGI series'; ORs fell with more screens.

claims.claim: In other words the largest study behind the recommendation found a 47 percent mortality reduction for endoscopy and none for barium, while Japan grades both B and still allows barium annually from 40.
claims.note: Guideline page: '胃内視鏡検診受診により、胃がん死亡率が47%減少したことが報告されました'; OR 0.98 for UGI.

claims.claim: The Japanese grade for barium rests on older Japanese case-control and cohort work rather than on this study, and the guideline has not been revised since 2014.
claims.note: Page heading '胃がん （最新：2014年度版）'.

claims.claim: National Cancer Center, gastric cancer screening guideline 2014 (胃がん検診ガイドライン)
claims.note: '「有効性評価に基づく胃がん検診ガイドライン」2014年度版'.

claims.claim: Effectiveness of the Korean National Cancer Screening Program in reducing gastric cancer mortality (Gastroenterology 2017)
claims.note: DOI resolves to Jun et al., 'Effectiveness of the Korean National Cancer Screening Program in Reducing Gastric Cancer Mortality', Gastroenterology 2017, PMID 28147224.

claims.claim: Treating the cause: Helicobacter since 2013, hepatitis since the 2000s
claims.note: 2013 correct (Helicobacter 2026 abstract: 'In February 2013 … coverage … was expanded'). 'hepatitis since the 2000s' is stated by no linked source; the Fourth Basic Plan describes hepatitis measures without that date.
claims.fixed: Title changed to 'Treating the cause: Helicobacter since 2013, and hepatitis B and C'.

claims.claim: Since 2013 the health insurance pays to eradicate Helicobacter pylori in anyone with gastritis seen at endoscopy, which in practice means almost anyone who is infected.
claims.note: Abstract: 'expanded to patients with H. pylori-positive, endoscopically diagnosed chronic gastritis' in February 2013.

claims.claim: In February 2013 insurance cover for Helicobacter eradication was extended from ulcer disease to endoscopically diagnosed chronic gastritis with a positive test.
claims.note: Abstract: 'In February 2013, Japanese national health insurance coverage for Helicobacter pylori eradication was expanded to patients with H. pylori-positive, endoscopically diagnosed chronic gastritis.'

claims.claim: A descriptive national time-trend study published in Helicobacter in 2026 reports annual stomach cancer deaths falling from 48,427 in 2013 to 37,394 in 2024, a 25.2 percent fall in crude deaths, with the decline concentrated below age 80 while deaths above 80 continued to rise; the authors are explicit that an ecological trend cannot separate eradication from endoscopy, birth-cohort effects and falling infection prevalence.
claims.note: Abstract: 'declined from 48,427 in 2013 to 37,394 in 2024, a 25.2% reduction in crude annual deaths'; <80 fell, 80+ rose; full text: 'aging of high-risk birth cohorts, secular decline in H. pylori prevalence … The aggregate data cannot distinguish these explanations.'

claims.claim: On the liver side the Fourth Basic Plan records hepatitis B surface antigen positivity of 0.54 percent and hepatitis C antibody positivity of 0.25 percent in the 2019 reporting year, against 0.87 and 0.60 percent in 2011.
claims.note: Plan footnote 12: 'ＨＢｓ抗原陽性率は 0.54％、ＨＣＶ抗体陽性率は 0.25％ … （平成 23（2011）年度 … 0.87％ … 0.60％）', i.e. positivity among people tested in local-government hepatitis screening, not population prevalence; the page did not say whose positivity.
claims.fixed: Added 'among people tested in local-government hepatitis virus screening'.

claims.note: DOI resolves to Helicobacter 2026 paper on trends after the 2013 insurance expansion, PMID 42708420.

claims.note: DOI resolves to 'Population-Based Gastric Cancer Screening in Japan: Evolution, Challenges, and Lessons for Implementation', Cancer Control 2026, PMID 42569856.

claims.claim: Every scheme covers the same treatments at the same nationally fixed prices, and the patient pays 30 percent of the bill at the counter, falling to 20 percent at 70 and 10 percent at 75 for most people.

claims.claim: At the end of March 2023 it counted 1,716 National Health Insurance schemes with about 24.1 million members, one nationally managed employees' scheme with about 39.4 million, 1,383 company health insurance societies with about 28.2 million, 85 mutual aid associations with about 9.8 million, and 47 Latter-Stage Elderly schemes with about 19.1 million.
claims.note: '国民健康保険 1,716 約2,413万人'; 協会けんぽ '1 約3,944万人'; '組合管掌健康保険 1,383 約2,820万人'; '共済組合 85 約982万人'; '後期高齢者医療制度 47 約1,913万人'; '令和５年３月末時点'.

claims.claim: Co-payment is 30 percent for adults under 70, 20 percent before compulsory school age, 20 percent from 70 to 74, and 10 percent from 75, with 30 percent for those on incomes comparable to the working population and 20 percent for certain others above an income threshold since October 2022.
claims.note: '75歳以上…１割（現役並み所得者は３割…一定所得以上の者は２割）'; '令和４年10月1日から'; '６歳（義務教育就学前）未満の者は２割'.

claims.claim: Patients paid 11.6 percent of national health expenditure in the 2022 financial year, about 5.4 trillion yen, against 50.0 percent from premiums and 37.9 percent from public funds.
claims.note: '国民医療費の負担構造（財源別）（令和４年度）' 患者負担 11.6%, 保険料 50.0%, 公費 37.9%; '患者負担5.4兆円'.

claims.claim: Whatever the treatment costs, a middle-income household under 70 pays at most about 80,000 yen in a month, and from the fourth month in a year of hitting the ceiling, 44,400 yen.
claims.note: Ceiling for the 3.7-7.7m band is '80,100円＋（医療費－267,000円）×１％' (87,430 yen on a 1m-yen month), not 'at most about 80,000'; 多数回 44,400 correct.
claims.fixed: Plain now gives 'about 80,000 yen … plus 1 percent of the bill above 267,000 yen (87,430 yen on a 1,000,000 yen month)' and 'barely enters into it'.

claims.claim: The ministry's own worked example, for someone under 70 on 3.7 to 7.7 million yen a year paying 30 percent: a month of care costing 1,000,000 yen means 300,000 yen at the counter, a ceiling of 80,100 yen plus 1 percent of the amount above 267,000 yen, so 87,430 yen, and 212,570 yen refunded.
Households can add members' bills together in a month, and after three qualifying months in twelve the ceiling falls to 44,400 yen for the two middle bands.
claims.note: '過去12か月以内に３回以上、上限額に達した場合は、４回目から「多数回」…' 44,400円 for 370-770万 and ~370万 bands; 世帯合算.

claims.claim: For inpatient care the ceiling is applied at the counter rather than reclaimed afterwards, and since April 2012 the same applies to outpatient care at a single institution.
claims.note: '（※１）入院の場合…現物給付化'; '（※２）外来でも、平成２４年４月から、同一医療機関で…現物給付化'.

claims.note: '患者負担割合及び高額療養費自己負担限度額（令和８年８月～令和９年７月）' with 年間上限 column.

claims.claim: After a public row in 2025 the government settled a package in December 2025: monthly ceilings rise from August 2026, but the reduced ceiling for people who are ill month after month is frozen, and a new yearly cap is added so that people who never quite reach the monthly ceiling stop paying once they reach the annual one.
claims.note: December 2025 package, August 2026 rise, frozen 多数回 ('多数回該当の金額を据え置き') and new 年間上限 all in source; 'After a public row in 2025' is in no linked source.
claims.fixed: Removed 'After a public row in 2025'.

claims.claim: The expert committee on the future of the benefit reported on 16 December 2025 and the ministry published the resulting figures.
claims.note: '令和７年12月16日 高額療養費制度の在り方に関する専門委員会'.

claims.claim: For the 3.7 to 7.7 million yen band under 70, the monthly ceiling becomes 85,800 yen plus 1 percent of the amount above 286,000 yen from August 2026, against 80,100 yen plus 1 percent above 267,000 yen now, with the multiple-month figure held at 44,400 yen and a new annual cap of 530,000 yen.
The top band moves to 270,300 yen plus 1 percent above 901,000 yen with an annual cap of 1,680,000 yen; the residence-tax-exempt band moves to 36,900 yen a month with an annual cap of 290,000 yen.
Income bands are subdivided further from August 2027, and households under about 2 million yen a year get a lower multiple-month figure.

claims.claim: For most of the 2000s a cancer drug reached Japanese patients years after American ones.

claims.claim: An analysis of 142 anticancer agents approved by both PMDA and the FDA between October 2004 and March 2025 found a median approval lag of 774 days, interquartile range 217 to 1,370, falling to about 100 days by the 2020s; in multivariate analysis development through a multi-regional clinical trial and concurrent approval in both countries were each independently associated with a shorter lag, while company origin, cancer type and use of an expedited pathway were not.

claims.claim: A separate study of the 55 anticancer drugs granted FDA accelerated approval between 2012 and 2021 put the median lag at 649 days and attributed most of it to the delay in filing rather than in reviewing, with Japanese participation in the pivotal study and use of a Japanese expedited pathway both shortening it.

claims.claim: KFF reports that the average marketplace deductible rose from 2,759 dollars in 2025 to 3,786 dollars in 2026, a 37 per cent increase it calls the steepest ever, and that the average net premium after subsidies rose 58 per cent, from 113 to 178 dollars a month, after the enhanced premium tax credits expired at the end of 2025.
claims.note: "a 37% increase, from $2,759 to $3,786. This marks the steepest increase ever"; "Premium payments from enrollees increased by an average of 58% from $113 to $178 per month".

claims.claim: Plan sign-ups fell by more than a million to 23.1 million for 2026, which KFF calls the sharpest single-year drop since the marketplaces opened, and it expects enrolment among people who actually pay their premiums to fall to about 17.5 million, possibly as low as 16.5 million, from 22.3 million in 2025.
claims.note: "Plan sign-ups fell by over a million to 23.1 million ... the sharpest single-year drop"; "could fall to about 17.5 million ... as low as 16.5 million people, down from 22.3 million people in 2025".

claims.claim: In employer coverage, KFF's 2025 Employer Health Benefits Survey puts the average annual premium at 9,325 dollars for single and 26,993 dollars for family coverage, with an average general deductible of 1,886 dollars for single coverage and 88 per cent of covered workers facing a deductible.
claims.note: "$9,325 for single coverage and $26,993 for family coverage"; "$1,886 for single coverage"; but the 88% is "Eighty-eight percent of workers with single coverage have a general annual deductible", not of all covered workers.
claims.fixed: Changed "88 per cent of covered workers" to "88 per cent of workers with single coverage".

claims.claim: When the price at the pharmacy counter rises, patients simply do not collect the prescription: half of those facing more than 2,000 dollars walk away from a new oral cancer drug.
claims.note: Doshi 2018: abandonment "49.4% for > $2,000 group" (risk-adjusted, new prescriptions); "half" is a fair rounding.

claims.claim: Ramsey and colleagues linked the Western Washington SEER registry to federal bankruptcy records for 1995 to 2009 and found people with cancer 2.65 times more likely to file for bankruptcy than people without, with rates two to five times higher in patients under 65 than in those over it.
claims.note: Ramsey 2013: Western District of Washington, 1995-2009; "cancer patients were 2.65 times more likely to go bankrupt"; "Younger cancer patients had 2-5 times higher rates of bankruptcy than cancer patients age sixty-five or older".

claims.claim: In a propensity-matched follow-up of 3,841 pairs from the same cohort, filing for bankruptcy after diagnosis carried an adjusted hazard ratio for death of 1.79 (95 per cent CI 1.64 to 1.96).
claims.note: Ramsey 2016: "After propensity score matching, 3,841 patients remained in each group ... adjusted hazard ratio for mortality ... 1.79 (95% CI, 1.64 to 1.96)".

claims.claim: Doshi and colleagues examined 38,111 new prescriptions for 38 oral anticancer agents in Medicare and commercial claims from 2014 to 2015: the risk-adjusted rate of abandoning the prescription entirely rose from 10.0 per cent where the out-of-pocket cost was 10 dollars or less, to 31.7 per cent at 100 to 500 dollars, 41.0 per cent at 500 to 2,000 dollars and 49.4 per cent above 2,000 dollars.
claims.note: "2014 to 2015 data ... Medicare and commercial ... 38 oral anticancer agents"; "(N = 38,111)"; "10.0% for <= $10 group ... 31.7% for $100.01 to $500 group, 41.0% for $500.01 to $2,000 group, and 49.4% for > $2,000 group".

claims.claim: Gilligan and colleagues, following adults aged 50 and over in the Health and Retirement Study, found 42.4 per cent had depleted their entire life's assets two years after diagnosis, with average losses of 92,098 dollars.
claims.note: Gilligan 2018 (PubMed abstract; Europe PMC copy truncated): persons >=50, Health and Retirement Study; "At year+2, 42.4% depleted their entire life's assets ... average losses were $92,098".

claims.claim: Han and colleagues compared 2,555,302 patients newly diagnosed with cancer aged 18 to 62 in 42 states' registries before (2010 to 2012) and after (2014 to 2016) the Affordable Care Act Medicaid expansion: two-year overall survival rose from 80.58 to 82.23 per cent in expansion states and from 78.71 to 80.04 per cent in non-expansion states, a difference-in-differences net gain of 0.44 percentage points overall, larger for liver (2.57), pancreatic (1.80), lung (1.29), non-Hodgkin lymphoma (1.07) and colorectal cancer (0.90), and larger among non-Hispanic Black patients (0.72).

claims.claim: Wagner and colleagues took the 47 drugs the FDA first approved for adult haematological or solid cancers between 2011 and 2015 and compared their labels with the NCCN guidelines.
claims.note: "47 drugs initially approved by the FDA between 2011 and 2015 for adult hematologic or solid cancers were examined".

claims.claim: The 47 drugs carried 69 FDA-approved indications but 113 NCCN recommendations: 69 (62 per cent) overlapped with the label and 44 (39 per cent) went beyond it, an average of 0.92 extra recommendations per drug.
claims.note: "69 FDA approved indications ... NCCN recommended these drugs for 113 indications, of which 69 (62%) overlapped ... and 44 (39%) were additional ... average number ... was 0.92".

claims.claim: Of those 44, 10 (23 per cent) rested on evidence from randomised controlled trials and 7 (16 per cent) on phase 3 studies.
claims.note: "23% (n=10) ... randomized controlled trials, and 16% (n=7) ... phase III studies".

claims.claim: Over 21 months of follow-up the FDA went on to approve 6 of the 44 (14 per cent).
claims.note: "During 21 months of follow-up, the FDA granted approval to 14% (n=6) of the additional recommendations". (The next sentence overstated the conclusion as fact; the abstract says the findings "raise concern that the NCCN justifies" coverage on weak evidence. Reworded.)

claims.claim: By the end of the 2010s a new cancer drug launched in the United States at a median 14,580 dollars a month, against about 6,000 to 7,000 dollars in England, Germany and Switzerland, and American prices then rose faster than inflation regardless of how well the drug worked.

claims.claim: Vokinger and colleagues compared 65 cancer drugs approved in the United States, England, Germany and Switzerland between 2009 and 2019.
claims.note: "The cohort included 65 drugs"; FDA approvals "between January 1, 2009, and December 31, 2019" in the US, England, Germany, Switzerland.

claims.claim: Median monthly treatment cost at launch in 2018 to 2019 was 14,580 dollars in the United States against 5,888 in Germany, 6,593 in Switzerland and 6,867 in England; the American figure in 2009 to 2010 had been 5,790 dollars.
claims.note: "median monthly treatment costs at launch were greater in 2018-2019 vs 2009-2010: $14 580 vs $5790 in the US, $5888 ... Germany, $6593 ... Switzerland, and $6867 ... England".

claims.claim: After launch, 48 of 65 (74 per cent) American cancer drugs had price increases greater than inflation, against 1 of 62 in England, 0 of 60 in Germany and 7 of 56 in Switzerland, and price changes were not associated with clinical benefit in any country.
claims.note: "48 of 65 (74%) cancer drugs had price increases in the US that were greater than inflation. Only 1 of 62 (2%) drugs in England, 0 of 60 drugs in Germany, and 7 of 56 drugs (13%) in Switzerland"; "There were no associations ... in any assessed country".

claims.claim: RAND's whole-market comparison for 2022 found United States manufacturer gross prices at 278 per cent of prices in 33 OECD comparison countries combined and 422 per cent for brand-name originators, before American rebates and discounts, which RAND notes are substantial and undisclosed; but unbranded generics, 90 per cent of American prescription volume, cost 67 per cent of comparison-country prices.

claims.fixed: Replaced the rebate clause with "falling to 308 per cent after RAND's estimated adjustment for American rebates".

claims.note: "74 ... 37 states and the District of Columbia ... 8 are Clinical Cancer Centers ... 58 are Comprehensive Cancer Centers ... substantial transdisciplinary research ... 8 are Basic Laboratory Cancer Centers".

claims.note: "four adult groups and one large group focused solely on childhood cancers ... Canadian Collaborating Clinical Trials Network"; "more than 2,200 sites".

claims.note: "coordinates and supports cancer clinical trials at more than 2,200 sites across the United States, Canada, and internationally ... NCI-funded treatment and primary advanced imaging trials"; groups listed match.

claims.note: "Thirty-two US academic institutions have been awarded a Lead Academic Participating Site (LAPS) grant ... most of the awardees are NCI-Designated Cancer Centers".

claims.claim: Alongside it, the NCI Community Oncology Research Program runs 7 research bases and 46 community sites: in the last five years it enrolled more than 20,000 patients to cancer treatment trials, 20 per cent of them from rural areas, more than 42,000 people to prevention and symptom-management trials, and more than 100,000 to screening trials.

Over 42,000 patients to NCI cancer prevention and symptom management trials ... Over 100,000 people to NCI screening trials." (on the About page of the linked site, not the home page).

claims.claim: Unger and colleagues pooled 13 studies covering 8,883 patients and found an overall trial participation rate of 8.1 per cent (95 per cent CI 6.3 to 10.0).
claims.note: Unger 2019: "13 studies ... with 8883 patients"; "8.1% (95% CI = 6.3% to 10.0%) enrolled".

claims.claim: Where patients did not enrol, no trial was available at their institution 55.6 per cent of the time; where a trial was available, 21.5 per cent of patients were ineligible for it; and among patients who were eligible with a trial available, 14.8 per cent declined.
claims.note: The four figures are shares of all patients along one decision pathway (55.6 + 21.5 + 14.8 + 8.1 = 100): "A trial was unavailable for patients at their institution 55.6% of the time ... 21.5% ... of patients were ineligible for an available trial, 14.8% ... did not enroll, and 8.1% ... enrolled". The page presented them as conditional rates ("where patients did not enrol", "where a trial was available", "among patients who were eligible"), which they are not.
claims.fixed: Rewritten as shares of all patients: 55.6 no trial available, 21.5 ineligible, 14.8 eligible and did not enrol, 8.1 enrolled.

claims.claim: Structural and clinical barriers together accounted for 77.1 per cent of non-enrolment.
claims.note: 77.1% is 55.6 + 21.5 as a share of all patients; the abstract: barriers "combined make trial participation unachievable for more than three of four cancer patients". The page said "77.1 per cent of non-enrolment".
claims.fixed: Changed to "ruled out a trial for 77.1 per cent of patients, more than three in four".

claims.note: "Most of the 1,724 counties without oncologists had oncologists in neighboring counties (n = 1,517 ...), while the 207 remaining counties had no oncologists in adjacent counties (486,000 adults age 55 years and older".

This progress largely reflects historical reductions in smoking initiation among Black teens, advances in treatment, and earlier detections".

scope: Census, not a sample: every numeric or dated sentence on the live country pages (src/data/country-us, -gb, -de, -il, -in, -jp, -ru, country-extras and china.ts) and every figure-bearing sentence on the 60 cancer pages with the most inbound links (summary, burden, prognosis, stateOfArt, standardOfCare, basics, openProblems).
